title: Address-based prefix and tail for the ripples and steam PIE kernels (gm-bzu.49 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to gm-bzu.49 (idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, bganim F1, oracle plan B22). gm-bzu.49 fixed SleepAnimation.cpp's halfBuf (now 16-byte aligned), AnimFireflies.cpp and AnimOrbits.cpp, plus the AnimPlasma and AnimAurora tails. This bead takes the two remaining PIE kernels.

## Astra correction (2026-09-30)
Aligning halfBuf is not enough. At width 466 the row stride is 932 B (4 mod 16), so ripples and steam fault on the second row of every band at full resolution too, and BgAnim.h only promises a 4-byte-aligned dst. Each kernel needs a prefix based on the address ((uintptr_t)p & 15), not the pixel index, and a correct tail, keeping pattern and dither phase.

## Where
- AnimRipples.cpp: the prefix aligns by pixel index (alignedStart = (x0 + 7) & ~7), which is 16-byte aligned only if the row is. Review lines 598-624 and the calls at 843, 852, 856.
- AnimSteam.cpp: fillRowPie is called when (w & 7) == 0 with no address check. Review lines 360-369 and 396-400.
ee.vst.128.ip and ee.vld.128.ip clear the low four address bits without a fault (CLAUDE.md, Animation kernels).

## How gm-bzu.49 did it (reuse the shape)
Keep the asm blocks byte-identical so tools/qemubench/check_copies.py still passes. Put the prefix and tail in a C++ wrapper around the kernel. Write the scalar pixels with bandRef's own per-pixel math so the pattern and dither phase stay tied to the absolute x. Give each kernel a host twin that stores to the address with its low four bits cleared, the way the vector store does, and route band() through the glue on every build. Then the host goldens, interlace_check and the fuzz exercise the prefix. If an asm block has to change, re-transcribe the QEMU test copy per tools/qemubench/README.md and run it under QEMU.

## Test matrix
dst offsets 0, 4, 8 and 12 bytes past a 16-byte boundary, widths 480, 240, 466 and 233. Rows per call are 1 and 2 for an even width and 1 for 233. tools/animbench/fuzz.cpp already has this pass (gm-bzu.49); run it with --align-only under ASan. It passes for ripples and steam on the host today only because their host band() is scalar: bandRef for ripples, bandPortable for steam. Add the host twins and it has to keep passing.

## Acceptance
- No masked-down PIE access precedes a permitted destination.
- The fuzz alignment pass is clean under ASan with the host twins in place.
- make check goldens stay exact and interlace_check passes at 480, 240, 466 and 233.
- QEMU tests pass if an asm block changed.
- On the device, /api/debug/animtest reports mismatch_px 0 for ripples and steam at half=1.
notes:
2026-10-01, commit b124911f.

Changed:
- AnimRipples.cpp: fillTileSpanPie stores scalar pixels until row + x is a multiple of 16 bytes (by address, not pixel index), then builds the 8-lane pattern rotated to that x (pat[i] = tile[(x + i) & 3]), so every pixel keeps tile[x & 3] of its absolute x. The function now exists on every build; off Xtensa the vector loop is a twin that stores to the address with its low four bits cleared. Host band() runs the device glue with accumulateBandRef in place of the asm accumulate.
- AnimSteam.cpp: new fillRow() does scalar prefix to a 16-byte address, fillRowPie over the whole groups of eight, scalar tail. fillRowPie returns early for w8 <= 0 (`loop` with 0 runs 2^32 times). Host twin of fillRowPie stores masked to 16 bytes; host band() runs the same glue (bc is a local alignas(16) array on the host, fillBcast on the device).
- Asm blocks unchanged. QEMU copies follow the new C: anim_ripples adds row starts at +4, +8, +12 bytes and compares the whole 64-word buffer; anim_steam adds the early return and a w8 = 0 case.
- tools/animbench/fuzz.cpp: header only (the alignment pass already covers every animation).

Verified:
- make check: goldens exact for ripples and steam. Plasma (max 9) and caustics (max 33) show nonzero diffs, as before this change. interlace_check OK at 480, 240, 466, 233.
- Fuzz under ASan and UBSan: full sweep clean, alignment pass clean, exit 0.
- Negative test in a scratch copy: with the old index prefix in Ripples and no prefix in Steam, the alignment pass fails for both with 2, 4 and 6 px written into the front guard at +4, +8, +12 bytes, at every width.
- make -f Makefile.lifecycle check: ALL OK.
- check_copies.py: PASS for all 15 tests. QEMU (firmware toolchain): anim_ripples PASS (10 fillTile, 7 accumulate cases), anim_steam PASS. With the old prefix put back temporarily, anim_ripples fails cases 5 to 9 (8 to 46 mismatches each), so the new cases see the masked store.
- pio run passes for display, display-loadtest, display-sim.

Float path (for gm-bzu.83): untouched. On the device band() still uses accumulateBandAsm (mul.s then add.s, two roundings) and bandRef's accumulateBandRef compiles to a fused madd.s at -O2, so device animtest can still show ripples mismatches from that, independent of this fill. Host band() and bandRef now share accumulateBandRef, so the host cannot show it.

Not done: agent-mail was unreachable (no answer on 127.0.0.1:8765), so no file reservations were made; the lead assigned the files.

Left for the bench (registry ids from BgAnimRegistry.cpp: ripples 5, steam 10; confirm against /api/debug/anim):
  http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=5&half=1
  http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=10&half=1
Both must report mismatch_px 0 (ripples may need gm-bzu.83 first, see above).
close_reason: Ripples and Steam PIE fills prefix by address with host twins; fuzz alignment pass, goldens, QEMU clean (b124911f)

title: Swatch checks in the device script and the legacy fallback must name the gradient
description:
Two more swatch checks count colours where their names claim they establish which gradient a row drew. Same fault as gm-nov3.33, different files. The gm-nov3.32 lane found them while reading nearby and neither is in a file it owned.

## The two, with the lines read on 2026-09-13

- `tools/picker_device_checks.py:164`, `global_row_draws_a_ramp`: `strip is not None and len(set(strip)) > 4`, on the "Global" row of the picker's first page.
- `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py:1021`, the `legacy_<name>_draws_a_ramp` family inside `check_legacy_unparsable_custom_falls_back`, three cases (empty, malformed, one_stop). Its threshold is **one** distinct colour, so anything that is not a flat block passes. The finder reported this at line 739, which is stale; 1021 is where it is now.

## Why the thresholds are meaningless

Measured on the simulator against the fixture library: all twelve entries draw between 46 and 80 distinct colours in their swatch. A threshold of 4 is cleared tenfold by every entry and a threshold of 1 by nearly anything. So a row drawing the wrong gradient, a built-in where a library entry belongs, or a fallback, passes either check.

## The oracle already exists and already handles tone

`swatch_matches_stops(strip, stops, tol=20)` in `test_animation.py`, with `toned_stops(settings, stops)`, `builtin_stops(index)` and the `check_swatch` wrapper around them. gm-nov3.33 built them and its docstring records why the two ends are the whole oracle. Reuse them rather than writing a second one; if reuse means moving them to a module both files can import, say so in the report and keep the move mechanical.

The legacy case has an exactly known target. Its sibling check `legacy_<name>_names_builtin_zero` already asserts the row names `THEME_NAMES[0]`, so the ramp to compare against is built-in 0's stops, toned.

`picker_device_checks.py` runs against the board, so say where its expected stops come from, and confirm the tone question there too: the board's stored tone is not guaranteed to be the identity.

## Do this after gm-nov3.33

That bead is landing the oracle and pointing four checks in `test_animation.py` at it, and may still move or rename it. Take your baseline at its HEAD.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both checks compare the strip against the stops of the entry the row is meant to show, with the tone setting applied, rather than against a colour count.
- [ ] The threshold of one distinct colour is gone, not raised.
- [ ] A mutation that makes each row draw a different gradient fails its check, shown passing before and failing after. Build the broken version in a scratch copy, never in the shared tree; the recipe is in `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md`.
- [ ] A repository search finds no remaining swatch check whose assertion is a count of distinct colours.
- [ ] The full settings UI suite passes, with before and after counts from the same tree. Say whether `picker_device_checks.py` was run against the board or only read, and if only read, say so plainly.

title: Smooth motion: every UI animation and transition at the loop rate
description: Owner's goal (2026-09-07): all animations and UI transitions extremely smooth. Plan synthesised from two oracle reports (GPT-6 Astra, oracle-astra2.md; Fable, oracle-fable2.md, both in the session scratchpad) and the round-one measurements (ui_results_2026-09-06.md). Agreed facts: a whole 480x480 frame is 461 KB and the GDMA push runs at 21.5 MB/s, so non-interlaced frames cannot reach the 50.7 Hz panel; the interlaced loop at 30 to 45 fps is the ceiling and a fade has no moving edge, so it stays smooth interlaced; the overlay blend is PSRAM-bound (vector equals scalar on the device), so assembly is not the lever for the UI side; the page snapshot (200 to 400 ms) is the real latency and only a fade started at the press hides it. Order: overlay alpha and fade transitions, press element with a touch path that does not wait behind LVGL, glyph atlas numbers, procedural needle/arc/tick elements, then shrink the page snapshot. Every step measured on the bench board (GM_UISTAT, GM_TOUCHLAT, blend_us, camera for comb) against ui_results_2026-09-06.md.

title: Global overlay alpha in the composite, with a per-frame ramp and a debug knob
description: Add an overlay alpha factor g (0..256) to SleepAnimation, latched once per frame beside the overlay index (the ofi latch in renderFrame), with a ramp record (t0, duration, from, to, ease) the UI task writes under the same seqlock pattern as layers. Apply g in blendRow and blendRowPie: a = (a * g) >> 8 before blend565; the a == 255 copy shortcut only applies when g == 256. ovg=N on /api/debug/anim sets g directly for measurement; ovramp=ms starts a test ramp. Acceptance on the board: blend_us at g=128 is at most 1.25x blend_us at g=256 on the brew screen; g=0 shows the bare animation; no visible comb or banding on camera during a 300 ms ramp with interlace on; bit-exact output at g=256 (fb compare).
close_reason: Done. Commit on idf5. blend_us 128/256 = 1.08x, gain 0 halves frame_us, midpoint check within 4 of 255.

title: Reduce translucent plate coverage on the brew screen (design decision)
description: The brew screen's plates are about 106k non-transparent overlay pixels and 12 to 13 ms of blend per frame, the largest fixed per-frame cost on the render task. Both oracles rank cutting coverage above any kernel work: removing 20k blended pixels saves 3.4 to 5 ms per frame. Propose a redesign to the owner (smaller supporting plates behind numbers only, or opaque plates that take the copy path) with mock renders; implement on approval. Acceptance: blend_us on the brew screen down by at least 3 ms with the approved design; owner sign-off on the look.
notes:
2026-09-08: proposal published for the owner: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2293d253-b60b-4762-8105-0c63e3885c3b (tools/plate_concepts.py renders the options from the board's own brew-screen pixels; tools/overlay_footprint/plate-concepts.json has the numbers). Options and per-frame blend: whole disc r=180 at 60 percent 101,792 px 12.2 ms (today's Custom); r=140 61,520 px 7.4 ms; r=110 38,000 px 4.6 ms but cuts the profile row; opaque disc 0 (copy path); no plate 0 (the shipping default: bgAnimClearPlates defaults to Hide, so the cost applies only when a user picks a translucent Custom plate). Implementation waits for the owner's choice; a disc size change is a generated-screen change shared by steam, water and status.

Decided 2026-09-09 by the owner: radius 140 at 60 percent (61,520 px, 7.4 ms of blend). Change the generated disc shared by brew, steam, water and status; verify blend_us on the brew screen with a Custom translucent plate drops by at least 3 ms (tools/blend_ab.py) and the profile row stays inside the plate.

Done 2026-09-09: DefaultUI::applyAnimPlates paints a radius-140 child disc behind the four dial panels in mode 2 and leaves the panels transparent (generated screens untouched). Bench board, brew screen, interlace pinned, cap 45, divider 8: blend 9.6 ms over 103k px before, 6.9 and 7.1 ms over 65k px after (two runs), 27.5 to 30.2 fps. 2.6 ms saved against the 3 ms asked; the shortfall is the kernel's per-pixel cost being 0.07 us now, not the 0.12 the estimate used. Framebuffer capture: profile row and centre controls inside the disc.
close_reason: Radius-140 disc shipped; owner chose it 2026-09-09; blend 9.6 to 7.0 ms on the brew screen.

title: Flat runs: composite constant-colour overlay spans without reading PSRAM
description:
The overlay blend is PSRAM bound: the brew, status and menu screens carry about 106k non-transparent overlay pixels, 3 bytes each, read from PSRAM every frame. Measured 2026-09-07 on the bench board: blend_us 13 to 20 ms on those screens, frame_us 43 to 71 ms at cap 45 (the loop runs at 15 to 23 fps), and gain 0 (no composite) drops frame_us to 25 ms. Most of those pixels are flat plates: long runs of one colour and one alpha.

Extend the span scan (publishOverlayRanges) to detect runs of identical 3-byte pixels of 16 px or more and store them as flat runs (colour, alpha, x0, x1) in a parallel table. In the composite, a flat run uses a constant-colour kernel like elemFillRow (two multiplies per pixel pair, no PSRAM read); textured runs keep blendRow. Interlace, gain, scrim and the copy repair are unchanged. Acceptance on the board: blend_us on the brew screen at least 2x lower with the plates on; bit-exact framebuffer against the old blend at gain 256 (the flat kernel must use the same blend565 arithmetic, so use a per-pixel path with the constant hoisted, not the Q5 kernel, unless the difference is shown to be at most 1 RGB565 step); span scan time within 1.3x of today; sim build unaffected; settings suites pass.
close_reason: Measured, not shipped. Flat runs were implemented (exact per-run classification, blendRowSplit, flatcheck 17,656 rows with 0 mismatches) and measured on the bench board 2026-09-07. Plates hidden (this board's setting): 3 to 4 percent of the covered pixels are flat, blend unchanged. Plates on (Custom, black 35 percent): 51 percent coverage, 77 percent of it in flat runs of 16 px or more, blend 25.3 ms with flat runs against 28.8 ms without, a 12 percent gain, far from the 2x acceptance. The blend under UI churn is bound by bus and cache contention with LVGL on core 1, not by the pixels it reads: the same brew screen blends in 4 ms when the UI is quiet and 12 to 17 ms while it refreshes 3 times a second. Code reverted; the /api/debug/ovl overlay dump written for the analysis stays (scratch ovl_analyse.py reads it). Follow-up is gm-2cl.12 (IRAM) and the display-list UI (.5/.6).

title: Render task hot path in IRAM so LVGL cannot halve the animation rate
description:
Measured 2026-09-07 on the bench board (display-loadtest, Starfield, cap 45): while the UI task runs LVGL passes for the status screen (about 3 refreshes a second, 40 to 55 ms of draw each), every stage of the render task doubles (band 7 to 14 ms, push 7 to 15, blend 4 to 17) and the loop drops from 39 to 17 fps. Nothing in the render task's data path changed; the band kernel reads and writes SRAM only. The cause is the 16 KB instruction cache both cores share: LVGL's code evicts the render loop, and every refetch queues on the MSPI bus behind the panel's PSRAM stream.

Experiment: IRAM_ATTR on renderFrame, renderLoop, pushLoop, presentFrame, scrimRow, scrimRowPie, expandScrimInv and Starfield's band, starfieldVigRowAsm and plotStarsAndShoot. IRAM text grew 9,296 B, dram0.dummy 9,216 B. Same load: 28 fps, band 7 to 9, blend 8 to 10, push 5 to 8.

Work:
- Decide the production set. renderFrame carries GM_TOUCH_PROBE census code that production does not build; measure the production IRAM delta and int_free/dma_free against the 20 KB asset gate floor.
- Every animation's band() and its row helpers get BGANIM_IRAM (BgAnimCommon.h); bandRef stays in flash. Report the total IRAM cost per animation.
- Rerun the brew timeline (scratch brew_timeline.py) with a serial capture and record fps, band, blend, push with and without UI churn.
- Update CLAUDE.md UI-pipeline invariants and the KB caches page (our work section).

Acceptance:
- Status screen under synthetic brew churn at cap 45: loop at or above 27 fps (was 17), band_us within 1.3x of the quiet value.
- Production build: dma_free at idle at least 8 KB above the 20 KB asset gate floor; document the measured delta.
- Sim and native builds unaffected (BGANIM_IRAM empty on host); settings suites pass.
notes: 2026-09-07 final set: renderFrame, renderLoop, presentFrame, pushLoop, scrimRow, scrimRowPie, expandScrimInv. IRAM text 98,335 to 105,983 B (+7,648), dram0.dummy +7,680. Loadtest int_free at 37 s uptime 37.1 KB (was about 46 KB), dma_free 29.4 KB (was 38.2). Brew timeline (scratch brew3.txt): 27.7 to 28.6 fps under churn (was 17), band median 10 to 12 ms (quiet 7 to 8), blend 8 to 10, push 6 to 8. With Starfield's kernel also pinned (brew2.txt, +9.2 KB total) 28 fps and band 7 to 9: kernel pinning buys about 2 ms of band for 1.1 KB per animation, not taken.
close_reason: Committed. Sim suite PASS (out_sim_iram), device scenarios all pass (temps, display, machine, schedules, status, rig); the device run's restart round trip crashed once on a None row after the reboot (standby takeover, known limit) and passed on rerun. Acceptance: 27.7 to 28.6 fps under churn (target 27), band median 10 to 12 ms against 7 to 8 quiet (1.4x, target 1.3x, recorded), DRAM cost 7,680 B.

title: POC: render the background at raster time into the bounce ring, no framebuffer
description:
Decided 2026-09-07 with the owner after the Codex (GPT-5.6) demo-scene review (scratch oracle-astra-demoscene.md, item 1): build a proof of concept, measured, before any display-list UI work, because the verdict decides which pipeline the UI work targets.

Idea: configure the RGB panel without its PSRAM framebuffer (esp_lcd no_fb bounce mode) and fill each internal bounce buffer from a frame-latched animation state plus the overlay composite. A producer task on core 0 keeps a ring of prepared bands ahead of the scan; the refill callback (IRAM, core 1) only hands over the next prepared buffer and counts underruns. Removes the 461 KB framebuffer, the 7 to 15 ms push and the constant 24 MB/s scan read.

Budget per 2-row band: 82 us at divider 6 (50.7 Hz), 96 us at divider 7 (43.4 Hz), 110 us at divider 8 (38 Hz). Starfield band 7 ms per frame is 29 us per band, overlay blend 4 ms is 17 us. Lava, ember, aurora and mandala (24 to 43 ms per frame) do not fit at any divider and would stay on the framebuffer path or drop to a lower internal rate.

Harness: display-loadtest env behind GM_RASTER_POC, Starfield plus the current overlay composite. Counters on /api/debug/anim: underruns, worst-case ring depth, producer band time max, ISR time max. Loads: two browser tabs and the synthetic brew cycle running, BLE link as on the bench.

Acceptance (kill criteria stated as their inverse):
- Zero underruns per minute at divider 8 and at divider 6 under the loads above; report both.
- Producer band time max under 60 us at divider 6 for Starfield with the overlay on.
- Camera check: no displaced band on a 60 s burst; note whether 38 Hz flickers on this panel.
- Internal RAM: report int_free and dma_free against the framebuffer path; the ring may not take more than the existing 15,360 B bounce pool plus 8 KB.
- Report which animations fit at each divider from measured band times, and what the two-pipeline cost would be.
notes:
Round 1, 2026-09-07 (display-raster env, GM_RASTER_POC, render task at its normal priority 1, Starfield kernel in flash, brew screen refreshing 3 times a second, panel at divider 8 = 38 Hz): requests 9,200 a second as expected (240 bands x 38 Hz); underruns 45 percent of requests, drops 25 percent, resyncs 700 a second, request-to-fill age max 58 ms quiet and 152 ms under synthetic brew, render task idle wait 0 to 2.7 ms a frame. Per frame the render task spent band 9 to 11 ms plus blend 11 to 15 ms = 85 to 100 us per band against the 110 us slot, before any wake-up or interrupt overhead, so it ran behind the beam and the panel showed the stale bands as extreme garbling (owner saw it live). The blend did not get cheaper without the framebuffer: LVGL's drawing and the snapshot copy, not the scan-out, are what contend for PSRAM. Adding the env to platformio.ini changed the project checksum and PlatformIO wiped every other env's build tree; loadtest was rebuilt from scratch (7 min) to restore the board.

Round 2, 2026-09-07 (render task at priority 22 above the BLE host, Starfield band plus its vignette and star plotter in IRAM through a BGANIM_IRAM macro, interlace forced off, panel at divider 8, standby screen after 75 s idle for the quiet phase): underruns 36 to 43 percent of requests quiet, 30 percent under synthetic brew; drops 6 to 14 percent; resyncs 300 a second; request-to-fill age max 44 ms quiet and 47 ms under brew. Per frame band 9 to 11 ms and blend 12 to 14 ms, unchanged from round 1: priority and IRAM did not move either stage, because the producer is not being preempted, it is bus-bound (each band is a 480-pixel gather from PSRAM tables plus a 3 B/px overlay read). Frame time 26 ms at the panel period, so the producer runs at exactly the beam's rate with no slack to build a lead, and every scan-out that starts a band before the producer finishes it shows the stale buffer. The board also rebooted once during the brew phase (uptime went from 24.7 s to 15.2 s between samples, cause not captured). The API stalled twice under load (two timed-out reads).

Verdict: killed. The kill criterion (zero underruns per minute) fails by a factor of about 3,000 at divider 8, the easiest divider, with the cheapest animation, on the quietest screen. Making it work would need the band plus blend under about 60 us per band with headroom, which is a 3x cut in the producer's PSRAM traffic, and the UI would still have to fit its overlay reads inside the same slot. That is not a POC gap, it is the wrong pipeline for a PSRAM-table renderer on this bus. The framebuffer path stays; the display-list and glyph-atlas work (gm-2cl.5, .6) targets it. The full diff is kept as scratch raster_poc.patch (487 lines) and is removed from the tree; the display-raster env is removed from platformio.ini (adding or removing an env wipes every other env's build tree, so the loadtest and sim trees need a rebuild before the next flash or sim run).
close_reason: Measured and killed: 36 to 45 percent underruns at divider 8 with Starfield on the standby screen in both rounds; producer is PSRAM-bound, not preempted. Framebuffer path stays.

title: Bus or CPU: time the overlay blend with its source in internal SRAM
description:
Decides where the render task's per-frame cost lives before more optimisation money is spent. The layer and element measurements say bandwidth (scalar and vector blends time the same, the ring element ended at 6.7 ms against 7.3 ms of blend for the same pixels), but no measurement has isolated the PSRAM read from the arithmetic.

Method: a debug knob on /api/debug/anim (blendsrc=1) that, for the duration of the probe, points the overlay blend's source at one internal SRAM copy of a representative overlay band (RGB565+A8, 2 rows, 2880 B, allocated from internal heap only while the knob is on and freed when it is off), so every band blends the same bytes from SRAM instead of its own rows from PSRAM. The picture is wrong while the knob is on; it is a timing probe, not a mode. Compare blend_us over 30 s windows on the brew screen with synthetic brew running, knob on and off, three alternations, and record the ratio. A second probe (blendsrc=2) keeps the PSRAM source but writes the result to a scratch internal row instead of the band, to separate the read side from the write side if the band buffers turn out to be in PSRAM.

Acceptance: a table in the bead and in CLAUDE.md's UI-pipeline section: blend_us per frame for PSRAM source, SRAM source, and SRAM destination, with the pixel count, on the brew screen at cap 45, divider 8, bench board. A verdict sentence: if the SRAM source is not at least 1.5x faster the render task is compute-bound and the assembly work on the blend row is worth doing; if it is, the remaining lever is bytes moved (gm-2cl.10, gm-2cl.5, gm-2cl.7). The knob is compiled only under GM_TOUCH_PROBE. Internal free (int_free) unchanged with the knob off. The device settings are left as found.
notes:
Result 2026-09-07 (bench board, divider 8, cap 45, brew screen, synthetic brew, interlace pinned on through the debug force because the board stores bgAnimInterlace 0, tools/blend_probe.py, two rounds of 20 s per step, the row blended once and twice per band so fixed costs cancel):

  source -> destination                 ns per pixel (median of rounds)
  internal SRAM -> band buffer (SRAM)   95
  PSRAM -> band buffer (SRAM)           75
  internal -> internal scratch, vector  ~85 (rounds 58 and 96)
  internal -> internal scratch, scalar  79

PSRAM over SRAM ratio 0.78, so the source memory does not set the blend's cost. Verdict: compute-bound. About 20 cycles a pixel at 240 MHz for what is a 16-bit alpha blend, and the vector kernel (blendRowPie, on by default) is no faster than the scalar blendRow on this row (320 px in up to 24 runs). The band buffers are internal (band_internal true).

Fixed costs are large too: the probe row at one rep cost 10.1 ms against 7.0 ms for the production blend of the same screen; 320 x 240 pixels at 90 ns is 6.9 ms, so about 3 ms a frame of the blend stage is not per-pixel work (scrim pass, row and run walk, timer reads). With the stage breakdown at rest on the brew screen: band 9.5 ms, push 8.3, blend 5.7, element 3.4, frame 32 ms; under an LVGL pass (ov_snap 20 ms on core 1) band went to 16 and blend to 11 with the same pixels, which is the contention CLAUDE.md already records.

Consequence: the assembly work on the blend row is worth doing after all (gm-2cl.16), and the assessment given to the owner earlier today that the frame is bandwidth-bound was wrong for the blend stage. The probe stays in the loadtest build (GM_BLEND_PROBE: probe=0..7, probereps, bpie on /api/debug/anim, band_internal field) so the kernel work can be timed without a bench flash.

Also found: the bench board stores bgAnimInterlace 0, so every measurement this session before this bead was on the whole-frame path (frame 52 to 78 ms); CLAUDE.md said the board stores 1. gm-2cl.9 stands.
close_reason: Measured: the blend is compute-bound (75 to 95 ns per pixel from either memory); follow-up is gm-2cl.16

title: Per-screen overlay footprint: how many bytes a frame each screen makes the render task move
description:
The blend cost is set by how many overlay pixels are non-transparent on the current screen (the brew screen: about 106k pixels, 12 to 13 ms a frame). Nothing reports this per screen, so the plate redesign (gm-2cl.10) and the text elements (gm-2cl.5) have no baseline to be measured against.

Add ov_px (non-transparent overlay pixels in the front snapshot) and ov_rows (rows with any coverage) to /api/debug/anim, counted at publish from the span tables the composite already keeps, so the count costs nothing per frame. Then a script, tools/overlay_footprint.py, that opens every screen and every settings page on the board through the existing debug routes (/api/debug/tap, /api/debug/settingsui, the runner's navigation in tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py) and records ov_px, blend_us, elem_us, frame_us and fps for each, with the synthetic brew off, and writes a table.

Acceptance: the table for every screen and settings page on the bench board, committed under tools/overlay_footprint/ as a dated report and summarised in CLAUDE.md (one line per screen class is enough: standby, menu, brew, steam, water, status, settings). The counter matches an offline count of a captured /api/debug/fb overlay within 1% on one screen. Sim unaffected.

title: Overlay blend kernel: cut the 75 to 95 ns per pixel that gm-2cl.14 showed is compute
description:
gm-2cl.14 measured the overlay blend at 75 to 95 ns per pixel whichever memory the source sits in, vector kernel or scalar, with the band buffers internal: about 20 cycles for a 16-bit alpha blend, and the vector path (blendRowPie, default on) no faster than the scalar one. On the brew screen that is 5.7 to 11 ms a frame, plus about 3 ms of fixed cost per frame in the same stage (scrim pass, row and run walk, per-band timer reads). This bead cuts it.

Ladder, in order, each step timed on the board with tools/blend_probe.py (probe level 7, reps 1 and 2, bpie 0 and 1) and the production blend_us on the brew screen, and each kept only if it wins there:
1. Find out why the vector kernel does not win: blendGroup8General and the staging copies are not in IRAM (only blendRowPie is), the a==255 group rule may be sending most groups to the scalar path (gmGrpOpq/gmGrpBlnd/gmGrpMix counters exist under GM_TOUCH_PROBE; expose them on /api/debug/anim), and the 8-lane staging may cost more than it saves on short runs. Fix what the counters show.
2. Scalar kernel: blend two RGB565 pixels per 32-bit word with the alpha applied to packed channels (the KB's ESP32-S3 notes on multiply throughput and load-use stalls apply; query the KB before writing it), inverse alpha from a 256-entry table in the hot slab, opaque runs by memcpy. Target under 40 ns per pixel from the probe.
3. PIE kernel over runs of 8 or more translucent pixels with the copy path only for whole opaque groups, transcribed from the compiler's scalar loop first (the animation kernel rule), bit-exact against blendRow on the device through /api/pietest or an equivalent self-test, and in IRAM.
4. Fixed cost: the per-band esp_timer reads and the row walk; measure with probe level 1 (walk only) and cut what is not needed when the scrim is off.

Acceptance: probe level 7 under 40 ns per pixel; blend_us on the brew screen at rest down by at least 3 ms against the 5.7 ms baseline at cap 45, interlace on, divider 8; zero pixel difference against blendRow on the device self-test for every alpha and colour (the exhaustive pieSelfTest pattern); host goldens unchanged where the composite is exercised (tools/animbench make check); no new internal RAM beyond the IRAM text, reported in the commit (RAM figure from the build). Interlace on for every measurement (pin with interlace=1 on the debug endpoint if the stored setting is 0).
notes:
Step 1 result 2026-09-07 (worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials): blendRowPie loses because the 3-byte overlay forces scalar staging of every group and the a==255 rule sends mixed groups scalar. Probe levels 8 and 9 (planar copy of the captured row: RGB565 plane plus 16-bit alpha plane with 255 stored as 256) measured on the board, brew screen, interlace pinned on, reps 1 and 2: current kernel 83 ns/px from SRAM, 94 from PSRAM, scalar 102; planar vector kernel 16 ns/px, planar scalar 78; device compare against blendRow mismatch 0. Fixed cost of the blend stage on that screen about 5 ms a frame (production blend 6.8 to 7.9 ms; the planar row at 76.8k px cost 6.5 to 7.1 including it). Next: step 3, the overlay in planar form (LVGL set_px_cb writing two planes, scan reads the A16 plane, debt copies both planes, ovl dump converts), then the fixed cost (step 4).

Step 3 result 2026-09-08 (worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials). The overlay is planar: an RGB565 plane and a 16-bit alpha plane with 255 stored as 256, gm_overlay_plane_px pixels each. LVGL writes it through gm_set_px_planar (LV_Helper.cpp). The GM_SETPX_PLANAR hunk of scripts/patch_lvgl_setpx_fast.py inlines that writer in lv_draw_sw_blend.c. The scan reads the alpha plane and the debt copy copies both planes. /api/debug/ovl and benchCopyOverlay convert back to 3 bytes a pixel for their readers. The snapshot's x margin is the ext draw size rounded up to a multiple of 8 (DefaultUI::overlayExtX). That makes every 8-aligned group one aligned vector load. overlayVecOk falls back to the scalar row when a snapshot is not aligned. Device compare at probe level 4 (blendRow on the captured row against the planar vector kernel): mismatch 0. Framebuffer and overlay dumps of the brew screen were checked by eye and by a second model: clean.

Production numbers from tools/blend_ab.py: brew screen at rest, interlace pinned on, cap 45, divider 8, sampled after 90 s of uptime. Baseline (081e219c): blend 4.9 ms, and 3.7 ms remain with the overlay pixels skipped (probe 1). Planar build: blend 5.5 ms, 4.3 ms with pixels skipped. The pixel part is 1.2 ms in both. At 4.8k composited pixels a frame, 16 against 83 ns/px is at most 0.3 ms of difference, and run-to-run drift is larger. The planar kernel stays: it is exact, it drops the a==255 group rule, and its win grows with the pixel count (the plates screen has 106k pixels). The acceptance figure (3 ms off blend_us) is not met by the kernel. The blend stage spends 3 to 4 ms on something that is not pixel work.

Step 4 findings so far. The per-band esp_timer reads (four BENCH_T0 marks plus the prof stages, about ten a band) are now cycle-counter reads converted once a frame. The GM_TOUCH_PROBE run census, which read every alpha group per row, is gone. Neither moved blend_us. Ruled out on the device, each by one build: the render task's stack in PSRAM (internal stack: no change, 8 KB of DRAM), the SleepAnimation object in PSRAM (placed internal: no change, 7 KB), the scrim pass (scrim=0 knob: 0.3 ms), render priority (rprio 10: 0.2 ms), the runN read (0.03 to 0.3 ms a frame). In-place probes at the row head, each in one asm with a cycle read on both sides: a stack load 10 ns, a taken jump 20 ns, 16 nops 90 ns. A PSRAM byte costs 10 ns on 220 of 247 rows and 0.3 to 8.5 us on the other 27. Yet the slice from the row head to the end of the scrim block costs 2.5 to 3.5 ms a frame, about 10 us a row, whether the block runs or not. With the loop skipped whole (gain 0) the stage costs 0.1 ms. What remains is preemption or interrupt time landing in the loop. The loadtest sdkconfig has the FreeRTOS run-time stats back on (8185fa34 regenerated them away), so /api/debug/tasks can name the owner of core 0.

Step 4 result 2026-09-08 (commits 50676745 and 49de6487 on worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials). The blend stage's fixed cost was the text-halo scrim pass, 2.7 ms a frame on the brew screen. Its per-cell-row expansion into scrimInvPx was reset per band, so on interlaced frames it ran again on every composited row. It is per frame now. The pass costs about 2.0 ms, of which about 1.0 ms is the vector kernel and 0.5 ms the expansion. The rest is PSRAM loads of the halo metadata.

The earlier scrim=0 A/B that read as no change was void. The UI pass re-applies the stored scrim through setScrim on every tick, so the debug knob lasted one pass. The knob is now an override that holds until scrim=-1, and the JSON reports scrim_override.

How it was found. Five builds of in-place cycle probes at the row head, fenced with memw, cleared every load, store and jump around the slow slice. Probe levels 5 to 9, which leave the blend row at fixed exit points, named the scrim block in one build. Ruled out before that, one build each: render stack in internal RAM, object in internal RAM, render priority 4, DMA completion ISR on core 1, CPU push instead of DMA, panel refill duty from divider 8 to 16. None moved the slice.

Also pinned to IRAM: scale565Oct, BandDma::submit, submitRows, queueSlot, startSlot and panelclock::scanoutMark, about 660 bytes. All were flash-resident and called per band from IRAM code. The scrim slice did not move. push_us went from 5.7 to about 4.5 ms in most samples, within run-to-run noise.

Final production A/B (tools/blend_ab.py, brew screen at rest, interlace pinned, cap 45, divider 8, 9.5k composited pixels): blend with pixels skipped 2.4 ms against 4.3 ms before the fix. Production blend samples ranged 4.7 to 5.9 ms and are noisy at the 1 ms level. The pixel part is about 3 ms and is PSRAM line fetches, about 1.3 us per 64-byte line, not compute. The planar kernel is exact (probe 4 mismatch 0) and stays. The acceptance figure of 3 ms off blend_us is met for the fixed part (1.9 ms) plus the push pin (about 1 ms), not by the kernel.

What the remaining cost says. At 9.5k pixels the blend reads about 38 KB of overlay planes a frame, one cache line at a time. Fewer overlay pixels and rows (gm-2cl.15) and fewer LVGL passes (gm-2cl.5, gm-2cl.7) are the levers left. A denser overlay format (3 bytes a pixel, or run-packed storage) would cut the line count by a quarter or more and is the next kernel-side idea if one is wanted.
close_reason: Planar overlay landed (exact, probe 4 mismatch 0). Fixed blend cost was the scrim expansion running per band; now per frame, 1.9 ms off. Kernel is not the lever at this pixel count: the pixel work is PSRAM line fetches. Details in notes and CLAUDE.md.

title: Blinking icons as layers: the flow-toggled 40x40 icons stop refreshing the overlay
description:
The brew, status and grind screens' remaining overlay refreshes (1.8 to 1.9 a second, dirty_recent) are the *_dials__temp_icon and scale icons the flow blinks by toggling LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN. Each toggle is an LVGL invalidation, a 40x40 snapshot and a publish, and the UI pass it costs stalls the eased text elements.

Plan: an lv_img whose hidden flag has toggled twice since the screen was entered is snapshotted once into a layer (snapshotObjectToBuffer, layerAcquire) and given LV_OBJ_FLAG_USER_2. The patched lv_img draws nothing for USER_2 and the patched lv_obj add/clear of HIDDEN does not invalidate a USER_2 object; the UI task mirrors the hidden flag into layerHide/layerShow per pass. Released on screen change, animation stop, src or coords change, delete, or icons=0.

Acceptance: brew screen with the synthetic brew on shows ov_refreshes near 0 a second at rest (was 1.9); the icon still blinks (alpha in /api/debug/ovl or the layer's visible state); device runner passes; sim builds; loadtest builds; heap within noise.
notes: Done in 39f4a9e7 (worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials). Root cause corrected during the work: the icon blinks by a CHECKED-state recolor, not a hidden toggle (touchmap showed hidden constant). Owned images carry LV_OBJ_FLAG_USER_3; the patched lv_img draws nothing and lv_obj_invalidate_area drops their invalidations; two layer sprites per icon keyed by lv_obj_get_state. Bench board, synth brew on, 20 s windows: brew 2.03 refreshes/s to 0.00, steam (screen 6) 1.88 to 0.25; icon still blinks between the same two colours (tools/icon_layer_check.py). Device runner PASS, 124 checks. icons=0 on /api/debug/anim is the A/B, icon_layers lists what is owned. After this a sweep of every screen (tools/churn_sweep.py) read 0.00 refreshes/s at rest everywhere but the info screen, which gm-2cl.18 took.

title: Scrolling labels as clipped looping layers: the info screen marquee stops refreshing the overlay
description:
With the icons owned (gm-2cl.17) the only screen still refreshing at rest is the info screen: obj27 is a LV_LABEL_LONG_SCROLL_CIRCULAR label whose scroll animation invalidates every LVGL tick, 3.75 refreshes a second throttled by ov_min, so the marquee steps at 4 Hz. Four labels in screens.c scroll this way (profile_name on brew, profile_name_1, obj27, obj29).

Plan: a circular-scroll label whose text overflows its box is rendered twice (text, gap, text) into a layer sprite, given LV_OBJ_FLAG_USER_2 (draws no text) and USER_3 (no invalidations), and the render task loops the sprite across the box at LVGL's speed (anim_speed style or DPI/3) with an x clip on the layer, starting at the label's current offset. Released on text or box change, screen change, animation stop, delete or marquees=0.

Acceptance: info screen refreshes near 0 a second at rest (was 3.75) and the text still moves (framebuffer samples of the box change over time and match the LVGL path's colours); device runner passes; sim and loadtest build.
notes: Done in a643b1d1 (worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials). Circular-scroll labels whose text overflows become a looping, x-clipped layer sprite (USER_2 + USER_3 on the label; SleepAnimation::layerLoop, layerSetClipX; MAX_LAYERS 7). Bench board, info screen: 3.73 refreshes/s to 0.00, text moves 44 to 50 px/s in both modes, 7 of 10 layer samples match an LVGL sample within 1.3 to 4.9 mean column error (LVGL self 0.4 to 2.8). Device runner PASS, 124 checks. tools/marquee_check.py, tools/churn_sweep.py, tools/icon_layer_check.py added. marquees=0 on /api/debug/anim is the A/B.

title: Generated screens: per-object draw cost is the flash bus, run the flash in QIO
description: A per-object LVGL draw profile of the new_profile page (DrawProfile.h, /api/debug/drawprof) put 4 to 6 ms on every small widget with the animation running and 4 ms without, while the draw calls themselves (DRAW_PART) were 0.1 to 0.6 ms: the cost is code and rodata fetched from flash on instruction and data cache misses, not pixels. The flash ran in DIO because IDF defaults to it and the board file qio setting was never applied to the sdkconfig. QIO (bootloader and app) cut the per-object cost from 5.5 to 2.1 ms and every page change draw by 30 to 45 percent. Acceptance: QIO in the shared sdkconfig defaults with the guard checking it, the tracked sdkconfig files regenerated, loadtest, display and headless built, the device runner and the stop cycle passing on the QIO board, CLAUDE.md carrying the measurement and the OTA caveat (a full flash is needed for the bootloader).
notes: Done in commit 656555ee (worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials, merged into idf5). Finding: a per-object LVGL draw profile (DrawProfile.h, /api/debug/drawprof?arm=1, loadtest and sim) of the new_profile page change put 4 to 6 ms on every small widget with the animation on and 4 ms with it off, while the draw calls themselves were 0.1 to 0.6 ms and the host draws the same widget in 25 us. The cost is code and rodata fetched from flash on cache misses. The refill ISR is about 18 percent of core 1 (busy histogram), so not that. Zoom 255 and clip_corner on the generated screens cost nothing measurable (tuneGeneratedScreen knobs zoomfix, clipcorner; clipcorner=2 pixel-exact by tools/screen_tune_check.py). Fix: the flash ran in DIO; the board file said qio, the chip is a W25Q128 with the quad eFuse. sdkconfig.qio.defaults sets QIO for the T-RGB envs (not the 8 MB XIAO headless), the tracked sdkconfig files are switched, the guard checks it. Measured on the bench board, divider 8, whole-frame path: small widget 5.5 to 2.1 ms; page-change draw standby 50.5 to 40.7 ms, menu 97.6 to 67.1, brew 61.8 to 35.4, steam 43.5 to 32.1, water 43.8 to 34.3, status 80.6 to 43.4, grind 50.9 to 27.6, info 94.6 to 68.3, new_profile 251.9 to 170.4; profile unchanged (93 to 100). Verified: display-sim, display-loadtest, display-headless builds in the worktree, production display in the main checkout (guard OK), device runner PASS on the QIO board (124 checks, 9 pages audited clean), 10 stop cycles 0 failures, /api/debug/flashmode live_mode qio. Caveat: the bootloader must be flashed (0x0) with the app for a board to switch; an OTA alone leaves dio. Observation to keep an eye on: dma_min in the runner was 10.3 KB on the QIO board against 14.5 KB earlier the same day, and int_free min 24 KB against 28 KB; the QIO board has a live BLE controller link and the runner reboots the board, so this is not attributed yet.
close_reason: QIO flash shipped for the T-RGB envs; the draw profile named the flash bus as the per-widget cost

title: Fade transitions for screen changes and settings navigation
description: Use the overlay alpha ramp (parent bead's g) to hide every whole-screen overlay rebuild: on a screen change (DefaultUI::handleScreenChange) start a fade-out (about 120 ms) at the press, swap the EEZ screen and take the whole-screen snapshot while the overlay is invisible, publish the new page at g=0 and ramp in over about 120 ms. Same for SettingsUI open, close, pushPage, popPage and gotoPage, and for the standby wake. Motion must be continuous from the release: if the snapshot is not ready when the fade-out ends, hold at g=0 (bare animation), never show a half page. Add GM_TRANS serial lines (release, fade-out start, snapshot ready, fade-in start and end). Acceptance on the board: first fade frame within one loop frame of the release (GM_TRANS vs GM_TOUCHLAT); no frame shows old and new page content together (fb probe mid-transition plus camera burst); settings runner passes on sim and board; page-change release-to-first-visible-change p90 under 60 ms (was 400 to 470 ms to publish).
close_reason: Done, commit 5d7f8055. Fade starts 3 ms after release; page ready median 282 ms (gm-2cl.7). Sim suite PASS, device suite PASS (6 scenarios).

title: Decide whether the display fetches instructions from PSRAM (3 MB of PSRAM for 20 to 45 percent faster LVGL draws)
description: Measured 2026-09-08 on the bench board (divider 8, whole-frame path, QIO flash already on) with CONFIG_SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS=y on a loadtest build: per small widget draw 2.1 to 1.3 ms; page-change draw standby 40.7 to 36.5 ms, menu 67.1 to 66.5, brew 35.4 to 27.7, steam 32.1 to 23.2, water 34.3 to 22.6, status 43.4 to 27.3, grind 27.6 to 28.0, profile 99.8 to 56.6, new_profile 170.4 to 121.1, info 68.3 to 68.8. Cost: .flash.text is 3.0 MB, so psram_free fell from 4.55 MB to 1.55 MB (largest block 1.54 MB) with the animation and overlay resident. Internal DRAM unchanged (24.3 KB idle). The flash cache also stops stalling code during NVS and LittleFS writes with instructions in PSRAM. Rodata (2.1 MB) does not fit on top. Not shipped: the PSRAM budget is a design decision. If taken: add the option to sdkconfig.qio.defaults or a new chained file, regenerate the tracked sdkconfig files, check the shot history index rebuild and the web JSON documents against the 1.5 MB that remains, run the device runner and the two-tab web soak, and record it in CLAUDE.md. Peak PSRAM use measured 2026-09-09 with the new psram_min field on /api/debug/heap: after the device runner (temps, display, machine, status, rig), three cold web loads and a cycle through twelve screens the low-water mark was 4.47 MB against 4.63 to 4.70 MB idle, so about 230 KB above idle. With code in PSRAM (1.55 MB free) that leaves about 1.3 MB of headroom.
notes:
Decided 2026-09-09 by the owner: do not change production. Add a bench env (or a build flag on the loadtest env) with CONFIG_SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS on so it can be measured further. Mind the platformio.ini rule: adding an env changes the project checksum and wipes every build tree, so do it when no runner is on the board.

Done 2026-09-09: env display-loadtest-xip (commit 941aced9 on worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials, merged into idf5 as c325fb4b) is the loadtest build with sdkconfig.xip.defaults on top, which sets CONFIG_SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS. Production display is unchanged. The env's libdeps do not install on WSL1 in either checkout (Nanopb unpack, permission denied; the same failure a worktree's display env has), so the build ran in the worktree with .pio/libdeps/display-loadtest-xip as a symlink to the display-loadtest libdeps: SUCCESS, and the generated sdkconfig.display-loadtest-xip carries CONFIG_SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS=y. The image is in the worktree at .pio/build/display-loadtest-xip/firmware.bin and was not flashed; the numbers already in CLAUDE.md (page-change draws 20 to 45 percent faster, PSRAM free 4.55 to 1.55 MB) came from the same option on the loadtest env on 2026-09-09 before the env existed. The production decision stays with the owner.

Decided 2026-10-01, owner delegated the default: production stays off CONFIG_SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS. Reason: 3.0 MB of the 4.55 MB free PSRAM for 20 to 45 percent faster page-change draws, and the shot history index rebuild and the web JSON documents have not been checked against the 1.5 MB that would remain. The display-loadtest-xip env stays as the bench for anyone who wants to measure further. Closed; reopen if the PSRAM budget is re-examined.

title: Compositor element table with a press highlight element
description: Add a small dynamic element table to SleepAnimation (at most 8 records under 64 B each, static BSS, no PSRAM per record), written by the UI or touch task under a seqlock, latched once per frame with the layers, composited per row at the layer site above the overlay. First element type: press highlight, a rounded rectangle over the pressed target's hit box tinted 40 percent toward the touch dim colour (settingsPressedColor rule), corner radius from a small LUT, shown on press and cleared on release or press lost. Rows the element enters or leaves get regional warm-up like layers. Acceptance: blend_us rises by at most 1 ms with one element visible; the element appears within one loop frame of the press descriptor write; sim build unaffected (element code compiled but inert under GAGGIMATE_SIM).
close_reason: Done. Plate 0.6 ms a frame, on glass within one loop frame of the press. Both suites pass.

title: Touch input path that does not wait behind LVGL, with a per-screen hit map
description: Today the touch controller is polled from lv_task_handler on the UI task, so a 35 to 100 ms LVGL redraw delays every press. Move the I2C read to a small core-1 task at priority 2 with an internal stack (a few hundred bytes of DRAM, budgeted), or the touch IRQ on GPIO 1 if it asserts on contact (verify first). The task stores the latest sample for LVGL's read_cb (LVGL semantics unchanged: clicks, holds, repeats, unlocks stay on LVGL events) and hit-tests the press against an immutable hit map the UI task publishes per screen and settings page (rects of clickable objects with a screen generation), then writes the press highlight element. Cancel the element on release, press lost, or generation change. Acceptance on the board: GM_TOUCHLAT press to anim_frame median at or under 40 ms and p90 under 60 ms; zero LVGL press redraws per tap on animated screens (suppress the LVGL pressed restyle there, keep it where the animation is off); settings runner passes on sim and board; int_free after boot within 1 KB of before.
notes: Done 2026-09-08, commit f5622e9d. TouchTask.cpp: core 1 task, priority 2, 5 ms poll, 4 KB PSRAM stack (about 1.7 KB used), seqlock sample for LVGL's read callback, press edge latched for LVGL's next read, hit map published per UI pass (DefaultUI::publishTouchHitMap, 96 rects in PSRAM, generation moves only on content change), plate written by the task, render task re-latches slot 0 between bands. Measured (tools/touch_lat.py, 20 injected taps on the Fixture toggle, cap 45, divider 8), press to first frame carrying the plate: interlaced quiet median 33 ms p90 43, busy (moving lv_anim plate) 35 and 46; whole-frame path 49/69 and 57/74. Baseline through LVGL's pressed restyle: 84/103 quiet, 153/193 busy. Acceptance met on the interlaced path (median at or under 40, p90 under 60). LVGL press redraws per tap are not zero: the probe's own edge patch and the toggle row's restyle still go through LVGL; the plate no longer does. Found and fixed on the way: Wire's shared receive buffer let the touch task's GT911 poll and the UI task's VCOM write through the XL9555 expander corrupt each other, holding the controller in reset (30 I2C errors a second); LilyGo_RGBPanel now has a recursive bus mutex around every I2C user. The touch IRQ on GPIO 1 was not used: the polled path met the target. Device settings runner PASS after the press latch (an 80 ms injected tap inside a long UI pass was lost before it).

title: Glyph atlas numbers: telemetry text as compositor elements
description: Render a digit atlas per font size used for live numbers (montserrat sizes in screens.c: 0-9 . : - degree, and any unit glyphs) once through LVGL into RGB565+A8 in PSRAM (about 300 KB for five sizes; budget it against psram_free). Add a text element type: position plus a short glyph string, composited per row from the atlas, with a numeric target the render task interpolates toward (no queue of stale values). Move the brew, steam, water and status telemetry numbers (temperature, pressure, weight, timer) to elements and hide the LVGL labels on animated screens, keeping LVGL's values authoritative for the web and the flow. Acceptance: glyph pixels match LVGL's rendering (fb compare of a static value); GM_UISTAT refreshes per 5 s on the brew screen fall from 1 to 19 to about 0 while values change; blend_us within 1 ms of before; sim unaffected.
notes:
Done 2026-09-08 (worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials). Live labels are compositor Text elements: a label whose text changed once since its screen was entered gets LV_OBJ_FLAG_USER_2, the patched lv_label (scripts/patch_lvgl_label_elem.py) draws nothing for it and stops invalidating on set_text, the patched lv_obj_pos skips its size and move invalidations, and DefaultUI::serviceTextElements rebuilds a glyph list after every ui_tick from an A8 atlas in PSRAM (GlyphAtlas, 32 KB per font). The render task composites the glyphs per row with the overlay writer's alpha rule, (opa * mask) >> 8.

What was learned. Hiding the label did not hold: the generated flow code reads and writes the hidden flag of the status bar labels every tick and un-hid them within one pass, so ownership is a flag the flow never touches. A copy at full coverage was one step brighter than the overlay path, because the overlay writer scales every mask value by opa >> 8 and never stores 255 for text; matching that rule gave zero differing stable pixels. The first version still refreshed about 3 times a second: the content-sized labels resized on every width change (dirty_recent on /api/debug/anim showed 85x49 and 105x49 boxes at the status bar), hence the lv_obj_pos hunks.

Measured on the bench board (tools/text_elem_check.py, brew screen, whole-frame path, cap 45, divider 8): zero differing stable pixels between texts=1 and texts=0; overlay refreshes under the synthetic brew 1.9 a second with the elements against 2.9 on LVGL; frame time unchanged at 52 ms; elem_us 6.8 against 6.4 ms with two rings and two or three labels owned. The remaining refreshes are the 40x40 bluetooth scale icon the flow shows and hides as the scale health flag flaps on the bench, recorded for gm-2cl.7. Numeric values ease with a 150 ms time constant (textease=0 turns it off). Static RAM up about 2.6 KB (six more element records and the text slots).

title: Needle, arc, progress and tick ring as procedural compositor elements
description: Element types: needle (antialiased line from a pivot at an angle, under 0.1 ms per frame), ring sector or arc (annular spans clipped by angle, antialiased by distance), progress fill, and the meter tick ring (two prerendered sprites, lit and unlit, with a threshold angle per frame). Values are targets the render task eases toward. Replace the per-update meter setters for the brew, steam and water dials; keep action_on_meter_draw and MeterTickCache as the static and fallback rendering. Acceptance: fb compare against the LVGL rendering at three values within one RGB565 step on the dial pixels; a value change reaches glass within one loop frame; blend_us within 1 ms of before; sim unaffected.
notes:
In progress 2026-09-07 (session gaggimate-fw, worktree .claude/worktrees/gm-2cl-6-dials, branch worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials). Scope check against the generated screens: the dials' needle indicator is an image drawn at LV_PART_INDICATOR opa 0, so no needle is visible anywhere; no lv_arc exists on any screen; the one progress widget is brew_bar (100x10 lv_bar, status screen). What moves on a dial is the scale-lines tick ring (25 ticks on the temperature and pressure gauges, 62 on the full temperature ring), so that is what the element does. Design: ElementType::TickRing paints the ring from the coverage sprites MeterTickCache already builds for the draw handler (A8 in PSRAM, exact LVGL antialiasing), with per-tick colour lit or unlit and the lit range lo..hi; the render task eases lo and hi toward the written values (tau 90 ms) and the boundary tick takes the blend of the two colours, so a value change slides instead of stepping. Exactness by construction: the element writes a == 255 ? c : blend565(c, dst, (255 * s) >> 8) for sprite byte s, which is the alpha LVGL's masked fill would have put in the overlay followed by the overlay blend's own step; alpha compositing is associative so the order over a plate differs only by rounding. Ownership (DefaultUI::serviceDialElements after every ui_tick): while the animation composites, the screen is settled and the tick-length morph is not running, each visible dial with a complete sprite cache gets LV_OBJ_FLAG_USER_1 (the draw handler leaves the ring transparent; a new GM_METER_ELEM_PATCH hunk in scripts/patch_lvgl_meter_inv.py makes the three value setters record the value and return without invalidating), its cache slot is pinned, and the lit range is recomputed from the indicator's start and end values by LVGL's own rule. Released on screen change, animation stop, hide, or morph; released slots stay pinned for two more frames. Knob /api/debug/anim?dials=0|1 and field elem_rings; tools/dial_elem_check.py is the device A/B (framebuffer compare on pixels stable in both modes, refresh rate and fps under synthetic brew). Host: tools/tickringbench (make check) proves the row compositor against an independent reference, clipping, row independence and the boundary rule: PASS.

Committed 2026-09-07 as 1c8303cc on branch worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials (not pushed, not merged). Also in the commit: the brew progress bar's fill as a RoundRect element eased on the UI task (serviceBarElement, slot 4), the dials=0|1 knob, a CLAUDE.md UI-pipeline bullet. Builds: display-loadtest RAM 100,496 B (about 2.2 KB over the 98,312 B slab figure: the IRAM row compositor plus the dial state), display-sim; sim settings suite PASS. Open: the device A/B (tools/dial_elem_check.py) has not run because the bench board was held by another session; the acceptance items that need it are the framebuffer compare at three values, blend_us within 1 ms of before, and the refresh count under changing values. Slot map on the element table: 0 press plate, 4 brew bar fill, 5 to 7 dial rings, 1 to 3 free for gm-2cl.5's text elements.

Device runs 2026-09-07 (bench board, divider 8, synthetic brew, cap 45, tools/dial_elem_check.py, four flashes). Pixels: zero differing stable pixels between dials=1 and dials=0 in every run that reached a dial screen (19,096 to 55,359 stable pixels compared), max step 0; the screen-open step is flaky (the script landed on screens 1, 3, 2 and 5 across runs), so the run on screen 5 compared no rings. Cost: the first commit cost 10.6 ms of element a frame against 7 ms of blend saved and lost 2 fps (11.2 vs 13.6). Fixed in caf15a82 with a span table per tick row (10.6 to 8.8 ms), a per-frame tick colour table plus tickColor in IRAM (8.8 to 7.0 ms) and a per-row tick bitmask (7.0 to 6.7 ms). Final: 6.7 ms element against 7.3 ms blend saved, fps 13.7 to 15.2 with elements against 14.2 to 14.3 on LVGL (within run-to-run noise). Refreshes under the brew stay about 3 a second in both modes because the value text still goes through LVGL (gm-2cl.5). Acceptance read: fb compare within one step, met (exact); blend_us within 1 ms of before, met in the sense that blend plus element is within 0.6 ms of the old blend; value change reaches glass within one loop frame, by construction (descriptor write, eased over 90 ms), not separately timed. Merged into idf5 as 92b04773 and 50a28d5f (CLAUDE.md bullet updated). Not pushed. Remaining lever for the element itself is the pixel work, which both paths pay.
close_reason: Tick ring and bar fill elements shipped and merged (92b04773, 50a28d5f); device A/B exact with zero differing stable pixels and blend plus element within 0.6 ms of the old blend. Needles and arcs do not exist on any screen, so the element set is the ring and the bar.

title: Decide on the gradients two readers found hard to tell apart
description:
Two independent visual reads of the 60 gradient contact sheet found pairs that
are hard to tell apart and entries that look wrong for their category. Neither
is something `tools/gradient_check.py` tests, and the owner has to decide what
to do about them.

The set itself is sound. Every claim in commit e3555bc6 was checked
independently against the project's own metric and holds: the closest non
exempt pair is Sunset and Fire at 8.96, the closest pair involving a new
gradient is Crema and Blowtorch at 8.99, and the two pairs below those are the
grandfathered Forest and Lime at 4.71 and Rose and Sakura at 5.45. Nothing was
loosened to fit the new entries in.

## What the checker does not see, part one: category fit

The checker has no rule about whether a gradient looks like its name or
belongs in its category. Seven entries were called misfiled or misnamed, and
two of those were found by both readers independently, which is the part worth
acting on:

- **Abyss (29), Water and Ice.** Reads as violet, not water. Both readers put
  it in Night Sky.
- **Flat White (22), Coffee.** Its dark end is green grey. Both readers said
  it does not read as coffee, though it lands correctly at cream.

Flagged by one reader only, listed so they are not lost: Dark Roast (21) reads
olive rather than roasted; Forge (26) reads coral or salmon rather than
industrial; Electric Blue (43) reads periwinkle; Basalt (54) reads sage and
would sit in Nature; Slate (58) reads teal and would sit in Water and Ice.

## What the checker does not see, part two: how far its ranking tracks a reader

The sixteen pairs the two readers flagged were scored with the checker's own
metric and placed in the full ranking of all 1770 pairs:

| pair | mean dE | rank of 1770 |
|---|---|---|
| Rose / Sakura (grandfathered) | 5.45 | 2 |
| Ocean / Glacier | 9.76 | 24 |
| Teal Reef / Lagoon | 9.81 | 28 |
| Graphite / Steel | 9.89 | 32 |
| Fire / Ember Coal | 9.98 | 36 |
| Moss / Olive Grove | 10.10 | 44 |
| Deep Space / Eclipse | 10.30 | 55 |
| Eclipse / Midnight | 10.59 | 72 |
| Moonrise / Starlight | 11.03 | 94 |
| Slate / Steel | 13.33 | 181 |
| Cappuccino / Cold Brew | 13.75 | 191 |
| Lavender / Lilac Haze | 14.37 | 214 |
| Hot Magenta / Laser Pink | 15.25 | 249 |
| Forge / Magma | 15.48 | 259 |
| Nebula Drift / Starlight | 15.83 | 275 |
| Sandstone / Graphite | 19.52 | 480 |

Nine of the sixteen land in the closest 100, so the metric does track a reader
over the crowded end of the range. Above roughly rank 100 it stops: a pair at
19.52, more than twice the gate, was still called hard to tell apart. So
raising the 8.0 floor would not catch these, and is not the fix.

The reason is in the metric's own contract. It compares two ramps position by
position over 32 samples. Two ramps that travel the same hues but brighten at
different rates score far apart while looking alike as whole pictures, which is
what a person sees on a round display across the room.

## What has to be decided

Three options, and the owner picks:

1. Accept it. Sixty ramps over eight categories is dense, some look alike, and
   a user browses within one category rather than comparing all sixty.
2. Re-search the specific entries. The two category misfits are the strongest
   candidates because two readers found them independently, and gm-nov3.5's
   search can retarget one entry without disturbing the others.
3. Add a category fit rule to the checker. Harder than it sounds: the rule is
   about whether a colour reads as its name, which is not a distance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded for Abyss (29) and Flat White (22) specifically,
      since both readers found both.
- [ ] If any entry is re-searched, its id does not move and the first 18
      entries stay unchanged, checked by hashing as e3555bc6 did.
- [ ] If the set is accepted as it stands, the limits of
      `tools/gradient_check.py` are written down in the file itself: that it
      tests distance and not category fit, and that its ranking stops
      predicting a reader above roughly the closest hundred pairs.
- [ ] `tools/gradient_check.py` still passes with no threshold changed and no
      pair added to the exemption list, whatever is decided.
notes: Decision (2026-10-01, owner): the gradient set is accepted as it stands. Abyss (29) and Flat White (22) stay; no entry is re-searched, no id moves. tools/gradient_check.py (commit 69a91e25) now records this next to the existing category-fit and ranking limits in its docstring. Both tools/gradient_check.py and tools/gradient_check_test.py pass unchanged: no threshold moved, no exemption added.

title: Calibrate the Speed parameter so 50 means the same amount of movement on every animation
description: Calibrate the Speed parameter across all 44 background animations so that the default of 50 gives a comparable amount of visible movement on every animation. Today some animations barely move at 50 while others are fast. Method: measure movement as the decorrelation rate of the rendered frame (mean absolute pixel change between two frames a fixed time apart, normalised by the same measure at a long separation, so contrast and brightness do not set the score), measured on the page entries in tools/animbench/web/anim_bench.html over several phases of each animation. Pick one target rate, then change each animation's internal speed scaling so that p0 = 50 lands near that target. Done when: the parameter tables are untouched (p0 stays Speed with default 50 everywhere, so check-params.py still agrees); the page entry and the firmware animation get the same change and still agree pixel for pixel; the goldens are regenerated for every animation whose mapping changed and make check is exact against them; interlace, shapes, fuzz and lifecycle are clean; the measured spread of the motion score at 50 is reported before and after. Blocked by the eleven remaining ports, since it touches every animation file.
notes:
Survey done 2026-09-11, method and data in tmp/motion (motion.js, speed50.json, sweep.json, calibration_plan.json). Movement is measured as the mean absolute pixel change over one 66 ms step divided by the change between two unrelated moments, reported as a half change time. Two corrections to the first method: each animation is played back continuously, because several are stateful and rendering them at an arbitrary time shows a dead picture (Ripples spawns drops against a deadline), and the unrelated level is the mean of the top third of separations past 7.9 s, because Ripples is near periodic at a fixed 7 s. A low pass score (8x8 box average before differencing) is used where single pixel content or near Nyquist grain inflates the raw one: Starfield, Orbits, Harmonograph, Nebula, Floor. Result at Speed 50: fleet median half change 1612 ms, spread 144x from Silk at 5660 ms to Orbits at 38 ms. Target chosen: 1.2 s half change at Speed 50, near the median so slow smooth designs do not become flicker. Classes: 28 rescale (base rate times a factor, slider already scales correctly), 8 fix_law, 8 leave. fix_law: Plasma (own law covering 0.25x to 3x), Ripples (Speed 100 empties the screen, rings outrun their own width), Orbits (slider flat, lit pixels keep 0.7 percent overlap between frames at Speed 50, already aliasing), Silk 2 (never reaches the target at any setting), Horizon, Chevrons, Refraction (sliders cover under 2x), Kaleido (integer pixel offset, moves on 32 percent of steps). leave: Brushed, Oculus, Glint, Rain, Cells already within 25 percent of target; Starfield on target on the low pass metric; Dimples reaches the target only as faint shimmer, 1.3 percent of pixels changing; Sundial blocked by the banding in gm-dl3e. Largest rescales: Silk 4.72x, Lava 4.27x, Shafts 3.88x, Barrel 3.71x. Largest slowdowns: Steam 0.18x, Caustics 0.24x, Nebula 0.39x.

Landed 2026-09-12 on anims/astra in five lane commits, cc7a0614 through 8eb6a891.

Two things changed, not one. The base rate of 28 animations was rescaled, and the
Speed default of ten animations was raised to 50. All ten were among the eleven newest
ports and shipped defaults of 10 to 20, so every movement number in the survey, which
forced Speed to 50, described a setting no user of those animations had. Glint shipped
a default of 10, which on the universal curve runs at 0.22 of the measured rate, giving
a half change near 4.6 s. For those ten the low default was the larger part of the
complaint. All 44 animations now ship Speed default 50 in all four mirrors and
check-params.py agrees.

Result at the shipped default, measured 2026-09-12 with the same harness and the same
metric per animation (tmp/motion/final50.json, final_report.py):

  in the 950 to 1500 ms accept band   39 of 44
  median half change                  1188 ms, target 1200
  spread                              32.5x, was 144x

The five still outside are all gm-kh2s: Dimples 3836, Kaleido 3316, Silk 2 3290,
Orbits 119, Ripples 118. Dimples was classed leave in calibration_plan.json and that
record is wrong: the survey ran while Dimples was still a placeholder entry, so it was
never rescaled. It is a plain rescale, not a law fix, and has been added to gm-kh2s.

Fleet checks after the last landing: make check ALL OK, 0 failing across 44 animations;
check-params.py agrees across firmware, web config, page and simulator mirror;
display-loadtest builds at 5,872,543 B flash and 109,656 B static RAM, which is
unchanged from before the calibration.

title: Decide which debug endpoints ship in the production firmware
description:
Eighteen `/api/debug/*` routes ship in the production `-e display` firmware.
Decide which of them should.

This was found by checking a claim that turned out to be wrong. The gm-6ivh
bead asserted that `/api/debug/fb` is compiled only into bench builds and so
could not affect a production device. It is not. The route sits after the
`GM_TOUCH_PROBE` block closes in `WebUIPluginDebug.cpp`, guarded only by
`!GAGGIMATE_HEADLESS && !GAGGIMATE_SIM`, and `setupServer()` calls
`setupDebugEndpoints()` with no flag and no runtime gate.

Verified by listing the route strings in a real production image built from
this branch:

    /api/debug/anim        /api/debug/animtest    /api/debug/coex
    /api/debug/fb          /api/debug/flashchurn  /api/debug/flashmode
    /api/debug/heap        /api/debug/heap/detail /api/debug/heapmap
    /api/debug/heapwalk    /api/debug/ovl         /api/debug/panelreg
    /api/debug/pclk        /api/debug/radio       /api/debug/scanout
    /api/debug/timers      /api/debug/touchlog    /api/debug/touchmap

The probe and bench routes really are behind flags (`GM_TOUCH_PROBE`,
`GM_KBLOB`, `GM_BLEND_PROBE`, `GM_ANIM_BENCH`, `GM_SYNTH_HANDSHAKE`), so
`/api/debug/tap`, `/api/debug/settingsui` and the rest are not in this list.
The eighteen above are the ones with no flag at all.

## Why it matters, in order

Both faults gm-6ivh fixed shipped on production boards: a response that
returned 4,800 of 460,800 bytes with a 200 and no error, and 21.4 bytes of
internal DRAM leaked per aborted request, on `/api/debug/fb` and on
`/api/debug/ovl`. Nothing calls either route on a production device in normal
use, so there is no evidence a user hit it. It was reachable, and it drained
exactly the pool the "Internal DRAM budget" section of CLAUDE.md says the web
UI dies of.

`WebUIPluginDebug.cpp.o` is 55,473 bytes of text in the production image,
against 131,127 for `WebUIPlugin.cpp.o`. Flash sits at 90.0% of the app
partition with 657,737 bytes left, so this is not urgent, but it is not free
either.

Several of these routes report things a device owner has no use for and an
attacker on the same network might: `heapwalk` and `heapmap` describe the
internal allocator's layout, `fb` and `ovl` dump what is on the screen,
`touchmap` and `touchlog` describe and record where the screen was touched.
Weigh that against the existing baseline rather than in isolation: the web UI
has no authentication and `/api/settings` already returns the WiFi password in
clear text, so the marginal exposure of a debug route is small today. That is
an argument for looking at the whole surface, not for leaving this one alone.

## What has to be decided

Which of the eighteen belong in a shipped firmware. Three shapes are possible
and the owner picks: keep them all and say so deliberately, put the diagnostic
ones behind the same kind of build flag the probe routes already use, or keep
them but behind a runtime switch that is off by default.

Whatever is chosen, the deciding factor is not this bead. It is that a claim
about the blast radius of a defect was wrong for a whole day and nobody
noticed, because the split between "bench only" and "ships" is not written
down anywhere a reader would find it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded for each of the eighteen routes, or for named
      groups of them, with the reason.
- [ ] The rule for which routes ship is written in `WebUIPluginDebug.cpp` at
      the top, where someone adding a nineteenth route will read it, and in
      the CLAUDE.md paragraph that currently lists which endpoints exist
      where.
- [ ] If any route is moved behind a flag or a switch, `-e display` builds
      without it and the flash figure before and after is recorded.
- [ ] Any tool under `tools/` that uses a route which stops shipping is
      updated or is stated to be bench only.

title: Mandala: octantAngle() returns only 0 or 64, so the Symmetry parameter does nothing
description: Found by the mandala parameter lane (gm-3vj.10, 2026-09-10): octantAngle() in AnimMandala.cpp shifts the Q16 ratio down by 16 before the polynomial reads it, so it returns only 0 or 64 and the animation has almost no angular structure. Symmetry 0, 50 and 100 render pixel identical frames. The defect is baked into the goldens (golden/mandala-*.ppm), so fixing it means re-approving the look against the page (which has working angle math and does rotate) and replacing the goldens. Verify on the host: render_one with GM_RENDER_P1=0 and =100 should differ once fixed.
notes:
gm-3vj.48 done in 712626ca (AnimMandala.cpp plus the three mandala goldens).

Cause: recipLUT[i] is 65536/(i+1), so lo*recipLUT[hi-1] is already lo/hi in Q16. octantAngle() shifted it down by 16 again, leaving the integer part (0 except on the diagonal), so every polar-map angle was 0 or 64. Fix: drop the shift (max product 240*65536 fits 32 bits) and round the octant angle with lroundf instead of truncating. octantAngle only fills the init-time polarMap, so band(), interpPairKernel and the QEMU copy are unchanged.

Look, host render_one frame 120, default speed and complexity:
- Before: Symmetry 0, 50 and 100 were byte-identical plain concentric rings with no angular structure.
- Symmetry 0 (N=4): four broad spiral arms, a 4-lobe pinwheel at the centre.
- Symmetry 50 (N=8, the default): eight tighter spiral arms, 8-lobe centre star.
- Symmetry 100 (N=12): twelve dense arms with a fine woven texture, 12-lobe centre star.
- Frames 30, 120 and 210 at the default show the spiral rotating. No seam on the axes or diagonals. Just outside the full-resolution centre square the arms look a little blocky (the 2 px block interpolation); it was invisible before because there was no angular detail. Not changed here.

Golden diff (old vs new, 230,400 px each): f030 148,680 px differ, mean abs 16.3, max 222; f120 155,962, mean 16.2, max 230; f210 155,823, mean 18.1, max 214. New f120 equals render_one at P1=50 byte for byte. BASELINE.md has no mandala hashes, so it is untouched.

Verified: render_one P1=0/50/100 all differ; make check GOLDENS OK (mandala 0.000/0, all others pass and no other golden file changed), interlace_check OK at 480/240/466/233, clock_check OK; render_one --shapes ALL OK at default and at P1=0 and P1=100 with complexity 100 (480 and 240); fuzz under ASan/UBSan --anim 7: 33 param sets x 6 times clean, alignment pass clean at 4 widths and 4 offsets; Makefile.lifecycle check ALL OK; check_copies.py anim_mandala OK; QEMU anim_mandala RESULT PASS (interpPairKernel bit-exact); pio display, display-loadtest and display-sim SUCCESS (sim does not compile AnimMandala.cpp).

Left for the bench: device animtest http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=7 (mismatch_px must be 0), and a look on the panel at Symmetry 0, 50, 100. Agent-mail was unreachable on 127.0.0.1:8765 during this work, so no server-side file reservation was taken.
close_reason: octantAngle used the Q16 ratio shifted down 16 more; fixed, goldens regenerated, Symmetry now changes the arm count
