title: Bigger, centred start control and a centred scale readout
description:
The start control is the one action its screen offers and it read small and sat
low. Measured on the simulator, the band between the last control above it and
the bottom icon row (which starts at y420) runs y264 to 419 on brew, y260 to 419
on water and y273 to 419 on grind, so the middles are 341, 340 and 346 and the
button's centre sat at 369, 369 and 377. At 40x40 it was also the smallest
target on the page, against the 56 px floor the settings pages are held to.

lv_imgbtn cannot scale its source: lv_obj_init_draw_img_dsc pins zoom to
LV_IMG_ZOOM_NONE for every widget that draws through it, so a bigger button
needs a bigger image. tools/icon_to_lvgl.py renders one from the same
icons/*.svg the 40x40 pair came from, in EEZ Studio's own format; it reproduces
the shipped 40x40 play byte for byte from that icon's own pixels, and
ImageMagick's rendering of the SVG matches Inkscape's to a mean alpha error of
2 of 255.

The new images live in src/display/ui/default/images/, not in the studio's tree,
because the studio rewrites eez/ wholesale on export and its images[] table is
indexed by asset number, so an extra row in it renumbers every asset after it.

DefaultUI::growActionButtons takes the four buttons to 60x60 and the three that
had room to y+103. The status screen's pause grows but does not move: its band
is only y335 to 419, since the shot readout ends at y334.

The scale cover changed too. Its readout is a 170 px right-aligned number box
plus a "g", centred as a row, so "0.0 g" sat 47 px right of the middle: the box
is as wide as the widest reading it must hold and a short reading sits against
its right edge, leaving the slack on the left. The row is now shifted left by
half the slack a representative two-digit reading leaves, which centres the ink
for a dose or a yield and leaves "0.0" about 15 px right. Re-aligning per
reading is not available: the number is painted by a compositor Text element
between LVGL refreshes, and moving its container on every value is gm-nly's flex
re-flow churn by another route. The tare pill moved from y+70 to y+100.

/api/debug/scalescreen?on=0|1 is new. The cover is reachable only from the menu,
and /api/debug/scale, which used to carry the screen knob, is a
GM_SYNTH_HANDSHAKE route, so the simulator had no way to open it and the screen
could not be shot.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] pio run -e display and -e display-sim both link.
- [ ] pio test -e native_settingsui passes.
- [ ] python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py passes.
- [ ] python3 tools/icon_to_lvgl.py icons/play.svg 40 --out <tmp> reproduces the
      structure of ui_image_play_40x40.c, and encode() reproduces all four of
      its blocks byte for byte from that file's own depth-32 pixels.
- [ ] tools/screen_shots.py --scale writes a scale.png on the simulator.
- [ ] Owner has judged the size and the positions from the screenshots.
notes:
Landed on anims/astra. The status screen's pause sits at y+118, not at the
y+103 the other three use: every one of these buttons carries a 25 px click
pad, so a 60x60 button answers to a 110x110 rectangle, and the dials' menu
chevron answers to 130x95 starting at y385. At y+130 the pause reached y424,
6 px from the chevron's own 40x40 body, where the old 40x40 button left 16.
y+118 leaves 18. Brew, water and grind end with less chevron overlap than they
had: 110x13 and 110x21 against 90x30 and 90x38.

Checks run: pio run -e display (5,934,979 B of 6,553,600, up 39 kB) and
-e display-sim both link, pio test -e native_settingsui 68 cases pass, and
tools/settings_ui_test.py passes on the simulator, 740 checks across 8
scenarios, 16 pages audited clean. Before and after screenshots of all six
screens are in the session.

Left open for the owner to judge the size and the positions.

Decided 2026-10-01, owner delegated the default: the sizes and positions landed on anims/astra are accepted as judged from the simulator screenshots (tools/screen_shots.py, brew, water, grind, status and --scale), now merged into idf5 at 307297d1 and running on the bench board as v1.9.22-idf5. The other five acceptance items passed on 2026-09-15 as recorded above. Closed.

title: Give the steam screen its start control back
description:
The steam screen shows whether it is steaming and offers no way to stop it.
Before b8e7831d ("Steam Rework and temperature indicator", June 2025) the slot
the other action screens put their start button in held an lv_imgbtn. That
commit added the auto-start in Controller::loopLogic, which calls activate()
once the boiler is within 5 C of the steam target, and guarded
action_on_simple_process_toggle with MODE_STEAM, which left the button inert.
The EEZ rework (2d10acb7, June 2026) then replaced it with a plain lv_img of a
wind icon whose hidden flag the generated tick drives from "!ui_flags.active".

The owner asked for the button back, with the auto-start kept, and for it to
stay visible while steaming so the screen says what is happening.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The steam screen carries a 60x60 imgbtn in the same slot and at the same
      coordinates as the water screen's start button: 210..269 x 313..372, hit
      rect 185..294 x 288..397 with the 25 px pad.
- [ ] It shows play when no process is running and pause while one is, and a
      tap toggles between them.
- [ ] The auto-start in Controller::loopLogic is unchanged.
- [ ] The wind image draws nothing and the generated tick that writes its
      hidden flag still runs without touching freed memory.
- [ ] The steam screen's rest churn is unchanged: no refreshes a second on
      tools/churn_sweep.py that the other dial screens do not also have.
- [ ] Rig.audit() on the steam screen reports what water reports and nothing
      more.
- [ ] pio run -e display and -e display-sim link; pio test -e native_settingsui
      and tools/settings_ui_test.py pass.

## Tests

- tools/settings_ui_test.py on the simulator (navigation, geometry audit).
- A simulator run that enters steam mode through the menu tile, taps the
  button, and reads the framebuffer in both states.
close_reason: Done on the simulator. The steam slot reads imgbtn 60x60 at 210..269 x 313..372 against water's identical 60x60 at the same box, the wind image reads 0x0, and Rig.audit() on steam reports what water reports and nothing more (chevron edge, chevron-to-button overlap 110x13). Entering steam mode through the menu tile and tapping the button starts a SteamProcess and shows pause; tapping again stops it and shows play. pio run -e display links at 5,935,623 B of 6,553,600 B, 644 B more than before; -e display-sim links; pio test -e native_settingsui passes 68 cases; tools/settings_ui_test.py passes, 740 checks across 8 scenarios, 0 failures. Not measured: the rest-churn criterion, which needs tools/churn_sweep.py on the bench board. Nothing in the change invalidates at rest by reading (the state follows the controller, the accent is cached, the wind image has no area), but that is reasoning, not a measurement.

title: Overlay UI steps instead of counting: whole-page invalidations from re-asserted flags
description:
The scale screen's weight readout advanced in visible jumps while a weight was
rising, and the same burstiness showed on any screen with a moving value.

Root cause, found with a new instrument (inval_src on /api/debug/anim, which
records the object, its class, both rectangles and lv_obj_invalidate's own
return address for every large invalidation):

1. DefaultUI::maintainScaleScreen re-asserted the scale cover's visible state
   on every UI pass. LVGL's lv_obj_add_flag and lv_obj_clear_flag invalidate
   the whole object for LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN whether or not the flag changes, and
   that cover is the full 480x480, so the screen invalidated the whole page
   14.65 times a second. Each one is a whole-page snapshot, 147 ms of the UI
   task, which starves the render task of the PSRAM bus and stops the
   compositor-owned readouts easing.

2. patch_lvgl_label_elem.py guarded lv_label_set_text and lv_label_refr_text
   but not lv_label_set_text_fmt, which invalidates on its own before it
   reaches refr_text. The scale readout formats its value, so a label that was
   already a compositor Text element still invalidated its own box on every
   value: 11.8 a second.

Measured on the bench board, divider 6, whole-frame path, 0.5 g/s synthetic
ramp on the scale screen: overlay publishes 3.70/s before, 0.11/s after.
tools/churn_sweep.py unchanged at 0.00 refreshes a second on every other
screen. All three envs build.

title: Framebuffer debug dumps degrade after a few hundred requests
description:
`/api/debug/fb` stops delivering a whole framebuffer dump after a few hundred
requests, and a reboot restores it.

Found while building the controlled gradient comparison (gm-nov3.10), which
reads that endpoint in bulk. Fresh boot delivers the whole dump. After a few
hundred requests the chunked response is dropped partway, at every step value,
while internal free falls from 30.9 kB to 26.2 kB and the largest block from
20.5 kB to 15.9 kB.

This is the internal DRAM starvation CLAUDE.md already describes for the web
UI, reached through a debug endpoint instead of through a browser tab. The
asset gate protects the big embedded assets; this path has no such gate.

`tools/gradient_fb_check.py` works around it: it retries and accepts a short
read that still reaches the rows it samples, so a run finishes. A long batch
still wants a reboot first. That workaround is why this is a separate item and
not a blocker.

Worth measuring before deciding anything: whether the allocations are leaked
or merely fragmented, since the two have different fixes. `/api/debug/heapmap`
gives the block-size histogram, and `/api/debug/heap` carries `int_free`,
`dma_free` and `dma_min`.

Note that this endpoint is compiled only into bench builds, so this does not
affect a production device. It does affect every measurement anyone takes with
it, which is why it matters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cause is named with evidence: a leak, fragmentation, or the response
      path holding buffers too long. `/api/debug/heapmap` before and after a
      few hundred requests, recorded.
- [ ] The number of requests that triggers the degradation is stated, with the
      board's uptime and what else was running.
- [ ] Either the endpoint holds up over a long batch, or it refuses cleanly
      when it cannot serve a whole dump, rather than dropping a response
      partway.
- [ ] A run of several hundred requests leaves internal free where it started,
      or the residual is explained.
- [ ] `tools/gradient_fb_check.py` still passes, and its retry workaround is
      removed if the endpoint no longer needs it.
notes:
Fixed in 28cec8ec. Two faults, both in the response path, neither one fragmentation.

CAUSE 1, the short read. The chunked filler wrote whole output rows and returned
0 when the budget was smaller than one row, and ESPAsyncWebServer reads 0 as
"no more data": it writes the terminating chunk and closes, so the client sees a
well formed short dump with a 200 and no error. At step 1 a row is 960 bytes.
The library calls the filler while the remaining TCP window is at least
MSS/2 (720 bytes), with a budget of min(2*MSS, window) - 8, so with
TCP_SND_BUF 5760 one send round goes 2 rows, 2 rows, 1 row, then a 928 byte
budget that cannot hold a row. That is 5 rows, 4,800 bytes, every time.
Steps 2 to 8 have rows of 480 bytes and under, which always fit, so they were
never affected.

Evidence, bench board, pre-fix firmware (commit 83ae968b loadtest, uptime 33
to 36 minutes, WiFi and BLE up, animation running, pixel clock divider 7):
  step 1, 20 requests: 20 of 20 returned exactly 4,800 of 460,800 bytes, with
    a valid chunked terminator. int_free unchanged at 24,011, largest block
    unchanged at 11,252.
  step 1, 50 more requests: 50 of 50 at 4,800. Same heap numbers.
  step 2, 200 requests: 200 of 200 whole (115,200 bytes). int_free delta 0.
  steps 3,4,5,6,8, 3 requests each: all whole.
So the short read is not request count dependent and not heap dependent. The
board was already below the bead's "after" heap numbers (24.0 kB free, 11.2 kB
largest, against 26.2 and 15.9) and still served step 2 perfectly.

CAUSE 2, the leak, which is the heap drift the bead saw. The filler kept its
row counter in a heap cell (new int) and deleted it only on the final call, so
a client that disconnected part way through never freed it.
  pre-fix, 300 requests aborted after 3 kB: int_free 24,011 -> 17,591
  (-6,420, 21.4 bytes each), largest 11,252 -> 7,668, dma_free -6,428, and
  none of it came back after 120 seconds of idle.
At 21.4 bytes a request the bead's own 4.7 kB drop is about 220 aborted
requests, which matches "a few hundred". A bulk reader with a retry loop
aborts on every retry, which is how the endpoint's own consumer produced it.
/api/debug/ovl had the identical cell and the same leak, and is fixed too.

THE FIX. The filler writes whole pixels instead of whole rows, and returns
RESPONSE_TRY_AGAIN (not 0) when two bytes do not fit, which parks the response
until the next ack. The position comes from the index the library already
passes, so nothing is allocated per request and nothing can leak. Checked first
against a host transcription of the library's send loop (every step, byte exact
against the row major expectation).

AFTER, bench board, new display-loadtest build, divider 7, animation running:
  step 1, 30 requests: 30 of 30 whole 460,800 bytes (was 0 of 30).
  step 1, 50 requests: 50 of 50 whole.
  step 2, 300 requests, board 2 to 4 minutes old: 300 of 300 whole,
    int_free -580.
  idle control, 5 minutes, no fb requests: int_free flat at 26,363, so idle
    drift is zero and the -580 above was the board still settling after boot.
  step 2, 300 requests, board settled at 11 minutes: 300 of 300 whole,
    int_free delta 0, largest delta 0. Criterion 4 met.
  300 aborted requests: int_free, largest and dma_free all delta 0.
  /api/debug/ovl at steps 1, 2 and 4: whole and complete (691,200 / 172,800 /
    43,200 bytes).
  tools/gradient_fb_check.py --selftest at the default step 2: PASS, 19,200
    samples, 0 mismatches, both negative controls fired.
  tools/gradient_fb_check.py --step 1: PASS, 76,800 samples, 0 mismatches, all
    256 ramp indices in one pass. That is the correctness proof for the new
    full resolution path against known pixel values.

tools/gradient_fb_check.py no longer accepts a short frame (the need_rows
tolerance and the IncompleteRead partial are gone) and requires the whole
frame, retrying only on a transport fault.

LEFT UNDONE. Three other files still carry the old "step 1 truncates" note and
belong to other agents: tools/picker_device_checks.py (says 4,800 every time,
which was right), tools/gradient_sheet.py, tools/dial_elem_check.py, and
CLAUDE.md's settings section. They want updating now that step 1 is whole.
`pio run -e display` was not run: another agent held that build.

Board left on this display-loadtest build (v1.9.8-sleep9-654-g7d3c8906-dirty,
built 2026-09-13T11:32:23Z, flashed at 0x10000 only, so NVS and the stored
settings are untouched). Stored pixel clock divider read 7 before and after.

ADDENDUM after the production build was freed. `pio run -e display` SUCCESS,
2 min 25 s incremental, 5,899,251 bytes, 90.0% of the app partition, RAM 32.1%.
That number is not all this fix: the lead measured 5,895,863 a few commits ago
and other agents have landed work since.

And the bead is wrong on one point. /api/debug/fb is NOT bench only. Its device
branch is inside `#if !GAGGIMATE_HEADLESS && !GAGGIMATE_SIM`, and
setupServer() calls setupDebugEndpoints() unconditionally, so the endpoint (and
the leak) shipped on production boards too. Nothing calls it there in normal
use, but it is reachable, and CLAUDE.md's internal DRAM budget is what it would
have eaten.

title: Press feedback on every settings target: tiles dimmed nothing, rows blanked
description: Reported 2026-09-06 on the bench board: settings screens showed no press colour change on many elements. Measured on the simulator: the category tiles changed 0 per pixel while held (plain lv_obj, skipped by the pressed-style walk), whole-row targets jumped to the touch dim colour itself (black) and vanished, arrows and chevrons dimmed 40%. Fix: one rule, settingsPressedColor, 40% toward the touch dim colour for tiles, rows, arrows and chevrons alike, matching the generated screens. Verified with a framebuffer diff mid-hold on the simulator and the board, full simulator runner PASS, device runner on six scenarios.
close_reason: settingsPressedColor rule in 7cce1e4f, docs cd6f4e37. Simulator: tiles 0 to 42 per pixel while held, rows 32 to 49 down to 13 to 27, arrows unchanged; full runner PASS 320 checks. Board flashed, probe shows every target changing while held, device runner PASS on six scenarios.

title: Settings runner: a missing row takes the whole device run down
description:
On the bench board, `tools/settings_ui_test.py --host 192.168.1.121` crashed
in `restart_round_trip` with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not
subscriptable` while reading the `Standby brightness` row, after the
animation scenario had passed.

The row lookup returned None and the caller indexed it without checking. A
row that is absent, disabled, or named differently than the test expects
should fail one check with the row name in the message, not take the whole
run down: everything after the crash goes unreported, which is how a passing
scenario ends a run with no report written.

Nothing about the Display category changed in the gm-tany work, so this is a
harness robustness gap rather than a firmware fault. It has not been
reproduced on the simulator.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every helper in `tools/settings_ui_tests/` that looks a row up by name
      either returns a value or records a failed check naming the row, and
      never lets a None reach an index or an attribute access.
- [ ] `restart_round_trip` reports a failed check and continues when a row it
      needs is missing.
- [ ] The device run finishes and writes `report.json` even when a row lookup
      fails.
- [ ] A test that forces a missing row (a name that cannot match) produces one
      failed check and a written report, not a traceback.
close_reason: Fixed in e376c307 with gm-bzu.31: row_value and tap_target(None) raise RowMissing (an AssertionError naming the row), require_tag names the row a lookup needed, the runner records ROW MISSING as one failed check and carries on, and restart_round_trip reports RESTART ROW MISSING and continues. Forced missing rows on the simulator gave one failed check each and a written report, no traceback crash.

title: Resolve idf5 branch review defects and validation gaps
description:
## Scope
Resolve the idf5 branch review findings, CI failures, and follow-up improvements from the 2026-09-05 review. Baseline: 7e9fddea; review snapshot: 8f8ad95e. More layer/compositor commits arrived later and are included in the final review/regression child.

The durable report is .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Each child is self-contained with evidence, source locations, acceptance criteria, and priority. Runtime findings are source-traced unless a reproduction is explicitly recorded; builds and sanitizer findings were observed locally.

## Success Criteria

Final validation records the exact tested SHA/configuration, confirms the complete build/check matrix, reviews later concurrent additions, and distinguishes hardware verification from host checks. Do not silently weaken existing goldens or change measured kernel defaults without device evidence.

title: Restore gradient validation linkage in headless firmware
description:
## Context
Review finding 1, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P1] Headless firmware cannot link, blocking nightly publishing.**

   Location: [WebUIPlugin.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/plugins/WebUIPlugin.cpp:2838), [src/CMakeLists.txt](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/CMakeLists.txt:23).

   The settings handler now calls `bg_library_valid()` and `bg_map_valid()` unconditionally. Their definitions are in `ui/default/bganim/BgAnimThemes.cpp`, but headless source selection excludes the entire UI tree and only adds PanelClock back. A real `pio run -e display-headless` reaches the linker and fails with undefined references to both functions. The 8 MB headless environment uses the same exclusion. The nightly workflow builds headless before its release job, so this also prevents publication of otherwise successful controller/display builds.

   Move the shared parsers/validators into a module included by headless, or deliberately exclude those settings there. Avoid pulling every renderer into the smaller headless image just to obtain two validators.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run pio run -e display-headless against the reviewed source with its dependencies installed. Observe undefined references to bg_library_valid and bg_map_valid in WebUIPlugin settings handling. The 8 MB environment shares the excluding CMake filter; repeat there with a writable dependency directory.

## Acceptance Criteria
Both headless environments compile and link, with valid gradient settings handled deliberately; controller and display still build; Checks and nightly source selection use the same validators.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Both headless environments compile and link, with valid gradient settings handled deliberately; controller and display still build; Checks and nightly source selection use the same validators.
notes: Fixed in c804d579 (BgAnimThemes.cpp added to the headless source list in src/CMakeLists.txt, the way PanelClock.cpp is) and 866c44d5 (the UI-only headers WebUIPlugin.cpp had grown since the review sit behind GAGGIMATE_HEADLESS; every use already did). display-headless builds: RAM 67,332 B, flash 2,842,167 B (2026-09-08, worktree). display-headless-8m shares the sources but could not be built on this WSL1 machine: PlatformIO fails to copy the git-based ESPBufferManager libdep into .pio/libdeps/display-headless-8m (shutil permission error on .git/hooks) in both checkouts, the same dependency-directory problem the review noted. CI or a Linux host should confirm it.

title: Calibrate load cells against acknowledged applied factors
description:
## Context
Review finding 10, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] Calibration calculates from an unsaved factor rather than the applied factor.**

   Location: [MachineTab.jsx](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/web/src/pages/Settings/tabs/MachineTab.jsx:108).

   `measuredWeight` reflects the controller's currently applied scale factor, but calibration multiplies it by the editable `formData.scaleFactorN`. Those differ after a manual edit, sign flip, or a previous calibration before Save. Example: applied factor 2500, reported 80 g, known mass 100 g gives the correct draft 2000. Re-entering 100 g and calibrating again before saving produces 1600 from the unchanged live reading. Saving that second result miscalibrates the scale.

   Calculate against the acknowledged applied factor, or perform calibration on the controller from raw readings. Prevent another calibration against a pending draft until the new factor is applied and fresh measurements arrive.

## Steps to Reproduce
Use an applied factor of 2500 and a fresh valid reading of 80 g. Enter a known 100 g mass and calibrate to get draft 2000. Before saving, re-enter 100 and calibrate again. The unchanged live reading multiplied by draft 2000 produces incorrect draft 1600. Repeat with an unsaved sign flip and with the second cell.

## Acceptance Criteria
Reported weight is paired with the factor that actually produced it; unsaved edits/sign flips/repeated calibration cannot compound the factor; applied 2500 with 80 g measured against 100 g remains draft 2000 on repeat until acknowledged; both cells and save/fresh-sample sequencing are covered.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Reported weight is paired with the factor that actually produced it; unsaved edits/sign flips/repeated calibration cannot compound the factor; applied 2500 with 80 g measured against 100 g remains draft 2000 on repeat until acknowledged; both cells and save/fresh-sample sequencing are covered.
notes: Fixed on the worktree branch (commit 'web: calibrate load cells against the factor the device measures with'), merged into idf5. Firmware: the evt:hardware-scale message carries sf1 and sf2, the stored scale factors setScaleFactors() sent to the controller (WebUIPlugin.cpp). Web: ApiService maps them to status.hardwareScaleFactor1/2; MachineTab computes newFactor = reading * appliedFactor / knownMass; the calibrate buttons are disabled while a cell's draft differs from its applied factor and a note asks for Save and a fresh reading; older firmware falls back to the loaded value (scaleFactor1Loaded/2Loaded, excluded from the POST). Repeating the bead's example (applied 2500, 80 g, 100 g) gives 2000 and then a disabled button until saved. Verified: npm run lint:check 0 errors, npm run build ok, display-loadtest build (web bundle embedded by embed_webui_pre.py). Not verified on a machine with a hardware scale; the bench board has none.

title: Serialize nightly publishing across master and idf5
description:
## Context
Review finding 11, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] Nightly concurrency does not serialize the shared release across branches.**

   Location: [build-nightly.yml](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/.github/workflows/build-nightly.yml:22).

   Both `master` and `idf5` trigger this workflow and mutate the same `nightly` tag, release assets, and Pages directory. The group includes `github.ref`, so those two runs have different locks and may publish concurrently. Their tag move, artifact removal, and asset uploads can interleave despite the comment promising serialization.

   Use a repository-wide concurrency group for that shared destination, or publish separate branch channels. This fixes overlap between runs; making downloads consistent during an individual mutable-release update is a separate opportunity below.

## Steps to Reproduce
Inspect workflow dispatch for concurrent pushes to master and idf5, or use a controlled workflow test. Both target the same nightly tag/release/Pages directory but compute different nightly-${github.ref} concurrency keys. Interleave tag movement, removeArtifacts and upload steps to demonstrate that both publishers can run together.

## Acceptance Criteria
All workflows targeting the same nightly tag/release/Pages destination share one concurrency group or have separate destinations; cross-branch pushes cannot interleave artifact removal and upload; queued publication does not abandon a partially mutated destination.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: All workflows targeting the same nightly tag/release/Pages destination share one concurrency group or have separate destinations; cross-branch pushes cannot interleave artifact removal and upload; queued publication does not abandon a partially mutated destination.
notes: Fixed on the worktree branch (commit 'ci: one concurrency group for every nightly publisher'), merged into idf5. build-nightly.yml concurrency group changed from nightly-${{ github.ref }} to the fixed name nightly-release; cancel-in-progress stays false so a queued run always completes the tag and asset republish. check.yml keeps its per-ref group: it mutates nothing shared. Not tested by a live workflow run (no push from this session); the change is the documented GitHub Actions behaviour for a shared group name.

title: Recover animation startup after partial overlay allocation failure
description:
## Context
Review finding 12, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] A transient overlay allocation failure disables animation until reboot.**

   Location: [SleepAnimation.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:1007), [allocation check](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:1076).

   `overlayCap` is set before allocating the overlay buffers and tables. If a required allocation returns null, `start()` returns with that capacity still nonzero. Future starts skip the whole allocation block because it is guarded only by `overlayCap == 0`; `overlayOk` then fails forever, even after memory pressure has cleared. Successful partial allocations also remain held.

   Retry individual missing allocations, or roll back partial construction and reset the initialization sentinel. Fault-inject each required allocation and verify a later start can succeed.

## Steps to Reproduce
Fault-inject one required ov.buf, ov.runs, or ov.runN allocation during the first SleepAnimation::start. Restore allocator availability and call start again. overlayCap remains nonzero, so allocation is skipped and overlayOk still fails. Repeat at every required allocation and check cleanup/retained allocation ownership.

## Acceptance Criteria
Each required allocation can fail without permanently latching a nonzero capacity; partial allocation is rolled back or missing buffers are retried; subsequent start succeeds after memory recovers; retained successful allocations are not leaked or double-freed.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Each required allocation can fail without permanently latching a nonzero capacity; partial allocation is rolled back or missing buffers are retried; subsequent start succeeds after memory recovers; retained successful allocations are not leaked or double-freed.
notes: Fixed in 75c391e3 (worktree branch, merged into idf5). New SleepAnimation::freeOverlayBuffers() frees ov.buf (heap_caps_free), runs, runN, haloRuns, haloN, scrimSrc, scrim for both overlays plus scrimTmp/scrimTmp2/scrimCmp, nulls all pointers and clears overlayCap, overlayPlanePx and gm_overlay_plane_px. start() calls it when overlayOk is false, so the next start re-runs the whole allocation block. Ownership: everything allocated in the block is freed exactly once (pointers nulled). Verified: display-loadtest and display-sim build. No fault-injection harness for heap_caps_aligned_alloc on the device; not exercised on hardware.

title: Execute simulator scripts from the main loop
description:
## Context
Review finding 13, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P3] The new simulator `--script` option does nothing.**

   Location: [sim/main.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/sim/main.cpp:128), [main loop](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/sim/main.cpp:146).

   The script file is parsed into a `ScriptRunner`, but the main loop never calls `script->pump(drv)`. WAIT/TAP/SHOT instructions are never executed. This remains a separate issue after the simulator compile errors are repaired. Wire the runner into the loop and specify completion/error behavior; check a short tap-and-screenshot script end to end.

## Steps to Reproduce
After the simulator builds, write a script containing WAIT 100, TAP 240 240, and SHOT /tmp/gaggimate-script.bmp. Launch the simulator with --script pointing to that file. The current loop never calls ScriptRunner::pump, so no script steps execute and the screenshot is absent.

## Acceptance Criteria
The loop pumps ScriptRunner; WAIT/TAP/SHOT execute in order; a short script produces its screenshot and follows documented completion behavior; missing/malformed input is reported; TAP releases reliably.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: The loop pumps ScriptRunner; WAIT/TAP/SHOT execute in order; a short script produces its screenshot and follows documented completion behavior; missing/malformed input is reported; TAP releases reliably.
notes:
Fixed on the worktree branch (commit 'sim: run --script steps from the main loop and report bad input'), merged into idf5. The main loop calls ScriptRunner::pump(drv) after drv->pumpAndRender(). On done() it renders one more frame (so the release reaches LVGL), prints "[script] done @t=" and exits 0. Missing file, malformed line (with line number) or an empty script: message on stderr, exit 2 before controller.setup().

Checked end to end with SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy on the display-sim build: script "WAIT 3000 / SHOT before.bmp / TAP 240 240 / WAIT 800 / SHOT after.bmp" printed each step at its simulated time, wrote two 691,254 byte BMPs that differ, exit 0. missing.txt: "[script] cannot open missing.txt", exit 2. "TAP 240": "[script] bad.txt:2: malformed line: TAP 240", exit 2. The TAP release happens in pump() 150 ms after the press, before the step index moves, so a script cannot end with a finger down.

title: Add animation lifecycle, allocation-failure, and band-shape CI coverage
description:
## Context
Existing golden/fuzz harnesses iterate animations without releasing the outgoing resident, forcing later hot tables into PSRAM instead of exercising production slab reuse. Fuzz covers width 480 and 16-row bands, while production includes 240/466/233 and one/two-row bands. INIT FAILED currently skips cases without failing the harness. The review probe in .beads/reviews/anim_lifecycle_probe.cpp performs 140 init/render/release cycles and exposed odd-width alignment UB; its success print is not a sanitizer verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria
Add an independent regression harness without weakening goldens; release outgoing residents and cover repeated dimension switches at 480/240/466/233, one/two-row tails, failed init/partial allocation/retry, and slab reuse; make initialization and sanitizer failures fail CI (UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1); retain existing golden/call-shape checks.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Add an independent regression harness without weakening goldens; release outgoing residents and cover repeated dimension switches at 480/240/466/233, one/two-row tails, failed init/partial allocation/retry, and slab reuse; make initialization and sanitizer failures fail CI (UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1); retain existing golden/call-shape checks.
notes:
Done in commit "animbench: lifecycle check with allocation faults, and five init() fixes it found (gm-bzu.15)" on worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials, merged into idf5.

New harness: tools/animbench/lifecycle_check.cpp, built and run by tools/animbench/Makefile.lifecycle (make -f Makefile.lifecycle check), ASan and UBSan on, UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1. CI runs it in the animations job of check.yml after the goldens.

What it covers:
- Phase A: every animation through 480, 240, 466, 233 and back, three passes, release between. Two-row bands at even sizes, one-row calls at 233, a one-row tail at every size. After each release the slab must be back at its level before the init and no new heap block may survive (baseline taken after the warm-up pass, which builds the lazy shared tables).
- Phase B: the heap runs out at each allocation an init() makes, in turn (sticky from that call on, through two hooks in shim/esp_heap_caps.h). init() must return false, a retry must succeed and render, release() must clean up.
- Phase C: slab empty at the end, zero allocHot fallbacks.
- Init failures exit non-zero. The bench and fuzz harnesses still print SKIP or INIT FAILED and go on; they were not changed.

What it found and what was fixed: starfield, fireflies, steam, ember and orbits allocated all tables in one block keyed on the first pointer and returned false without releasing on a partial failure. Retry then ran with null tables (UBSan: null store in starfield's and ember's frame()) or leaked hot tables in the slab. All five now call release() before returning false. Successful init paths are unchanged.

title: Retain framebuffer ownership until animation shutdown is confirmed
description:
## Context
SleepAnimation::stop waits up to 500 ms for each worker and endDirectPath only bounds its DMA drain, then proceeds even if retirement is unconfirmed. DefaultUI::stopSleepAnimation immediately enables LVGL framebuffer rendering. A worker blocked in a band or delayed DMA completion can outlive the handoff; push-task creation failure also marks stopped while the render task may still be running.

## Steps to Reproduce
In a controlled task/DMA test, hold a worker in a band-slot wait or delay DMA completion past the stop deadlines. Invoke stopSleepAnimation and observe whether LVGL gets framebuffer ownership while the worker/transfer is still live. Separately fail creation of SleepPush after SleepAnim starts. These are targeted fault-injection scenarios derived from source, not physical-device reproductions performed during review.

## Acceptance Criteria
Represent stop completion explicitly; do not return shared buffers/gates to LVGL or reuse task state while a worker/DMA can still access them; provide bounded UI responsiveness via deferred completion/quarantine; inject delayed slot/DMA retirement and push-task creation failure and verify no races, double deletion, or permanent gate loss.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Represent stop completion explicitly; do not return shared buffers/gates to LVGL or reuse task state while a worker/DMA can still access them; provide bounded UI responsiveness via deferred completion/quarantine; inject delayed slot/DMA retirement and push-task creation failure and verify no races, double deletion, or permanent gate loss.
notes:
Fixed in worktree commit 96bcde75, merged into idf5. SleepAnimation::stop() now returns true only when both workers parked and the DMA drained. stopConfirmed() re-checks the same. endDirectPath() returns the drain result. finishStop() holds the body of stop() and is shared with the push-task creation failure in start(), which no longer sets stopped by hand. DefaultUI keeps LVGL on the scratch buffer while animStopPending is set, and neither starts nor stops the animation. The loop finishes the handoff once confirmed or after a 3 s cap with an error log. The panel stop path waits up to 3 s the same way before it deletes the panel. startSleepAnimation checks stopConfirmed() when start() declined.

Device check: 10 animoff/on cycles on the bench board. Every stop confirmed at once. LVGL presents resumed after each stop. anim_frames stood still while off. No flip timeouts. Heap steady (int_free 30.3 KB, dma_min 15.7 KB).

Not done: fault injection of a stuck worker or DMA. The quarantine path is verified by reading. Reaping is unchanged (keyed on the task handle, the next start reaps).

title: Require successful validation before publishing nightly releases
description:
## Context
Nightly publishes independently of Checks. Even when its own builds pass, formatting, simulator, autotune, or animation checks can be red for the same revision without blocking the release. Avoid duplicating inconsistent command sets between publication and Checks.

## Acceptance Criteria
The exact commit being published must pass required firmware, web/lint, simulator boot, formatting, and relevant tests; a failing required check prevents tag/assets/Pages mutations; concurrency and workflow triggers do not allow stale success from another SHA; avoid a race between independent workflows.

notes: Done in commit "ci: publish a nightly only after Checks passed on the same commit (gm-bzu.17)" on worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials, merged into idf5. title: Pin OTA downloads to an immutable versioned asset manifest

title: Separate renderer lifecycle code from experimental diagnostics
description:
## Context
SleepAnimation, WebUIPlugin, and framework patch code combine rendering/ownership logic with large benchmarking and disruptive diagnostic subsystems. Ownership is implemented separately in LVGL, render/push workers, and endpoint paths. This increases the chance that a new debug experiment violates production invariants.

## Acceptance Criteria
Extract bounded modules for diagnostics/bench dispatch while centralizing framebuffer/worker ownership; preserve useful read-only production diagnostics; intentionally gate disruptive experiments; retain core-affinity, bounce-pool and SRAM invariants; measure any ISR instrumentation removal rather than assuming it improves performance.

## Evidence

Remaining and not done: SleepAnimation.cpp holds about 1,000 lines under GM_ANIM_BENCH (492), GM_KBLOB (277), GM_BLEND_PROBE (202) and GM_TOUCH_PROBE (64), in about 40 small blocks interleaved with the render loop, several inside the IRAM-pinned functions. title: Fix the AMOLED rectangle contract for animation band pushes
description:
## Context
Review finding 2, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P1] Animation band pushes can read beyond their buffers on AMOLED displays.**

   Location: [SleepAnimation.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:1636), [Amoled_DisplayPanel.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/drivers/AmoledDisplay/Amoled_DisplayPanel.cpp:214).

   SleepAnimation passes exclusive rectangle endpoints to `pushColors(x0, y0, x1, y1, pixels)`. The AMOLED implementation interprets the last two coordinates as width and height and forwards them to `draw16bitRGBBitmap`. AMOLED exposes no direct framebuffer, so animations use this fallback. For example, a two-row band at y=100 passes a height of 102 while its allocation contains only two rows. Display clipping does not repair the source-buffer length mismatch. Cropped x coordinates introduce the corresponding width mismatch.

   Standardize the Display rectangle contract and convert endpoints to dimensions in the AMOLED adapter. Verify it with a fake panel that checks the supplied source extent and with an AMOLED device. The pre-existing adapter mismatch is newly exposed by repeated small animation bands.

## Steps to Reproduce
Using a checked fake AMOLED adapter, submit a two-row animation band at y=100 and nonzero/cropped x. Trace SleepAnimation::pushLoop passing exclusive x1/y1 into Amoled_DisplayPanel::pushColors, then draw16bitRGBBitmap receiving them as width/height. Check the requested source extent exceeds w*2 pixels. Device reproduction remains to be done on a 466x466 AMOLED panel.

## Acceptance Criteria
Display::pushColors has one explicit coordinate contract across all adapters; a checked fake panel accepts cropped and uncropped bands at nonzero x/y with no source overread; 466x466 AMOLED animation and ordinary LVGL updates are verified.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Display::pushColors has one explicit coordinate contract across all adapters; a checked fake panel accepts cropped and uncropped bands at nonzero x/y with no source overread; 466x466 AMOLED animation and ordinary LVGL updates are verified.
notes: Fixed in 372e67fa (worktree branch, merged into idf5). Display::pushColors now names its parameters xEnd/yEnd and documents the exclusive-end contract (matches esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap and the LVGL flush's x2+1, y2+1). Amoled_DisplayPanel converts to width/height for Arduino_GFX draw16bitRGBBitmap and returns on an empty rectangle. LilyGo and Waveshare panels only renamed (they were already correct). Verified: display-loadtest builds all three adapters (SUCCESS), display-sim SUCCESS. Not verified on AMOLED hardware: the bench board is a LilyGo T-RGB.

title: Fix or explicitly constrain paired stores for odd-width multi-row bands
description:
## Context
The fresh review lifecycle probe rendered two-row bands at w=233 under ASan/UBSan and reported misaligned uint32_t stores in AnimPlasma.cpp:189, AnimSilk.cpp:1152-1173, AnimMandala.cpp:770, and AnimSteam.cpp:322. Row 1 starts 466 bytes after row 0, which breaks 4-byte alignment. BgAnimation::band currently documents w*rows pixels without an even-width restriction. The production 233-wide half-resolution path currently uses one source row per band; this is proven API/portable-path UB, not a reproduced production crash.

## Steps to Reproduce
Compile .beads/reviews/anim_lifecycle_probe.cpp with all src/display/ui/default/bganim/*.cpp, the tools/animbench/shim includes, and -fsanitize=address,undefined. Run with ASAN_OPTIONS=verify_asan_link_order=0 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1. At width 233, two-row output gives row 1 only two-byte alignment and paired uint32_t stores trigger UBSan. The retained .log records the recovery-mode run across all animations; its final PASS line does not negate sanitizer errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
Use alignment-aware stores/fallbacks or enforce and document a valid API precondition consistently at every caller; UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 lifecycle tests pass for advertised odd-width shapes and all existing even-width goldens; do not weaken the 233-width coverage just to hide errors.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Use alignment-aware stores/fallbacks or enforce and document a valid API precondition consistently at every caller; UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 lifecycle tests pass for advertised odd-width shapes and all existing even-width goldens; do not weaken the 233-width coverage just to hide errors.
notes:
Resolved by constraining the API and holding every caller to it. Commit on the worktree branch: 'animations: state band()'s alignment precondition and hold every caller to it', merged into idf5.

Contract (BgAnim.h): dst is 4-byte aligned, and w is even whenever rows > 1. An odd width (233) is rendered one row per call into an aligned destination. Production already did this: the half path renders one source row per band (BAND_H is 2), and a static_assert in SleepAnimation.cpp now ties the two together.

Harnesses: interlace_check and render_one --shapes use an even row stride for their frame buffers and run only the one-row shapes at an odd width. Before, the harness itself placed odd rows 466 bytes in, which is what UBSan reported at 233 even with one-row calls.

Evidence: interlace_check built with -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all, UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1, ASAN_OPTIONS=verify_asan_link_order=0: ALL OK at 233x233, 466x466 and 480x480. make check: ALL OK, goldens unchanged. display-loadtest builds.

Not changed: .beads/reviews/anim_lifecycle_probe.cpp renders two-row bands at 233 into a 233-stride buffer. That call is outside the contract as now stated. The file is a review artefact.

title: Shot history: a file lookup in /h walks the whole FAT directory (4 to 5 s per shot file on the bench card)
description: Measured 2026-09-09 on the bench board (SD card, about 3,000 shots, 333 MB): a shot file in /h takes 2.3 s to open through fopen (one walk; FS::open took 4.8 s with its stat walk on top), a missing id 5 s, index.bin 3 s. FAT has no directory index, each step of the walk is one 512 B sector read through sdmmc, and the .slog extension needs long-file-name entries so every shot is two entries. The web history handler now does these opens on a worker task so the web server no longer trips the task watchdog (see WebUIPlugin.cpp, /api/history/*), but each shot still costs seconds and requests serialise. Options, in the order to try: shard /h into subdirectories by id (for example /h/010/010643.slog), which needs the writer, the index, the recovery walk, the rebuild, the delete path, the web paths and a migration of existing files; or 8.3 names to halve the directory; or a per-boot cache of directory positions, which FATFS does not expose. Owner decision because the on-card layout changes. Evidence: hist_open_us_max on /api/debug/heap, tools timing in the session notes.
notes: Decided 2026-09-09 by the owner: leave the flat /h layout. The history worker keeps the web server alive and seconds per open are accepted. Close as decided; reopen if the shot count or the card makes it worse.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-09-09: leave the flat /h layout; the history worker keeps the web server alive.

title: Remove the PHY PLL-track deferral patch, which the core-1 interrupt fix made vestigial
description:
The PHY PLL-track deferral (scripts/patch_phy_track_defer.py, the phyTrackTask and the VSYNC release in src/display/drivers/common/PanelClock.cpp) was written for one displaced band a second when the panel's interrupts shared core 0 with the radio. The panel's interrupts have lived on core 1 since Controller::setupPanel pinned them, and the revert test on 2026-09-09 (bench board, loadtest build, WiFi and the BLE controller link up, standby screen with the animation on) found no difference with the deferral off: /api/debug/scanout?phydefer=0|1 toggled it within one boot, four phases each, at the stored divider 8 (5 minute phases) and at the production divider 6 set live (4 minute phases). Every phase read 0 resyncs and 0 slips; catchups were 0.03 to 0.05 a second at divider 8 and 0.2 a second at divider 6 either way, depth max 2 of 8. tools/phydefer_ab.py is the A/B and CLAUDE.md (Open cleanups) carries the numbers.

Removing the deferral drops a framework patch that must be re-anchored on every IDF bump. It also removes a runtime task, the VSYNC release and the phy_us slip attribution. Keep the BLE scan backoff and the 5 s PLL-track period, which are separate knobs.

title: The standby screen logs its brightness 3.7 times a second
description:
The standby screen re-applies the standby brightness on every UI pass, and each call logs a line. On the bench board that is 3.69 lines a second forever, and it was 47.8% of the bytes in an 807 second serial capture.

## What the code does

`DefaultUI::loop` calls `setBrightness(settings.getStandbyBrightness())` unconditionally once the standby dim timeout has passed, every pass, with no check against what is already applied (`src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp:1994` to `:2001`). `DefaultUI::setBrightness` logs the value and then calls the panel driver (`:188` to `:194`).

The panel driver is not the cost. `LilyGo_RGBPanel::setBrightness` returns immediately when the value has not changed (`src/display/drivers/LilyGo-T-RGB/LilyGo_RGBPanel.cpp:134` to `:139`), so no GPIO or bus traffic happens. The whole cost is the `ESP_LOGI` on the UI task and the serial bytes it produces.

## The measurement

Taken from the gm-t9ld soak capture on the bench board (`display-loadtest`, standby screen, 807 seconds):

- 2,979 brightness lines out of 7,952 total, 37.5% of lines.
- 137,034 bytes of 286,907, 47.8% of bytes.
- 3.69 lines a second, and exactly one distinct value in the whole capture (11).

For scale, the next most frequent line is `GM_UISTAT` at 180 lines in the same window, which is once per 5 second window by design. Every other repeated line in the capture is once per window or once per event.

## What the noise costs

CLAUDE.md's rule for this rig is that telemetry rides the serial log, not HTTP, because the rig's DMA ballast starves WiFi exactly when the rig is working. So the serial log is the measurement channel, and half of it is one line that never changes. A person reading the log to diagnose a fault (which is what the capture above was for) is reading mostly this.

This is not a claim that the logging causes a fault. It is a claim that the channel used to find faults is half noise, and that the fix is small.

## What the fix must keep

The line is deliberate and three checks read it. The comment at `DefaultUI.cpp:189` says the Display category's tests read it on both the device and the simulator, because neither has a way to sample backlight PWM directly. The three readers are in `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_display.py`:

- `main_brightness_log_line` (`:297`) expects a line with the new value after a minus tap.
- `main_brightness_reassert_log` (`:342`) expects a line with the touched value after a web save races a live edit. **This one re-applies a value that may already be applied**, so a fix that gates the log itself on a change can break it.
- The docstrings at `:284` and `:314` describe the same line.

So gate the caller, not the log. Keep `setBrightness` logging every call as it does now, and stop the standby path calling it when the value it would apply is the value already applied. Then every explicit route (a row tap, a web save, a re-assert, a screen change) still logs, and only the per pass repeat stops.

Check whether `:3108` and `:3236`, the two main brightness call sites, have the same shape before deciding where the state lives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the standby screen past the dim timeout, the brightness line is logged when the applied value changes and not on every UI pass.
- [ ] A capture of at least 300 seconds on the standby screen contains at most a handful of brightness lines, and the rate is stated beside the 3.69 a second measured here.
- [ ] `python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only display` passes, and `main_brightness_log_line` and `main_brightness_reassert_log` are named as passing.
- [ ] A row tap, a web save and a re-assert of an already applied value each still produce the line.
- [ ] The comment at `DefaultUI.cpp:189` still says what the line is for and now also says why the standby path is gated.
notes:
Implemented: gated the standby per-pass brightness call, not the log.

Changed only src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp and DefaultUI.h.
DefaultUI::setBrightness() keeps logging unconditionally (comment updated
to explain why). Added int standbyAppliedBrightness = -1 (DefaultUI.h),
reset to -1 at both places standbyEnterTime is set on entering standby
(DefaultUI.cpp init()'s bluetooth:connect handler, and
handleScreenChange()). The per-pass dim check in loop() now reads
settings.getStandbyBrightness() once, compares it to
standbyAppliedBrightness, and only calls setBrightness() (updating the
tracker) when they differ.

The two main-brightness call sites at the old :3108/:3236 line numbers
(now setBrightness(settings.getMainBrightness()) in init() and in
handleScreenChange()'s standby-exit branch) are one-shot, not per-pass, so
they were left alone. CatDisplay.cpp's two setBrightness call sites
(row edit and web-save reconcile) also call unconditionally, as before,
so main_brightness_log_line and main_brightness_reassert_log in
tools/settings_ui_tests/test_display.py are unaffected by this change.

Verified: `pio-locked run -e display-sim` and `-e display` both build
clean (SUCCESS, no new warnings; display build 5,744,591 bytes flash,
87.7%, within the pre-existing budget).

Left for the bench: the serial-rate re-measurement. Expected result:
on the standby screen past the dim timeout, at most one "Display:
brightness" line per actual value change (typically one line total
per standby visit, since the stored standby brightness rarely changes
mid-visit), down from the measured 3.69 lines/sec baseline in this
bead. Also left for the bench: running
`python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only display` to confirm
main_brightness_log_line and main_brightness_reassert_log still pass,
and a >=300s standby-screen serial capture to confirm the new rate.
close_reason: Gated the standby per-pass brightness call on an actual value change; setBrightness() itself still logs unconditionally so explicit routes (tap, web save, reassert) are unaffected.

title: Why the bench board's radio link degrades in place
description:
gm-t9ld established where the eight minute stall is: the board's own radio link degrades in place, minutes into a boot, and a reboot clears it. It did not establish why, and that is this bead.

## What is already settled, so nobody re-runs it

From gm-t9ld's closing notes, 2026-09-13, bench board, `display-loadtest`:

- Ping with a gateway control, back to back from the same host: 55% loss to the board, 0% to the gateway, 53% to the board again. Sustained at 20 to 60% for at least six more minutes.
- The board's own counters are healthy the whole time: `egress ok` every five seconds, zero LogicLoop overruns, 21.7 fps, normal UI pass times.
- The heap is unchanged: `int_free` 24,855 to 26,719, `int_largest` 15,348 to 15,860, `dma_free` 16,103 to 18,943, which are the same numbers a healthy window records.
- The serial log for the bad window carries no WiFi driver event at all. No roam, no disconnect, no reassociation, no softAP, no 4WAY_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, no FAILED ALLOC, no `wifi:m f null`. The association stays up.
- A reset with no flash cures it: same BSSID 14:91:82:a2:08:a1, rssi -55, then 0% loss and 0.18 to 0.20 s GETs for eight consecutive rounds.
- The esptool reset that begins every session is not the cause. The same command on the same board an hour earlier gave 15 clean minutes and 336 whole framebuffer reads.

So the cause is in the board's radio state and it leaves no log line.

## The candidates, and what would separate them

None of these has been tested. They are named because each one is reset by a reboot and none of them logs.

1. **Rate control settling on a rate the link cannot sustain.** The signature would be a low PHY rate with a high retry count while rssi stays put. `esp_wifi_sta_get_ap_info` gives rssi but not the negotiated rate; `esp_wifi_get_max_tx_power`, the rate control internals and the `wifi:` debug log level are the places to look.
2. **WiFi and BLE coexistence arbitration.** The board holds a BLE link to the controller. If coexistence starts starving WiFi slots, loss climbs with no WiFi event. Testing it needs a run with the BLE link down, which is a real configuration and easy to arrange.
3. **Modem sleep.** Listen interval and DTIM handling can leave a station missing frames. `esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_NONE)` for one soak is the cheap test.

The shape of a good experiment here is a long soak with the board pinged once a second from the host, so the onset is timestamped, plus whichever one knob is being varied. The onset time matters: six minutes in one case, more than fifteen in another, so it is not deterministic and one run proves little.

## Why this is worth doing rather than living with

Every device measurement in this repo runs over this link, and a sick board looks like a firmware fault. It cost gm-nov3.10 a wrong explanation (DRAM starvation), gm-t9ld a second wrong one (the framebuffer endpoint), and at least two sessions of measurement that had to be discarded. The three GET discriminator in CLAUDE.md detects it, which is enough to stop believing bad data, but it does not stop the board going sick in the middle of a long run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A soak with a once per second ping from the host reproduces the onset and timestamps it, at least twice, with the onset times recorded.
- [ ] Each of the three candidates is either ruled out with evidence or named as the cause, and the evidence is stated rather than inferred.
- [ ] If a knob prevents it (power save off, BLE down, a fixed rate), the cost of that knob is measured, not assumed: internal free, DMA free, and the web UI load time under two tabs.
- [ ] If the cause cannot be found, that is recorded plainly with what was ruled out, and the CLAUDE.md entry is updated to say so.
- [ ] Nothing in the production firmware changes on the strength of one board. The bench board is one radio in one place, and a fix that costs power or heap needs more than that.
notes:
2026-10-01 partial run, cut short by the pump incident (gm-warz). Bench board, display-loadtest built from idf5 at 94a0ffa6 (the /api/debug/wifi knob, commits 94a0ffa6 and ba8021f6), deployed over the air, fresh boot at 15:47, BSSID 14:91:82:a1:da:6f at rssi -76 on channel 11 (gm-t9ld saw a2:08:a1 at -55: the mesh roams), 802.11n, power save MIN_MODEM, BLE client connected to the real controller within seconds of boot (so the "BLE link" candidate is a live link here, not a scan).

Soak: tools in the session scratchpad (ping_soak.py: one ping a second to the board and to the gateway, one /api/debug/heap and /api/debug/wifi read every 30 s, per-minute windows).
- Phase A, defaults, 15:47 to 16:07 from boot: 19 windows, board loss 0% and gateway loss 0% in every one, board rtt median 61 to 74 ms. No onset.
- Phase B, esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_NONE) at run time (accepted: ps_rc 0, ps read back 0; the "aborts coex" note in Controller.cpp is about enable time, not a running link), 16:07 to 16:27: 20 windows, 0% and 0%, board rtt median 18 to 28 ms. No onset.
- Not run: the BLE-off phase (the knob with the link drop is built, ba8021f6, but was never deployed) and a second boot.

So the onset did not reproduce in 40 minutes on this boot, with or without modem sleep. Modem sleep costs about 45 ms of ping latency and nothing else visible. The earlier 6.8 day boot (astra-lineage loadtest, 2026-09-24 to 10-01) also pinged clean at 0% loss when sampled. Nothing is ruled in or out yet; the acceptance criteria stand.

One side observation worth a look: /api/debug/scanout on the idf5 loadtest boot read 31 resyncs in the first 20 minutes and 52 after 40, with slips 0, against 0 resyncs in 6.8 days on the previous build. The soak's own heap polls account for at most 2 of them (gm-jjb8: 0.04 per /api/debug/heap request). Candidates are the live BLE link (the previous boot's link state is unknown) or something in idf5; the BLE-off phase would have separated them.

title: Make the framework and LVGL patch scripts re-apply when their hunks change
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, oracle plan B1. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/.

## Findings
drivers F2, drivers F7

## Files
scripts/patch_esp_lcd_rgb.py, scripts/patch_lvgl_meter_inv.py, scripts/patch_flash_cache_flag.py

## Description
Every patch script decides "already patched" by finding its marker in the target, so a file patched by an older version of the script stays old. The meter patch's element hunks are an empty list and apply_hunks returns success for an empty list. The three scripts also disagree about where the IDF lives. Give each hunk a version stamp in the marker, compare the stamp, and re-apply from the .gm-orig copy when it differs. Write a .gm-orig for the esp_lcd patch, which has none. Resolve the IDF path one way, from PlatformIO's package directory, and log the resolved path.

## Acceptance
a build log line per patch says "applied vN" or "already vN"; deleting .pio/libdeps/display/lvgl and rebuilding produces byte-identical patched files to the ones the stamp claims; `grep -c gm-patch-v` on the vendored files matches the scripts.

## Test
bench. Rebuild -e display and -e display-loadtest, confirm the patched lv_meter.c and esp_lcd_panel_rgb.c match the scripts' current hunks, then re-run tools/dial_elem_check.py and a 5-minute tools/rig_soak.py at divider 6 and record whether any CLAUDE.md number moved.

## Related beads
none (gm-bzu epic is the home)

## Second oracle (Astra) notes, 2026-09-30
Oracle 2 (Astra) corrections. Do not trust an existing .gm-orig: it may already be patched, and restoring one script's baseline can erase another script's hunks in a shared file. Check a .gm-orig against a known pristine hash before using it, and fail the build on an unknown baseline. Remove the empty-hunk success path. Serialise patching of shared package files so two env builds cannot interleave writes. The installed tree is stale today: production lv_meter.c lacks the element guard and needle fix, and loadtest's lv_draw_sw_blend.c lacks the row tracking and opaque fill. Scope: the same versioned check must reach the other six scripts. This bead keeps its three files; split the rest into follow-ups that depend on it: (a) patch_lvgl_setpx_fast.py, patch_lvgl_label_elem.py, patch_lvgl_walkstat.py; (b) patch_asynctcp_backlog.py, patch_asyncws_erase_safe.py, patch_ble_scan_duty.py. Test fixtures: pristine, older version, current, and contaminated input for each script.
close_reason: Done in aba96750. New scripts/gm_patch.py: patched file is always rendered from a sha256-verified pristine copy (target or .gm-orig), one gm-patch-vN stamp line per patch set with a hunk digest, unknown baseline fails the build, empty hunk list is an error, target stamped by another script is refused, mkdir lock per target, IDF path from PlatformIO's package dir logged once. esp_lcd, flash cache flag and lv_meter scripts ported (all v1); meter's empty ELEM_HUNKS path and esp_lcd --revert-gaplog removed. Verified: scripts/test_gm_patch.py 14 tests pass (pristine, older, current, unstamped, contaminated gm-orig, unknown, foreign stamp, stale lock); -e display build log shows applied v1 on first run and already v1 on the next for all four patch sets; installed esp_lcd_panel_rgb.c (2 stamps), cache_utils.c (1), display lv_meter.c (1, now with element guard and needle fix) are byte-identical to patching a fresh pristine copy; the three files compile clean with production flags. The IDF .gm-orig copies match upstream v5.5.1 exactly. Full display link did not complete: HEAD fails on gm_record_inval_src from a stale hand-applied hunk in lv_obj_pos.c (label_elem territory, noted on gm-bzu.80), not on these files. Still needs the bench: display-loadtest rebuild, tools/dial_elem_check.py, 5 minute rig_soak at divider 6. Follow-ups gm-bzu.80 and gm-bzu.81 port the other six scripts.

title: Make allocation-failure monitoring nonblocking and allocation-free
description:
## Context
Review finding 3, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P1] Allocation-failure monitoring can deadlock on its own allocations.**

   Location: [memory_monitor.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/ESPMemoryMonitor/src/esp_memory_monitor/memory_monitor.cpp:657), [memory_monitor.h](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/ESPMemoryMonitor/src/esp_memory_monitor/memory_monitor.h:304).

   `sampleNow()` holds `_mutex` while growing history, building threshold vectors, and copying the public snapshot. The globally registered allocation-failure hook synchronously enters `handleAllocEvent()`, which takes the same non-recursive mutex with `portMAX_DELAY`. If any allocation made under that lock fails, the allocating task waits for a lock it already owns. Other allocation failures can subsequently block behind it. Failed-allocation reporting is enabled in the production configuration.

   Make this hook allocation-free and nonblocking: record a small event into preallocated storage and dispatch/log it later. Merely making the mutex recursive still leaves callback-copy allocation and reentrancy concerns. Add failure injection during a history/snapshot allocation.

## Steps to Reproduce
Enable failed-allocation events as production does. In a controlled test, inject allocation failure while sampleNow holds _mutex and grows history or copies its public snapshot. The synchronous heap hook enters handleAllocEvent and attempts xSemaphoreTake on that same non-recursive mutex. Assert the hook returns without waiting after the fix; this was source-traced, not fault-injected on a device during review.

## Acceptance Criteria
Failure reporting cannot take the monitor mutex or allocate; allocation failure during locked history/threshold/public-snapshot construction does not deadlock; reporting still records an event without recursive callback allocation.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Failure reporting cannot take the monitor mutex or allocate; allocation failure during locked history/threshold/public-snapshot construction does not deadlock; reporting still records an event without recursive callback allocation.
notes: Fixed in 43e6c43f (worktree branch, merged into idf5). ESPMemoryMonitor::handleAllocEvent no longer takes _mutex or calls the user callback inside the failing allocation. It records the event into a fixed 8-slot lock-free ring (CAS-claimed slot, per-slot sequence publish, multi-producer safe), counts overflow in failedAllocDropped() and totals in failedAllocCount(). sampleNow() drains the ring outside the lock and invokes the callback on the sampler task, at most sampleIntervalMs later. Ring reset on deinit after the hook is unregistered. CHANGELOG Unreleased/Fixed updated. Verified: display-loadtest and display-sim build. No device repro of the deadlock exists; the app callback only logs so deferred delivery is acceptable.

title: Release the frame gate on a mid-frame stop and make teardown wait for the render task
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, oracle plan B11. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/.

## Findings
render F1, render F4, render F9

## Files
src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp, src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.h

## Description
When running goes false inside the band loop, the gate taken on the first band is never given, and finishStop calls endDirectPath after a fixed wait whether the render task has parked or not. Give the gate on every exit from renderFrame, make finishStop wait for the parked flags with the 500 ms as the error path rather than the normal one, and have start() refuse to create a second push task while pushStopped is false.

## Acceptance
ten animoff/on cycles on the bench log no gate timeout and no "stop not confirmed"; the whole-frame path never presents a partial frame after a stop.

## Test
bench, `/api/debug/anim?animoff=1` toggled 20 times with lv_flip_timeouts and the gate counters read before and after.

## Second oracle (Astra) notes, 2026-09-30
Astra rates render F4 high: finishStop must confirm that render, push and every band DMA completion have stopped before it frees anything or lets LVGL take the buffers. A timeout must not authorise reclamation; on timeout keep the resources and quarantine, as animStopPending does.
notes:
Commits e414456f and 955c0ddc (the second fixes the definition's return type; amend was not allowed). Files: src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp and SleepAnimation.h.

What changed: renderFrame() returns bool. When running goes false between bands it drains the submitted bands (200 ms bound) and gives the framebuffer gate itself; the push-stall exit and the init-failure exit also return false. renderLoop never presents a frame that returned false, and breaks at once when stopping. The render task calls endDirectPath() after its loop, before taskEntry sets stopped, so the direct path is torn down on the task and core that own it. finishStop() waits for stopped, then wakes and waits for pushStopped (500 ms each, the error bound), reaps parked tasks, and confirms through stopConfirmed(). It no longer calls endDirectPath() or gives the gate: on a timeout nothing is torn down and stop() returns false, so DefaultUI's animStopPending quarantine applies. start() also refuses while pushStopped is false.

Counters: file statics in SleepAnimation.cpp with public accessors, so the class layout is unchanged (no new members). stopGateEarlyGives(), stopFramesAborted(), stopWaitUsLast(), stopWaitUsMax(), stopTimeouts(); the sim stub returns 0. They are NOT yet on /api/debug/anim: that JSON is built in src/display/plugins/WebUIPluginDebug.cpp, outside this bead's files. Suggested keys for the leader: stop_gate_gives, stop_frames_aborted, stop_wait_us, stop_wait_us_max, stop_timeouts.

Verified: -e display, -e display-loadtest and -e display-sim build (display RAM 98,464 B). Reasoned from code, not measured: the old failure was presentFrame() blocking on the self-held gate with portMAX_DELAY until finishStop's forced give after 500 ms, then flipping the partial frame.

Left for the bench (board not touched): on a display-loadtest build, read /api/debug/anim for lv_flip_timeouts (and the new counters once wired), toggle animoff=1 then animoff=0 twenty times with a few seconds between, read again. Expect no 'stop unconfirmed' and no gate timeout in the serial log, lv_flip_timeouts unchanged, stop_timeouts 0, stop_wait_us_max well under 500000 (about one frame), and stop_frames_aborted equal to stop_gate_gives on the whole-frame path. Pin interlace=1 for one pass and 0 for another, since the bench board stores bgAnimInterlace 0.

Agent-mail was unreachable (health endpoint gave no answer), so no file reservation was taken; the leader had reserved these files.
close_reason: Gate given on every early exit from renderFrame, partial frames never presented, render task tears down the direct path, finishStop quarantines on timeout; builds pass, bench toggle test pending

title: Recover from a render self-stop and from a flip timeout without a restart
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, oracle plan B12. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/.

## Findings
render F2, render F3, render F7, render F10, render F11, render F13

## Files
src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp, src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp

## Description
An init failure in renderFrame sets running false and leaves dmaActive set, so the panel is not handed back until a screen change ends the 3 s quarantine. A presentFrame timeout stores -1 in scanFb and the interlaced path then writes the hidden buffer forever, because requestWholeFrames has no caller. Route the self-stop through finishStop, call requestWholeFrames from DefaultUI on the timeout counter, and take the small fixes in the same file: atomic decrement for the warm-up counters, free layers released while stopped, guard overlayPixels against -1, and delete the dead pairMode branch.

## Acceptance
a forced init failure (debug knob) hands the panel back within one UI pass; after a forced flip timeout the next two frames are whole and lv_flip_timeouts stops climbing.

## Test
bench, with the two debug knobs added for this bead.

## Second oracle (Astra) notes, 2026-09-30
Astra corrections. render F7: a compare-exchange on the warm-up counter has an ABA case when a new request writes the same value; use a request generation that the render task acknowledges. render F3: calling requestWholeFrames on the timeout counter is not enough by itself; treat scanFb as unknown until a whole frame has been presented and a flip confirmed, and only then resume the interlaced path.
notes:
Commits 2c93727d (SleepAnimation.cpp/.h, WebUIPluginDebug.cpp) and f422a1ca (DefaultUI.cpp).

What changed:
- Self-stop (render F2): an init() failure sets a file-static self-stop flag (selfStopped(), selfStopCount()) before running goes false. The render task wakes the push task after endDirectPath() on loop exit. stop() on a self-stopped run calls finishStop(), which waits for both workers; any other !running state still only reads stopConfirmed(), so a quarantined stop does not block the UI task again. DefaultUI::loop, after the animStopPending check: if !isActive() && selfStopped(), call stopSleepAnimation() (un-suppresses LVGL when confirmed, quarantines otherwise) and arm lastSleepAnimAttempt. start() and stop() clear the flag.
- Flip timeout (render F3, Astra correction): directInterlacedFrame now also needs scanFb >= 0 (or fbCount < 2). While scanFb is unknown the frame renders whole and flips; the first confirmed flip grounds scanFb and interlacing resumes. The timeout path also calls requestWholeFrames(). start() resets scanFb to -1. renderFrame latches one interlace decision per frame, and a frame that will flip (direct path, two buffers, not directInterlacedFrame) never interlaces a band. The bead asked DefaultUI to call requestWholeFrames on the timeout counter; presentFrame does it itself instead, because the render task sees the timeout first and a UI-pass-late request would let interlaced frames through.
- Warm-up counters (render F7, Astra correction): no compare-exchange on absolute values. requestWholeFrames() does fetch_or(kWarmReq), requestBandWarmup() does fetch_or(kBandWarmReq). The render task acknowledges the bit with a compare-exchange (whole frame: at the top of renderLoop, count = max(count, 2); per band: at the band's visit, count = 1 after this frame) and owns the countdown. The UI task only ever sets a bit, so there is no ABA: a failed exchange means a new request, which the retry takes.
- Layers (render F10): freeReleasedLayer()/sweepReleasedLayers() (new private member functions, no new data members). layerRelease() frees at once when !running && stopped; finishStop() sweeps when the render task has parked.
- overlayPixels()/overlayPixelRows() return 0 while overlayFront is -1 (render F11).
- Dead code (render F13): pairMode, the half-resolution splitRender path, 2-row groups and push mode 2 in pushLoop are removed; nothingOwnedThisBand stays as a guard with its comment rewritten. The other two comments F13 names (bench-only aligned alloc at the msync, BAND_H 8-row comment in SleepAnimationInternal.h, directPushOn header comment) were NOT rewritten.
- Layout: no new data members in SleepAnimation. New state is file statics (s_selfStop, s_selfStops, s_scanUnknownFrames; s_forceInitFail and s_forceFlipTimeout only under GM_ANIM_FAULT_KNOBS). Two static constexpr members (kWarmReq, kBandWarmReq). Production RAM 98,464 to 98,480 B.

/api/debug/anim: knobs failinit=1 and fliptimeout=1 inside GM_DEBUG_WRITE_ROUTES (one-shot; the SleepAnimation side compiles them only where GM_TOUCH_PROBE, GM_KBLOB, GM_BLEND_PROBE, GM_ANIM_BENCH or GM_SYNTH_HANDSHAKE is set).
