title: Keep an empty-string settings write dirty when NVS fails
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B44, N1. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
N1

## Files
src/display/core/Property.h, src/display/core/Settings.cpp

## Description
Property.h treats every empty-string write as a success, because it infers success from the byte count and an empty value writes zero bytes. Property::store then clears the dirty flag. If NVS fails on that write or on the commit, the UI reports success, the property stops retrying, and the old value comes back after a reboot. This breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that a failed NVS write is reported. Use the status-returning NVS calls and keep the property dirty until both the set and the commit succeed. Keep an explicit empty value distinct from a missing key.

## Acceptance
An empty string or empty serialised list whose set or commit fails stays dirty, is retried, and makes Settings::flushNow() return false.

## Test
Host test with an injected set failure and commit failure, for empty and non-empty values; check dirty state, retry and the value after a simulated reboot. GM_SIM_FAIL_FLUSH on the simulator for the Restart row.
close_reason: c63c1a35: nvsPutString uses nvs_set_str + nvs_commit on the Preferences handle (member-pointer access to the protected _handle/_started), so a failed empty-string or empty-list write stays dirty, is retried and makes flushNow() return false. Sim shim path verifies by read-back. Host test against the sim Preferences shim (scratchpad, injected read-only failure): new code PASS, old Property.h fails the 7 empty-value checks. Settings.cpp cross-compiled with display flags, references nvs_set_str/nvs_commit. Commit-only failure has no injection point on the host; covered by reading. Settings.h flushNow() comment still states the old known limit (gm-bzu.45 owns that file). Schedule list keeps reading "" as default (pre-refactor firmware stored "").

title: Report a failed settings save to the browser
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B45, N2; web F5. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
N2, web F5

## Files
src/display/core/Settings.cpp, src/display/plugins/WebUIPlugin.cpp, web/src/pages/Settings/index.jsx

## Description
Settings.cpp:137-140 drops doSave()'s result, and the web settings handler (WebUIPlugin.cpp around 1473) then answers with success. A save that failed to persist looks saved in the browser and is lost on reboot. Use the status-returning flush, send a failure response when it fails, and make the form keep the unsaved values and show the error. In the same change, run the save response through transformFetchedSettings, as the load path does (web F5). gm-nov3.26 is the same response channel for a malformed field; use one error shape for both.

## Acceptance
An injected flush failure gives a non-2xx response and a visible error, and the form keeps the edited values. A successful save shows the same normalised values as a fresh load.

## Test
Simulator with GM_SIM_FAIL_FLUSH=1 and a browser save; API fixture for the response shape.
close_reason: ef048184. The settings POST saves with flushNow() and answers 500 {error, code: persist_failed} when NVS fails, skipping a requested restart. The form keeps its edits, shows the error with Retry, and routes a success through transformFetchedSettings plus the schedule parser. Verified: display and display-sim build; simulator with GM_SIM_FAIL_FLUSH=1 gave 500 on the first POST and 200 on the second, with the value applied; web lint and build pass. The form's error banner was not exercised in a browser.

title: Keep the shot index sorted after an id reset and serve index.bin from one snapshot
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B39, B43. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
webplugin F11, webplugin F12 (header and length)

## Files
src/display/plugins/ShotHistoryPlugin.cpp, src/display/plugins/ShotHistoryPlugin.h, src/display/plugins/WebUIPlugin.cpp

## Description
findEntryPosition binary-searches the index, and only rebuildIndex keeps it sorted. Settings::historyIndex is raised to the SD card's highest id only inside rebuild (ShotHistoryPlugin.cpp:1165), so after an NVS reset with the SD history kept, new shots get low ids, appends break the order and lookups miss. Raise historyIndex to the index's highest id at startup, and refuse or re-sort an append whose id is not above the last entry. Also build the index.bin response's length header and body from one snapshot, so a concurrent append cannot make them disagree.

## Acceptance
After historyIndex is reset to 0 with shots on the card, the next shot id is above every existing id and every shot is found by id. index.bin's Content-Length always equals the bytes sent.

## Test
Simulator or bench: seed a card, reset the NVS key, record a shot, then look up old and new ids. Fetch index.bin while a shot is being appended.
close_reason: Done in e20daffd (ShotHistoryPlugin only). historyIndex is raised above every index id once per boot (syncNextIdWithIndex, on the history loop task and again before a shot id is chosen); an out-of-order append or index sets indexOrderBroken and binary-search misses fall back to a linear scan until a rebuild; rebuild now sets historyIndex to max id + 1 (it set it equal, so the next shot reused that id); every index read and write takes one recursive index lock. OPEN FOLLOW-UP for WebUIPlugin.cpp (held by gm-bzu.64): the history worker still serves index.bin by fopen+fstat+chunked reads, so Content-Length and body can disagree with a concurrent append. Change the worker's index.bin case to call ShotHistory.snapshotIndex(&buf, &len), serve buf with Content-Length len from memory, and free(buf) when the response is done. The snapshot is 32 + 128 x entryCount bytes of PSRAM (about 384 KB at 3,000 shots). Verified: pio run -e display and -e display-sim compile clean. Not verified: no scripted sim case (no hook to reset NVS mid-run) and no bench run; bench acceptance (seed card, reset NVS key, record, look up old and new ids) is still open.

title: Clamp a stored theme mode before the Animation page indexes its labels
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B29. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
settings F7

## Files
src/display/ui/default/settings/CatAnimation.cpp, src/display/core/Settings.cpp

## Description
The web handler stores themeMode from toInt() with no range check (WebUIPlugin.cpp:1397, Settings.cpp:335). CatAnimation copies it at enter (line 610) and indexes kThemeModeLabels with it (line 497), so a POST with themeMode=5 reads a pointer past the table and can crash. Clamp in setThemeMode and clamp again at enter and reconcile, the way bgAnimId is clamped in the same file.

## Acceptance
A stored themeMode of -1, 2 or 99 opens the Animation page showing Dark and does not read outside the table.

## Test
Simulator: store each bad value through the settings API, open the Animation category and step the theme row.
notes: c050fba3: setThemeMode stores anything but 1 as 0; Settings::load repairs a stored value outside 0..1 (set(), so it is written back); CatAnimation clamps at enter and reconcile (clampThemeMode). Found on the way: a stored theme of -1 segfaulted the simulator at boot (DefaultUI::applyTheme indexes with it), which the load repair fixes. Verified on the simulator (scratch script, not committed): stored -1, 2, 99 each boot, open the Animation page on Dark, step Dark->Light->Dark; a web save of each is stored as 0 and shows Dark. With the load repair disabled, stored 2 and 99 still show Dark and step correctly, so the page clamp holds alone. Builds: display-sim and display pass. Bench: nothing device-specific; the Amoled THEME_ID_AMOLED_DARK override only triggers on 0, unchanged.
close_reason: themeMode clamped in setter, at load and in CatAnimation; verified on simulator

title: Keep a reconnect's full control resend from being lost
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B51. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
core F9

## Files
src/display/core/Controller.cpp, src/display/core/Controller.h

## Description
The BLE connect callback sets controlStateSent to false to force a full resend (Controller.cpp:393). updateControl sends deltas and then sets it true at line 1472. A connect that lands between the send and that line loses the reset, and the controller, which starts with no state, gets no boiler setpoint until something changes. Replace the flag with a connection generation that the callback increments and updateControl records after a full send.

## Acceptance
A reconnect at any point in updateControl is followed by a full four-part control batch on the new link.

## Test
Loadtest or fake-controller build: force reconnects in a tight loop and check the first control frame after each connect.
close_reason: 56e4dc82: the connect callback bumps an atomic connectionGen; updateControl reads it once before the batch, records it in controlSentGen after the send, and sends all four parts whenever they differ. A connect during the send leaves a newer generation, so the next pass resends in full. display build passes. Bench acceptance (forced reconnect loop on a loadtest or fake-controller build, check first control frame after each connect) not run.

title: Never initialise the panel on the caller's core
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B52. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
core F7

## Files
src/display/core/Controller.cpp

## Description
When the pinned panel_init task cannot be created, setupPanel calls driver->init() on the caller's task (Controller.cpp:342), which runs on core 0. That puts the LCD and DMA interrupts on the BLE core, the hardware invariant CLAUDE.md says must not break, and the 'panel init on core' tripwire line is not printed. Retry the pinned task a few times, then log an error with the core and fail visibly instead of initialising in place.

## Acceptance
With task creation forced to fail, the panel is never initialised on core 0 and the log names the failure.

## Test
Inject xTaskCreatePinnedToCore failure in a loadtest build and read the boot log.
notes: 2026-10-01 (b09ea631): setupPanel no longer falls back to driver->init() on the caller's task. It tries the core 1 panel_init task 5 times, 100 ms apart, logging ESP_LOGE with internal free and largest block per failure. After the last failure it logs 'panel NOT initialised: no core 1 task after 5 attempts; refusing to init on caller core N; restarting in 5 s', keeps the cached panel model in NVS, waits 5 s and calls ESP.restart(). Choice: reboot rather than continue setup without a panel, because DefaultUI::init and web handlers (getUI()) dereference the UI and driver, and a heap that cannot give an 8 KB internal stack cannot start WiFi or BLE either, so the web UI would not come up to diagnose it. Visibility is the error line plus the software-restart reset reason on the next boot. A deterministic boot-time heap shortage will boot-loop; that is visible and preferable to the core 0 regression. Verified: pio run -e display and -e display-sim both SUCCESS (the sim takes its own branch). Not verified, left for the bench: the injection test. Build display-loadtest with PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS=-DGM_INJECT_PANEL_TASK_FAIL (honoured only under GM_TOUCH_PROBE), flash, read the boot log for five 'panel_init task create failed' lines, the 'panel NOT initialised' line, no 'panel init on core' line, and a restart. The injection branch was read, not compiled; it may warn that ctx is unused. Rebuild the loadtest env without the flag afterwards.
close_reason: setupPanel retries the core 1 init task and reboots with an error log instead of initialising on core 0

title: Keep the held press target across unrelated hit-map changes, and end injected drags at their endpoint
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B31. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
elements F4, elements F9

## Files
src/display/ui/default/TouchTask.cpp, src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp, src/display/core/TouchInject.cpp

## Description
The touch task clears a held plate whenever the hit map's generation moves, and the generation moves on any rect change, not only a screen change. collectHitRects also drops the topmost targets past 96. TouchInject ends a scripted drag at the last pressed sample instead of (x2, y2), which the header promises and Rig.swipe relies on. Keep the held target while its own rect is unchanged, drop the lowest targets first on overflow, and release injected drags at their endpoint.

## Acceptance
A hold survives an unrelated widget moving. /api/debug/tap with x2 and y2 releases at x2, y2.

## Test
Simulator: hold a row while a label changes size; scripted swipe with a framebuffer or touchmap read of the release point.
notes: Commits b4176f82 and 1b1535df (swarm-69). (1) TouchTask: a synthetic release keeps the injected point, so a drag through /api/debug/tap ends at (x2, y2); a real release still keeps the last pressed point. (2) TouchTask: when the hit map's generation moves under a held plate, the task looks up the held object (HitRect.id, the object address, new field; HitRect is now 24 bytes with an explicit reserved field and a static_assert, still memcmp-safe) and keeps the plate while that object has the same hit and object boxes and plates are on; otherwise it clears it. (3) DefaultUI::collectHitRects fills a ring of 96 and publishTouchHitMap rotates it, so past the cap the lowest targets in z order are dropped, never the topmost. Verified: -e display, -e display-sim and -e display-loadtest build; python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only press,rig PASS on the simulator (press 108 checks including the Fixture edge swipes through Rig.swipe, rig 19 checks). Not verifiable on the simulator: TouchTask is stubbed there, its mouse path already took TouchInject's release at (x2, y2), and it writes no touch log. Left for the bench (display-loadtest; nothing was flashed): (a) drag: GET /api/debug/tap?x=100&y=240&x2=380&y2=240&ms=20, then /api/debug/touchlog: the release entry must read x=380 y=240. Use ms=20, not 250: the task polls every 5 ms, so at 250 ms the last pressed sample is within about 6 px of x2 and old and new code look the same; at 20 ms the old code released near x=310. (b) hold: on the brew screen with the synthetic brew running and plates on, GET /api/debug/tap?x=<centre of a plate target>&y=..&ms=3000, read hitmap_gen from /api/debug/anim twice during the hold, and if it moved, a /api/debug/fb read mid-hold must still show the plate. Agent-mail was unreachable (health check returned nothing), so no file reservations were taken; the leader had assigned the files.
close_reason: Held plate follows its own object across hit-map changes, overflow drops lowest targets, injected drags release at x2,y2 (b4176f82, 1b1535df)

title: Preserve recoverable profiles and notes when replacement fails
description:
## Context
Review finding 7, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] A failed replacement rename deletes both versions of a profile or notes file.**

   Location: [ProfileManager.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/core/ProfileManager.cpp:221), [ShotHistoryPlugin.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/plugins/ShotHistoryPlugin.cpp:682).

   The new temporary-file path protects against short writes, but removes the original before renaming the completed temporary file. If that rename fails, the error branch removes the temporary file too: neither version survives. A power cut between remove and rename leaves only `.tmp`; profile enumeration deliberately ignores it and there is no startup recovery. The comment calling it recoverable does not supply a recovery path.

   Use overwrite-rename where the filesystem supports it. For FAT, retain a backup and implement rollback/startup recovery. At minimum, preserve the completed temporary file after a failed commit. Inject rename failure after successful serialization and check that a recoverable complete version remains.

## Steps to Reproduce
Save an existing profile/notes file through a filesystem double. Allow complete temporary serialization and removal of the target, then fail rename(tmp,target). Observe cleanup also removes tmp and no complete version remains. Separately simulate power loss between target removal and rename and restart the loader.

## Acceptance Criteria
Short writes and failed rename leave at least one complete recoverable version; FAT uses rollback/startup recovery and LittleFS uses suitable atomic replacement; power interruption at each commit phase recovers deterministically; failed saves do not announce success.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Short writes and failed rename leave at least one complete recoverable version; FAT uses rollback/startup recovery and LittleFS uses suitable atomic replacement; power interruption at each commit phase recovers deterministically; failed saves do not announce success.
notes:
Fixed on the worktree branch (commit 'storage: keep the old profile or notes file until the new one is in place'), merged into idf5. New src/display/util/SafeReplace.{h,cpp}: commitReplace renames target to .bak, .tmp to target, drops .bak; a failed rename rolls the .bak back and keeps the complete .tmp. recoverReplace runs at ProfileManager::setup (profile dir) and ShotHistoryPlugin::setup (/h) and settles leftovers: .bak+target drops .bak; .bak+.tmp promotes .tmp; .bak alone rolls back; .tmp+target drops .tmp; .tmp alone is promoted only if it parses as JSON. Both filesystems (LittleFS, SD FAT) use the same path, so FAT's refusal to rename onto an existing name is handled without a special case.

Checked on display-sim by planting six leftover shapes in sim_data/littlefs/p and booting: every case resolved as the table says; promoted files carried the .tmp content. display-sim and display-loadtest build. A failing rename was not injected (no filesystem double exists); the branch is verified by reading.

title: Refresh icon and marquee sprites on a theme change, and stop press states counting as blinks
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B24. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
defaultui F7, defaultui F8

## Files
src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp

## Description
applyTheme releases no layer, so icon and marquee sprites keep the old colours until their state or text changes. scanIcons counts every lv_obj_get_state change, so one press and release counts as two toggles and takes an icon into layer ownership. Release icon and marquee layers on a theme change, and ignore PRESSED and FOCUSED bits when counting blinks.

## Acceptance
A theme change repaints owned icons and marquees in the new colours on the next pass. Pressing a static icon twice does not make it a layer.

## Test
Simulator frame captures across a theme change; icon_layers on /api/debug/anim after repeated presses.
notes:
Commit a328c327 (DefaultUI.cpp only).

Changed:
- applyTheme releases every icon layer and marquee (releaseIconLayers, releaseMarquees) after change_color_theme, inside the theme-changed branch. The release clears USER_2/USER_3 and invalidates under the new style. A blinking icon keeps its candidate toggle count and a marquee is always eligible, so both are taken again on the next pass with sprites in the new colours.
- scanIcons masks LV_STATE_PRESSED, LV_STATE_FOCUSED and LV_STATE_FOCUS_KEY before comparing states, so a press and release is no longer two toggles. The owned-sprite lookup in serviceIconLayers still keys on the full state (pixel-correct: a press on an owned blinking icon is a third state and hands it back to LVGL, as before).

Verified: -e display-sim, -e display (RAM 98,608 B, unchanged) and -e display-loadtest build. Simulator: python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only rig,animation --skip-restart: PASS, 70 checks, including theme_recolor (framebuffer pixels on the Animation page change on a Dark/Light flip and the mode restores). Report in scratchpad b70/report.json. The simulator compiles the layer code out (GAGGIMATE_SIM), so no icon or marquee was ever owned there; the release and the press masking were checked by reading only.

Left for the bench (display-loadtest, all-screens on, interlace=1 pinned):
1. Theme repaint: go to the brew screen with synthetic brew on and wait until icon_layers on /api/debug/anim lists the temperature icon as owned. Flip Theme in the Animation category (or the web UI), return to brew, and sample the icon box through /api/debug/fb (tools/icon_layer_check.py): both blink colours should be the new theme's, and icon_layers should show the icon owned again within a second.
2. Marquee: info screen, marquee_layers lists obj27/obj29; flip theme; the scrolling text should be in the new colour and marquee_layers repopulated on the next pass.
3. Press: on a screen with a static clickable image (a menu tile icon or a chevron that is lv_img), tap it 5 times with /api/debug/tap at 300 ms spacing without leaving the screen (or a target that does not navigate). icon_layers must stay without that object.
close_reason: Theme change releases icon and marquee sprites; press and focus states no longer count as blinks (a328c327)

title: Give each palette build one complete theme generation
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B33. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
bganim F6

## Files
src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimCommon.cpp, src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimCommon.h

## Description
themeRGB reads g_themeGen on every call (BgAnimCommon.cpp:487), and g_themeGen is a plain volatile. A palette build on the render task can mix two generations, and two publishes in a row rewrite the buffer the render task is reading. Snapshot the generation once per palette build and read stops, count and positions from that buffer only; publish with release and read with acquire; and do not reuse a buffer until the render task has acknowledged the newer generation.

## Acceptance
Rapid theme changes never leave a palette that matches neither theme.

## Test
Host test that alternates two very different themes while a palette is built, checking each result matches one theme; tools/animbench goldens unchanged.
close_reason: Triple buffer with atomic exchange; reads hold one theme from first read to next themeGen(); themeGen() reports an out-of-band value when a theme arrived during held reads. Commit 773786a4. Host test tools/animbench/theme_gen_check.cpp: 200k builds under a writer alternating two themes, 0 mixed (old code 169,942 mixed). Goldens, interlace, lifecycle unchanged; pio run -e display SUCCESS.

title: Snapshot draw-profile labels on the UI task before the report reads them
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B15. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

src/display/ui/default/DrawProfile.cpp, src/display/ui/default/DrawProfile.h

## Description
The drawprof report handler reads LVGL objects from async_tcp (DrawProfile.cpp:201-204). A screen change during a report can free them. Only loadtest and sim builds have it, but it can corrupt the bench build the numbers come from. title: Give the memory monitor's event ring one consumer and rename the shutdown hook
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B54. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
libs F7, libs F13

## Files
lib/ESPMemoryMonitor/src/esp_memory_monitor/memory_monitor.cpp, lib/ESPMemoryMonitor/src/esp_memory_monitor/memory_monitor.h, src/display/plugins/WebUIPlugin.cpp

## Description
drainAllocEvents is written for one consumer, but both the monitor task and the web server drain it, so events can be lost or read twice. registerPanicHandler uses esp_register_shutdown_handler, which a panic does not call. Let only the monitor task drain the ring and give the web path a copied snapshot; rename the hook to say it runs on shutdown only.

## Acceptance
Concurrent web reads and periodic sampling report each allocation failure once. No code or doc claims panic coverage.

## Test
Loadtest build: generate allocation failures while polling the heap endpoint; compare counts.
notes: gm-bzu.73 (fa40f868): The web paths (/api/debug/heap, OTA status push) now call the new read-only snapshotNow(), which takes no history entry, fires no callback and never touches the alloc ring. sampleNow() drains the ring only on the sampler task while the sampler runs. drainAllocEvents holds an atomic flag, so a second concurrent caller skips the pass and leaves the events for the next one. installPanicHook is renamed installShutdownHook (ShutdownCallback), with the log line, README, CHANGELOG, sim stub and utils.h comment all saying it runs on esp_restart() only. Verified: display-sim and display both build, and the sim binary exports snapshotNow and installShutdownHook. Not done: no host test of the ring, because memory_monitor.cpp needs Arduino.h, heap_caps and FreeRTOS and has no off-target build. Left for the bench: the loadtest test (make allocations fail while polling /api/debug/heap and check that each FAILED ALLOC line appears once and matches failedAllocCount). Agent-mail was down, so no file reservations were taken.
close_reason: Web reads use a read-only snapshot, the ring has one consumer, and the shutdown hook no longer claims panic coverage (fa40f868)

title: Make kb.py, elf_func_diff and the core-dump analyser fail on a mismatch or a foreign ELF
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B10, B11. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
tools F10, tools F11, tools F16

## Files
tools/kblob/kb.py, tools/elf_func_diff.py, scripts/analyze_coredump.py

## Description
kb.py prints MISMATCH and LEAK and still exits 0 (kb.py:442-473). elf_func_diff --loose cuts everything after a function's last return and folds struct offsets, and the gm-bzu.19 proof in CLAUDE.md used --loose. analyze_coredump.py never checks that the ELF matches the dump. Make kb.py exit non-zero on a rejected start, a mismatch or a leak, and refuse to run when the linked ELF's sha or the ABI headers it lists changed since the firmware build. Keep code after the last return in --loose and fold only relocation noise. Refuse to symbolise a dump whose ELF sha differs.

## Acceptance
Each of MISMATCH, LEAK and a rejected start returns non-zero. A changed struct offset or a changed block after the last return shows in --loose. A mismatched ELF is refused.

## Test
Synthetic objdump pairs for elf_func_diff; recorded kb.py responses; one matched and one mismatched core dump.
close_reason: Fixed in commit d160790d. kb.py bench()/print_bench() now exit 1 with a 'kb: FAIL: ...' line on a rejected init(), a pixel MISMATCH, or a hot-slab LEAK. tools/elf_func_diff.py --loose now truncates each function to its ELF-linked size (nm -S) instead of guessing from 'the last return', and only folds a literal offset into a linker-assigned label, never a named symbol; strict mode is unchanged. scripts/analyze_coredump.py now compares the crashed device's versions.displayVersion against the same BUILD_GIT_VERSION-shaped string embedded in the candidate ELF and refuses to run GDB on a mismatch unless --force. Verified host-only with unit tests and synthetic objdump/nm/core-dump fixtures; no PlatformIO build, no board access.

title: Take xtensa-asm14.sh's compiler and flags from the firmware build
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B12. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings
tools F15

## Files
tools/animbench/xtensa-asm14.sh

## Description
xtensa-asm14.sh compiles through a shim with no firmware defines, so GM_ANIM_IRAM is empty and the output is not what the firmware builds. CLAUDE.md says it uses the firmware build's flags and toolchain. Take the compile command for the named source from the env's compile_commands.json, fail when it is missing or older than the source, and print the command used next to the listing.

## Acceptance
The listing for a kernel matches the instructions of the same function in the firmware ELF.

## Test
Compare one kernel's output with objdump of the display-loadtest ELF.

title: Retry a busy history response in the web client
description:
Source: idf5 branch review 2026-09-27, second oracle (Astra) plan astra B57. Report: https://claude.ai/artifact/MsBaAWV76x5z4Q6St3JWMj ; raw files in .claude/scratch-oracle/branch-review-2026-09-27/ (astra.md, reconcile.json).

## Findings

## Files
web/src/services/historyFetch.js (new), web/src/pages/ShotHistory/index.jsx, web/src/pages/ShotAnalyzer/services/LibraryService.js

## Description
The history worker answers 503 when its queue of eight is full, and every web caller treats that as a final failure, so a Home load with a second tab open can drop shots from the list. Add one fetch helper that retries a 503 with bounded backoff, honours Retry-After when present, stops when the view is cancelled, and passes other errors through. Use it in ShotHistory and LibraryService.

## Test

fetchHistoryWithRetry(input, init, options): retries a 503 up to 4 attempts
(default backoff 500ms/1s/2s, last entry repeats), honours a Retry-After
header (seconds) over the configured backoff, aborts immediately (rejects
with AbortError) if init.signal fires either before or during a retry wait,
and returns any non-503 response (success or a permanent error) unchanged on
the first attempt. Wired into ShotHistory/index.jsx (index.bin load and the
per-shot .slog load-on-demand) and LibraryService.js (getGaggiMateShots and
loadShot). For gm-bzu.77: import fetchHistoryWithRetry from

have such calls today.

Verified: npm run lint:check (0 errors, 6 pre-existing unrelated warnings),
npm run build (succeeds), and node --test src/services/historyFetch.test.js
(7/7 passing: immediate success, 503-then-200 retry, Retry-After honoured
over backoff, retries exhausted returns the last 503 for the caller's
existing !response.ok check, non-503 passed through untouched, abort
mid-retry, and abort before the first retry).

title: Ripples kernel differs by 1 ULP under GCC 14 -O2 in the QEMU harness
description:
Found by gm-bzu.35. Building the QEMU tests with the firmware toolchain (toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf, GCC 14, -O2) instead of the 2021r2 toolchain at -O1 gives bit-exact results for 13 of 14 kernels; anim_ripples shows a 1-ULP float mismatch in 6 lanes that the old toolchain does not show. Likely FP contraction or a libm sqrtf codegen difference. Decide whether the reference or the kernel is at fault, then switch build.sh's default to the firmware toolchain so the harness tests what ships. Details in tools/qemubench/README.md (gm-bzu.35 section).

## Acceptance
build.sh defaults to the firmware toolchain and all 14 anim tests pass, or the README records why ripples is exempt and how much it differs.
notes: Cause: the C reference moved, not the kernel. GCC's default -ffp-contract=fast fuses the reference's 'hAccBuf[x] += amp*cos*env' into one madd.s at -O2 (single rounding); accumulateBandAsm rounds after mul.s and add.s. GCC 8 -O1 never fused (needs -fexpensive-optimizations). Proof: -S under GCC 14 -O2 shows 1 madd.s in the inlined reference, 0 with -ffp-contract=off; built without the flag the test fails with 6 lanes (case 0: 3, case 3: 3), each 1 ULP either way (0x3ef8649e vs 0x3ef8649f, 0x3e95092c vs 0x3e95092b); with it, PASS. Change (10e346b5): build.sh defaults to toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf GCC 14.2 -O2 native binaries, GM_QEMUBENCH_TOOLCHAIN=2021r2 keeps GCC 8.4 -O1 via cmd.exe; -ffp-contract=off on all tests; README section added. Results firmware toolchain: PASS anim_aurora, caustics, ember, fireflies, lava, mandala, nebula, orbits, plasma, ripples, silk, silk2, starfield, steam, blend_row. 2021r2 path: PASS ripples, fireflies, blend_row. Production finding: display ELF ripples bandRef has madd.s f0,f4,f1 at 0x4207910e, so band() vs bandRef() on device can differ by 1 ULP before RGB565 packing; follow-up gm-bzu.83.
close_reason: Reference fused madd.s at -O2; harness now builds with firmware GCC 14 -O2 and -ffp-contract=off, all 15 tests pass

title: Propagate controller installation failure to the overall OTA result
description:
## Context
Review finding 8, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] Controller installation failures still produce a successful overall OTA sequence.**

   Location: [GitHubOTA.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/OTA/src/GitHubOTA.cpp:130), [ControllerOTA.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/OTA/src/ControllerOTA.cpp:391).

   Receiving the image (`0xF2`) is distinct from installing it. The new result handler logs every `0x0F` message and sets one `installResultReceived` flag, including explicit messages for insufficient space, a refused single-slot update, or `Update.end()` failure. `waitForInstallResult()` therefore treats receipt of a negative result as success, and GitHubOTA ignores even its boolean return. The display can then update itself and report completion while the controller retains its old firmware.

   Represent success, failure, and unknown separately. Propagate explicit installation failures to `PHASE_ERROR`; define a deliberate compatibility policy for older controllers that do not report a final result. This is a remaining gap in the OTA hardening, not a claim that the branch newly invented all false-success behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce
In a controlled transport test, acknowledge complete image receipt with 0xF2, then send a 0x0F result containing an explicit refusal, insufficient-space error, or Update.end error. Observe installResultReceived is set without success parsing and GitHubOTA continues after waitForInstallResult. Also test timeout and legacy peers; do not use a working machine for destructive failure injection.

## Acceptance Criteria
Receipt, install success, install failure, and unknown result are distinct; explicit controller refusals/Update.end failures stop the combined update before display flashing; PHASE_ERROR reaches the UI; timeout/legacy-controller policy is explicit and tested.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Receipt, install success, install failure, and unknown result are distinct; explicit controller refusals/Update.end failures stop the combined update before display flashing; PHASE_ERROR reaches the UI; timeout/legacy-controller policy is explicit and tested.
notes:
Done in commit "ota: fail the combined update when the controller reports a failed install (gm-bzu.8)" on worktree-gm-2cl-6-dials, merged into idf5.

What changed:
- lib/OTA/src/ControllerInstallResult.h reads the controller's 0x0F report. Success, Failure or Unrecognised. Failure markers win over a Success marker.
- ControllerOTA::waitForInstallResult returns Success, Failure, Unrecognised, LinkDropped or Timeout.
- GitHubOTA::update stops with PHASE_ERROR on Failure and does not flash the display. Success carries on. Unrecognised, LinkDropped and Timeout carry on with a warning. That is the legacy policy: the controller acknowledged the image, and silence must not strand the display. kUnconfirmedControllerInstallIsError flips it.

Tests:
- pio test -e native_otaresult: 11 of 11 pass. New env in platformio.ini, test in test/test_ota_result.
- Format check with clang-format-14 passes.
- display-loadtest builds.

Limits: no controller on the bench. The BLE path (0xF2 then 0x0F) is verified by reading the code, not on hardware. Failure injection on a real machine was not done, per the bead.

title: Ripples bandRef rounds differently from band() on the device (fused madd.s)
description:
Found by gm-bzu.79. The firmware builds with GCC's default -ffp-contract=fast at -O2, so the production accumulateBandRef in src/display/ui/default/bganim/AnimRipples.cpp compiles 'hAccBuf[x] += amp * cos * env' into one madd.s (a single rounding). Seen in the display ELF built 2026-10-01: bandRef at 0x42079000 has madd.s f0, f4, f1 at 0x4207910e. The production accumulateBandAsm uses mul.s then add.s (two roundings), and so do the host goldens (x86 without FMA). So on the device band() and bandRef() can differ by 1 ULP per accumulated ring sample before RGB565 packing, and /api/debug/animtest?anim=<ripples> compares a kernel against a reference that is not the host spec. In the QEMU harness the same fusion gave 6 lanes 1 ULP apart in 7 cases (for example 0x3ef8649e against 0x3ef8649f). Fix options: build AnimRipples.cpp (or just accumulateBandRef) with -ffp-contract=off, for example a function attribute optimize("fp-contract=off") or a pragma, then check with animtest that mismatch_px stays 0 and that the host goldens are unchanged. Also worth a grep: other bandRef paths in bganim/ may fuse against an unfused kernel the same way; objdump the display ELF for madd.s/msub.s inside each bandRef.

## Acceptance
The production ripples bandRef has no madd.s or msub.s in the accumulate (objdump of the display ELF), animtest for ripples reports mismatch_px 0, and host goldens pass.
notes:
2026-10-01, commit 19c64b3b.

Changed: AnimRipples.cpp only. accumulateBandRef carries noinline plus optimize("fp-contract=off") through a local macro, RIPPLES_NO_FP_CONTRACT (Clang gets noinline only). noinline is needed because GCC applies fp-contract per function after inlining: inlined into bandRef the loop would compile under bandRef's fast setting again. The attribute is not on bandRef or the file, because blendPackSpan (6 madd.s) and buildRowState (2 madd.s, 10 msub.s) are shared by band() and bandRef() and must keep compiling the same in both. No shared macro in BgAnimCommon.h: ripples is the only animation that needs it. The QEMU test copy is unchanged, since build.sh already passes -ffp-contract=off for every test.

Objdump survey, per object file in .pio/build/display (before the change), madd.s/msub.s by function:
- ripples: bandRef 1 madd.s (the inlined accumulate, the bug). blendPackSpan, buildRowState, frame, init also fuse, but they are shared by band() and bandRef(), so both sides round the same.
- silk: bandRef 1 madd.s, 1 msub.s in the per-row vignette (1 - vignK*dy*dy). band() under GM_BGANIM_SILK_ASM=1 has the same C expression, and with the flag at its default 0 band() is bandRef(). No mismatch.
- lava: renderRow and renderRowAsm each 2 madd.s, 1 msub.s, in the per-row float setup (tt0f, step0f) that the two share; the field loop is integer. No mismatch.
- orbits: drawOverlays, rebuildGeometry, frame fuse; drawOverlays is called by both band() and bandRef(). No mismatch.
- aurora (not mine, noted): computeRowState 2 madd.s, 1 msub.s, called by both band() and bandRef(). No mismatch.
- starfield (not mine, noted): plotStarsAndShoot 2 madd.s, 4 msub.s, called by both. No mismatch.
- ember, fireflies, mandala (not mine), caustics, nebula, silk2, steam: fused ops only in frame(), init() or theme and LUT builders, shared state. No mismatch. plasma: none.
Side note, not in scope: every shared fused site makes the device round differently from the host goldens (x86, no FMA). Device output is never compared with the goldens, so it is not a band/bandRef mismatch.

Verified:
- display ELF after: bandRef calls accumulateBandRef, which is mul.s, mul.s, add.s, no madd.s or msub.s. Ripples band(), blendPackSpan, buildRowState and accumulateBandAsm have the same instruction streams as before (addresses stripped; buildRowState differs only in decoded padding). Same result in the display-loadtest object.
- tools/animbench make check: ALL OK, ripples max 0 on all three frames.
- check_copies.py PASS (15 tests). QEMU anim_ripples (firmware toolchain) PASS: 10 fillTile, 7 accumulate cases, 0 mismatches.
- pio run -e display, -e display-loadtest, -e display-sim: SUCCESS.

Left for the bench (ripples is registry id 5): http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=5 must report mismatch_px 0. Not run, by rule.
Agent-mail was unreachable (127.0.0.1:8765, no answer), so no file reservation was made; the lead assigned the file.
close_reason: Ripples reference accumulate built without FP contraction; bandRef has no madd.s, band() unchanged, goldens and QEMU pass; device animtest left for the bench

title: Sundial dither is column only, and the page entry wrote past the row end
description: Sundial (id 21) carries full width horizontal scanline flicker. Found on 2026-09-11 while measuring movement across the fleet for gm-33fm. The frame to frame difference is dominated by whole rows flipping rather than by the wedge turning: the largest single 66 ms step measures 133.9 against a mean of 15.5, and the banding is visible in a single static frame as well, so it is row structure near the sampling limit rather than motion. It also explains why Sundial scores near the top of the movement table (0.15, fifth fastest) while its wedge turns slowly, and why its Speed parameter barely changes the score. The page entry in tools/animbench/web/anim_bench.html owns the design, and the firmware port reproduces it exactly, so the fix belongs in the page entry first and then in the port. Likely cause to check first: a per row term whose step is close to one palette index per row, or a radial term evaluated per row without smoothing. Done when: a static frame shows no row banding, the movement score reflects the wedge turning rather than row flips, and the port and the page still agree pixel for pixel with regenerated goldens. Evidence: tmp/motion/frames and the numbers in the gm-33fm survey.
notes:
Cause found 2026-09-12 by the sundial port lane, independently of the movement survey. The page entry folds the Bayer dither into the column table only, so the per row surface and radial terms quantise in whole palette entries across the full width. Measured on the static golden frame: row to row steps in mean brightness average 1.12 with a peak of 2.73, against 0.29 and 0.89 for columns, and the fast part of the row profile carries ten times the energy of the column one. The firmware port (landed as 9b5b18e3) reproduces this exactly on purpose, so the fix goes into the page entry first, then into AnimSundial.cpp, then the goldens are regenerated. Until then gm-33fm leaves Sundial's speed alone, since its movement score is flicker rather than travel.

Correction 2026-09-12, from the cal-5 lane: there are two separate effects here and the loud one never reached a device. The big flicker, the 133.9 single step against a mean of 15.5, is a bug in the page entry alone. When a ray runs nearly parallel to a row it meets that row outside the panel, and the span clip could push the span start past the row width; the page's prefix loop then walked to that start and wrote up to 123 pixels past the end of the row, shifting every later pixel. The firmware's beamSpan has always guarded exactly that case, so no device ever showed it. It stayed hidden because the shipped Speed default of 10 never reached those wedge angles inside the 240 golden frames; at Speed 50 it does, and the regenerated golden and the page then disagreed over about 188,000 pixels at frame 120. The cal-5 lane gave the page the same guard the firmware has, landed in 97998d7c. Largest frame to frame step fell from 133.9 to 3.7, and Sundial's half change time went from a false 1175 ms to an honest 1474 ms. The second effect is the mild one the port lane measured on the firmware's own static golden: row to row brightness steps of mean 1.12 and peak 2.73 against 0.29 and 0.89 for columns, because the Bayer dither is folded into the column table only. That one is real on the device, is a much smaller artifact than the numbers in this bead's original description suggest, and is what remains to be decided. Sundial now sits 26 ms inside the accept band, so if the dither is ever spread across rows its rate wants re-measuring.

Closed 2026-09-12 by d78ab529. The cause was not what either earlier note guessed.

The page entry and the firmware both already indexed the shared 8x8 Bayer matrix by row
and column, so the dither was two dimensional. The row artifact came from the matrix
itself: every column of BAYER8 sums to 252, which is the ideal, but its rows sum to 168,
296, 200, 328, 176, 304, 208 and 336. On a face as flat as Sundial's, each row carried a
mean offset of up to a third of the dither swing, so every eighth row came out brighter
than its neighbour.

Measured on the goldens as the mean luma of each row and column over the three golden
times: row to row steps averaged 1.09 with a peak of 2.73 against 0.25 and 1.11 for
columns, and the fast part of the row profile carried 40 to 90 times the energy of the
column one. Two controls: with the dither zeroed the rows measured 0.24, the same as the
columns, and with the matrix transposed the excess moved to the columns. So the matrix
was the whole of it.

Sundial now builds its dither from the Bayer matrix with each column rotated by an xor on
the row index, ROT = 0 6 2 4 5 3 7 1, which keeps the column sums and makes every row sum
252 too. Of the 5,832 rotations that balance both axes, that one has the least power at
low spatial frequencies, 2 percent above plain Bayer, with no row or column stripe
component. After: row steps 0.24 with a peak of 1.21, columns 0.25 and 1.16, and the row
profile carries 0.3 to 0.6 times the energy of the column one.

The table is still read as dith[(y & 7) * 8 + (x & 7)], so the Xtensa kernels are
untouched and the QEMU test still passes bit exact. Speed 50 half change time 1474 ms
before and 1475 after, so the base rate did not move. Sundial stays pixel exact against
its page entry.

The defect is fleet wide and is now gm-404a. Thirty-seven of the 44 animations read
BAYER8 or BAYER4, and BAYER4 has the same imbalance at the same ratio: columns all 30
against an ideal of 30, rows 20, 36, 24 and 40. It is inherent to the standard recursive
Bayer construction, not a transcription error. Fixing the shared tables changes 37
animations at once, so it needs its own deliberate pass with the whole verification chain
behind it, which is why it is a separate bead rather than part of this one.

Sundial's Speed slider is still flat at the top, 3.75 times outside tolerance at Speed
100, and that is in gm-kh2s round two rather than here.

title: Per-frame time from a wrapped delta: Orbits, Steam, Mandala (gm-bzu.50 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to gm-bzu.50 (bganim F2, Astra notes 2026-09-30). These frame() functions still build motion from absolute millis() in float, so motion steps in 32 ms jumps after 3.1 days of uptime (256 ms after 24.9 days) and jumps at the 49.7-day wrap and on a speed change.

Where (line numbers from the review, at the commit before gm-bzu.50): AnimOrbits.cpp:191, AnimSteam.cpp:233, AnimMandala.cpp:560.

How: move each onto bganim::AnimClock (src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimClock.h, added by gm-bzu.50, commit e0288060). Keep each oscillator's own phase (a Q48 rate per oscillator, oscRad/oscTurnQ32), not one shared modulus. Keep the clock in a file-scope static that release() does not reset. A rate that depends on a parameter accumulates its own phase (see AnimFireflies.cpp g_ringQ32). Fireflies, Aurora, Starfield and Ember are worked examples.

Acceptance: add each animation to kOnClock in tools/animbench/clock_check.cpp; make -C tools/animbench check passes (goldens, interlace_check and clock_check at 480, 240, 466 and 233); fuzz under ASan and make -f Makefile.lifecycle check pass; QEMU check_copies and the animation's test pass if a kernel changes; one bench animtest per animation.
notes:
2026-10-01, commits 47dc2de2 (Orbits, Steam) and d0dee99f (Mandala).

Changed:
- Orbits: per-orbit Q48 rate (one turn per T s), on an AnimClock that carries the speed. Trail samples stay 1/90 turn apart (the old dt=T/90 was already speed-independent in angle).
- Steam: two clocks. g_clock at speed 1 carries blob lifecycles (uint32 ms births) and per-wisp sway rates (Q48). g_rise carries the speed; each blob stores riseBirth (Q16) and its rise is g_rise minus that, back-dated at the current speed when a blob is built or reborn (reborn blobs are invisible, L near 0). At constant speed rise = 0.034 * age exactly as before; a speed change bends the rise instead of moving every blob.
- Mandala: ring offsets A and B and the breathing are Q48 rates; offsets are oscTurnQ32 >> 24 (256 ticks a turn, the old 40.74 constant kept in the rate).
- All clocks are file-scope statics that release() does not reset. clock_check kOnClock gains orbits, steam, mandala (tools/animbench/clock_check.cpp, one line, needed by the acceptance).
- No asm or kernel changed, so no QEMU copy or golden changed.

Verified:
- make -C tools/animbench check: GOLDENS OK with orbits, steam and mandala exact (max 0 on all 9 frames), interlace_check ALL OK at 480/240/466/233, CLOCK CHECK OK at all four sizes for all 7 animations.
- Negative: clock_check built against the HEAD versions fails orbits, steam (before 47dc2de2) and mandala (before d0dee99f).
- render_one --shapes ALL OK for orbits, steam, mandala.
- Fuzz under ASan+UBSan (ASAN_OPTIONS=verify_asan_link_order=0): exit 0, all three ok in sweep and align pass. Makefile.lifecycle lifecycle_check: ALL OK (run with detect_leaks=0, the make target's detect_leaks=1 aborts on WSL1).
- QEMU: check_copies PASS (15 tests); anim_orbits, anim_steam, anim_mandala RESULT: PASS.
- pio display-sim, display, display-loadtest SUCCESS after each change.
- Speed-change continuity is by construction (clock steps scaled per step); not exercised by a test.

Left for the bench (not run, board not touched):
- /api/debug/animtest?anim=7 (mandala), ?anim=8 (orbits), ?anim=10 (steam): mismatch_px must be 0. Ids are 0-based positions in BgAnimRegistry.cpp.
- kdev note: these three now carry state in frame() (the clock), so on tools/kblob compare blobref vs blob, not blob vs the firmware's band().
- agent-mail was unreachable (127.0.0.1:8765 refused), so no file reservations were taken; the lead's assignment was the reservation.
close_reason: Orbits, Steam and Mandala on AnimClock; goldens exact, clock_check covers all three

title: On-display settings screens
description:
Let the most important settings be changed on the display itself, without the web UI: a gear tile on the menu opens a settings screen with five category tiles, each category is a paged list of rows (steppers, choices, toggles, locked calibration rows, read-only status rows), visual settings change live, everything else is saved when the category is left. Agreed in the 2026-09-05 interview; the decisions below are the spec.

## Navigation
- Menu (`objects.menu_screen_new`) gains the settings gear tile (`objects.btn_settings_1`, currently hidden). Tap: settings cover opens on the menu screen.
- Settings home: five category tiles (Temperatures & timing, Display, Animation, Machine, Status) plus the exit chevron back to the menu.
- Category: title, up/down page arrows with a "page n/m" indicator, five rows per page, exit chevron back to the tiles. Sub-pages (wake-up schedule list and editor) stack on top; the exit chevron pops one level.

## Categories and rows
- Temperatures & timing: Temperature offset (locked, 1 C steps), Pressure sensor (locked, 0.1 bar steps), Brew delay (50 ms), Grind delay (50 ms), Delay auto-adjust (toggle).
- Display: Main brightness (1..16, live), Standby brightness (0..16), Dim after (standby dim timeout, 30 s steps), 24-hour clock (toggle), Time zone region (choice), City (choice).
- Animation (all live): Animation (choice by name), Frame rate (5..60, step 5), All screens (toggle), Theme (Dark/Light), Gradient (Default, built-in themes, stored library gradients, for the current animation), Plates (Keep/Hide/Custom), Plate colour (palette), Plate opacity (0..100, step 5), Element tint (toggle), Tint colour (palette), Text scrim (0..100, step 5).
- Machine: Startup mode (Standby/Brew), Standby timeout (Never, 1..240 min), Auto wake-up (toggle), Schedules (opens the list: add up to 8, each with hour and minute steppers, seven weekday toggles, remove).
- Status (read-only, refreshed every second): Display firmware, Controller firmware, Network, IP address, Controller, Scale, Time; plus Restart (hold 2 s).
- Excluded on purpose: steam pump assist, boiler fill, momentary buttons, scale source, HomeKit, Home Assistant, OTA, WiFi credentials, reset to defaults.

## Structure of the work
- gm-flw.1 value model (host-tested), .2 shell, .3 row widgets, .4 menu tile, .5 synthetic tap injection (`TouchInject` module, LVGL and SDL hooks, `/api/debug/tap`), .15 bench readouts (active-screen touchmap with label texts and debug tags, `anim_id` and `uptime_ms`, `/api/debug/synth`, `tools/touchmap.py`), .16 rig helper (`tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` with the simulator launcher), .6 settings debug route, .7 Temperatures & timing, .8 Display, .9 Animation, .10 Machine, .11 schedule editor, .12 Status, .13 end-to-end runner, .14 documentation.
- Dependencies: .1 has none; .2 and .5 need the simulator build (gm-bzu.9); .15 follows .5 and .2; .16 follows .5 and .15; .6 follows .2, .5, .15 and .16; .3 follows .2, .6 and .15 (its rows are verified through the debug route, the tap route and the tagged touchmap); .4 follows .2, .6 and .15 (all three edit `DefaultUI.cpp`); the categories (.7, .8, .9, .10, .12) need .1, .2, .3, .6 and .16; .11 follows .10; .13 needs every user-facing bead plus .16 and gm-bzu.9; .14 follows .13. Waves that may run in parallel touch disjoint files.
- One file per category under `src/display/ui/default/settings/`. The shell's table names five `extern const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` symbols, defined weak in `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp`; each category bead defines the strong symbol in its own file and edits no shared file, so the five category beads run in parallel without collisions, and the runner bead deletes the placeholders.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`display-sim`, the same HTTP instruments on 127.0.0.1:8080, state in `sim_data/`), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` at 192.168.1.121). Memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only.

## Shared contract (identical in every bead of this epic)

- Code-built LVGL, not EEZ Studio. The settings UI lives in `src/display/ui/default/settings/` and is built with `lv_*` calls; the runtime-built scale overlay (`DefaultUI::buildScaleScreen` in `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`) is the precedent for construction and for delete-event pointer cleanup. It is one full-screen cover object created as a child of `objects.menu_screen_new` when settings opens and deleted when it closes. The flow screen never changes while settings is open (`currentScreen` stays `SCREEN_ID_MENU_SCREEN_NEW`), so the animation host, plate handling and screen-change code in DefaultUI are untouched. While the cover is up, every direct child of the menu screen except `objects.status_icons` is hidden (their original visibility captured and restored on close); the flow tick keeps driving flags on the menu's individual tiles and icons, which is why parents are hidden, never individual flow-controlled children.
- Look: the current style. Text and icons in `theme_colors[eez_flow_get_selected_theme_index()][0]`, backgrounds in `theme_colors[..][1]`; fonts `lv_font_montserrat_16/18/20/24` (34 and 48 exist for large values); icons from `src/display/ui/default/eez/images.h` (`img_angle_up/down/left/right_40x40`, `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_check_40x40`, `img_thermometer_half_40x40`, `img_clock_40x40`, `img_settings_40x40`, `img_info_40x40`, `img_tachometer_fast_40x40`, `img_power_40x40`) recoloured with the accent, or `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs from the Montserrat fonts. Page title in Montserrat 24 below the status icons (which sit at y 20..40). The exit chevron is `img_angle_up_40x40` at `LV_ALIGN_CENTER` + 210 px with `lv_obj_set_ext_click_area(btn, 45)`, exactly where every other screen has it; its hit rectangle is clipped by the screen to 130x95 px and it is exempt from the size and edge rules below. No translucent plates over the animation: rows are text and icons directly on the screen background (the cover has `bg_opa` 0, so the theme background or the animation shows through, whichever the menu screen has). Every translucent pixel costs blend time per animation frame (CLAUDE.md, UI-pipeline invariants). Text that does not fit its slot is truncated with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT`; the row keeps the canonical value string in its own storage and the debug dump exports that (the label's buffer holds the dots, `lv_label_get_text` returns them).
- Geometry: 480x480 round panel, 0.111 mm/px. For every tappable target except the exit chevron: its effective hit rectangle (coords grown by its ext click pad, clipped by every ancestor without `LV_OBJ_FLAG_OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`; `tools/touchmap.py` and `tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` compute this from the dumped absolute coords, which already include any translate) is at least 56x56 px, no two hit rectangles on one page overlap, and no hit rectangle reaches within 12 px of the panel edge circle (radius 240 around 240,240). Row widgets are 320x56 px, five rows per page. Every settings object that a test must find carries a `SettingsDebugTag` (row name, role: `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `exit`, `tile`, `cover`, and for role `value` a pointer to the row-owned canonical value string) in its LVGL `user_data`; the touchmap dump exports the tag, and for value tags the canonical text in full, for descendants of the cover.
- Interaction: steppers step once on `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` and once on each `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` (LVGL defaults: `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED` 400 ms after press, then a repeat every 100 ms; no step on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`), and report `fast` after 2 s of continuous hold, whereupon the field's `fastStep` from the model applies (there is no universal multiplier). LVGL delivers at most one `LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` per `lv_task_handler` call and resets its repeat timestamp on each, so the number of repeats in a hold depends on the UI pass cadence (a 100 ms rerender pass yields one repeat per pass); tests assert the protocol (one step per event, none on CLICKED) and wide count windows, never an exact cadence. Holds are cancelled by `LV_EVENT_RELEASED`, `LV_EVENT_PRESS_LOST`, disabling the row, page removal and deletion; hold and progress state lives in the row object and is driven only by the events LVGL delivers to it (PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT, RELEASED, PRESS_LOST, DELETE), never by a free-standing `lv_timer` that could outlive the row. Choices show `< value >` and cycle with the arrows, wrapping at both ends, arrows repeating while held. Toggles flip on tap. Locked rows (calibration) unlock after a 1 s press on the row, consume that press until release, and relock whenever the category is left. Confirm rows (Restart, Remove schedule) act once after a 2 s hold with visible progress and cancel on release. `setEnabled(false)` disables every interactive descendant and cancels pending holds.
- Saving: visual settings apply on every change (brightness, animation, frame rate, all-screens, theme, gradient, plates, tint, scrim) and each live write is followed by `ui->markDirty()` so `DefaultUI::updateState` applies it on the next pass rather than after the 2.5 s idle rerender interval. Everything else is written to `Settings` when the category is left, by any route the UI task can see (exit chevron, standby timeout, controller mode change, brew start, any flow screen change), and never lost on those routes. A category's `commit` writes only the fields the user changed. A web UI save while a category is open does not close it: the web values land first, the shell refreshes every row the user has not touched from `Settings` on the next pass after `settings:changed`, and the user's touched fields keep their draft and win at commit (per field, last writer wins). A web-requested restart (`/api/settings` POST with `restart`) reboots from the web task at once; an uncommitted display draft is lost then, the same as a power cut, and that is accepted. `Settings` properties mark themselves dirty on `set` and `Settings::loopTask` flushes every dirty property to NVS every 5 s (a flush is one or more NVS key writes, each stalling the flash cache for a scan-out slip); live rows therefore reach flash through the periodic saver while the category is still open, deferred fields become dirty only at commit, and nothing calls an immediate save per step. Concurrency: `Settings::lock()` (a FreeRTOS recursive mutex added by the shell bead, a no-op on the simulator's single thread) serialises whole transactions: the web save's `batchUpdate`, `doSave` (periodic flush, `save(true)`, `flushNow`), a category's `enter` snapshot and `commit`, and `Controller::loopLogic`'s delay auto-adjust writes. Between transactions the rule is per field, last writer wins; readers outside a transaction (`DefaultUI::updateState`) are unchanged.
- Activity: every touch inside settings calls `controller->updateLastAction()` so the standby timeout (`Controller::loopLogic`: `now > lastAction + settings.getStandbyTimeout()`, on the logic task on the device and in the one main loop on the simulator) does not fire mid-edit.
- Memory: immutable lookup tables are `const` PODs in flash (a `const std::vector` or `String` is not); runtime drafts, strings and callback contexts are small, bounded and owned by the shell for the life of the cover; anything sizeable goes to PSRAM; settings code never touches the animation hot slab (`bganim::allocHot`). LVGL objects allocate from PSRAM through `gm_lv_malloc`, so widget count is not an internal-DRAM concern, but plain C++ allocations are, and `/api/debug/heap` (`int_free`, `dma_free`) is read with the largest page and draft open.
- Wire format of GET `/api/settings` (the oracle for what was written): `standbyTimeout` and `standbyBrightnessTimeout` are in seconds (stored in ms), `temperatureOffset` and `pressureScaling` are numeric strings, `bgAnimPlateColor` and `elementTintColor` are `#rrggbb` strings, `startupMode` is `standby` or `brew`, `autowakeupSchedules` is `HH:MM|ddddddd;...` (Mon..Sun). Scripts parse before comparing.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`pio run -e display-sim`, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy GM_SIM_PORT=<port> ./.pio/build/display-sim/program`, web server on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (8080 by default), state under `sim_data/` in the working directory; the build is repaired by gm-bzu.9), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` build at 192.168.1.121). The simulator runs the LVGL UI, Settings, the web server and the debug routes on one cooperative thread with no panel and no background animation renderer (`SleepAnimation` is a stub under `GAGGIMATE_SIM` and `updateState` skips animation and plate application): it verifies navigation, interaction, values, persistence and theme colours. Animation frame counters, the applied frame-rate cap, rendered gradients, plate pixels, memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only, and a simulator pass says nothing about the device's concurrency (TouchInject's critical section and the Settings lock are reviewed on their own merits). Build note: a new or deleted source file under `src/` needs `touch src/CMakeLists.txt` before the ESP-IDF envs pick it up (the glob has no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS); when a symbol's provenance matters, check the ELF with the toolchain's `nm` (`~/.platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf/bin/xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`).
- Rules: never POST `/api/settings` by hand (the web UI is the only safe writer) and never print the `wifiPassword` field of GET `/api/settings`; scripts read it through a filter that drops that key. No em dashes or double hyphens in prose, comments or commit messages.
close_reason: All 14 child beads implemented, reviewed and closed. Simulator runner PASS (316 checks, 7 scenarios, 16 pages clean); bench board runner PASS on 6 scenarios (Animation blocked by the board's off-palette stored tint colour); docs in 6cb39a1a.

title: Build the host-tested settings value model (ranges, steps, formats, zones, schedules)
description:
Build the value model behind the on-display settings as plain C++ with no LVGL or Arduino dependency, and unit-test it natively. Every range, step, wrap rule, display format, choice list, time-zone split and wake-up schedule edit that the settings screens need is decided here once, so the screen code only wires rows to model calls and the rules are testable on the host.

## Context
- Settings fields and their storage (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `temperatureOffset` (int, C), `pressureScaling` (float, bar, default 16.0), `brewDelay`/`grindDelay` (double, ms), `delayAdjust` (bool), `mainBrightness` (int 1..16), `standbyBrightness` (int 0..16), `standbyBrightnessTimeout` (int ms, default 60000), `standbyTimeout` (int ms, default 900000, 0 = never), `startupMode` (int, `MODE_STANDBY` 0 or `MODE_BREW` 1 from `constants.h`), `bgAnimFps` (int 5..60), `bgAnimId` (int index into the animation table), `bgAnimAllScreens` (bool), `themeMode` (int, 0 Dark, 1 Light), `bgAnimClearPlates` (0 keep, 1 hide, 2 custom), `bgAnimPlateColor` (int 0xRRGGBB), `bgAnimPlateOpacity` (0..100), `elementTintEnabled` (bool), `elementTintColor` (int 0xRRGGBB), `bgAnimScrim` (0..100), `clock24hFormat` (bool), `timezone` (String, an IANA name such as `Europe/Oslo`), `autowakeupEnabled` (bool), `autowakeupSchedules` (`std::vector<AutoWakeupSchedule>`: `String time` "HH:MM", `bool days[7]` Mon..Sun; NVS and the web UI serialise it as `HH:MM|1111100;HH:MM|0000011`).
- Animation names: `bg_animation(i).name` for `i < bg_animation_count()` (`src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnim.h`). Gradients: `bg_theme_count()` built-ins named by `bg_theme_name(i)`; the user library `bgAnimGradients` is `id|name|gradient;...` (up to 12 entries, `BG_GRADIENT_LIB_MAX`); the per-animation assignment `bgAnimThemeMap` is `ref;ref;...` indexed by animation id where a ref is empty (use the global `bgAnimTheme`), a built-in index, or `c<id>` for a library entry; `bg_map_valid` and `bg_library_valid` check the syntax. The web UI mirrors all of this in `web/src/config/bgAnimations.js`.
- Time zones: `src/display/core/zones.h` declares `zones_t {const char *name; const char *zones;}` (IANA name, POSIX TZ string) and a header-local `static const zones_t zones[]` of 461 entries plus `resolve_timezone(name)`. Controller.cpp and DefaultUI.cpp both include it today. Regions are the text before the first `/`: Africa 52, America 149, Antarctica 11, Arctic 1, Asia 82, Atlantic 10, Australia 12, Etc 35, Europe 60, Indian 11, Pacific 38.
- Storage clamps that the model must agree with: `Settings::setBrewDelay` and `setGrindDelay` clamp to 0..4000 ms (`Settings.cpp`); the web handler clamps `bgAnimClearPlates` to 0..2. The web UI's own input ranges are in `web/src/pages/Settings/tabs/*.jsx` (brightness 1..16 and 0..16, fps 5..60, opacity and scrim 0..100).
- `autowakeupSchedules` can hold more than 8 entries today (neither the web Add handler nor the setter caps it); a cap in the model limits adding, never importing.
- The host unit-test pattern is `[env:native_autotune]` in `platformio.ini` with `test/test_autotune_simc/` (Unity, `pio test -e native_autotune`).

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.h`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.cpp`, `test/test_settings_model/test_settings_model.cpp`, `platformio.ini` (new `[env:native_settingsui]`), plus a header-independent accessor to the zone table (`size_t zones_count()` and `const zones_t &zones_entry(size_t)` declared in `zones.h` and defined in exactly one TU, for example a new `src/display/core/zones.cpp`), so the model never includes the table itself.

## Requirements
- Numeric specs, one per field: minimum, maximum, step, fast step (used after 2 s of holding), wrap or clamp, unit, decimals, and a formatter. Values:
  - Temperature offset: -20..20 C, step 1, fast 5, clamp, shown "-3 C".
  - Pressure sensor rating: 1.0..30.0 bar, step 0.1, fast 1.0, clamp, one decimal, shown "16.0 bar".
  - Brew delay, Grind delay: 0..4000 ms (the setter's clamp), step 50, fast 250, clamp, shown "800 ms".
  - Main brightness 1..16, Standby brightness 0..16, step 1, fast 4, clamp.
  - Dim after (standbyBrightnessTimeout): stored ms; 30 s..30 min, step 30 s, fast 5 min, clamp, shown "m:ss" ("1:30"). A stored value off the grid is shown as is and the first step lands on the grid.
  - Standby timeout: stored ms; 0 shown as "Never", then 1..240 min, step 1 min, fast 10 min, clamp at both ends (stepping down from 1 min reaches Never; stepping up from Never gives 1 min), shown "15 min".
  - Frame rate 5..60, step 5, fast 10, clamp, shown "30 fps". Plate opacity and Text scrim 0..100, step 5, fast 20, clamp, shown "35 %".
  - Schedule hour 0..23 and minute 0..59, step 1, fast 5, wrap.
- Choice lists (index-based, wrap at both ends): Startup mode {Standby, Brew} mapped to `MODE_STANDBY`/`MODE_BREW`; Theme {Dark, Light} mapped to 0/1; Plates {Keep, Hide, Custom} mapped to 0/1/2; Animation names from the animation table; Gradient for animation N: entry 0 "Default", then every built-in theme by name, then every library gradient by name, each mapping to the map ref ("", built-in index, `c<id>`), with functions to read the current ref for animation N out of a map string and to write a new ref back leaving every other entry intact and the result accepted by `bg_map_valid`; a colour palette of 12 named colours (for example White, Warm white, Amber, Orange, Red, Pink, Purple, Blue, Cyan, Teal, Green, Black) where a stored colour that is not in the palette is presented as a 13th entry named by its hex value so cycling never silently changes it.

The flow screen never changes while settings is open (`currentScreen` stays `SCREEN_ID_MENU_SCREEN_NEW`), so the animation host, plate handling and screen-change code in DefaultUI are untouched. - Look: the current style. Text and icons in `theme_colors[eez_flow_get_selected_theme_index()][0]`, backgrounds in `theme_colors[..][1]`; fonts `lv_font_montserrat_16/18/20/24` (34 and 48 exist for large values); icons from `src/display/ui/default/eez/images.h` (`img_angle_up/down/left/right_40x40`, `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_check_40x40`, `img_thermometer_half_40x40`, `img_clock_40x40`, `img_settings_40x40`, `img_info_40x40`, `img_tachometer_fast_40x40`, `img_power_40x40`) recoloured with the accent, or `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs from the Montserrat fonts. Page title in Montserrat 24 below the status icons (which sit at y 20..40). Every translucent pixel costs blend time per animation frame (CLAUDE.md, UI-pipeline invariants). - Geometry: 480x480 round panel, 0.111 mm/px. Row widgets are 320x56 px, five rows per page. Every settings object that a test must find carries a `SettingsDebugTag` (row name, role: `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `exit`, `tile`, `cover`, and for role `value` a pointer to the row-owned canonical value string) in its LVGL `user_data`; the touchmap dump exports the tag, and for value tags the canonical text in full, for descendants of the cover.

title: Implement the Machine category (startup mode, standby timeout, auto wake-up toggle)
description:
Implement the Machine category: startup mode, standby timeout and the auto wake-up master toggle, saved when the category is left. The schedule list and editor are a separate bead that adds its own row to this category.

## Context
- Fields and setters (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `startupMode` (`setStartupMode`, `MODE_STANDBY` 0 or `MODE_BREW` 1 from `src/display/core/constants.h`; the web UI posts "standby"/"brew"), `standbyTimeout` (`setStandbyTimeout`, ms, 0 = never; the web UI edits it in seconds), `autowakeupEnabled` (`setAutoWakeupEnabled`).
- Consumers: `Controller::loopLogic` reads `getStandbyTimeout()` every pass (`now > lastAction + standbyTimeout` triggers `activateStandby`), `DefaultUI` and `Controller` read `getStartupMode()` at boot only, `AutoWakeupPlugin::loop` reads `isAutoWakeupEnabled()` and the schedules every minute and needs no re-arm.
- Model specs: Startup mode choice {Standby, Brew}; Standby timeout Never then 1..240 min in 1 min steps (fast 10), shown "15 min" or "Never".

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatMachine.cpp`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatMachine.h` (the draft struct the schedule bead edits; `CatMachine.cpp` defines `kCatMachine`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_machine.py`.

## Requirements
- Rows, in this order and with these names: "Startup mode" (choice), "Standby timeout" (stepper), "Auto wake-up" (toggle). One page (the schedule bead appends "Schedules" as row 4). Title "Machine", icon `img_power_40x40`.
- All deferred: `commit` writes touched fields and triggers `settings:changed` if anything was written.
- `CatMachine.h` publishes the draft struct (`MachineDraft`: startup mode, standby timeout ms, auto wake-up flag, a `std::vector` of the model's schedule struct, and per-field touched flags including `schedulesTouched`) and a row-provider hook so the schedule bead can append its "Schedules" action row and push its pages with a pointer to this draft; `commit` writes `setAutoWakeupSchedules` (converting to `AutoWakeupSchedule`) only when `schedulesTouched`. This file never knows the editor's internals.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` succeed.
- [ ] Simulator (then loadtest device with `synth(0)`), via `settingsui(cat=3)`: rows show the stored values (`startupMode`, `standbyTimeout` from GET `/api/settings` is in seconds: divide by 60 for the minutes shown, 0 shows Never, `autowakeupEnabled`).
- [ ] Startup mode Standby to Brew and `settingsui(pop=1)`: `/api/settings` `startupMode` is `brew` within 6 s; after a restart (sim: `Sim.restart()`; device: the Status page's Restart row on a build that honours `startupMode`, which the loadtest build with the synthetic handshake does not) the display lands on the brew screen once the controller connects. Set it back afterwards.
- [ ] Standby timeout: from 15 min, holding minus 1500 ms reaches 1..6 min; single taps down to 1 min, one more shows Never and pop persists `standbyTimeout` 0; a tap up from Never shows 1 min.
- [ ] With the timeout set to 1 min through this page and popped, and no touch afterwards, the machine enters standby 60..70 s later (`/api/status` `mode` 0, or the standby screen in `touchmap --screens 0`); on the device this needs `synth(0)`.
- [ ] Auto wake-up toggle persists (`autowakeupEnabled`), and the log shows the plugin's `Auto-wakeup enabled with n schedule(s)` line after the `settings:changed` trigger.
- [ ] Leaving with no change writes nothing; a web save of `standbyTimeout` while the page is open shows on the row (reconcile) and survives the pop.
- [ ] `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_machine.py` covers what the instruments can observe on the current venue (the restart check on the sim only) and restores the starting values through the UI.

## Out of scope
Schedules (next bead), momentary buttons, boiler fill, steam pump.
## How a category plugs in (same for every category bead)
- Code against the header that landed with the shell, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.h`: a category is a `SettingsCategoryDef` (title, 40x40 icon, `rowCount`, `buildRow(ctx, index, parent, ui)`, `enter` once per push, `refresh` once per second while visible, `commit` exactly once when the page is removed by any route, `reconcile` after a web save, `createCtx`/`destroyCtx` for the draft). The shell's table already names this category's symbol (`extern const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` in `SettingsUI.h`) and `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` defines it weak; this bead defines the strong `const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` in its own `Cat<Name>.cpp`, which includes `SettingsUI.h` before the definition (without the prior `extern` declaration a namespace-scope `const` object has internal linkage and the weak placeholder silently wins with no error), and edits neither `SettingsUI.cpp` nor `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` (the category beads run in parallel; no shared file). - Values, ranges, steps, wrap rules, formatting and choice lists come from `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.h` (host-tested); the category calls the model and never repeats a range.
