title: Build the settings row widgets: stepper, choice, toggle, locked, confirm and info rows
description:
Build the seven row widgets every settings category is made of, as LVGL objects sized for the shell's 320x56 slots: stepper, choice, toggle, action, locked (hold to unlock), confirm (hold to act) and info. Fill the shell's bench-only Fixture category with one of each so they can be exercised and measured before any real category exists.

## Context
- The shell (`src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.h`) creates rows through a category's `buildRow(ctx, index, parent, ui)` into a 320x56 parent slot, exposes `kRowW`/`kRowH`, defines `SettingsDebugTag {row, role}` (stored in `lv_obj_t::user_data`, roles `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`) and owns a `GM_TOUCH_PROBE`/`GAGGIMATE_SIM`-only Fixture category with 11 info rows, an enter/commit counter and one integer draft value.
- LVGL 8.4 pointer events on a pressed object: `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` at touch-down, `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED` 400 ms later (`LV_INDEV_DEF_LONG_PRESS_TIME`), `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` every 100 ms after that (`LV_INDEV_DEF_LONG_PRESS_REP_TIME`), `LV_EVENT_RELEASED` at lift, `LV_EVENT_CLICKED` after a release with no drag (also after a long hold), `LV_EVENT_PRESS_LOST` if the pointer leaves the object; `lv_conf.h` does not override the timings. Hit testing: `lv_indev_search_obj` visits children before the parent, `lv_obj_hit_test` honours each object's own disabled state, so disabling a row does not disable its children.
- Icons: `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_angle_left_40x40`, `img_angle_right_40x40`, `img_check_40x40` in `eez/images.h`, recoloured with `lv_obj_set_style_img_recolor(_opa)`; `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs are in the Montserrat fonts. Pressed feedback from `DefaultUI::applyPressedFeedback` covers `lv_imgbtn`, clickable `lv_img`, and `lv_btn` whose background opacity is at least 20 percent; transparent text rows get nothing from it and must style their own `LV_STATE_PRESSED` text/image colour.
- Row text: a 320 px row with two 56 px controls leaves about 200 px for label and value; values such as "Argentina/Buenos Aires" in Montserrat 20 are around 240 px wide, so a one-line layout cannot hold every label and value.
- Touch targets are audited with `tools/touchmap.py` (effective hit rect = coords grown by the ext click pad, clipped by ancestors without `LV_OBJ_FLAG_OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`; padding a button inside a tight row container gains nothing unless the row has that flag, see `applyClickArea` in `eez/actions.cpp`).

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsRows.h`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsRows.cpp`, and the Fixture category content in `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.cpp` (or a `SettingsFixture.cpp` beside it).

## Requirements
- Common: each row is created with `lv_obj_t *row = settingsRow*Create(parent, "Label", const SettingsDebugTag *tags, user)`, fills the 320x56 slot, has `bg_opa` 0, and carries its label as a direct child (Montserrat 18) and its value as a direct child (Montserrat 20), laid out as two lines (label above value at the left) when the value plus controls would not fit one line, with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT` truncation as the last resort; `settingsRowSetValue` copies the canonical string into row-owned storage (bounded, PSRAM or a fixed buffer) and the value tag's `text` points at it, because LVGL writes the dots into the label's own buffer and `lv_label_get_text` returns them. Each row exposes `settingsRowSetValue(row, const char *)`, `settingsRowSetEnabled(row, bool)` (dims text and icons, disables every interactive descendant, cancels pending holds; re-enabling never resumes a hold) and the user pointer, which callbacks receive. Row, value and every control get their debug tags.
- Stepper: minus and plus `lv_imgbtn` controls at the right; callback `onStep(user, int dir, bool fast)` once on `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` and once per `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` while held, never on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`; `fast` becomes true after 2 s of continuous hold measured from `PRESSED`; `RELEASED`, `PRESS_LOST`, disable, page removal and deletion end the hold. Hold and progress state (elapsed time, fast flag, unlock and confirm progress) is derived only from the events LVGL delivers to the row object; a free-standing `lv_timer` holding a row pointer is not acceptable (LVGL's `obj_del_core` resets the indev but delivers no cancel event, so such a timer would dangle after a page rebuild mid-hold). Each button's effective hit rectangle is at least 56x56 px and the two do not overlap.
- Choice: `<` and `>` arrows around the value; callback `onCycle(user, int dir)` with the same press-and-repeat protocol (no fast flag). Same target rules.
- Toggle: the whole row is the target (row object clickable, children not); the value shows "On"/"Off"; callback `onToggle(user, bool)` on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`. Pressed state visibly changes the text colour.
- Action: whole-row target, optional value, callback `onActivate(user)` once per completed tap (`LV_EVENT_CLICKED`), used for navigation rows (Schedules, a schedule entry, Add schedule).
- Locked: wraps a stepper. Locked state hides the buttons and shows a lock glyph (`LV_SYMBOL_EYE_CLOSE` or `LV_SYMBOL_WARNING` is acceptable) and "hold to unlock"; pressing the row for 1 s (measured from `PRESSED`, progress shown, for example a growing underline) unlocks, reveals the buttons and consumes the current press until release so the unlocking press cannot step; releasing earlier cancels; `settingsRowSetLocked(row, bool)` relocks; callback `onUnlocked(user)`.
- Confirm: whole-row target; holding 2 s with visible progress calls `onConfirm(user)` once; release before that cancels and resets; disabled rows ignore the hold.
- Info: label and value only, not clickable, no controls.
- Fixture category (`GM_TOUCH_PROBE` and `GAGGIMATE_SIM` builds only): rows 1..7 are one of each kind (stepper editing the shell's integer draft with step 1 and fast step 4, choice cycling a 3-entry list, toggle, action incrementing a counter, locked stepper on a second counter, confirm counting confirmations, info showing uptime), rows 8..11 stay info rows; the shell's `fixtureCounters()` exposes the draft value, action count, confirm count, lock state, the number of `LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` steps and the number of fast steps seen for the debug route.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` succeed; production RAM figure within 256 B of the previous commit.
- [ ] Simulator, then device, via `/api/debug/settingsui?cat=5`: `tools/touchmap.py --screens 0` with the Fixture category open reports every stepper button, choice arrow, toggle row, action row, locked row and confirm row with effective hit rectangles of at least 56x56 px, none overlapping, none within 12 px of the edge circle, each with its debug tag, and the value tags carry the canonical text.
- [ ] Through the synthetic tap route (`/api/debug/tap`): one tap on plus raises the draft by exactly 1 (PRESSED steps, CLICKED does not); a hold of 1500 ms raises it by 6..14 (one on press, then one per `LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT`, of which LVGL delivers at most one per `lv_task_handler` call, so the count follows the UI pass cadence and is not asserted more tightly); a 3000 ms hold ends with every repeat after the 2 s mark adding 4 (the draft delta equals `repeats_before + 4 * fast_repeats` from `fixtureCounters()`, and `fast_repeats` is at least 3); a 500 ms press on the locked row leaves it locked, a 1200 ms press unlocks it and does not step; a 1500 ms press on the confirm row does nothing, a 2500 ms press fires once; a tap on the toggle flips it and the value text follows; a tap on the action row increments its counter once.
- [ ] `settingsRowSetEnabled(false)` on the stepper leaves the draft unchanged under a 1500 ms hold on plus and dims the row; a rebuild during a hold (page change through the debug route) cancels the hold without a further step.

title: Add the synthetic tap route: TouchInject module with LVGL and SDL hooks, /api/debug/tap
description:
Give the bench and the simulator a way to touch the display over HTTP: a synthetic tap route with a hold duration, implemented as one driver-independent injection module that both the device's touch read callback and the simulator's mouse read callback consult, so the same scripted taps drive both venues.

## Context
- Device input: `touchpad_read` in `src/display/drivers/common/LV_Helper.cpp` polls the touch controller every `LV_INDEV_DEF_READ_PERIOD` (10 ms, when the UI task gets to it; a UI pass can take 100 ms or more, so samples are not evenly spaced), stamps press/release edges into `g_touchLog` (`TouchLogEntry`, 32 entries, served by `/api/debug/touchlog`) and, under `GM_TOUCH_PROBE`, the latency probe. `GM_TOUCH_PROBE` is defined in the `display-loadtest` and `display-qemu` envs (`platformio.ini`), never in `display`. `src/display/drivers/` is excluded from the simulator build.
- Simulator input: `mouse_read` in `sim/driver/SdlDriver.cpp` reports `s_mouseX/Y/Pressed`, which SDL events and `SdlDriver::injectPointer(x, y, pressed)` set. The sim's web server (`sim/web/ESPAsyncWebServer.cpp`) is pumped from the main loop (`gm_web_pump()`), so its handlers never race the firmware; the HTTP tap route needs nothing from the sim's `--script` mode (gm-bzu.13, other epic).

Add a bench-only HTTP route that opens, closes and navigates the settings UI and reports where it is, so scripted tests can reach any settings page directly and reset the display between scenarios without walking the menu by taps.

## Context
- The shell (`src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.h`) exposes `open()`, `close()`, `isOpen()`, `openCategory(int)`, `gotoPage(int)`, `popPage()`, a page stack, a published `State {open, depth, category, page, pages, title}` struct, and `fixtureCounters()` (enter/commit counters, draft value, action and confirm counts, lock state of the Fixture category that exists in `GM_TOUCH_PROBE` and `GAGGIMATE_SIM` builds).
- LVGL must only be touched from the UI task: web requests set a request that `DefaultUI::loop` consumes (see `serviceTouchMap` and `g_touchMapReq` in `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp` and `WebUIPlugin.cpp`); a plain request flag can be overwritten by a second request before the UI task sees the first, so completion must be reported per request.
- On the device the web handler runs on the async_tcp task while the UI task mutates the shell; on the simulator both run on one thread. `GM_TOUCH_PROBE` marks the bench builds (`display-loadtest`, `display-qemu`), `GAGGIMATE_SIM` the simulator; production has none of the debug UI hooks.

## Scope
Files: `src/display/plugins/WebUIPlugin.cpp`, `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp` (request queue and service), `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.h`.

## Requirements
- `/api/debug/settingsui` under `GM_TOUCH_PROBE` or `GAGGIMATE_SIM` only. GET without arguments returns the shell's last published `State` plus `fixture` (the counters) and `seq` (the id of the last completed command), copied under a mutex or as one atomically swapped struct so a reader never sees a half-updated state. One command per request: `open=1` (opens settings; if the active screen is not the menu the command first changes to the menu screen and completes on a following pass), `close=1` (unwinds every page, committing each, and closes), `cat=<index>` (from the tile page pushes that category; from inside a category pops to the tiles first, committing), `page=<n>` (jumps to that page of the open category), `pop=1` (one chevron). The response is `{"seq":n,"accepted":true}`; a request while a command is pending gets 409, a malformed or out-of-range argument 400, two commands in one request 400. The UI task executes the command on its next pass and publishes the new state with `seq`; scripts poll GET until `seq` matches.
- Every executed command logs `SettingsDbg: <command> -> depth=.. category=.. page=..`.
- Production build has no trace of the route.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display` RAM figure unchanged and `strings` on its ELF contains no `settingsui`; `pio run -e display-loadtest` and `pio run -e display-sim` succeed.

- [ ] `?open=1` twice in a row: the second is either 409 (pending) or a no-op; the touchmap shows one cover and `GM_LVMEM` `n` (device) is the same after the second call as after the first.
- [ ] `?cat=9` and `?page=-1` return 400; `?open=1&cat=2` returns 400.

- The checks above, scripted with `tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` (`settingsui()` and `settingsui_state()`), against the placeholder categories and the shell's 11-info-row Fixture.

title: Implement the Temperatures & timing category (offset, pressure rating, delays, auto-adjust)
description:
Implement the Temperatures & timing category: temperature offset and pressure sensor rating behind hold-to-unlock, brew and grind delay steppers, and the delay auto-adjust toggle, all saved when the category is left and reaching the controller board the way the web UI's save does.

## Context
- Fields (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `temperatureOffset` (int C, `setTemperatureOffset`), `pressureScaling` (float bar, `setPressureScaling`), `brewDelay`/`grindDelay` (double ms, `setBrewDelay`/`setGrindDelay`, both clamped to 0..4000 by the setter), `delayAdjust` (bool, `setDelayAdjust`).
- How the controller board learns about them: the boiler setpoint is `target + temperatureOffset`, computed in `Controller::updateControl` and sent in the next control batch whenever it changes, so a new offset reaches the board on the next `loopLogic` pass with no call needed; the web save additionally calls `controller->setTargetTemp(controller->getTargetTemp())`, which assigns the current mode's target back to itself, calls `updateLastAction()` and re-emits the `boiler:targetTemperature:change` event; none of that is needed to propagate an offset. `Controller::setPressureScale()` (public) sends the pressure scaling when the board reports the pressure capability. Delays are read when a process starts. `Controller::loopLogic` writes `brewDelay`/`grindDelay` itself after a shot when `delayAdjust` is on, and can still be finishing that after the UI has returned to the menu, so `commit` must write only fields the user touched.
- The Fixture and placeholder rows, the row widgets, model and shell are described below.

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatTemps.cpp` (defines `kCatTemps`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_temps.py`. `Controller.cpp` is not edited: the shell bead already wraps `loopLogic`'s delay auto-adjust writes in `Settings::Guard`.

## Requirements
- Rows, in this order and with these names: "Temperature offset" (locked stepper, model spec -20..20 C step 1), "Pressure sensor" (locked stepper, 1.0..30.0 bar step 0.1), "Brew delay" (stepper, 0..4000 ms step 50), "Grind delay" (same), "Delay auto-adjust" (toggle). One page. Title "Temperatures & timing", icon `img_thermometer_half_40x40`.
- All five deferred: edits go to the draft with touched flags; `commit` writes touched fields, calls `setPressureScale()` if the rating was written, logs `SettingsTemps: committed offset=%d scaling=%.1f brew=%d grind=%d adjust=%d` naming only the written fields, then triggers `settings:changed` if anything was written.
- `enter` relocks both locked rows; leaving and re-entering shows them locked again.
- Display formats from the model ("-3 C", "16.0 bar", "800 ms").

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` succeed.
- [ ] Simulator (then loadtest device with `synth(0)`), via `settingsui(cat=0)` and taps: the five rows show the current values parsed from GET `/api/settings` (`temperatureOffset`, `pressureScaling`, `brewDelay`, `grindDelay`, `delayAdjust`), read through the dump's `Temperature offset/value` and sibling tags.
- [ ] A tap on the offset row's plus does nothing while locked; a 1200 ms press on the row unlocks it and does not step; a plus tap then shows the value +1; `/api/settings` still shows the old value until `settingsui(pop=1)`, after which it shows the new one within 6 s and the log has one `SettingsTemps: committed offset=` line.
- [ ] Changing the pressure sensor from 16.0 to 16.1 and popping produces one `SettingsTemps: committed ... scaling=16.1` line and `/api/settings` reads 16.1 (on the device, also one `sendPressureScale` in the comms trace when the pressure capability is on).
- [ ] Holding brew delay plus for 1500 ms moves it by 450..700 ms (9..14 steps of 50) and the value text tracks; popping persists it. At 4000 a plus tap leaves 4000. Toggling auto-adjust and popping flips `delayAdjust`.
- [ ] Leaving with no change writes nothing: no `SettingsTemps: committed` line appears after a pop that followed no edit, and `/api/settings` is byte-identical for the five fields before and after (the global `Settings: Saving changed settings` line is not used as evidence: the periodic flush carries unrelated pending writes).
- [ ] Untouched fields survive external writes: with the page open, change `grindDelay` on the web UI; the row updates on the next pass (reconcile) and popping does not overwrite it.
- [ ] A forced external leave (standby timeout set to 1 min beforehand, or the sim mock's brew start) while the offset is edited but not yet popped still persists the edit.
- [ ] `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_temps.py` covers every check above that the instruments can observe.

## Out of scope
Steam pump assist, boiler fill (excluded by the interview).
## How a category plugs in (same for every category bead)
- Code against the header that landed with the shell, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.h`: a category is a `SettingsCategoryDef` (title, 40x40 icon, `rowCount`, `buildRow(ctx, index, parent, ui)`, `enter` once per push, `refresh` once per second while visible, `commit` exactly once when the page is removed by any route, `reconcile` after a web save, `createCtx`/`destroyCtx` for the draft). The shell's table already names this category's symbol (`extern const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` in `SettingsUI.h`) and `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` defines it weak; this bead defines the strong `const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` in its own `Cat<Name>.cpp`, which includes `SettingsUI.h` before the definition (without the prior `extern` declaration a namespace-scope `const` object has internal linkage and the weak placeholder silently wins with no error), and edits neither `SettingsUI.cpp` nor `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` (the category beads run in parallel; no shared file). Acceptance for every category: the toolchain's `nm` on the display ELF lists `kCat<Name>` as `R` or `D`, never `V`, and its page shows the bead's row names, not "Row n". Rows are created with the widgets in `SettingsRows.h` (stepper `onStep(user, dir, fast)`, choice `onCycle(user, dir)`, toggle `onToggle(user, bool)`, action `onActivate(user)`, locked stepper `onUnlocked(user)`, confirm `onConfirm(user)`, info) into the 320x56 slot the shell passes in, each with a `SettingsDebugTag` naming the row (the test scripts find rows and controls by these names, so use the row names given in the bead verbatim); five rows per page, the shell pages them and rebuilds rows on a page change, so row state lives in the category's `ctx`, never in a widget.
- Values, ranges, steps, wrap rules, formatting and choice lists come from `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.h` (host-tested); the category calls the model and never repeats a range.
- `enter` snapshots the current `Settings` values into the category's draft under `Settings::lock()`, clears the per-field "touched" flags and relocks locked rows. A live row writes `Settings` on every change, marks its field touched and remembers the value, then calls `ui.ui().markDirty()` so `DefaultUI::updateState` applies it on the next pass. A deferred row edits the draft and marks the field touched. `commit`, under `Settings::lock()`, writes touched deferred fields, re-asserts any touched live field whose `Settings` value no longer equals the visit's last value (a web save landed in between), calls `markDirty()` if a live field was re-asserted, and then, if anything was written, triggers `plugins().trigger("settings:changed")` once. `reconcile` re-reads only untouched fields from `Settings` and calls `rebuildPage()` when one changed. A visit with no edits makes no setter call and logs no category commit line; the global `Settings: Saving changed settings` line proves nothing either way, because the periodic flush carries every pending write on the device (live edits, restorations, Controller delay adjustments). `Settings` is reached through `controller().getSettings()`; a `Property::set` marks the property dirty and the 5 s flush persists it; GET `/api/settings` (read with the filter, never printing `wifiPassword`) is the oracle for what was written, in its wire format (timeouts in seconds, numeric strings for calibration values, `#rrggbb` colours).
- One source file per category under `src/display/ui/default/settings/` (for example `CatTemps.cpp`) holding the strong `kCat<Name>` definition; a scenario file `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_<category>.py` built on `rig.py` that runs against the simulator by default (`Sim` launcher) and against the device with `--host`, logs every step, exits non-zero on the first failed assertion, and restores every value it changed by driving the UI back (never by POSTing `/api/settings`), reporting what it could not restore.
## Shared contract (identical in every bead of this epic)

- Code-built LVGL, not EEZ Studio. The settings UI lives in `src/display/ui/default/settings/` and is built with `lv_*` calls; the runtime-built scale overlay (`DefaultUI::buildScaleScreen` in `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`) is the precedent for construction and for delete-event pointer cleanup. It is one full-screen cover object created as a child of `objects.menu_screen_new` when settings opens and deleted when it closes. The flow screen never changes while settings is open (`currentScreen` stays `SCREEN_ID_MENU_SCREEN_NEW`), so the animation host, plate handling and screen-change code in DefaultUI are untouched. While the cover is up, every direct child of the menu screen except `objects.status_icons` is hidden (their original visibility captured and restored on close); the flow tick keeps driving flags on the menu's individual tiles and icons, which is why parents are hidden, never individual flow-controlled children.
- Look: the current style. Text and icons in `theme_colors[eez_flow_get_selected_theme_index()][0]`, backgrounds in `theme_colors[..][1]`; fonts `lv_font_montserrat_16/18/20/24` (34 and 48 exist for large values); icons from `src/display/ui/default/eez/images.h` (`img_angle_up/down/left/right_40x40`, `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_check_40x40`, `img_thermometer_half_40x40`, `img_clock_40x40`, `img_settings_40x40`, `img_info_40x40`, `img_tachometer_fast_40x40`, `img_power_40x40`) recoloured with the accent, or `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs from the Montserrat fonts. Page title in Montserrat 24 below the status icons (which sit at y 20..40). The exit chevron is `img_angle_up_40x40` at `LV_ALIGN_CENTER` + 210 px with `lv_obj_set_ext_click_area(btn, 45)`, exactly where every other screen has it; its hit rectangle is clipped by the screen to 130x95 px and it is exempt from the size and edge rules below. No translucent plates over the animation: rows are text and icons directly on the screen background (the cover has `bg_opa` 0, so the theme background or the animation shows through, whichever the menu screen has). Every translucent pixel costs blend time per animation frame (CLAUDE.md, UI-pipeline invariants). Text that does not fit its slot is truncated with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT`; the row keeps the canonical value string in its own storage and the debug dump exports that (the label's buffer holds the dots, `lv_label_get_text` returns them).
- Geometry: 480x480 round panel, 0.111 mm/px. For every tappable target except the exit chevron: its effective hit rectangle (coords grown by its ext click pad, clipped by every ancestor without `LV_OBJ_FLAG_OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`; `tools/touchmap.py` and `tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` compute this from the dumped absolute coords, which already include any translate) is at least 56x56 px, no two hit rectangles on one page overlap, and no hit rectangle reaches within 12 px of the panel edge circle (radius 240 around 240,240). Row widgets are 320x56 px, five rows per page. Every settings object that a test must find carries a `SettingsDebugTag` (row name, role: `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `exit`, `tile`, `cover`, and for role `value` a pointer to the row-owned canonical value string) in its LVGL `user_data`; the touchmap dump exports the tag, and for value tags the canonical text in full, for descendants of the cover.
- Interaction: steppers step once on `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` and once on each `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` (LVGL defaults: `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED` 400 ms after press, then a repeat every 100 ms; no step on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`), and report `fast` after 2 s of continuous hold, whereupon the field's `fastStep` from the model applies (there is no universal multiplier). LVGL delivers at most one `LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` per `lv_task_handler` call and resets its repeat timestamp on each, so the number of repeats in a hold depends on the UI pass cadence (a 100 ms rerender pass yields one repeat per pass); tests assert the protocol (one step per event, none on CLICKED) and wide count windows, never an exact cadence. Holds are cancelled by `LV_EVENT_RELEASED`, `LV_EVENT_PRESS_LOST`, disabling the row, page removal and deletion; hold and progress state lives in the row object and is driven only by the events LVGL delivers to it (PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT, RELEASED, PRESS_LOST, DELETE), never by a free-standing `lv_timer` that could outlive the row. Choices show `< value >` and cycle with the arrows, wrapping at both ends, arrows repeating while held. Toggles flip on tap. Locked rows (calibration) unlock after a 1 s press on the row, consume that press until release, and relock whenever the category is left. Confirm rows (Restart, Remove schedule) act once after a 2 s hold with visible progress and cancel on release. `setEnabled(false)` disables every interactive descendant and cancels pending holds.
- Saving: visual settings apply on every change (brightness, animation, frame rate, all-screens, theme, gradient, plates, tint, scrim) and each live write is followed by `ui->markDirty()` so `DefaultUI::updateState` applies it on the next pass rather than after the 2.5 s idle rerender interval. Everything else is written to `Settings` when the category is left, by any route the UI task can see (exit chevron, standby timeout, controller mode change, brew start, any flow screen change), and never lost on those routes. A category's `commit` writes only the fields the user changed. A web UI save while a category is open does not close it: the web values land first, the shell refreshes every row the user has not touched from `Settings` on the next pass after `settings:changed`, and the user's touched fields keep their draft and win at commit (per field, last writer wins). A web-requested restart (`/api/settings` POST with `restart`) reboots from the web task at once; an uncommitted display draft is lost then, the same as a power cut, and that is accepted. `Settings` properties mark themselves dirty on `set` and `Settings::loopTask` flushes every dirty property to NVS every 5 s (a flush is one or more NVS key writes, each stalling the flash cache for a scan-out slip); live rows therefore reach flash through the periodic saver while the category is still open, deferred fields become dirty only at commit, and nothing calls an immediate save per step. Concurrency: `Settings::lock()` (a FreeRTOS recursive mutex added by the shell bead, a no-op on the simulator's single thread) serialises whole transactions: the web save's `batchUpdate`, `doSave` (periodic flush, `save(true)`, `flushNow`), a category's `enter` snapshot and `commit`, and `Controller::loopLogic`'s delay auto-adjust writes. Between transactions the rule is per field, last writer wins; readers outside a transaction (`DefaultUI::updateState`) are unchanged.
- Activity: every touch inside settings calls `controller->updateLastAction()` so the standby timeout (`Controller::loopLogic`: `now > lastAction + settings.getStandbyTimeout()`, on the logic task on the device and in the one main loop on the simulator) does not fire mid-edit.
- Memory: immutable lookup tables are `const` PODs in flash (a `const std::vector` or `String` is not); runtime drafts, strings and callback contexts are small, bounded and owned by the shell for the life of the cover; anything sizeable goes to PSRAM; settings code never touches the animation hot slab (`bganim::allocHot`). LVGL objects allocate from PSRAM through `gm_lv_malloc`, so widget count is not an internal-DRAM concern, but plain C++ allocations are, and `/api/debug/heap` (`int_free`, `dma_free`) is read with the largest page and draft open.
- Wire format of GET `/api/settings` (the oracle for what was written): `standbyTimeout` and `standbyBrightnessTimeout` are in seconds (stored in ms), `temperatureOffset` and `pressureScaling` are numeric strings, `bgAnimPlateColor` and `elementTintColor` are `#rrggbb` strings, `startupMode` is `standby` or `brew`, `autowakeupSchedules` is `HH:MM|ddddddd;...` (Mon..Sun). Scripts parse before comparing.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`pio run -e display-sim`, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy GM_SIM_PORT=<port> ./.pio/build/display-sim/program`, web server on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (8080 by default), state under `sim_data/` in the working directory; the build is repaired by gm-bzu.9), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` build at 192.168.1.121). The simulator runs the LVGL UI, Settings, the web server and the debug routes on one cooperative thread with no panel and no background animation renderer (`SleepAnimation` is a stub under `GAGGIMATE_SIM` and `updateState` skips animation and plate application): it verifies navigation, interaction, values, persistence and theme colours. Animation frame counters, the applied frame-rate cap, rendered gradients, plate pixels, memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only, and a simulator pass says nothing about the device's concurrency (TouchInject's critical section and the Settings lock are reviewed on their own merits). Build note: a new or deleted source file under `src/` needs `touch src/CMakeLists.txt` before the ESP-IDF envs pick it up (the glob has no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS); when a symbol's provenance matters, check the ELF with the toolchain's `nm` (`~/.platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf/bin/xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`).
- Rules: never POST `/api/settings` by hand (the web UI is the only safe writer) and never print the `wifiPassword` field of GET `/api/settings`; scripts read it through a filter that drops that key. No em dashes or double hyphens in prose, comments or commit messages.
close_reason: Implemented CatTemps.cpp (kCatTemps) and test_temps.py; all builds pass and the sim scenario passes 44/44 checks (2 device-only skips). Commits 9d49dde6, 594ee7c9.

title: Implement the Display category (brightness, dim timeout, clock format, time zone) with live TZ apply
description:
Implement the Display category: main brightness applied live, standby brightness, the standby dim timeout, the 24-hour clock toggle, and the time zone as a region row and a city row, with the zone applied to the running clock without a reboot.

## Context
- Fields (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `mainBrightness` (1..16, `setMainBrightness`), `standbyBrightness` (0..16, `setStandbyBrightness`), `standbyBrightnessTimeout` (ms, `setStandbyBrightnessTimeout`), `clock24hFormat` (`setClockFormat(bool)`), `timezone` (IANA name string, `setTimezone`).
- Brightness reaches the panel through `DefaultUI::setBrightness(int)` (declared in `DefaultUI.h`, logs `Display: brightness %d` since the shell bead; this bead does not edit `DefaultUI.h`), which `handleScreenChange` calls with `getMainBrightness()` when leaving standby and `loop` calls with `getStandbyBrightness()` after `standbyBrightnessTimeout` on the standby screen. The standby clock text is formatted in `DefaultUI` (`strftime` with `isClock24hFormat()`).
- The time zone is applied once at boot in `Controller::startNtp()` (`configTzTime`, `setenv("TZ", resolve_timezone(name), 1)`, `tzset()`), guarded by `ntpStarted`, so a changed setting takes effect only after a reboot today. `resolve_timezone` is in `src/display/core/zones.h`.
- The model provides the zone split (`regionCount`, `regionName`, `cityCount`, `cityLabel`, `zoneName`, `locate`) and the numeric specs and formats ("1:30" for the dim timeout).

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatDisplay.cpp` (defines `kCatDisplay`), `src/display/core/Controller.h` and `Controller.cpp` (new `applyTimezone()`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_display.py`.

## Requirements
- Rows, in this order and with these names: "Main brightness" (stepper 1..16, live: `setMainBrightness`, `ui().setBrightness()` and `markDirty()` on each step), "Standby brightness" (stepper 0..16, deferred), "Dim after" (stepper, 30 s..30 min in 30 s steps, shown m:ss, deferred), "24-hour clock" (toggle, deferred), "Time zone region" (choice over the model's regions, deferred), "City" (choice over the region's cities, repeating while held, deferred; changing the region selects that region's first city). Two pages. Title "Display", icon `img_tachometer_fast_40x40` or `img_clock_40x40`.
- `Controller::applyTimezone()`: sets `TZ` from `resolve_timezone(settings.getTimezone())` and calls `tzset()`; safe to call at any time after boot, does not touch SNTP. `startNtp` keeps its behaviour.
- `commit`: writes changed fields; if the zone changed calls `applyTimezone()`; triggers `settings:changed` if anything changed and, if anything was written, logs `SettingsDisplay: committed <field>=<value> ...` naming only the written fields (mirroring `SettingsTemps: committed`). Main brightness is already applied live; if the user leaves via the standby timeout the standby brightness path takes over as it does today.
- `enter` locates the stored zone in the model (`locate`); a stored name that is not in the table shows the model's fallback (region "Etc", city "UTC") without writing anything until the user changes a zone row.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` succeed.
- [ ] Simulator (then loadtest device with `synth(0)`), via `settingsui(cat=1)` and taps: the six rows show the stored values (`mainBrightness`, `standbyBrightness`, `standbyBrightnessTimeout` in seconds formatted m:ss, `clock24hFormat`, and the region and city of `timezone` from GET `/api/settings`), read through the dump's value tags.
- [ ] Tapping main brightness minus changes the backlight at once (device: the info log line `Display: brightness %d` that the shell bead added to `DefaultUI::setBrightness`, or the camera burst `C:\work\camshots\burst.bat` comparing mean frame brightness; sim: the log line) and `/api/settings` shows the new value within 6 s without leaving the category.
- [ ] Setting the region to "Pacific" and the city to "Kiritimati", then `settingsui(pop=1)`: `/api/settings` `timezone` is `Pacific/Kiritimati` within 6 s and the standby clock (screen 1, read through the dump's label texts) shows the UTC+14 time within 2 s, with no reboot; setting it back restores the original time. Requires a synchronised clock (sim: host time; device: NTP).
- [ ] Holding the city `>` for 1500 ms advances 9..14 cities; the region wraps from the last to the first and the city resets to that region's first.
- [ ] Dim after from 1:00 stepping up twice shows 2:00 and `/api/settings` reads `standbyBrightnessTimeout` 120 (seconds) after pop. The 24-hour toggle persists and the standby clock format follows it on the next standby entry.
- [ ] Leaving with no change writes nothing (no `SettingsDisplay: committed` line, the six fields on `/api/settings` byte-identical). A web save of `standbyBrightness` while the page is open shows on the row (reconcile) and is not overwritten by the pop; a web save of `mainBrightness` after the display changed it in the same visit is re-asserted by the pop (touched live field wins) and `Display: brightness` logs the display's value.
- [ ] `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_display.py` covers the checks above that the instruments can observe and restores the starting values through the UI (it refuses to start, with a message, when the stored dim timeout or zone is not representable on the model's grid, so restoration stays possible).

Every translucent pixel costs blend time per animation frame (CLAUDE.md, UI-pipeline invariants). Text that does not fit its slot is truncated with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT`; the row keeps the canonical value string in its own storage and the debug dump exports that (the label's buffer holds the dots, `lv_label_get_text` returns them).
- Geometry: 480x480 round panel, 0.111 mm/px. title: Implement the Animation category (animation, fps, theme, gradient, plates, tint, scrim) all live
description:
Implement the Animation category: eleven live rows that change the background animation, its frame rate, whether it runs on all screens, the UI theme, the gradient the current animation draws with, the plate mode, colour and opacity, the element tint and its colour, and the text scrim, every one applied on the spot through the same Settings properties the web UI writes.

## Context
- Fields and setters (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `bgAnimId` (`setBgAnimId`), `bgAnimFps` (`setBgAnimFps`, 5..60), `bgAnimAllScreens` (`setBgAnimAllScreens`, default false), `themeMode` (`setThemeMode`, 0 Dark, 1 Light), `bgAnimThemeMap` (`setBgAnimThemeMap`, the per-animation gradient refs), `bgAnimTheme` (the global built-in used by animations with an empty map entry), `bgAnimGradients` (the user library, read-only here, empty by default), `bgAnimClearPlates` (`setBgAnimClearPlates`, 0 keep, 1 hide, 2 custom), `bgAnimPlateColor` (`setBgAnimPlateColor`, 0xRRGGBB), `bgAnimPlateOpacity` (`setBgAnimPlateOpacity`, 0..100), `elementTintEnabled`/`elementTintColor` (`setElementTintEnabled`/`setElementTintColor`), `bgAnimScrim` (`setBgAnimScrim`, 0..100).
- Live application already exists for the web UI: `DefaultUI::updateState` (`src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`) compares these properties on every rerender pass and applies changes (animation switch with init/release of its tables, `sleepAnimation.setMaxFps`, theme via `change_color_theme`, plates via `applyAnimPlates` on the screens that carry plates, which the menu does not, tint by rewriting `theme_colors` slot 0, scrim and all-screens through the animation). A rerender pass runs every 2.5 s when idle, so a live write must be followed by `markDirty()`. `change_color_theme` recolours the generated objects only; the shell restyles its own rows when the theme or accent changes.
- The web gradient editor's preview (`bganim:preview` event, 15 s hold per message, `previewAnim`/`previewStops` in DefaultUI) overrides the drawn animation and gradient while active; the web save ends it with `pluginManager->trigger("bganim:preview-end")`.
- Animation names and gradient lists come from the model (`SettingsModel.h`: animation choice list from `bg_animation(i).name`, gradient list for animation N as Default + built-ins + library names with read/write of the map ref, the 12-colour palette with an off-palette 13th entry).
- Switching animations rebuilds tables from the 12 KB hot slab (`bganim::allocHot`); `/api/debug/heap` reports `int_free`, `psram_free`, `hot_used`, `hot_fail`, `uptime_ms`; `/api/debug/anim` reports `anim_id`, `uptime_ms`, the frame counter and the cap.

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatAnimation.cpp` (defines `kCatAnimation`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py`.

## Requirements
- Rows, in this order and with these names: "Animation" (choice, names), "Frame rate" (stepper 5..60 step 5), "All screens" (toggle), "Theme" (choice Dark/Light), "Gradient" (choice for the current animation: Default, built-ins, library), "Plates" (choice Keep/Hide/Custom), "Plate colour" (palette choice), "Plate opacity" (stepper 0..100 step 5), "Element tint" (toggle), "Tint colour" (palette choice), "Text scrim" (stepper 0..100 step 5). Three pages. Title "Animation", icon `img_settings_40x40` or a Montserrat symbol.
- Every row writes its Settings property immediately, marks its field touched with the value, and calls `markDirty()`; a change to Animation or Gradient also triggers `bganim:preview-end` so a running web preview does not mask it. `reconcile` re-reads only untouched fields; `commit` re-asserts any touched field whose Settings value no longer equals the visit's last value (a web save landed in between), calls `markDirty()` if it did, and triggers `settings:changed` once if the visit wrote anything.
- The Gradient row's value shows the name; for Default it shows "Default (<global theme name>)". Changing Animation re-reads the Gradient row's value for the new animation.
- Plate colour and Plate opacity rows are enabled only when Plates is Custom; Tint colour only when Element tint is on (`settingsRowSetEnabled`, re-evaluated on each change).
- An off-palette stored colour stays selectable as its hex entry for the whole visit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` succeed; production RAM figure within 256 B of the previous commit.
- [ ] Simulator (then loadtest device with `synth(0)`), via `settingsui(cat=2)`: the eleven rows show the stored values as GET `/api/settings` reports them (the model's animation names and gradient parsing are host code, so the sim shows them without a renderer) (`bgAnimId` by name, `bgAnimFps`, `bgAnimAllScreens`, `themeMode`, the map ref of the current animation by name, `bgAnimClearPlates`, colours by palette name or hex, `bgAnimPlateOpacity`, `elementTintEnabled`, `elementTintColor`, `bgAnimScrim`).
- [ ] Device: one tap on Animation `>` changes `bgAnimId` on `/api/settings` within 6 s and `/api/debug/anim` `anim_id` within 500 ms; cycling through every animation once (a tap per second, with all-screens on so the change is visible under the page) ends with `int_free` within 2 KB of the start, `hot_fail` unchanged and `uptime_ms` monotonic (no reboot).
- [ ] Device: Frame rate 30 to 60 makes `/api/debug/anim` report cap 60 within 500 ms and `/api/settings` `bgAnimFps` 60. The rate assertion (passive frame-counter delta over 5 s rises, then falls back at 30) runs only when All screens is on, the animation is orbits and `/api/debug/anim` confirms interlace active with no renderer debug override; otherwise the scenario reports the rate check as unsupported for the stored configuration (`bgAnimInterlace` defaults to 0 and a full-frame loop cannot exceed about 25 fps, CLAUDE.md). On the sim only the stored value is checked (no renderer).
- [ ] Theme Dark to Light recolours the settings page's own labels to the light theme's accent within 500 ms (sample the framebuffer at a label's pixels or the sim screenshot) and back; the web UI's Display tab shows `themeMode` 1 after the change.
- [ ] Gradient: choosing a library gradient (the scenario first creates one through the web UI if the library is empty, and removes it afterwards) writes a `c<id>` ref for the current animation only (`bgAnimThemeMap` differs in exactly that entry) and the web UI still loads the Display tab; choosing Default clears the entry. A change made while a web preview is active takes effect at once (preview ended).
- [ ] Plates Custom enables the colour and opacity rows; Keep or Hide disables them (taps ignored); the same for Element tint and Tint colour. After popping and opening the brew screen, the plates reflect the chosen mode and colour (device framebuffer at a plate pixel; the sim has no plate rendering, so there only the stored values are checked).
- [ ] A visit that changes nothing writes nothing (no setter call: the eleven fields on `/api/settings` byte-identical before and after; the global save log is not evidence).
- [ ] Touched field precedence: change Frame rate on the display, then save a different `bgAnimFps` from the web UI while the page is open, then pop: `/api/settings` shows the display's value within 6 s.
- [ ] `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py` covers the checks above the instruments can observe on the current venue and restores the starting values through the UI.

Per-animation parameters (`bgAnimParams`), half resolution, interlace, brightness and highlight knee, the gradient editor (web UI only), panel clock and VCOM.

The shell's table already names this category's symbol (`extern const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` in `SettingsUI.h`) and `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` defines it weak; this bead defines the strong `const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` in its own `Cat<Name>.cpp`, which includes `SettingsUI.h` before the definition (without the prior `extern` declaration a namespace-scope `const` object has internal linkage and the weak placeholder silently wins with no error), and edits neither `SettingsUI.cpp` nor `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` (the category beads run in parallel; no shared file). - Values, ranges, steps, wrap rules, formatting and choice lists come from `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.h` (host-tested); the category calls the model and never repeats a range.

Animation frame counters, the applied frame-rate cap, rendered gradients, plate pixels, memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only, and a simulator pass says nothing about the device's concurrency (TouchInject's critical section and the Settings lock are reviewed on their own merits). Build note: a new or deleted source file under `src/` needs `touch src/CMakeLists.txt` before the ESP-IDF envs pick it up (the glob has no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS); when a symbol's provenance matters, check the ELF with the toolchain's `nm` (`~/.platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf/bin/xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`).
- Rules: never POST `/api/settings` by hand (the web UI is the only safe writer) and never print the `wifiPassword` field of GET `/api/settings`; scripts read it through a filter that drops that key. No em dashes or double hyphens in prose, comments or commit messages.
close_reason: Landed in eed10a33, 501b60cb, bc0a3d89, 7bc8f2bf (per-animation gradient touched-state after Codex review); test_animation.py 49/49 on the simulator, verified by the leader after the worker was lost to a reboot

title: Settings form: name the refused fields when a save answers 422
description: Since gm-nov3.26 the settings POST answers HTTP 422 with {"error":"invalid fields","code":"invalid_fields","fields":[...]} when a posted field fails validation (bgAnimGradients, bgAnimThemeMap, autowakeupSchedules, a non-empty apPassword under 8 characters). Every valid field in the same save is stored. The form's onSubmit (web/src/pages/Settings/index.jsx) already keeps its edits on any non-2xx answer and shows data.error, so the user sees the bare text 'invalid fields' with a Retry button and no field names. Change: when data.code is invalid_fields, show which settings were refused, by their form labels, and say the rest was saved. Retrying unchanged will fail the same way, so the message should ask the user to correct those fields. A refetch of /api/settings after a 422 would show the stored values of the fields that did save.
notes:
Commit 0afac2ca on idf5. Changed: web/src/pages/Settings/index.jsx. Added
FIELD_LABELS (apPassword -> Access Point Password, bgAnimGradients ->
Custom gradients, bgAnimThemeMap -> Animation colour assignments,
autowakeupSchedules -> Auto Wakeup Schedule; these are the only keys
WebUIPlugin.cpp's handler can push into the 422 fields array) and
describeInvalidFields(), which builds the message listing the refused
fields' labels, states the rest of the save was stored, and asks the
user to fix them and save again. onSubmit now reads data.code ===
'invalid_fields' and data.fields (array) and uses this message instead
of the bare "invalid fields" text; saveError carries an invalidFields
flag so the banner heading reads "Partly saved." instead of "Not
saved." for this case. The form still keeps every edit in formData as
before (unchanged behaviour); no refetch of /api/settings was added,
matching the leader's stated design (keep edits, name fields, say the
rest was saved).

Not done: no Playwright setup for the web UI was found in the repo or

was not rendered in a browser at phone or desktop width. Left for the

Agent-mail at 127.0.0.1:8765 did not answer (curl to /health and /mcp/
