title: Allow the display picker to select saved gradient IDs above 13
description:
Commit 3b0db5a7 added an incorrect ID limit in GradientSwatch.cpp:66. It confuses the twelve-entry library capacity with the accepted ID range of 1 through 99999. Commit 265501e0 then made this resolver the selection gate in CatGradientPicker.cpp:204.

A valid saved entry such as `14|Saved|112233,445566` appears in My gradients but has no swatch. Tapping it closes the picker without assigning c14. The web nextGradientId function can allocate 14 during ordinary copying and deletion.

Make swatch ref parsing agree with the production ref grammar, including its digit limit and malformed-input handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolver tests accept existing entries c14 and c99999 and compare their ramps with the production library resolution.
- [ ] Tests reject zero, out-of-range IDs, excessive digits, trailing junk and missing entries without integer overflow.
- [ ] Simulator checks choose a saved ID above 13 through Gradient all, Gradient and Standby grad, then verify the exact stored ref, row value and visible swatch.
- [ ] Selection preserves unrelated map slots and applies the existing rollback mirror policy.
- [ ] The swatch parity harness and animation runner pass with the new fixtures.

title: Show the retained global gradient draft after a web save
description:
Commit 2fd637eb changed the global row label to read stored settings through globalGradientLabel. Commit 265501e0 added a swatch and picker marker that also read stored settings.

CatAnimation.cpp preserves ctx->globalGradientRef when globalGradientTouched is true, and animCommit later restores that ref. However, animBuildRow and the global picker's currentRef callback display the intervening web value.

Make the global row label, swatch and selected marker describe the retained draft when the display has touched that field. Untouched fields must continue following web saves. Preserve the accurate read-only legacy fallback representation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A simulator test selects global ref A on the display, saves a distinct ref B through the web path, and verifies B actually reached Settings before checking reconciliation.
- [x] With the Animation category visible, its global label and swatch continue showing retained draft A; exiting commits A with its correct mirror.
- [x] Repeat while each picker level is open. The marker and the parent row shown after cancellation agree with A.
- [x] An untouched-global variant follows B through the row, swatch, picker marker and category exit.
- [x] Legacy fallback fixtures remain accurately named and opening or cancelling does not write gradient settings.
notes:
Fixed in 35f3edd3.

What changed. CatAnimation.cpp grew one helper, globalRefInEffect(), and every
reading of the global gradient now goes through it: globalGradientChoiceIndex
(so the row label), legacyCustomFallbackActive (so the "Custom (legacy)" name),
applyRowSwatch by way of settingsGlobalGradientRef (so the row swatch), the
"Global (name)" text on the per-animation rows, the global picker's currentRef
callback, and the two exported functions CatGradientPicker.cpp calls for its own
Global entry. It returns the visit's draft while the category is open and that
row has been touched, and the stored field otherwise. A file-static pointer to
the open category's context, set in animCreateCtx and cleared in animDestroyCtx,
is what lets the two exported functions reach the draft; the shell creates and
destroys that context on push and pop, so at most one is ever live.

No change was needed in CatGradientPicker.cpp or GradientSwatch.cpp, which
another agent held. Line 564 of the bead's trace is the global picker's
currentRef lambda and it is in CatAnimation.cpp.

The per-animation Gradient row and the Standby grad row did not share the
defect. Their draft is kept per animation id, and draftRefForAnim was already
the single reading of it: the rows read ctx->gradientRef/standbyGradientRef,
reconcile keeps them when touched, and both pickers' currentRef callbacks call
draftRefForAnim. The global was the exception and now follows the same shape.

Residual, recorded not fixed: the panel keeps drawing the web's gradient until
the category is left, because the row writes Settings the moment it changes and
the web save overwrote that write. The exit puts the display's choice back with
its legacy mirror. Making the display re-assert a touched live field at
reconcile time would be a change to the commit-time precedence rule for every
field, not just this one, so it was not done here.

Evidence. New simulator scenario tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py,
registered in tools/settings_ui_test.py between animation and machine, skipped
on a device venue because every check needs the web save route. Run against a
build with the fix reverted: 8 of 34 checks failed, all on the display side
(row text, row swatch, per-animation row, picker marker at both levels, row
after cancellation), while the two commit checks passed, which is exactly the
split this bead describes. With the fix: 35 of 35 pass, standalone and through
the runner.

Acceptance criteria, all checked:

1. Done. store() POSTs through web_save and reads the field back from
   GET /api/settings before any UI assertion (checks untouched_setup_a,
   touched_setup, touched_web_save_landed, touched_web_save_under_picker_landed,
   legacy_setup). A rejected POST fails the check rather than passing silently.
2. Done. touched_row_keeps_draft, touched_swatch_keeps_draft (framebuffer
   pixels against the same row's ramp captured while A was stored),
   touched_per_anim_row_names_draft, touched_exit_commits_draft,
   touched_exit_mirrors_draft.
3. Done. touched_picker_group_marks_draft and touched_picker_gradient_marks_draft
   cover both levels, touched_picker_group_keeps_draft covers a third web save
   landing under the open picker, and touched_row_after_cancel and
   touched_swatch_after_cancel cover the parent row after cancelling out of both
   levels. The under-picker save also adds a library entry, and the check waits
   for "My gradients" to appear before judging the marker, so a marker that had
   simply not been redrawn cannot pass.
4. Done. untouched_row_follows_web, untouched_swatch_follows_web,
   untouched_picker_marks_web_group, untouched_picker_marks_web_gradient,
   untouched_row_after_cancel, untouched_exit_keeps_web_value.
5. Done. legacy_row_named ("Custom (legacy)"), legacy_row_has_no_swatch,
   legacy_per_anim_row_named ("Global (Custom (legacy))"),
   legacy_picker_marks_nothing, legacy_visit_writes_nothing (the five gradient
   fields byte for byte around a visit that opens and cancels the picker).
   These five pass before the fix as well: they are the regression guard the
   criterion asks for, not a bug.

Also ran: the animation scenario, 213 checks, none failed, so the shared helpers
and the category are unharmed; pio test -e native_settingsui, 68 cases;
pio run -e display-loadtest, success.

Not run: pio run -e display, which does not link in this worktree on WSL1
(Nanopb unpack permission error), and nothing on the bench board, which another
agent holds. The runner's own post-scenario restart step crashed on the last
run because another agent's PlatformIO build deleted .pio/build mid-run; both
scenarios had already passed in that run.

title: Keep gradient validation and assignment in one settings transaction
description:
Commit 265501e0 releases Settings::Guard after resolving a selected ref in CatGradientPicker.cpp:202, before invoking onPick at line 217. animGradientPicked takes a separate guard for its map write, while globalGradientPicked writes the global ref and mirror without a surrounding transaction.

Inference from the device lock scopes: a web library deletion can land between validation and assignment, allowing the picker to publish a ref whose entry has already disappeared. The simulator's cooperative thread and no-op guard cannot reproduce this interleaving.

Keep current-data validation and the resulting settings assignment in one guarded transaction. Include the global ref and rollback mirror in that transaction. Preserve captured-slot behavior and release the guard safely around page teardown and other side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Source inspection confirms that no web batchUpdate can interleave between selected-ref validation and its map or global assignment.
- [ ] A controlled concurrency regression covers deletion before validation and an attempted deletion during the selection transaction. Selection never writes a ref validated against an already superseded library.
- [ ] The global ref and its mirror cannot be split by a web settings transaction.
- [ ] Invalid refs and invalid targets close without marking a new selection as touched.
- [ ] Existing simulator navigation, web-interference and teardown checks pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Source inspection confirms that no web batchUpdate can interleave between selected-ref validation and its map or global assignment.
- [x] A controlled concurrency regression covers deletion before validation and an attempted deletion during the selection transaction. Selection never writes a ref validated against an already superseded library.
- [x] The global ref and its mirror cannot be split by a web settings transaction.
- [x] Invalid refs and invalid targets close without marking a new selection as touched.
- [x] Existing simulator navigation, web-interference and teardown checks pass.
notes:
Done in b0305ca0.

What changed. New header src/display/ui/default/settings/GradientPickTransaction.h:
one function, gradientPickTransaction, that holds a guard over its whole body and
does three things inside it, resolve the ref, check the target slot, assign. It is a
function rather than a second Settings::Guard at the call site so that a later reader
cannot shorten the scope without deleting the function. CatGradientPicker.cpp's
applyPick supplies the production side (Settings::Guard, the stored library, the
spec's callbacks) and keeps popPages outside the transaction, since that deletes LVGL
objects and runs the opening category's own commit. CatAnimation.cpp is untouched: it
was held by another agent, and the fix did not need it, because the picker's guard now
covers whatever onPick writes.

Acceptance criteria.

[x] No web batchUpdate can interleave between validation and assignment. Source
    inspection plus the host test below. The guard is Settings::Guard, which is
    recursive, so animGradientPicked's own guard for the read-modify-write of the map
    string nests inside the picker's.

[x] Controlled concurrency regression. Group L of test/test_settings_model
    (pio test -e native_settingsui), seven cases, covering a deletion before the tap
    and a deletion attempted during the transaction, for the picked ref and for an
    unrelated one. They instantiate the production template against a fake Settings
    with a modelled lock and a web writer that blocks while the lock is held and lands
    at the release. Proof that they can fail: a scratch copy of the header with the
    transaction split the old way, compiled in a temporary directory that shadowed the
    real header (the shared tree never held the broken version), fails two of the seven
    (excludes_a_deletion_during_the_transaction, excludes_an_unrelated_deletion_too).
    Against the shipped header, 68 of 68 pass.

[x] The global ref and its mirror cannot be split. globalGradientPicked writes
    bgAnimGradientRef and then mirrorGlobalRefIntoLegacyTheme with no guard of its own;
    both now run inside the picker's transaction. Source inspection only.

[x] Invalid refs and invalid targets close without marking a new selection as touched.
    onPick is the only thing that sets the touched flags and it is skipped on both
    paths. Source inspection plus two host cases that assert nothing was assigned.

[x] Existing simulator checks pass. tools/settings_ui_test.py --only animation:
    PASS, 213 checks, 0 failed, 4 pages audited clean. The picker's navigation,
    web-interference and teardown checks are in that scenario and ran (confirmed by
    their per-check log lines, not just the total).

Limits, stated plainly. The simulator cannot show this bug or the fix: its
Settings::Guard is a no-op and everything runs on one cooperative thread, so the
simulator scenario above passes with or without the change. The host test exercises the
real production template but a modelled lock, so it proves the transaction's shape, not
that the device's Settings::Guard is a real mutex (that is Settings.cpp's
xSemaphoreTakeRecursive, untouched here). Nothing was run on the bench board: this
agent did not hold it.

One behaviour change worth knowing. onPick now runs with the settings lock held, and it
triggers bganim:preview-end, whose listener takes DefaultUI's previewMutex for two
assignments. Checked for lock inversion: no path takes previewMutex and then the
settings lock (DefaultUI.cpp scopes its previewMutex block and releases it before
reading Settings), so the order is consistent.

Builds run: pio run -e display-sim, pio run -e display-loadtest, both SUCCESS.
pio run -e display was not built; it does not build in this worktree on WSL1.

title: Preserve legacy uniform rendering on both settings surfaces
description:
Commit 2fd637eb added the web legacy representation, but gradientForRef returns the positions parsed from bgAnimCustomTheme. Firmware deliberately discards those positions for the legacy fallback.

With legacy theme 18, no resolving global ref, and custom string `ff0000@0,00ff00@10,0000ff@255`, the committed JavaScript returns positions 0, 10 and 255. Firmware resolves the same legacy colors uniformly at 0, 127 and 255. GradientEditor serializes its returned stops into the live panel preview, so opening the editor can change the displayed gradient temporarily. The existing 53 mirror checks pass this omission.

Commit 265501e0 also hides the display swatches for retained legacy fallback because settingsGlobalGradientRef returns an empty string. The global row and a per-animation Global row need a read-only sample of the actual fallback.

Normalize only the legacy representation to its firmware uniform semantics. Preserve positions in ordinary library gradients and preserve all stored legacy fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Web tests cover the positioned legacy fixture and verify uniform returned stops and uniform preview serialization.
- [ ] A positional library fixture retains its original positions.
- [ ] Simulator fixtures show Custom (legacy) and its toned swatch on the global entry row and rows following that fallback, including the picker's Global entry.
- [ ] The runner's expected_global_gradient_text helper applies the frozen legacy namespace instead of indexing THEME_NAMES directly with bgAnimTheme.
- [ ] Opening and cancelling both surfaces leaves bgAnimTheme, bgAnimCustomTheme, bgAnimGradientRef, bgAnimThemeMap and bgAnimGradients unchanged.
- [ ] Mirror checks and the animation runner pass, including valid, empty and malformed legacy custom strings.
notes:
Done in b415d8a5.

What changed:

- web/src/config/bgAnimations.js: legacyCustomGradient() replaces the stored
  positions with even spacing, and gradientForRef uses it for the legacy
  stand-in. Every web reading of the legacy pair goes through gradientForRef,
  so the picker name, the CSS preview bar, the browse dialog's Global item and
  the editor's live panel preview all move together. The preview string then
  carries no @pos at all, which is what puts the firmware's parser back on the
  uniform path.
- GradientSwatch.h/.cpp: swatchFromLegacyCustom(), bg_parse_gradient followed
  by the resolver's uniform fill.
- CatAnimation.cpp: settingsGlobalGradientSwatch(), exported through
  CatGradientPicker.h. applyRowSwatch resolves an empty ref through it, and the
  global row now passes "" instead of the ref, so the global row, a per
  animation row on Global and the standby row share one reading.
- CatGradientPicker.cpp: the Global entry holds the resolved gradient rather
  than a choice index, because the legacy fallback is in no choice list.
- tools/gradient_mirror_check.mjs: 53 checks to 63.
- tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py: expected_global_gradient_text goes
  through the frozen legacy namespace (new legacy_builtin and
  custom_theme_valid mirrors), instead of indexing THEME_NAMES with
  bgAnimTheme.
- tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py: the legacy scenario now drives
  a positioned custom string and compares the swatch against two ground truths
  captured from the same widget, a library entry with the same colours spaced
  evenly and one with the stored positions. A second check covers the empty,
  malformed and one stop strings.

Acceptance criteria, all checked:

- Web tests cover the positioned legacy fixture: yes. The two new failing
  checks before the fix were the returned stops (0, 10, 255 against 0, 127,
  255) and the serialized preview ("ff0000@0,00ff00@10,0000ff@255" against
  "ff0000,00ff00,0000ff").
- A positional library fixture keeps its positions: yes, checked in the mirror
  harness with the same colours as the legacy fixture.
- Simulator fixtures show Custom (legacy) and its toned swatch on the global
  row, the per animation row on Global and the picker's Global entry: yes,
  three new checks, each comparing the pixels against the uniform ground truth.
- expected_global_gradient_text uses the frozen namespace: yes.
- Opening and cancelling writes none of the five fields: yes, unchanged from
  before and now also checked for the three unparsable strings.
- Mirror checks and the animation runner pass, valid, empty and malformed
  included: yes.

What was run:

- node tools/gradient_mirror_check.mjs: 63 pass. Against the code before the
  fix, 2 fail.
- python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only animation,gradientdraft: PASS,
  animation 215 checks, gradientdraft 56 checks, 0 failed.
- The failure proof for the display half used two scratch builds outside the
  shared tree. A build of pristine HEAD fails the four new checks with no
  swatch at all. A build carrying this change with the uniform fill removed
  fails the three swatch checks with "the stored positions were kept: this is
  the positional reading", which is what makes the check discriminate the bug
  rather than the absence of a swatch.
- tools/animbench swatch_parity, rebuilt after the GradientSwatch change: PASS,
  511 ramps, all 256 entries exact.
- web: npm run lint:check 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings in
  pages/Statistics), npx prettier --check clean, npm run build clean.
- pio run -e display-sim, -e display-loadtest and -e display all build.

One correction to the commit message of b415d8a5. Its body says the production
build was not run because it does not build in this worktree on WSL1. That was
the standing note at the time and it is wrong: `pio run -e display` succeeded
here afterwards, in 2 min 29 s on the tree carrying this change. The commit was
not amended, because rewriting the tip of a branch that several agents commit
to would put their in flight work at risk. This note is the record.

Two things for whoever reads this next:

- pio test -e native_settingsui fails 2 of 68 in the working tree right now
  (test_explicit_builtin_refs_resolve_directly and
  test_upgrade_rollback_upgrade_keeps_the_same_gradient). That is not this
  change. A pristine HEAD passes 67 of 67, and the same HEAD with only the
  working tree's uncommitted data/gradients.json and BgAnimThemeTable.h copied
  in fails the same 2 of 68. It belongs to the gradient set extension in
  flight.
- Not fixed here, and not this bead: the web previews every gradient through
  gradientCss, which interpolates in CSS, while the panel uses the integer
  arithmetic in config/gradientRamp.js. The two differ slightly at the top of a
  uniform ramp. That gap applies to all gradients, not just the legacy one, so
  changing it for the legacy preview alone would have made the editor
  inconsistent with itself.

title: Exercise category fixtures through the provider both builds use
description:
Commit 3654b80c made the category-order fixture exercise the simulator's production provider. Commit 265501e0 subsequently switched both builds to bg_theme_* accessors, leaving that fixture on the independent tableThemeProvider implementation.

At HEAD, ThemeProviderTable.h is included only by the host test. The production simulator split has already been removed, and source inspection finds no second production table inclusion to remove. The missing coverage is the reordered and empty-category fixture passing through the current production accessors.

Move the fixture onto those accessors using injected test data or a shared production implementation. Keep declared category order and empty-category reporting at the provider level, while preserving the picker's intentional omission of empty groups.

Clean up the obsolete simulator premise. CLAUDE.md:797 still instructs contributors to add BgAnimThemes stubs. SettingsModel.h:121 and scripts/gen_gradients.py:161 also describe the former split, and the host test comments still call its generated provider the simulator path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fixture with declared categories Coffee, Neon and Pastel, first encountered category Neon and empty Pastel, runs through the production provider used by both builds.
- [ ] Deliberately changing production category enumeration to encounter order or dropping empty declared categories makes the fixture fail.
- [ ] Provider tests preserve names, stops, stored indices and out-of-range behavior.
- [ ] Source inspection confirms both builds use the real accessors without duplicate production stop tables or replacement always-false stubs.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md, SettingsModel.h, test comments and the runner generator accurately describe the current linkage; regenerated output passes the generator check.
- [ ] Host provider tests and the simulator build pass.
notes:
Done in a374bd70.

What production calls now: CatAnimation.cpp's makeThemeProvider wires the six
bg_theme_* functions from BgAnimThemes.cpp, on the device and on the simulator
alike. There is no factory in between, so the fixture reads those functions
directly. bg_test_set_theme_table now swaps the declared category list as well
as the gradient table (two new optional arguments; a null pointer keeps the
shipped one), and bg_theme_category_count and bg_theme_category_name read the
swappable pointers. The three fixture cases install their table and build the
provider the same six ways CatAnimation.cpp does. The restore moved into
tearDown so a fixture table cannot leak into the next case when an assertion
ends one early. ThemeProviderTable.h is deleted, with the case that compared
it against bg_theme_*.

Mutation proof, built from copies of src and test outside the shared tree and
compiled with g++ against the Unity in .pio/libdeps:

  encounter order instead of the declared list
    old fixture (HEAD): 2 failures, both the whole-table case, not the fixture
    new fixture:        4 failures, all three fixture cases among them
  empty declared categories dropped
    old fixture (HEAD): 0 failures, 68 of 68 passed
    new fixture:        1 failure, the fixture case

The second is the discriminating one: every shipped category has a gradient in
it, so only a fixture with an empty category can see that rule break, and the
old suite could not.

Acceptance criteria:
  1 met. The Coffee/Neon/Pastel fixture runs through bg_theme_*.
  2 met. Both mutations above.
  3 met. Names, stops, stored index order and the out-of-range reads are all
    still asserted, now off the same accessors.
  4 met. Source inspection: BgAnimThemes.cpp is the only firmware file that
    includes BgAnimThemeTable.h, the host test includes it because it links
    that file, nothing else does, and sim/platform/bganim_stub.cpp holds only
    the allocation counters.
  5 partly met. CLAUDE.md (the stub claim at 797 and the ThemeProviderTable
    sentence at 811), SettingsModel.h and the test comments are corrected, and
    scripts/gen_gradients.py --check is clean. Left undone: the docstring
    render_runner writes into tools/settings_ui_tests/gradients_gen.py still
    says the firmware table "compiles only outside GAGGIMATE_SIM, so there is
    no route the runner could read it from instead". Fixing it means
    regenerating that file, which another agent holds while the gradient set
    is being extended. The true reason is simply that the runner is Python
    driving the display over HTTP and cannot read a C++ table.
  6 met. pio test -e native_settingsui, 67 of 67 pass, and pio run -e
    display-sim succeeds, both re-run after gm-nov3.16 landed underneath.

Not run: pio run -e display, which does not build in this worktree on WSL1.
No device work: the board was held by another agent.

title: Categories on both surfaces: firmware lookups and web optgroups
description:
Carry categories through the firmware provider and web picker so the long collection reads as eight short lists.

Depends on gm-nov3.1, which defines and generates the category metadata.

## Existing partial work

Keep the seven-file partial implementation. It adds the three firmware category lookups, simulator link stubs, a per-gradient category provider, GradientChoice.category, and optgroups in both GradientEditor select branches. The option values remain the original decimal indices.

The partial work is not complete: ThemeNameProvider still needs the declared category list and built-in stops, both build variants need that wiring, and tests and build checks remain.

## Firmware

bg_theme_category(int) returns a built-in's category. bg_theme_category_count() and bg_theme_category_name(int) expose the declared category list.

Use the categories array order from data/gradients.json. It is the owner's presentation order, independent of the gradient array's stored-index order.

The simulator excludes BgAnimThemes.cpp and its category stubs return empty values. The picker therefore reads through settingsui::ThemeNameProvider. Extend it with categoryCount, categoryName and stops alongside count, name and the per-gradient category accessor.

CatAnimation.cpp fills the provider from the generated table under GAGGIMATE_SIM and from the firmware free functions on the device. Device code must not include the generated stop table again solely to fill this provider.

gradientChoices() retains its order: the empty-ref default entry, built-ins in table order, then saved gradients. Built-ins carry their category. The default entry and saved gradients carry an empty category; the picker groups saved entries under My gradients.

## Web

GradientEditor.jsx keeps one optgroup per non-empty declared category, in declared order, with My gradients first when the library is non-empty. Both its collapsed per-animation branch and full editor branch must use the grouping.

Do not change refs, storage or preview behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The built-in category and declared category list are available through the provider on device and simulator without handwritten category-name lists.
- [ ] ThemeNameProvider carries count, name, category, categoryCount, categoryName and stops. CatAnimation.cpp fills every accessor on both build paths.
- [ ] A provider test checks all built-in names, categories and six stops against generated data, including the simulator provider path rather than only the real firmware free functions.
- [ ] Host tests verify gradientChoices order, unchanged refs, correct built-in categories, and empty categories for the default and saved entries.
- [ ] A fixture whose first gradient is outside the first declared category still returns the declared category order.
- [ ] Tests cover valid endpoints and the documented out-of-range fallback of the new firmware lookups.
- [ ] Browser checks cover both GradientEditor select branches, declared group order and My gradients appearing only for a non-empty library.
- [ ] Selecting from each group still produces its original decimal or c<id> ref.
- [ ] pio test -e native_settingsui passes with the new cases.
- [ ] pio run -e display-sim and pio run -e display-loadtest build and link. pio run -e display also passes in a checkout where its dependencies install, following CLAUDE.md's worktree limitation.
- [ ] npm run lint:check and npm run build pass.
- [ ] A browser check against the device finds every category heading and verifies the expected saved ref after choosing one gradient from each category.
notes:
Done in commit cf648c2d on anims/astra.

What landed, on top of the seven-file partial work, which was kept:

- ThemeNameProvider now carries count, name, category, categoryCount,
  categoryName and stops (SettingsModel.h). Stops use a ThemeStops alias for
  the shape bg_theme_stops returns.
- New src/display/ui/default/settings/ThemeProviderTable.h fills a provider
  from the generated table. CatAnimation.cpp calls it under GAGGIMATE_SIM and
  fills all six from the bg_theme_* functions on the device, so the stop table
  is not pulled into a device build twice.
- Host tests: five new cases in test/test_settings_model.
- New tools/gradient_groups_check.mjs renders GradientEditor with
  preact-render-to-string and reads the markup.

Criteria, with what was run:

1. Category and declared list through the provider on both builds, no
   handwritten name lists: yes. Both come from the generated table.
2. Provider carries all six, filled on both paths: yes. Both compiled
   (display-sim, display-loadtest).
3. Provider test against generated data including the simulator path: yes.
   test_theme_provider_device_path_matches_table and
   test_theme_provider_simulator_path_matches_table check all 18 names,
   categories and 6 stops each, both ways, and that the two paths agree.
4. gradientChoices order, refs, built-in categories, empty for default and
   saved: yes, test_gradient_choices_carry_categories.
5. Fixture whose first gradient is outside the first declared category:
   yes, test_theme_category_order_is_declared_not_encountered.

title: Improve category heading contrast in the gradient browser
description:
Commit c0946a54 renders category headings with text-base-content/60 and text-xs in GradientBrowser.jsx:120. The default light palette produces approximately 3.05:1 contrast by calculation from the committed theme colors. The headings identify the groups users browse, so their small text needs stronger contrast.

Use the project's theme colors to improve heading legibility and verify the result in the rendered component.

Keep gradientCss for the browse swatches. This satisfies gm-nov3.6's requirement to agree with the editor's neighboring bar. Firmware-exact sampling remains appropriate for the display swatches. The comment's claim that a 40 px swatch cannot show differences is unsupported: h-10 specifies height and width is responsive. Document the shared editor rendering as the reason for this choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rendered category headings have at least 4.5:1 contrast against the dialog background in light, dark, coffee and nord themes.
- [ ] Browser checks at 1440x900 and 390x844 confirm the headings remain legible and fit their groups.
- [ ] GradientBrowser.jsx explains the shared gradientCss rendering without asserting invisibility based on the swatch height.
- [ ] Existing browse interaction checks and web lint pass.
notes:
Done in 83ae968b. The category headings in GradientBrowser.jsx went from
text-base-content/60 to /80.

Contrast against the dialog's bg-base-100, measured in Chrome by painting
the heading's computed colour over the panel colour on a canvas and
reading the pixel back (the opacity modifier is a color-mix(), so the
browser resolves it rather than a parser):

  theme    at /60    at /80
  light    3.05:1    4.97:1
  dark     4.70:1    7.35:1
  coffee   3.25:1    4.76:1
  nord     3.49:1    6.03:1

An offline calculation straight from the oklch values in web/src/style.css
agrees within rounding (3.05 / 4.70 / 3.29 / 3.50 before, 4.95 / 7.40 /
4.79 / 6.07 after), and the light figure matches the 3.05 the review
reported.

tools/gradient_browse_browser.py now measures all four themes at both
widths it already drives (1440x900 and 390x844) and checks that a heading
stays on one line inside its group box. Real Chrome, 54 checks, PASS.
tools/gradient_browse_check.mjs PASS. In web/: eslint 0 errors (6
pre-existing warnings in Statistics/components/statisticsView/hooks.js,
untouched), prettier clean, npm run build clean.

The comment above the component no longer claims that the two gradient
paths differ only in the last bits of RGB565 and that a 40 px swatch
cannot show it. It now gives the real reason for gradientCss(): the
swatch sits beside the bar the editor draws with the same function, so
those two have to agree. It also records the actual size of the gap to
the firmware-exact sampler (a gradient with no stop positions takes the
firmware's uniform path, which reaches only 251/256 of the way to the
final stop).

Left alone on purpose, reported rather than fixed: the same /60 treatment
is on the dialog's notice paragraph (line 111) and on about forty other
places in the web UI, including CardTitle at /55. That is a wider
decision than this bead. No firmware build was run and the bench board
was not touched; this change is web only.

title: Keep copied gradient IDs inside the firmware range
description:
Commit `47f6faeb` made saved IDs through 99999 selectable, but the web allocator introduced by `1b33975d` still returns one more than the largest ID. With fewer than 12 entries and an existing ID 99999, Copy creates ID 100000 and assigns `c100000`. The web accepts that state, while the firmware rejects both strings and silently retains the previous stored fields.

Allocate only IDs in 1 through `BG_GRADIENT_ID_MAX`. Reusing a gap must not activate a previously dangling global or per-animation ref. If no safe ID is available, disable Copy and explain that state. Align the JavaScript library and ref parsers with the firmware's exact grammar.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A web test copies a gradient from a library containing ID 99999 while below capacity and obtains either a safe five-digit ID or an explicit unavailable result.
- [ ] Any reused ID is absent from the library, global ref and every stored map slot.
- [ ] JavaScript and firmware boundary tests accept 99999 and reject 100000, trailing characters and malformed custom refs consistently.
- [ ] A copy at the boundary can be saved, reopened and selected with the exact stored ref and stops.
- [ ] An invalid gradient library or ref submitted directly cannot produce a successful partial gradient save without an explicit error.
notes:
Done in commit e32c4577 (branch anims/astra). Four files: web/src/config/bgAnimations.js, web/src/components/GradientEditor.jsx, tools/gradient_mirror_check.mjs, test/test_settings_model/test_settings_model.cpp.

What changed:

- nextGradientId(library, refStrings) now returns the lowest id in 1 to BG_GRADIENT_ID_MAX that nothing reserves, or null. reservedGradientIds reserves every library id plus every library id a stored ref names, resolving or not, read from the raw bgAnimThemeMap and bgAnimGradientRef strings rather than the parsed arrays, because parsing drops exactly the dangling refs. Mirrors ReservedIds in BgAnimThemes.cpp.
- The editor computes the free id once per form state, disables Copy when there is none, and shows a visible line saying why. That state is not reachable from a device: at most 12 entries and one ref per animation reserve a few dozen ids out of 99999.
- The JavaScript parsers now use the firmware's grammar: readId stops at five digits, parseRefParts mirrors parseRef, and the library walk mirrors walkLibrary (stray separator skipped, entry count capped, stop at the first malformed entry instead of stepping over it). gradientRefValid, themeMapValid and gradientLibraryValid mirror bg_ref_valid, bg_map_valid and bg_library_valid. refResolves, parseThemeMap and legacyThemeMirror all go through the same grammar now.

Evidence:

- The defect reproduced on the code at HEAD, built in a scratch directory outside the shared tree: nextGradientId over a library of ids 3 and 99999 returned 100000 and the ref c100000; parseThemeMap accepted c100000 and c0; parseGradientLibrary accepted an entry with id 100000 and stepped over a malformed entry to keep the one after it.
- Seven of the new assertions fail against that pre-fix module, including the dangerous one: with a library of id 1, a map of ";;c2;;c7" and a global ref of "c3", the old allocator returned 2 while c2 was still in the map, so the dangling ref would have resolved again.
- Boundary parity was measured, not assumed. The firmware parsers were compiled on the host straight out of the checkout and asked 23 boundary strings; the web mirror was asked the same 23; the two outputs are identical. Both accept "99999" and "c99999", reject "100000", "c100000", "c0", "c", "5x", "c5x", "c 5" and "099999", accept a library entry with id 99999 and reject one with 100000, id 0, "99999x", an empty name, and a library with one malformed entry among good ones. Those answers are now tests on both sides.

Checks run:

- node tools/gradient_mirror_check.mjs: 63 checks before, 120 after, all passing.
- pio test -e native_settingsui: 67 cases before, 68 after, all passing (the new one is test_gradient_id_boundary_ref_and_library).
- node tools/gradient_browse_check.mjs and tools/gradient_groups_check.mjs: PASS.
- In web: npm run lint:check (0 errors, 6 pre-existing warnings in files this does not touch), npx prettier --check (3 pre-existing warnings, same), npm run build clean.
- No firmware image was built: the change reaches no firmware source, and the web bundle only reaches the image through scripts/build_webui.sh, which was not run.
- No device work. The board was held by another agent this round.

Criterion not met: the fifth one. The firmware's settings handler (WebUIPlugin.cpp, the bgAnimGradients, bgAnimThemeMap and bgAnimGradientRef block) still skips an invalid field in silence rather than reporting an error, so a library or ref submitted directly by curl still produces a 200 with the previous stored value kept. That file was outside this change's assigned scope, and turning a skipped field into a rejected save changes the result of every settings save, so it wants its own bead and its own review. The other four criteria are met.

title: Fix the framebuffer probe tone race and its overclaim
description:
Raised by review round 4 against commit `f580985a`, which closed gm-nov3.10. That bead stays closed and keeps its record; this is the follow up work the review found in what it landed.

Commit `f580985a` implemented the deferred bench-only gradient fixture and host comparison. It paints known ramp indices after compositing, reads both framebuffer allocations through `/api/debug/fb`, records the active stops and tone, and exercises negative controls. The recorded 172,800-sample result is evidence about framebuffer memory.

The instrument does not observe RGB scanout, panel timing, wiring, controller behavior or the glass. A pixel clock divider of 7 does not affect the framebuffer comparison and neither invalidates the zero mismatch result nor extends it to the physical panel.

The HTTP task does more than set atomics. Fixture geometry and mode use atomics, and preview data follows the existing mutex-protected event path, but the tone overrides are `volatile int` values written by the HTTP task and read by the UI task. Replace that data race with explicit cross-task synchronization. Keep the disabled path semantically unchanged and keep framebuffer writes owned by the render task.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The tone override values shared between the HTTP and UI tasks use atomics or another explicit synchronization mechanism.
- [ ] A host test confirms requested tone percentages settle to the matching `brightness256` and `knee` values before samples are accepted.
- [ ] The fixture remains bench-only, and the HTTP callback does not write a framebuffer or render buffer.
- [ ] Comments and `tools/gradient_fb_check.py` consistently call the result a framebuffer comparison and list the scanout and physical-panel behavior it cannot establish.
- [ ] The comparison still covers both framebuffer allocations, ramp index 255, uniform and positional semantics, 100/100 and 60/65 tone settings, and deliberate negative controls.
- [ ] With the fixture disabled, production resolution, compositing and presentation behavior are unchanged.
notes:
Done in 2e284b8c on branch anims/astra (worktree gm-2cl-6-dials).

The race. `g_animToneBrightnessPct` and `g_animToneKneePct` are gone. One
`std::atomic<uint32_t> g_animToneOverride` holds both percentages, one byte
each, with 0xFF meaning "use the stored setting" (`gm_tone_pack` and
`gm_tone_unpack` in LV_Helper.h). The gradfix handler parses both arguments
first and publishes them in a single release store, so a request carrying both
can never be seen half applied; an absent argument keeps what is held, read
back first, which is safe because every request runs on the async_tcp task and
it is the only writer. DefaultUI reads the pair in one acquire load. The report
now reads the percentages before calling `themeToneState`, so the integers it
prints are never older than the percentages beside them.

The host test. `tools/gradient_fb_check.py --host-test` drives the settle gate
against a scripted device (FakeDevice) with no board: it proves the gate waits
until the reported brightness256 and knee are the conversion of the reported
percentages, that a device which never applies the request times out and names
the conversion, that a device holding a different tone is refused, and that an
already settled device costs one poll. It has teeth: run against the old gate
(percentages only) it fails with exit 1 on four of its checks. The gate itself
now runs inside `arm()`, so no sample is taken before the requested tone has
reached the integers the render task draws with.

Measured on the bench board why that matters: after a tone change the device
reported the new percentages beside the previous integers for 4 to 6
consecutive reads, 230 to 394 ms (three changes, 40/45, 85/90, 100/100). The
old gate's six-frame wait is about 270 ms at 22 fps, so it covered that window
by accident, and not always.

The overclaim. The endpoint comment, the tool's docstring and
tools/gradient_sheet.py's "comparing this against the panel" section now call
the result a framebuffer comparison and list what it cannot establish: RGB
scan-out (bounce buffers, DMA, LCD_CAM), panel timing, the ribbon and wiring,
the controller board, and the glass. The pixel clock divider is not in this
path, so the 7 the bench board stores neither qualifies a pass nor explains a
failure; it is recorded that way rather than as a condition of the result.

Device runs, bench board 192.168.1.121, this build flashed
(v1.9.8-sleep9-666-g1528d468-dirty, display-loadtest, 2026-09-13T12:59Z),
stored divider 7, whole-frame path, no NVS write of any kind:

  - 38,400 samples, 0 mismatches: both framebuffers, tones 100/100 and 60/65,
    xoff 0 and 1 (ramp index up to 255 on the xoff 1 passes).
  - negative controls fired: the same strip against a 50/50 ramp 4,800
    mismatches, the correct ramp against the region with the fixture off 4,717.
  - positional stops through the preview path, 19,200 samples, 0 mismatches,
    device reporting uniform=false.
  - all 60 built-ins, buffer 0, 576,000 samples, 0 mismatches, the same count
    the previous session recorded.

Fixture disabled. The production image contains no `/api/debug/gradfix` string
at all (0 occurrences against 1 in display-loadtest), `setRampFixture` and the
paint block are inside `#ifdef GM_TOUCH_PROBE`, and in production `rampFix` is
a `constexpr int 0`, so the interlace expression is the pre-fixture one. On the
bench build, off and armed and off again: 23.87, 22.51 and 23.50 anim fps,
scan-out 43.5 Hz throughout, interlace false throughout, and the tone returns
to the stored 100/100 (256, 255) with toneOverride false. The HTTP callback
writes no framebuffer or render buffer; it sets atomics, triggers the existing
preview event and serialises JSON.

Builds: `pio run -e display-loadtest` SUCCESS, `pio run -e display` SUCCESS,
production image 5,900,319 bytes.

Not checked: nothing in the acceptance criteria was left unchecked. The board
is left running this build with the fixture off and the tone released.

title: Keep the global gradient row and live panel in agreement
description:
Commit `35f3edd3` made the global row describe the touched value that will win at commit. It left a user-visible contradiction when another surface saves during the visit.

If the display selects gradient A and the web then saves gradient B, the panel changes to B while the display row, swatch and picker marker continue to show A. Leaving the category commits A and changes the panel back. The touched-field precedence is intentional, but the open page must not claim that A is currently being displayed while the panel draws B.

Either reapply the pending display choice when reconciliation observes the web save, or show the pending and currently displayed states distinctly. Do not change the established touched-field precedence for unrelated settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test selects global gradient A on the display, saves B from the web while the category remains open, and verifies that the row, swatch, picker marker and live rendered gradient do not contradict each other.
- [ ] The same case is covered while the grouped picker is open.
- [ ] Leaving the category saves the value the display said would be saved, and reopening shows the same value.
- [ ] If the display has not touched the global gradient, a web save is still adopted immediately.
- [ ] Tests for the other touched and untouched animation fields retain their existing commit-time precedence.
notes:
Done in affbc12f on anims/astra.

Shape chosen: reapply the pending display choice to the live panel when
reconciliation sees the web save. The alternative (showing the pending and the
drawn state as two things) was rejected because it adds a state to the row for
a window that can be closed instead.

animReconcile (CatAnimation.cpp) now writes the touched global ref, and its
legacy mirror, back into Settings when a web save has replaced it. That is the
same write globalGradientPicked already makes, so it restores a live field
rather than adding a rule, and it is scoped to this one field: the
commit-time precedence of every other animation field is untouched.

What the user sees in the two seconds after the web save: nothing changes.
SettingsUI::service() reconciles before DefaultUI::updateState() in the same UI
pass, and updateState re-resolves the palette only when the stored ref moved
under it, so the render task normally never sees the web's ref. A POST landing
between those two calls of one pass can still show the web's gradient for that
pass, up to a few hundred milliseconds, and the next pass puts it back.

Checks, all on the simulator and the host. The board was held by another agent,
so nothing here ran on hardware, and no criterion needed it.

  pio run -e display-sim: SUCCESS
  pio run -e display-loadtest: SUCCESS (the device compile of the same file)
  pio test -e native_settingsui: 68 of 68, unchanged (no model change)
  python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only animation,gradientdraft: PASS
      animation     222 of 222 before, 222 of 222 after
      gradientdraft  56 of 56 before,   78 of 78 after

Failing first: a binary built from a scratch copy of HEAD (exported into a temp
directory with its own pio tree, never by reverting a file in the shared tree)
fails 4 of the new file's 78 checks, and only those four:
agree_row_panel_back_to_draft, agree_row_mirror_back_to_draft,
agree_group_panel_back_to_draft and agree_list_panel_back_to_draft. Each
reports the panel sitting on the web's gradient while the row named the draft.

Criteria:
  1. Covered by check_touched_global_agrees_with_panel: row text, row swatch
     pixels, picker marker and the stored fields the panel resolves from.
  2. Covered at both picker levels by the same check.
  3. Covered: agree_exit_saves_the_named_value, agree_exit_mirrors_the_named_value,
     agree_reopen_names_the_same_value, agree_reopen_swatch_draws_it.
  4. Covered: untouched_panel_keeps_web, added to the untouched check.
  5. Covered: the animation scenario is unchanged at 222 of 222.

One limit worth recording. "The live rendered gradient" is read on the
simulator as bgAnimGradientRef and bgAnimTheme, the two stored fields
DefaultUI::updateState resolves the palette from. The simulator has no render
loop at all (sim/platform/bganim_stub.cpp), so the panel itself cannot be
sampled on that venue. The row swatch is checked in the same breath and is held
to the real palette code by tools/animbench/swatch_parity.cpp, so a fix that
moved one and not the other would be caught.

Not done, for the lead to place: CLAUDE.md's on-display settings section has no
line for this rule. The task brief scoped me to five files and CLAUDE.md is
contended, so I left it alone.

title: Freeze the original gradients and expose set crowding
description:
Commit `71bd9f20` says the original 18 are immutable, but `check_original_set` stores and compares only their names. Commit `e3555bc6` preserved the full original records, as an independent comparison against its parent confirms, but a later stop or category change could pass the checker.

The near-duplicate rule also considers each pair independently and fails only below mean dE2000 8. On the current 60-entry set, 36 pairs are below 10 and 133 are below 12 while the checker passes. This does not prove that a pair is visually confusing, but it proves that a passing minimum-pair gate cannot rule out aggregate crowding. Make that density visible to an independent reviewer at the actual picker swatch size.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The checker compares the complete first 18 records, including name, category and all stops, against a frozen trusted baseline.
- [ ] Mutation tests independently change an original name, category, order and stop and verify that each change fails.
- [ ] The checker reports each gradient's nearest neighbor and per-category pair counts below documented review bands without changing the established dE2000 8 rejection threshold.
- [ ] An adversarial fixture with all pairs at or above 8 but many close neighbors verifies that the crowding report is populated even though the pair gate passes.
- [ ] An independent review of the final 60 gradients at the display picker's rendered swatch dimensions records any confusing pairs and the disposition of each.
- [ ] The baseline exemption list remains restricted to the original entries and is not extended for a new gradient.
notes:
Done in commit 1a688e32 on branch anims/astra. Two files changed, both mine:
tools/gradient_check.py and tools/gradient_check_test.py. Nothing in
data/gradients.json was touched, the 8.0 threshold is unchanged, and no pair was
added to the exemption list.

## The freeze

ORIGINAL_18_RECORDS holds the name, the category and all six stops of each of
the first 18 entries at the index it is frozen at, copied from
data/gradients.json at commit 8f61e73a. check_original_set compares the whole
record and reports four codes: original_name_changed (a rename or a reorder),
original_category_changed, original_stops_changed, original_set_short.

The shipped first 18 match the baseline exactly, so nothing was broken. What was
missing was the guard. The four mutations were run against the checker at HEAD,
out of a scratch copy so the shared worktree never held the old file:

    a renamed original               -> original_set_moved
    a reordered original             -> original_set_moved
    a recategorised original         -> (clean)
    a changed stop on an original    -> (clean)

Half of them passed silently. All four now fail, with a distinct code each.

## The crowding report

Beside the gate, never inside it. It prints pair counts under three review
bands (10.0, 16.0, 20.0), the same counts per category, every gradient's nearest
neighbour overall and inside its own category, and a review list of the
within-category pairs closest first. It also lands in the --json output under
"crowding". --no-crowding skips it, --review N sets the list length.

On the shipped 60: 196 of the 1770 pairs are inside a category, 36 pairs are
under 10.0 (15 of them within a category), 290 under 16.0 (91 within) and 504
under 20.0 (126 within).

Why within-category is the lens. All sixteen pairs gm-2tqj's two readers flagged
are within a category, and within-category pairs are 11% of the table. Fifteen
of the sixteen are in the closest 89 of those 196, and the sixteenth is at 125.

## The read at picker swatch size, criterion five

Two further reads were taken at the settings picker's own swatch geometry, 96 by
30 pixels from 96 ramp samples (kSettingsRowSwatchSamples and kSwatchH in
SettingsRows.cpp), sampled at (i * 255) / 95 exactly as swatchBuildRamp565 does.
One read is mine, one is GPT via the codex CLI on the same sheet. Together with
gm-2tqj's two readers that is 27 distinct pairs called hard to tell apart.

All 27 are inside a category. 26 of the 27 are in the review list, that is under
20.0. Ranks are (mean dE2000, rank of 1770, rank of 196):

    Rose / Sakura              5.45    2    2   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Fern / Forest              9.22    9    5   swatch
    Mint Cream / Seafoam       9.23   10    6   codex, swatch
    Glacier / Ocean            9.76   24    9   codex, gm-2tqj, swatch
    Lagoon / Teal Reef         9.81   28   10   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Magma / Solar Flare        9.84   29   11   swatch
    Graphite / Steel           9.89   32   13   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Ember Coal / Fire          9.98   36   15   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Lilac Haze / Sakura       10.04   40   18   codex
    Moss / Olive Grove        10.10   44   20   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Deep Space / Eclipse      10.30   55   27   gm-2tqj
    Eclipse / Midnight        10.59   72   35   gm-2tqj
    Arctic Night / Ice        10.98   90   38   codex
    Moonrise / Starlight      11.03   94   39   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Eclipse / Nebula Drift    11.06   95   40   swatch
    Crema / Espresso          11.53  110   43   swatch
    Dark Roast / Flat White   11.58  113   46   swatch
    Midnight / Violet Dusk    11.59  114   47   codex, swatch
    Slate / Steel             13.33  181   64   gm-2tqj
    Cappuccino / Cold Brew    13.75  191   68   codex, gm-2tqj, swatch
    Lavender / Lilac Haze     14.37  214   73   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Hot Magenta / Laser Pink  15.25  249   82   codex, gm-2tqj, swatch
    Forge / Magma             15.48  259   85   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Nebula Drift / Starlight  15.83  275   89   gm-2tqj
    Cyber / Hot Magenta       16.40  307   96   swatch
    Graphite / Sandstone      19.52  480  125   gm-2tqj, swatch
    Basalt / Gold             20.99  575  133   swatch, NOT in the review list

Category fit at swatch size, which the checker does not measure. Corrected
2026-09-13 after the team lead asked what the two new reads were actually asked;
the first version of this paragraph got two entries wrong.

Codex was asked both questions. Its prompt was, in full: which pairs within the
same category are hard to tell apart at this size, and which entries look wrong
for their category or their name. So its silence on an entry is a real answer,
not an unasked question. My own read had no prompt, since I was the reader, and
I looked with both questions in mind.

  entry          gm-2tqj        swatch read                     codex
  Abyss          both readers   raised, violet not water        not raised
  Flat White     both readers   not raised                      not raised
  Basalt         one reader     raised, sage                    raised, mossy green
  Electric Blue  one reader     not raised                      raised, periwinkle
  Slate          one reader     raised, teal grey               not raised
  Sandstone      not raised     raised, olive khaki             not raised
  Aurora         not raised     raised, teal, odd for its name  not raised
  Arctic Night   not raised     not raised                      raised, reads as
                                                                ordinary ice and
                                                                duplicates Ice

So Abyss is named by three of the four readers and only Flat White is a genuine
two of four split.

One caveat that changes how much these two reads are worth. My read is not
blind: I had read gm-2tqj's table before I looked at the sheet, so my agreement
on Abyss, Basalt, Slate and Sandstone is contaminated and is not independent
confirmation. Codex's read is the only blind one at picker size, since its
prompt named no prior finding and carried no history. A fourth independent
reader has to be someone who has not seen gm-2tqj.

None of this touches the crowding report. All 27 pairs are within a category
whoever named them, and Codex's seven, produced blind, are all within a category
and all inside the review list.

The disposition of each pair is not recorded here. That is the decision gm-2tqj
holds and it is the owner's, not mine. This bead built the instrument and the
evidence; gm-2tqj is where accept, re-search or add a rule gets chosen.

## Tests

python3 tools/gradient_check_test.py: 13 cases before, 30 after, all pass, about
3.5 s. New cases: the baseline equals the shipped first 18; four independent
mutations of an original (name, order, category, one stop) each failing with its
own code; a document shorter than the freeze; the same stop edit on a later
entry staying clean; the exemption list still being the four grandfathered pairs
of the original 18; five cases checking the crowding report against the pair
table it summarises; and the adversarial fixture.

The seven source-rule fixtures were moved off the frozen 18 (Gold to Mocha, Deep
Space to Midnight) so each still differs from the real set in exactly one way.
On the frozen entries they were tripping the freeze as well as their own rule.

The adversarial fixture is built, not written out: a greedy packing over a fixed
pool of hue ramps that accepts a candidate only if it clears 8.0 against
