title: A malformed settings field is dropped and the save reports success
description:
A settings save that carries a malformed gradient field returns 200 and keeps
the old value, telling the caller nothing.

Three fields in `WebUIPlugin.cpp`'s settings handler are structurally
validated and then dropped on failure:

    if (request->hasArg("bgAnimGradients") && bg_library_valid(...))
        settings->setBgAnimGradients(...);
    if (request->hasArg("bgAnimThemeMap") && bg_map_valid(...))
        settings->setBgAnimThemeMap(...);
    if (request->hasArg("bgAnimGradientRef") && bg_ref_valid(...))
        ...

Validating them is right and the comment above the first one explains why: a
malformed library would make every animation that references it fall back to
the global theme, and the strings come straight from the form. What is wrong
is the failure behaviour. The field is skipped, the rest of the save proceeds,
and the response is a success, so a caller that sent a bad value is told its
save worked while the device kept the old one.

This was found by gm-nov3.21, which fixed the web allocator that could produce
such a value (an id of 100000, which the firmware's five digit parser cannot
read). With that fixed, the product no longer generates the case. Anything
else that posts to the endpoint still can, including a hand written request,
an older web bundle cached in a browser, and any future field whose two
validators drift apart. The silence is what made the original defect invisible
for as long as it was.

## Why this is its own bead

Turning a skipped field into a failed save changes the outcome of every
settings save, not only these three. A save that carries twenty good fields
and one malformed one currently stores the twenty. Refusing the whole save
would be a different contract, and refusing only the field while reporting it
is a third. That decision belongs with someone who can weigh the web form, the
display, and anything else posting to this endpoint, and it should not be made
inside a bead about gradient ids.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on what a malformed field does: refuse the whole
      save, apply the rest and report which fields were dropped, or keep the
      present behaviour deliberately.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen, a caller can tell from the response whether the
      value it sent was stored. A 200 that means "some of it" is only
      acceptable if the response says which parts.
- [ ] The three gradient fields above behave the same way as each other.
- [ ] A test posts a malformed library, map and ref, and asserts both the
      response and the stored value. It fails against the current code.
- [ ] The web form's behaviour is stated: whether it can still surface the
      result to the user, and whether it needs to change.
- [ ] If any other field in the same handler is validated and silently
      dropped, it is listed here or fixed with these three.
notes:
Decision (leader, idf5): apply every valid field, refuse the malformed ones, and say so. The handler answers 422 with {error:'invalid fields', code:'invalid_fields', fields:[...]} when any field was refused, and does not honour a restart, the same as the 500 persist_failed path. On idf5 there are two gradient fields, bgAnimGradients and bgAnimThemeMap. The ref travels inside the map, and the web's bgAnimGradientRef select has no name, so it is never posted. Both gradient fields behave the same way.
Other fields in the handler that were validated and silently dropped, now fixed the same way: autowakeupSchedules, where an entry without a valid HH:MM time used to be dropped while the rest was stored; now the whole field is refused and the stored list kept. Also apPassword under 8 characters; an empty value still means not set, because the form echoes the stored value and the sim stores none.
Fields that are coerced, not dropped, left as they are: bgAnimClearPlates outside 0..2 becomes 1, and panelClockDiv outside MIN_USER_DIV..12 becomes 0. The setters clamp brightness, tone, VCOM, plate colour and delays. Days in a schedule entry that are not 7 characters long fall back to every day. Numeric fields read through toInt/toFloat, so garbage becomes 0. wifiPassword '---unchanged---' is a sentinel, not a validation.
Also changed: sim/platform/bganim_stub.cpp now compiles the real BgAnimThemes.cpp. Its always-false validators would have made every simulator web save answer 422. test_schedules and test_animation were updated where they encoded the old behaviour. The animation precedence check can now run its web-write step on the sim.
Verified: the new scenario tools/settings_ui_tests/test_reject.py, registered as 'reject', fails 9 of 22 checks against a sim built with the old handler and the real validators, and passes 22 of 22 with the fix. Full simulator runner, all 9 scenarios, PASS. The display-sim and display envs both build; I built them in a scratch clone because SettingsRows.cpp in the shared tree had another teammate's uncommitted edit that does not compile.
Web: the form keeps its edits on a non-2xx answer and shows data.error, so the user sees only 'invalid fields' with no names. Follow-up bead gm-hvpj covers that. Commit 64a308f9.
close_reason: Malformed settings fields are refused with a 422 naming them; valid fields still saved (64a308f9)

title: Publish the applied fixture tone after the palette is ready
description:
Follow up commit 2e284b8c and the original reader from f580985a.

**Settle the direction of the fault first, because it changes how much this
matters and nobody has established it.** An early sample reads a framebuffer
still drawn with the old tone. If the expected ramp is computed from the
request, that is a mismatch the check reports as a failure, so the fault is
flakiness and not false confidence. If the expected ramp is derived from the
same stale reported state, both sides are consistently stale and the check
passes on a panel that has not applied the tone, which is false confidence.
Read `tools/gradient_fb_check.py` and say which it is, with the line, before
changing anything. The bead stands either way: a gate whose accept condition
can fire before the thing it gates is wrong in both directions.

The race itself is confirmed by reading. `setThemeTone` assigns
`g_brightness256` and `g_knee` and only then calls `publishStops()`, which is
what advances `g_themeGen`
(`src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimCommon.cpp:492`). `themeToneState` hands
both integers back with no synchronization at all
(`src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimCommon.cpp:522`). So a reader on another
task can see the new pair while the old palette is still the published one.
Note that the "torn read" wording in the finding is the weak part: these are
aligned 32 bit integers and a torn read is not the realistic failure. The
ordering is.

The requested percentages are now one atomic value, but the reported applied tone is still read from `g_brightness256` and `g_knee` across tasks without synchronization. `setThemeTone` writes those integers before `publishStops()` publishes the matching palette. The HTTP task can therefore observe the requested integer pair while the old palette is still published. It can also observe the new palette generation before the render task has rebuilt and painted the fixture LUT.

The host gate checks an accumulated frame count that may already exceed the threshold before either event. Its fake device models only the measured ordering where percentages change first and integers follow later. It does not model integers becoming visible before palette publication, palette publication before a fixture frame, or a torn read of the two plain integers.

A device below 22 fps is not accepted early today because the gate checks the actual frame count. It may time out after 15 seconds. Preserve that explicit refusal rather than replacing it with an assumed frame duration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The HTTP task no longer reads `g_brightness256` or `g_knee` through an unsynchronized cross-task path.
- [ ] The applied tone state is published only after the matching toned palette is published.
- [ ] A sample is accepted only after the fixture has completed a frame using that published tone, not merely after frames painted with the previous tone.
- [ ] `tools/gradient_fb_check.py --host-test` scripts percentages published, integers changed, palette published, and fixture frame completed as separate states. It rejects every intermediate state and accepts only the final one.
- [ ] The host test includes a mutation where both reported integers equal the request before the palette changes, and that mutation fails the gate.
- [ ] Slow frame progress is governed by observed completed frames and the named timeout, with no assumed 22 fps delay.
notes:
Direction of the fault, settled before any change.

It is flakiness, not false confidence. The expected ramp is computed from the
request, so an early sample is reported as a pixel mismatch and not as a pass.

The line is tools/gradient_fb_check.py:322, in run_pass_once:

    ramp = sample_ramp(st[stops], st[brightnessPct], st[kneePct],
                       st[gain256], mode, node=args.node)

It reads the percentages out of the reported state, which looks like the
second possibility, but the gate has already pinned those to the request:
tone_problems() at lines 258 to 261 refuses any state whose brightnessPct or
kneePct is not the value that was asked for, and arm() will not return until
tone_problems() is empty. So whenever a tone is requested, the reported
percentages are the request.

The stale halves are the published palette and the fixture LUT built from it,
and neither of those ever reaches the expected side. A sample taken before the
palette catches up compares a fresh expectation against a stale strip, which is
a non-zero mismatch count and a FAIL. So the cost was a run that failed for a
reason that was not a pixel fault, in the one instrument that exists to tell
those two apart. With no --tone the reported percentages are the stored setting
and do not move, so that case is not a race at all.

## What landed (commit b24b3fcb)

bganim packs the applied tone and the generation that published it into one
word (BgAnimCommon.cpp, packApplied) and stores it last in publishStops() with
release ordering, so seeing a tone means seeing the palette it was applied to.
g_brightness256 and g_knee stay as the writer own state and are read only on
the task that writes them; themeToneState() now unpacks the word.

The fixture keys its lookup table on that word instead of on the generation,
records which word it built from, and counts whole frames drawn with it. A
frame that rebuilt the table part way through is not counted. The count
restarts at every arm, because the region and the column offset move with it.
The endpoint reports applied, fixApplied, tonedFrames and consistent.

The host gate is gate_problems(): percentages equal the request, integers the
conversion of the percentages, fixApplied equal to applied, and tonedFrames at
or above --settle. Still frames the device says it drew, and still the 15
second deadline as an explicit refusal, so a slow device times out and the
message names the step it stopped at. --settle is raised to one frame per
framebuffer read, since one rendered frame writes one buffer.

## Checks run

- python3 tools/gradient_fb_check.py --host-test: PASS, 9 cases. It was PASS
  with 5 before. The four steps are scripted as separate states, the first
  three refused and only the last accepted.
- The mutation, both integers equal to the request before the palette changes,
  run against both gates from a scratch copy of HEAD: accepted by HEAD on the
  first poll (tonedFrames 0, the strip still on the old palette), refused here
  with "the strip was drawn from palette 235699, the published one is 215705".
- pio run -e display-loadtest: SUCCESS.
- pio run -e display: SUCCESS, 5,899,947 bytes, 90.0% of the app partition.
- pio run -e display-sim: SUCCESS.
- Host compile of BgAnimCommon.cpp against the animbench shims: clean.

## Open, needs the board

The device leg was not run: nobody held the bench board this round. What has to
be re-run on a display-loadtest build is

    python3 tools/gradient_fb_check.py --host 192.168.1.121 --tone 60,65 --tone 90,95

and it should show tonedFrames climbing, fixApplied catching up with applied
after each tone change, and no pass left waiting at the 15 second deadline. The
measurement this replaces (new percentages beside the previous integers for 4
to 6 reads, 230 to 394 ms, 2026-09-13) is worth taking again beside the new
counters, since the window it named is now only part of what the gate covers.

## Also

The lookup table used to be keyed on the theme generation, which starts at zero
on both sides, so a fixture armed before the first palette publish would have
drawn a table of zeros. The published word does not start equal, so the first
armed frame always builds.

SleepAnimation.h was edited as well, which the brief did not list among the
files for this bead. The fixture state it changes lives in that header and
SleepAnimation.cpp was listed, so it reads as an omission rather than another
agent territory. Agent-mail was unreachable for the whole of this work
(127.0.0.1:8765 answered nothing on /health or /mcp/), so no file reservation
was taken.

DEVICE LEG RUN, 2026-09-13. PASS.

Build: display-loadtest at anims/astra b24b3fcb, reported by the endpoint as
v1.9.8-sleep9-672-gb24b3fcb-dirty, built 2026-09-13T14:04:01Z. The -dirty is
three uncommitted files other agents had in flight in the shared checkout
(AnimOrbits.cpp, CatGradientPicker.cpp and .h, SettingsUI.h); none of them is
in the tone publish path, which is BgAnimCommon.cpp, SleepAnimation.cpp and .h
and WebUIPluginDebug.cpp, all clean at b24b3fcb. Bench board 192.168.1.121,
pixel clock divider 7 read live from /api/debug/pclk. Stored settings
untouched; the fixture was disarmed and the tone override cleared at the end.

THE CHECK

  python3 tools/gradient_fb_check.py --host 192.168.1.121 --tone 60,65 --tone 90,95

  PASS: 38,400 samples compared, 0 mismatches.
  Four passes, two tones by two column offsets, both framebuffers each.
  60/65 converted to 153/165, 90/95 to 230/242, ramp indices 0 to 255 covered.
  No pass was left waiting: every arm settled and the 15 second deadline never
  fired, so no run ended with the message naming the step it stopped at.

THE THREE THINGS THE BEAD ASKED FOR

1. tonedFrames climbs, and it climbs at the render rate. Measured over a 10.23
s window with the fixture armed: anim_frames 16.1 a second and tonedFrames
16.1 a second, so every rendered frame is counted and none is lost to a
rebuild of the table. It restarts at 0 on every arm and on every tone change,
which is what the region and offset moving with the arm requires.

2. fixApplied catches up with applied after a tone change. Watched across
three changes with the endpoint polled as fast as it answers
(tone_window_obs.py in job 54de0aae tmp):

  arm at 60/65     0.000 s  pct 60/65  int 256/255  applied 655104  fix 517350  toned 0
                   0.166 s  pct 60/65  int 256/255  applied 655104  fix 655104  toned 1
                   0.293 s  pct 60/65  int 153/165  applied 739993  fix 655104  toned 0
                   0.371 s  pct 60/65  int 153/165  applied 739993  fix 739993  toned 0
                   6.003 s                                                      toned 46
  change to 90/95  0.000 s  pct 90/95  int 153/165  applied 739993  fix 739993  toned 0
                   0.230 s  pct 90/95  int 230/242  applied 910566  fix 910566  toned 1
  change to 40/45  0.000 s  pct 40/45  int 230/242  applied 910566  fix 910566  toned 0
                   0.338 s  pct 40/45  int 102/114  applied 975974  fix 975974  toned 0

3. The window this replaces, measured again beside the new counters. The
reported percentages are the request from the moment the arm returns, while
the integers and the published palette are still the previous tone: 293 ms at
the first arm, 230 ms and 338 ms at the two later changes. That sits inside
the 230 to 394 ms the earlier measurement named, so the window is the same
size as before and the counters are what now make it visible.

WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS ABOUT THE OLD GATE

Read the first arm again at 0.166 s. The percentages are the request, the
integers are the previous tone, applied and fixApplied are equal at 655104,
consistent is true, and tonedFrames has reached 1. Every condition the old
gate could see is satisfied, and the strip at that instant is drawn from the
previous palette: applied moves to 739993 only at 0.293 s. So the accepted
sample would have been a stale strip against a fresh expectation, which is
the failure mode the bead set out to remove.

What keeps the new gate out of it is the frame count, and the margin is not
large. Frames arrive about every 62 ms, --settle is 2 (one per framebuffer
read), so two frames is about 124 ms against a palette that published at
293 ms here. On this board the gate has roughly 170 ms of margin. A device
drawing faster, or a longer publish, would narrow it. Worth knowing if
--settle is ever lowered or the fixture is ever run on a faster panel.

THE LATENT FAULT IS FIXED

No black or flat strip on the first arm after boot. Read straight after a
boot and before any arm, /api/debug/gradfix gave applied 261888 with
fixApplied 0, so the two do not start equal and the first armed frame builds
its table. The first arm after the reset was the check's own first pass and
it compared 9,600 samples with 0 mismatches.

ONE THING THAT COST A RUN, NOT A FAULT IN THIS WORK

The first attempt at the check hung for nine minutes with no output and was
killed. The board's WiFi link had degraded to 20 to 60 percent packet loss
(gm-t9ld), which a framebuffer read cannot survive. A reset restored the link
and the check then passed first time. Nothing in this bead's code was
involved: the fixture counters read healthy throughout the bad window.

CORRECTION to the paragraph above headed "What keeps the new gate out of it".

I attributed the protection to the frame count and to a 170 ms margin. That
is wrong, and reading the trace again says so. The protection is structural
and there is no margin to lose.

Look at what moves together in all three changes:

  arm 60/65    0.166 s  int 256/255  applied 655104
               0.293 s  int 153/165  applied 739993
  to 90/95     0.000 s  int 153/165  applied 739993
               0.230 s  int 230/242  applied 910566
  to 40/45     0.000 s  int 230/242  applied 910566
               0.338 s  int 102/114  applied 975974

The reported integers and the published palette word change in the same
sample, every time. That is this commit: themeToneState() unpacks the word
that publishStops() stored last with release ordering, so the integers the
endpoint reports can no longer be ahead of the palette they belong to.

So at 0.166 s the gate refuses on the integer condition, not on the frame
count: the percentages are 60/65 but the integers are 256/255, which is the
conversion of 100/100, and gate_problems requires the integers to be the
conversion of the reported percentages. The stale state is unreachable by
construction rather than by timing.

That also corrects what I said about the production divider. There is nothing
divider dependent here: the answer does not change at divider 6, because it
never depended on the frame cadence.

WHY --settle MUST NOT GO BELOW 2 ANYWAY

The reason is not the race. One rendered frame writes one framebuffer, the
check reads both, so two framebuffers need two frames drawn from the new
palette before both carry it. At --settle 1 the second buffer can still hold
the previous frame, which is the stale-buffer failure the tool's own comment
about vetoing interlacing exists to prevent. The tool already raises --settle
to the number of buffers being read, and that floor is the correct one.

The measured cost of that floor on this board: frames arrive about every 62 ms
with the fixture armed, so two frames add about 124 ms to each pass, and a
four pass run spends about half a second waiting. Cheap.

title: Make duplicate gradient names addressable in settings tests
description:
Follow up commit 66526a20.

`Rig.rows_on_page` now preserves duplicate visible names, but the rest of the harness still treats a name as row identity. `find_tag`, `picker_tap`, `picker_selected_rows`, and `swatch_strip` select the first matching tag. The repeated-name fixture gives both `Custom` entries identical stops and checks only row names and counts.

The current checks all pass under these mutations:

- Both `Custom` rows draw c1's swatch.
- Tapping the second `Custom` row writes c1 instead of c3.
- The c1 and c3 callbacks are swapped.
- The selection marker is attached to the wrong duplicate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The repeated-name fixture gives c1 and c3 visibly distinct stop strings.
- [ ] Test helpers can address each duplicate row by stable row object or position rather than by visible name alone.
- [ ] Named checks verify the swatch of each `Custom` row against its own stored stops.
- [ ] Named checks tap each duplicate separately and verify that the exact c1 or c3 ref is stored.
- [ ] Named checks preselect c1 and c3 separately and verify that the marker appears on the corresponding row.
- [ ] A mutation that makes both rows draw or select c1 fails at least one named check.
- [ ] The full settings UI suite passes with the new checks counted.
notes:
Done in 1c6d91d6.

What changed. Rig gained row_slots (the page's row containers top to bottom,
the same order and the same set rows_on_page names) and find_in_row (the
lookup find_tag does, narrowed to one row's subtree), plus tag_row and
tag_role as static methods. The repeated-name fixture gives c1 "ff0000,ff2000"
and c3 "0000ff,0020ff" while the other ten keep the grey ramp. Eight checks
address the two Custom rows by slot rather than by name: slots_match_names,
slot0_swatch_is_c1, slot2_swatch_is_c3, custom_swatches_differ,
slot2_tap_writes_c3, slot0_tap_writes_c1, c1_marks_slot0, c3_marks_slot2.
The swatch oracle reads the strip's two ends against that row's own stored
stops, with a tolerance of 20 for RGB565 quantisation; the interior is
GradientSwatch.cpp's own transcription and swatch_parity.cpp is what holds
that to the real palette code.

Mutations. All four were built in a scratch copy of the worktree under the
job tmp directory and never entered the shared tree. Against the checks as
they stood at HEAD every one passed, 7 checks and 0 failures each. Against
the new checks:

  both rows draw c1        fails slot2_swatch_is_c3 and custom_swatches_differ
  second row writes c1     fails slot2_tap_writes_c3
  the callbacks swapped    fails slot2_tap_writes_c3 and slot0_tap_writes_c1
  marker on the wrong row  fails c1_marks_slot0 and c3_marks_slot2

Checks. python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py: PASS, 607 checks over 8 scenarios,
animation 222 to 230, every other scenario unchanged. Nothing needed the
board.

Every acceptance criterion is met.

Left standing, worth its own bead: picker_selected_rows still reads the
marker by name (rig.find_tag), so on this fixture it reports no marked row at
all when the second Custom is the selected one. gm-nov3.31 uses it in waits
rather than assertions, so it fails as a timeout and not as a false pass.

title: Make restart and missing route checks reject unrelated HTTP errors
description:
The settings harness treats every `RigHTTPError` as proof of two specific conditions.

`long_hold_restarts_process` and `second_hold_restarts_after_forced_failure` pass whenever the tap request or any release poll raises `RigHTTPError`. The exception also covers HTTP 500, malformed JSON, and unrelated socket faults. Those failures do not establish that the simulator process exited.

`anim_unavailable_on_sim` and `synth_unavailable_on_sim` likewise pass on every `RigHTTPError`. They are meant to establish that the route fell through to the simulator's static web response. A registered but broken route returning 500 or malformed JSON currently passes too.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restart checks verify that the simulator process actually exited, or otherwise distinguish expected process termination from an HTTP error while it remains alive.
- [ ] An injected HTTP 500 during either restart tap fails the intended restart check.
- [ ] An injected malformed response or transient socket error while the simulator remains alive fails the intended restart check.
- [ ] Route-absence checks verify the documented static or SPA fallback rather than accepting every `RigHTTPError`.
- [ ] A simulator route registered but returning HTTP 500 fails its absence check.
- [ ] A simulator route registered with malformed JSON fails its absence check.
- [ ] The full settings UI suite passes after the checks are hardened.
notes:
Done in e86f39da.

What changed. Rig gained fetch() (status, headers and body, no exception on
an HTTP status error) and route_absent() (the reply must match GET /, which
is what WebUIPlugin.cpp's onNotFound sends an unrouted URL outside /assets/
to). Sim gained exit_code() and wait_exited(). The two restart checks in
test_status.py now wait for the simulator process to exit instead of
accepting a failed request, and the two route checks in test_rig.py call
route_absent().

Proof. Faults were injected at urllib.request.urlopen inside the rig module,
so the copy of the harness at HEAD and the fixed copy saw the same fault.
Eight injections, each passing before and failing after: HTTP 500, a
non-JSON 200 and a socket reset on the first Restart hold; the same three on
the second hold in the forced flush failure scenario; HTTP 500 on
/api/debug/anim and /api/debug/synth; a malformed JSON 200 on the same two.
With no fault all four checks pass on both copies. The driver is
tmp/nov329/inject.py in the job scratch directory, not checked in.

Checks. Full suite 572 checks over 8 scenarios, no change in count (this
bead hardens checks, it does not add any): temps 48, display 35, animation
222, gradientdraft 105, machine 39, schedules 91, status 40, rig 19. status
and rig both pass. One earlier full run failed display_firmware_matches_build
because the display-sim binary was two commits older than src/version.h; a
rebuild and a rerun of status and rig passed. gradientdraft reads 105 here
against 78 at HEAD because another agent's work is in flight in that file.

Every acceptance criterion is met. Nothing needed the board.

title: Display gradient picker page with swatch rows
description:
Replace the display's three gradient cycles with one reusable child-page picker showing names and swatches.

Depend on gm-nov3.2 for the category and stops provider, gm-nov3.7 for the safe ref and mirror rules, and gm-nov3.8 for the generated runner data before changing its arrow-based interactions.

The existing arrows wrap and repeat on hold. The reason to replace them is to make the larger collection visible before selection.

## Navigation and selection

Turn "Gradient all", "Gradient" and "Standby grad" into whole-row targets showing their current values. Remove their arrow targets rather than covering them with another clickable object.

Use SettingsUI::pushPage and the existing page lifecycle:

- The first child lists Global first for a per-animation picker, then My gradients when non-empty, then the declared categories with counts.
- Gradient all does not offer Global. It must select a concrete gradient.
- Choosing a category or My gradients opens its gradients, each with a name, swatch and selected marker.
- Choosing a gradient writes its stable ref and returns to the Animation category. Choosing Global clears only the captured animation's map slot and returns directly from the first child.
- Header arrows and horizontal swipes paginate within a child. They do not leave the picker or select a gradient.
- The exit chevron pops one child without making a selection.

One component serves all three entry rows and returns a ref through a callback. Capture which animation slot is being edited. Do not silently retarget a picker because a web save changed the main or standby animation.

Keep Standby grad disabled when standby follows the main animation or names the same animation. Preserve the current "Same as main" text.

Apply a selection through the existing live-write behavior: track touched fields, write the correct map slot or global ref, follow gm-nov3.7's mirror policy, mark the UI dirty and end any conflicting preview.

## Swatches

Show a toned RGB565 ramp using the current animation brightness and highlight rolloff. Match the production uniform and positional interpolation paths, including 2 to 16 library stops, repeated positions and flat endpoint extensions. A standard ramp does not claim to reproduce Plasma's wheel or an animation's extra gain.

Keep LV_GRADIENT_MAX_STOPS at 2. Raising it enlarges value-held gradient and rect draw descriptors for unrelated draws. The drawing method is the implementer's choice.

Sampling another gradient for a swatch must not publish it as the active animation theme. Release any row-owned image or buffer through the page lifecycle.

## Reconcile and teardown

Only the top page receives reconcile. A child must also bring its retained Animation draft up to date for untouched fields, as schedule children do for their parent.

On a web save, either rebuild the picker from current settings or close it without making a new selection. In both cases, reconcile the parent draft before it becomes visible. Preserve earlier touched display choices under the existing per-field rule.

Validate a chosen ref against current data under Settings::Guard. A deleted library entry or stale list index must not be selected. If the edited animation is no longer a valid target, close without selecting.

Deleting a page root precedes destroying its context. Do not access a row, child context or invalidated stack reference after popping it. An external screen change tears down the full settings cover through the existing shell path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] SettingsRows contains the named swatch row, with debug tags and a canonical current value available through the touch map.
- [x] All three entry rows use the same picker and write through callbacks that preserve live writes, touched-field tracking and the safe mirror policy.
- [x] Simulator tests open each enabled entry row, paginate categories and gradients, choose a built-in and a saved gradient, and verify the row text and exact stored ref.
- [x] Global appears first only for per-animation pickers, names the current global, and clears only the captured animation's map slot when chosen.
- [x] Empty and full library fixtures respectively hide My gradients and make all twelve entries reachable. Every built-in is reachable, including the final partial page.
- [x] Standby grad stays disabled for standby -1 and for standby equal to main, with no setting change when tapped.
- [x] Pixel tests compare swatch samples with production ramp samples for a six-stop built-in and library fixtures with 2 and 16 stops, non-uniform and repeated positions, and flat endpoint runs at default and non-default tone settings.
- [x] Source inspection confirms swatch generation does not change the active theme and LV_GRADIENT_MAX_STOPS remains 2.
- [x] Tests cover web changes to an untouched parent field while each child level is open, then return to the parent and verify fresh values. Earlier touched display fields retain their drafts and win at commit.
- [x] Tests cover deletion of the displayed library entry and a change of the edited animation while the picker is open. No stale entry or unintended animation slot is written.
- [x] Web-interference tests verify that the external write actually landed before checking reconciliation. Use a simulator fixture or test adapter that exercises the real rules, or a recorded browser-driven device test. The simulator's always-false validators are not a passing result.
- [x] Rig.audit passes on all picker page shapes, including longest labels and the full library. Keep the existing exit-role size and edge exemptions; no overlap exemption is added.
- [x] Tests distinguish pagination from exit: swiping a row does not select it, chevrons cancel one level, and choosing returns to Animation. No-choice visits leave gradient settings unchanged.
- [ ] External brew and standby transitions commit prior touched fields and remove the entire cover without stale objects or callbacks.
- [x] Update the runner's old gradient-arrow scenarios to use the picker while retaining their map isolation and touched-field checks.
- [ ] Simulator and device runs pass the new navigation and geometry checks. Device measurements record picker and ordinary settings page frame rates under the same animation, parameters, tone, frame cap, interlace and panel divider. Record repeated baseline variation and investigate a picker cost outside that variation.
- [ ] Source inspection and device captures confirm the picker remains a transparent settings cover on the menu screen with no translucent page plate.
notes:
Landed on anims/astra in two commits: 3b0db5a7 (the swatch row, the swatch

and their host tests) and 265501e0 (the picker, the three rows wired to it,

What is where:

Evidence:

Three criteria left unchecked, all for the same reason: the bench board was

Also worth knowing for the follow-up beads:

title: Correct stale descriptions of gradient id allocation
description:
Commit e32c4577 replaced largest-id-plus-one allocation with the lowest id in 1 through 99999 that is not held by a library entry or named by a stored ref. Several comments still describe the removed allocator as current behavior.

Correct the comments without weakening the high-id compatibility coverage. Existing devices and valid stored strings may still contain ids produced by the old allocator. Id 14 is also reachable with the current allocator when ids 1 through 13 are reserved by entries or dangling refs. Id 99999 remains valid grammar and a useful boundary fixture, but the current UI cannot normally reach it under the library and map caps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnim.h` describes lowest-unreserved allocation in both id-range comments.
- [ ] `src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimThemes.cpp` no longer says the current web editor increments the largest id.
- [ ] `src/display/ui/default/settings/GradientSwatch.cpp` distinguishes legacy high ids from ids generated by the current allocator.
- [ ] `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py` and `tools/animbench/swatch_parity.cpp` give an accurate reason for retaining the c14 and c99999 fixtures.
- [ ] The high-id parser, resolver, swatch, and picker checks remain in place and pass.
notes:
Done in ddc897c5. Comments only, no code.

Six stale lines, not the five the bead counted. BgAnim.h has two (the
BG_GRADIENT_ID_MAX comment and the migration's allocation rule),
BgAnimThemes.cpp one (why ReservedIds is a list), GradientSwatch.cpp one (why
the id range is not the capacity), test_animation.py one (library_renumbered's
docstring) and swatch_parity.cpp one (why the fixture ids are 1, 14 and
99999). All six said the web editor allocates by incrementing the largest id.

Each now carries both halves, because both are live. The current allocator
fills gaps, but an id a stored ref still names stays reserved, so 1 to 13 can
all be held while three entries exist and the next id is 14. Anything higher
is legacy: the old allocator had no ceiling, and the entries it wrote are on
devices and still valid. The c14 and c99999 fixtures are kept, one for each
route to a high id, and their comments now say which is which.

One line that reads like a member of the group is not stale and was checked
rather than rewritten: test_animation.py's "14 is the first id the old
resolver refused; 99999 is the largest the ref grammar accepts". Both halves
are true and it says nothing about allocation. It is extended to name the two
routes, not corrected.

Checks. pio run -e display-sim passes. pio test -e native_settingsui, 68 of 68.
tools/animbench make check, which builds and runs swatch_parity, ALL OK (42 of
44 exact, 2 within a recorded allowance). The settings UI suite was run on a
scratch copy carrying this change alone on top of HEAD: animation 230 checks
and gradientdraft 105, both with no failures, which covers the high-id parser,
resolver, swatch and picker checks. That copy is not a git repository, so its
build wrote an empty BUILD_GIT_VERSION and two version checks in the status
scenario fail there for that reason alone; in the shared checkout the status
scenario runs 40 checks with no failures. Animation and gradientdraft do fail
in the shared checkout right now, on gm-nov3.32's uncommitted work
(gradient_row_has_no_arrows, high_id_row_draws_the_chosen_ramp,
legacy_picker_global_swatch_is_uniform), not on this.

Nothing needed the board. Every acceptance criterion is met.

title: Keep the gradient picker open when a gradient is picked
description:
Owner's request, 2026-09-13: it must be possible to cycle through the gradients
on the display quickly, changing to the next one with a single tap.

This bead is half of that. It makes browsing inside the picker one tap per
gradient. The other half, stepping without opening the picker at all, is a
separate bead.

## What is slow now

Applying is already live. `globalGradientPicked` writes `bgAnimGradientRef` the
moment the picker returns and the panel resolves its palette from that stored
ref, so the gradient is on screen immediately. What costs the time is that a
pick calls `popPages` and throws the user out of the picker
(`applyPick`, `CatGradientPicker.cpp:228`). Trying five gradients is five trips
in and out of a two level page stack.

## What to change

A pick applies the gradient and leaves the user on the page. The selection
marker moves to the tapped row. The chevron is how you leave.

That is the whole feature: `applyPick` stops popping. Everything it does before
the pop is already correct and stays exactly as it is, including the ordering
note in the comment above it, which is about the draft and the rebuild rather
than about leaving.

Apply the same rule to the "Global" entry on the top level page: it assigns and
the marker moves, rather than assigning and closing. A user comparing the
global gradient against a per animation override should not be thrown out for
picking one of them.

## What must not break

Four things the picker already gets right, all of them recorded in
`src/display/ui/default/settings/README.md` and in CLAUDE.md.

A pick is written before `popPages`, because the pop rebuilds the page
underneath from the draft. With the pop gone from the ordinary path, check that
the page underneath is still rebuilt correctly when the user finally does
leave, and that the marker on the page underneath agrees.

The picker captures the animation slot it was opened for and never retargets it
under a web save. `pickerReconcile` still pops when `stillValid` goes false (the
standby animation being turned off, say). That pop stays, and it must still
free both ctxs safely now that a pick no longer does.

Each level calls the opening category's reconcile itself, since the shell
reconciles only the top page. A pick that stays open now happens many times per
visit rather than once, so confirm the reconcile path is idempotent and does not
accumulate anything per pick.

gm-nov3.23's rule holds: the global gradient row is a live field re-asserted at
reconcile when a web save has replaced it. Repeated picks must not fight that.

## What to check about writes

Stepping is not this bead, but repeated picks are, and each one writes a
settings property. Confirm that a pick writes the in-memory property and that
NVS is written by the periodic flush rather than once per pick, and say so in
the notes with the line that establishes it. If a pick does force a flush, say
so plainly: that changes what the stepper bead is allowed to do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tapping a gradient in a picker group page applies it and the page stays
      open, with the selection marker on the tapped row.
- [ ] Tapping the "Global" entry on the top level page assigns and stays open
      with the marker moved.
- [ ] The chevron leaves the picker and the page underneath shows the gradient
      that was last picked.
- [ ] Picking three different gradients in one visit and then leaving commits
      the third, and the panel is on the third throughout.
- [ ] A scenario check in `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py` drives
      three picks in one visit and asserts the stored ref after each, the marker
      position after each, and the value on the page underneath after leaving.
- [ ] The check fails against a binary built from a scratch copy of the parent
      commit, and the report says which assertions failed.
- [ ] `pickerReconcile`'s pop on `stillValid` going false still works: a check
      turns the standby animation off with the picker open and the picker
      closes without selecting.
- [ ] `pio run -e display-sim`, `python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only
      animation,gradientdraft` and `pio test -e native_settingsui` all pass,
      with check counts before and after.
- [ ] The notes say whether a pick writes NVS or only the in-memory property,
      with the line that shows it.
notes:
Done in 9bc2f24c (branch anims/astra). The message was amended from 57791225;
the tree is identical and only the wording changed.

What changed. applyPick no longer pops. It runs the same guarded transaction
and returns whether the picker may stay open; each row handler then redraws
its own page. The first page calls rebuildEntries, the group page calls
rebuildEntries and then refreshGroup, because the group's rows index into the
parent's list. Two outcomes still pop: TargetGone closes both levels, which is
the same answer pickerReconcile gives when stillValid goes false, and a group
page left with no entries goes back one level, which groupReconcile already
does. A ref that no longer resolves (RefGone) used to close the picker; it now
leaves the user on the page with the deleted row dropped by the rebuild, and
still writes nothing.

THE WRITE QUESTION. A pick writes the in-memory property only. It does not
touch NVS. Property::set stores the value and sets the dirty flag
(src/display/core/Property.h:85, "bool set(const T &newValue)"), and NVS is
written by the periodic flush: Settings::loopTask calls doSave() and then
vTaskDelay(5000 / portTICK_PERIOD_MS) (src/display/core/Settings.cpp:495).
Nothing on the pick path calls flushNow; the only flushNow in the settings UI
is CatStatus.cpp's Restart row. So a stepper that repeats ten times a second
costs ten Property::set calls a second and at most one NVS write per five
seconds, whatever the rate. That is the answer gm-nov3.32 was waiting on.

What must not break, checked. The write ordering is unchanged and still
matters, because the chevron pops in the end: the pick writes the draft and
popPages rebuilds the page underneath from it. A new scenario check drives
that. The reconcile path is idempotent and accumulates nothing per pick:
animReconcile recomputes from fixed size per animation vectors and its global
re-assertion is a compare then set, and the preview-end trigger it fires sets
previewUntil to 0. gm-nov3.23's live global field is untouched.

Checks. pio run -e display-sim and pio run -e display both build; the
production image is 5,905,563 bytes, 90.1% of the app partition. pio test -e
native_settingsui 68 of 68, same as the parent. settings_ui_test.py --only
animation,gradientdraft: animation 222 of 222 before and after, gradientdraft
78 of 78 before and 105 of 105 after.

Failing first. A scratch copy of the parent commit (e536caf1) with its own pio
tree, carrying the new test file and nothing else of mine: gradientdraft 96
checks, 7 failed. stay_open_pick0_stays_open (depth 1, want 3),
stay_open_pick0_marker_moved (marked [], want ['Espresso']),
pick_keeps_the_picker_open_exception (no row 'Cappuccino' on any of the 4
pages, because the second tap landed on the Animation page),
global_entry_stays_open (depth 1, want 2), global_entry_marker_moved,
global_entry_chevron_leaves (depth 0, want 1) and
global_entry_keeps_the_picker_open_exception.

Why the helper waits changed, since it reads as a loosened check and is not.
test_animation.py's picker helpers waited for the page stack to shrink, which
a pick no longer does. They wait for the selection marker instead. A shrinking
page stack only proved the picker left, and it would have proved that whether
or not the pick wrote anything, including on the two outcomes above that leave
without writing. The marker proves the selection landed on the row the caller
named, which is what those checks were about. None of the ten checks that go
through picker_choose failed under the stronger wait, so none was relying on
the weaker one.

Scope note for whoever picks up gm-nov3.32. Five sites in test_animation.py
assumed the pop and had to move with the firmware: picker_choose, pick_ref's
Global branch, and three checks that waited for the pop inline
(gradient_picker_navigation, gradient_picker_high_library_ids,
gradient_picker_web_interference). No check was added or removed, so the count
stays 222. CatAnimation.cpp was not touched.

Not checked: the device. Another agent held the board, so nothing here ran on
hardware. Everything above is the simulator and the host.

title: Step to the next gradient from the row, without opening the picker
description:
Owner's request, 2026-09-13: it must be possible to cycle through the gradients
on the display quickly, changing to the next one with a single tap.

This bead is the half that does not open the picker at all. The other half,
making a pick inside the picker keep the page open, is a separate bead.

## This reopens a decision, on purpose

gm-nov3.3 took the arrows off the three gradient rows and made each row a whole
row target that pushes the picker. The reason recorded in CLAUDE.md is a real
constraint and not a preference: "a row-wide target laid over them is two
targets in one place and `Rig.audit()` fails on the overlap". The owner has now
said the stepping was worth having. Both can be true, because the overlap came
from the target being row wide, not from the arrows existing.

## The layout

Three targets in one 320x56 row, none overlapping, each at least 56x56
effective:

    +------------------------------------------+
    |  Gradient          Ember Glow   |  <  |  > |
    +------------------------------------------+
       centre band, 200 px            prev  next
       tap opens the picker           step  step

`kTextColW` is already 200 (`SettingsRows.cpp:101`) and `settingsRowChoiceCreate`
already builds a text column with a prev and a next arrow, so this is close to
the existing choice row. What is new is that the centre column becomes a tap
target of its own, opening the picker, instead of the row container being the
target.

`Rig.audit()` is the check, not the argument. Every effective hit rectangle must
be at least 56x56, must not overlap another on the same page, and must keep
12 px of clearance from the panel's edge circle. Run it and quote the smallest
target and the closest pair. If the three targets cannot be made to fit, say so
with the measured numbers and fall back to a separate "Browse gradients" row,
which costs one of the five row slots on that page. Do not ship an overlap.

## Hold to run

The arrows repeat while held, which is what makes 60 gradients browsable.
`wireRepeatBtn` and LVGL's defaults already give 400 ms then every 100 ms.
Use the existing mechanism rather than a timer: CLAUDE.md requires holds to be
driven only by the events LVGL delivers to the row, never by an `lv_timer` that
could outlive it.

The choice row's arrow deliberately has no fast tier (`choiceStepAdapter` drops
`fast`). Keep that: ten gradients a second is already fast, and a fast tier
would skip past the one the user wanted.

## The order has to be the picker's order

Stepping walks a flat list of every gradient the picker can reach, in the same
order the picker shows them: category by category, entries within a category in
their existing order. A user who steps to something and then opens the picker
must find the marker where they expect it. Wrap at both ends.

Say in the notes what the list does about the "Global" entry on a per animation
row, since that is a real choice and not an obvious one: it is a member of the
list on rows where it exists, so stepping can reach it.

## Live apply, and the write path

Each step applies immediately, the same write the row already makes.

**Read the picker bead's finding about writes before building the repeat.** If
a step writes the in-memory property and NVS is persisted by the periodic flush,
holding an arrow is fine. If a step forces a flush, ten flushes a second is not
acceptable and the step needs to write the property and let the existing flush
carry it. State which it is, with the line that shows it.

## What must not break

The three rows are the global gradient, the per animation gradient and the
standby gradient. All three get the same treatment.

gm-nov3.23's rule holds on the global row: it is a live field, and
`animReconcile` re-asserts the touched value when a web save has replaced it.
Stepping sets that touched state the same way picking does.

The per animation and standby rows are inert when `bgAnimStandbyId` is -1
(follow the main animation). An inert row's arrows must be inert too, not
stepping a value nobody can see.

`CatAnimation.cpp` clamps `bgAnimId` into the live registry at `enter` and at
`reconcile`, because a stored id from a longer registry wrote past the end of a
heap vector on the first Gradient arrow press once already (91cb0ed5). The
arrows are coming back, so that clamp is load bearing again: check it covers
the new stepping path and add a check that exercises it.

Every target presses the same way, 40% toward the touch dim colour
(`settingsPressedColor`). The arrows are `lv_img` inside a button, which
`applyPressedFeedbackTo` already covers, but confirm it on the device or the
simulator rather than assuming.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the three gradient rows has a prev and a next arrow that step to
      the adjacent gradient in the picker's own flat order, wrapping at both
      ends.
- [ ] A tap on the row's centre band still opens the picker.
- [ ] `Rig.audit()` passes on every page carrying a gradient row, and the report
      quotes the smallest target and the closest non overlapping pair.
- [ ] Holding an arrow repeats at LVGL's default cadence and steps once per
      repeat, with no fast tier.
- [ ] Each step applies to the panel immediately.
- [ ] The notes state whether a step writes NVS or only the in-memory property,
      with the line that shows it, and holding an arrow for five seconds does
      not write NVS once per step.
- [ ] Stepping to a gradient and then opening the picker shows the marker on
      that gradient.
- [ ] The standby row's arrows are inert when the standby animation follows the
      main one.
- [ ] A check exercises the registry clamp through the new stepping path, in
      the shape 91cb0ed5 fixed.
- [ ] `pio run -e display-sim`, `python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only
      animation,gradientdraft`, `pio test -e native_settingsui` and
      `pio run -e display` all pass, with check counts before and after.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's "A gradient is chosen on a pushed picker page" bullet is
      corrected: the arrows are back, the reason they were removed is recorded
      as solved by the centre band rather than as wrong, and the audit numbers
      are quoted.
notes:
Done in 8caa4cc6 (branch anims/astra). Simulator and host only; the board was
not held and nothing was flashed.

What landed. A new row widget, settingsRowSwatchStepCreate (SettingsRows.h,
SettingsRows.cpp), and the three gradient rows in CatAnimation.cpp built from
it. Three targets in the 320x56 slot: a centre band 200 px wide (kTextColW, the
width a choice row's text column has) that pushes the picker through the same
onActivate the whole row used to, and a prev and a next arrow. The row
container is no longer clickable, so it is not a target and there is no
overlap. It keeps its "action" tag, which is what lets a caller that taps the
row's centre still land on the band (centre x 239, band 80 to 279) and what
keeps rows_on_page counting one row here.

Layout, measured with Rig.audit() on all four Animation pages (simulator): no
violations on any page, smallest target 200x56 (the band), closest pair inside
a gradient row 4 px (prev to next), band to prev 12 px. The arrows sit exactly
where a choice row's arrows sit, hit boxes (292,y)-(347,y+55) and
(352,y)-(407,y+55), which is a layout the audit already passed, and the edge
rule has almost no slack there: the bottom row's far corner is 227.2 px from
the panel centre against a 228 px limit, so the band could not have been made
wider.

Order. gradientStepOrder/gradientStepRef (CatAnimation.cpp) flatten
CatGradientPicker's own order: Global first where the row offers it, then the
saved gradients in stored order, then each declared category's built-ins in
table order, wrapping at both ends. The "Global" entry is a member of the list
on the two per-animation rows, so stepping reaches it; the global row's own
list has no Global in it, because the global is what "Global" means and its
picker offers no such entry. A ref that is in no group (a deleted library
entry, or the retained pre-library custom gradient on the global row) is not a
position, so the next arrow enters at the head and the prev arrow at the tail.
The global row steps from what it displays, not from the raw ref: with no ref
stored the row names the built-in the legacy pair resolves to.

Writes. A step writes only the in-memory property. Property::set stores the
value and raises a dirty flag (src/display/core/Property.h:85); NVS is written
by the periodic flush, Settings::loopTask calling doSave() and then waiting
5000 ms (src/display/core/Settings.cpp:496), and doSave returns early when
nothing is dirty. Nothing on the step path calls flushNow. Measured: a five
second hold stepped 45 times and left three distinct readings of bg_thm in the
simulator's NVS file. The simulator does not run loopTask at all, it flushes
from sim/main.cpp:199 every 2000 ms, so three readings (the one before the hold
plus two flushes) is the venue's own period and not one write per step. The
device's period is the 5000 ms above, which is stricter.

Repeat cadence: wireRepeatBtn and LVGL's own events, once on PRESSED and once
per LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT (400 ms then every 100 ms), no fast tier, no lv_timer.

The clamp. animGradientPicked was split into animGradientAssign(ctx, animId,
ref) so the arrows and the picker write through one function with its bounds
check. clampAnimId at enter and at reconcile still covers the stepping path,
and check_step_survives_an_anim_id_past_the_registry exercises it in the shape
91cb0ed5 fixed: store bgAnimId past the roster, open the category, press the
Gradient next arrow. It passes.

Press feedback, confirmed rather than assumed (simulator, mean framebuffer

title: Make the gradient swatch checks assert which gradient, not that one exists
description:
The seventh and eighth instances of the cannot-fail pattern in this epic, both in `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py`. Found and measured by the lane that closed gm-nov3.28, which also built the oracle that fixes them.

## The fault

Four checks assert `len(set(strip)) > 4` over a swatch strip and are named as though they establish which gradient was drawn:

    picker_row_draws_a_ramp            line ~913
    high_id_picker_row_draws_a_ramp    ~1169
    high_id_all_row_draws_a_ramp       ~1205
    high_id_standby_row_draws_a_ramp   ~1230

The name claims the row drew the chosen gradient. The assertion says only that some ramp was drawn.

**Measured on the simulator against the fixture library, 2026-09-13: all twelve entries draw between 46 and 80 distinct colours.** Every one clears the threshold by a factor of ten. So a row drawing any other library entry, or a built-in, or a fallback, passes all four.

## Where it is weakest

`high_id_all_row_draws_a_ramp` and `high_id_standby_row_draws_a_ramp` are the only two checks covering ref `c99999`. That is the top of the ref grammar and the whole reason the fixture id exists. A resolver that quietly fell back to a default for `c99999` while still drawing something would pass both, and nothing else would notice.

Only `high_id_row_draws_the_chosen_ramp` is already a real identity check: it compares the row strip against the picker strip.

## The oracle already exists

`swatch_matches_stops(strip, stops)` in the same file, added by gm-nov3.28, compares the strip's two ends against that row's own stored stops with a tolerance of 20 for RGB565 quantisation. The two ends are enough, and the interior is deliberately not re-derived here: `GradientSwatch.cpp` is already a transcription of the palette arithmetic, and `tools/animbench/swatch_parity.cpp` is what holds it to the real one. The tolerance comes from a measurement, `ff0000,ff2000` drawing (255,0,0) to (255,28,0) against a nominal (255,32,0).

Point the four checks at it, taking each row's stops from the stored library.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four checks compare the strip against the stops of the entry the row is meant to be showing, not against a colour count.
- [ ] A mutation that makes the row draw a different library entry fails each of the four, shown failing before and passing after, built in a scratch copy of the worktree. The recipe is in `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md` under "Proving a check fails, without breaking the shared checkout". The broken version must never enter the shared tree.
- [ ] `picker_selected_rows` (`test_animation.py` ~474) addresses the selection marker by row position through `rig.row_slots` and `rig.find_in_row`, not by name through `rig.find_tag`. On the repeated-name fixture it currently reports no marked row at all when the second "Custom" is the selected one. gm-nov3.31 uses it in `wait_until` rather than as an assertion, so today it fails as a timeout and not as a false pass, but it is one line from becoming one.
- [ ] The full settings UI suite passes, with the before and after counts quoted. It was 607 checks at ddc897c5.
notes:

committed README.md with a pathspec. Content is intact, attribution is not.

and the all/standby pair are high_id_all_row_draws_the_chosen_ramp and
high_id_standby_row_draws_the_chosen_ramp. A saved gradient's stops come

  M1, every saved gradient resolves to library entry 1
    before: all four passed, 50 to 73 distinct colours

           (drew Sunrise 255,153,57..0,214,156 against Citrus and Dusk)

--- Added after the lead's follow-up, same lane ---

Clobber check. Another lane wrote this file for about eleven minutes and

Two more commits, both in this file, after the lead handed them over.

40e91e72, open_picker. It tapped the row container's centre, x 239, which is

Counts after all four commits, against the tree at 40e91e72: animation 234

title: Four test helpers still address a gradient row by its name
description:
Four helpers in `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py` resolve a gradient row by its visible name through `rig.find_tag`, which returns the first match. Where two library entries carry the same user-typed name, they silently address the wrong one. Two independent reviews found this on 2026-09-13 and each caught something the other missed, so read the false-pass section below rather than either half.

## Scope, which is smaller than it first looks

`find_tag` has 127 call sites across the scenarios and all of them inherit first-match semantics, but only a helper that can be pointed at a **user-named** list can meet a duplicate. Every other row name in the harness is generated from code and is unique per page. So `tap_row`, `open_picker`, `picker_cancel` (a fixed `exit` tag), `rig.row_value`, and everything in `test_schedules.py`, `test_status.py`, `test_machine.py`, `test_display.py` and `test_temps.py` are out of scope.

`Rig.audit` is immune for its own reason: it walks hit rectangles and never resolves an object by tag.

## The four

- **`picker_tap`** (around line 430) taps `find_tag(dump, name, "action")`. Tapping the second `Custom` by name is impossible; it always taps the first.
- **`swatch_strip`** (around 488) reads `find_tag(dump, row, "swatch")`. It always reads the first duplicate's swatch. That is the mutation gm-nov3.28 had to catch by slot, so the fix is proven and only needs applying here.
- **`page_with_row`** (around 353) picks the page with `find_tag(dump, name, "value")`. With the duplicates on **different pages** it returns the first page holding one, so `picker_tap` then cannot reach the other at all. The current fixture puts both on page 0, which hides this completely.
- **`picker_selected_rows`** (around 474) loops over `rows_on_page`, which correctly keeps duplicates, but asks `find_tag` for the marker on each pass, so every iteration inspects the same object. Measured on the repeated-name fixture: with c1 selected it returns `['Custom', 'Custom']` where the truth is slot 0; with c3 selected it returns `[]` where the truth is slot 2. Wrong in both directions.

`pick_ref` (around 798) is the fifth caller and needs no separate fix: it converts a specific library ref back to a display name that is not unique, and then uses the helpers above. It is correct once they are.

## The false pass, which is live today

The two reviews disagreed about whether this can pass rather than fail, and resolving it makes the case worse than either said.

Most callers compare with `marked == [name]`, an exact list, so a wrong answer is a wrong failure and not a silent pass. But `picker_choose` (line 457) waits on **membership**:

    rig.wait_until(lambda: name in picker_selected_rows(rig), timeout=5)

With two rows named `Custom` and c3 intended, a marker landing on c1 gives `['Custom', 'Custom']`, membership is true, and the helper returns having confirmed the wrong row. Ten checks reach `picker_choose`. So this is a false pass now, not one edit away from being one.

`picker_selected_rows` has 19 call sites in all: 6 in `test_animation.py` and 13 in `test_gradientdraft.py`. Line 457 is the one that matters.

## What to build

`rig.row_slots` and `rig.find_in_row`, both added by gm-nov3.28, are what each of the four needs. A helper handed an ambiguous visible name should raise an explicit ambiguity error rather than quietly taking the first row: a loud failure is recoverable and a silent wrong answer is not.

## Not in this bead

The four swatch checks that assert a colour count instead of an identity are gm-nov3.33, which also owns this file. **Do this bead after gm-nov3.33 lands** and take your baseline at that HEAD.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `picker_tap`, `swatch_strip`, `page_with_row` and `picker_selected_rows` address a row by position or by ref, not by visible name alone.
- [ ] A picker helper handed an ambiguous visible name raises an explicit ambiguity error instead of selecting the first row.
- [ ] `picker_choose` no longer accepts name membership as proof that the intended row was selected.
- [ ] `pick_ref` restores c1 and c3 correctly when both entries have the same visible name.
- [ ] The repeated-name fixture places its two duplicates on **different pages**, so `page_with_row`'s fault is reachable. State what that change does to the existing checks.
- [ ] A mutation table in the shape gm-nov3.28 used, covering at least: asking `pick_ref` for c3 and watching it tap c1; moving the intended c3 marker to c1 and watching `picker_choose` accept it; corrupting c3's swatch while c1 is intact; and swapping the two rows' callbacks. Each shown passing before and failing after, built in a scratch copy, with the broken version never entering the shared tree. The recipe is in `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md`.
- [ ] The four positional regression checks from gm-nov3.28 remain and still fail under their original product mutations.
- [ ] The full settings UI suite passes, with before and after counts from the same tree.
- [ ] The "A name stood in for a row" bullet in `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md` names all four helpers and says which are fixed.
notes:
Done in ba4b5801 (tools/settings_ui_tests/test_animation.py, README.md).
rig.py needed no change: Rig.row_slots and Rig.find_in_row already had what
the helpers needed.

What changed. page_with_row sweeps every page of the list on top, and
row_place raises AmbiguousRowName when two rows carry the name; picker_tap
and swatch_strip take the row from its slot; row_at and picker_tap_at
address a row by its position in the list; picker_choose takes an index and
waits for the marker on that position and on no other row, instead of
waiting on name membership; pick_ref chooses a saved gradient by its place
in the library (library_row_index) and a built-in still by name, since all
60 built-in names are unique. picker_selected splits into
picker_selected_rows (names, 19 call sites unchanged) and
picker_selected_slots (positions). picker_selected_rows itself was already
fixed by gm-nov3.33 in 1e592cb0, verified, left alone.

Fixture. REPEATED_NAMES now repeats two names: "Custom" at list positions 0
and 5 (pages 0 and 1), which is what makes page_with_row's fault reachable,
and "Sunrise" at 1 and 3 (both on page 0), which keeps gm-xiu6's own fault
reachable, since a cross-page pair cannot show a page reading keyed by the
name. The four duplicated entries carry four different flat ramps. Effect on
the existing checks: repeated_names_both_customs_listed became one check per
pair; the swatch, tap and marker checks are keyed by list index rather than
by page 0 slot and now cover both pairs (the same-page pair keeps gm-nov3.28's
own arrangement); repeated_names_first_page_keeps_repeat still reads a repeat
on page 0, now the Sunrise pair. Nine checks added in that scenario, three of
them saying the helpers refuse a repeated name and one that a unique name
still resolves.

Mutations, each built in a scratch copy
(/mnt/c/Users/Oystein/.claude/jobs/54de0aae/tmp/nov3_34/scratch), never in the
shared tree. Control: 27 of 27 pass.
1. Harness back to addressing by name (row_place takes the first hit,
   pick_ref by name): repeated_names_pick_ref_restores_c6 fails with
   "pick_ref(c6) left 'c1'", and the page_with_row and picker_tap refusal
   checks fail.
2. CatGradientPicker.cpp marks the first row carrying the selected entry's
   name: repeated_names_c6_marks_index5 fails ("marked [0], want [5]"),
   c4_marks_index3 fails, and picker_choose refuses the pick (a 5 s
   timeout). With picker_choose put back to the old name membership wait,
   the same firmware mutation produces no failure from picker_choose at
   all, which is the false pass the bead named.
3. CatGradientPicker.cpp draws the first same-named entry's swatch:
   index5_swatch_is_c6 and index3_swatch_is_c4 fail, and both
   swatches_differ checks fail.
4. CatGradientPicker.cpp swaps the two same-named rows' callbacks:
   index5_tap_writes_c6, index0_tap_writes_c1 and index3_tap_writes_c4 fail.

Runs, simulator. Before (HEAD 3368100c): animation 234 checks clean in
211.1 s, gradientdraft 188 clean. After, same tree: animation 246 clean in
353 s, gradientdraft 188 clean. The whole suite in that tree passes every
scenario (the copy is not a git repository, so the status scenario's version
check fails there for that reason alone). The whole suite in the worktree at
HEAD a376536b: temps 48, display 35, animation 246 with 1 failed,
gradientdraft 209, machine 39, schedules 91, status 40, rig 19.

The one failure is not this bead: check_frame_rate_live_and_precedence's
web_save_landed reads bgAnimFps back after a web save, and gm-nov3.39
(995b4ba2) made the open category re-assert its touched frame rate, so the
read sees this visit's 35 rather than the web's 40. Isolated by running that
check alone against two builds of the same tree: it fails with gm-nov3.39's
CatAnimation.cpp and passes with HEAD's. The fix is the witness form
gm-nov3.39's own README section describes, and it belongs to whoever owns
that check next; test_animation.py was held by this lane while gm-nov3.39
landed.

Cost: a helper now turns to every page of the list rather than stopping at
the first hit, which is what makes a duplicate on a later page reachable.
That is about 85 s of the animation scenario's 144 s increase; the 19 new
checks are the other 59 s.

title: Make fleet parity fail without an independent comparison
description:
Commit d7051b3f added `tools/anim_parity.py` as the fleet proof, but it can exit successfully without checking every independent Xtensa kernel.

The current false-pass mutations are:

1. Append a registry entry after Cube without extending `NAMES`. The default run still checks only `range(len(NAMES))` and exits PASS.
2. Set an animation's `bandRef` to null. The tool prints `has_ref NO`, records the name, and still exits 0.
3. Return a successful, advancing JSON result with `has_ref=true` but omit `bands` and `mismatch_px`. Both default to zero and the tool reports a pass with no demonstrated work.
4. Break Silk's dormant Xtensa kernel while leaving its shipped `GM_BGANIM_SILK_ASM=0`. The device compares `bandRef()` with a `band()` that directly calls `bandRef()`, so the broken kernel remains green.

A missing endpoint or non-JSON body raises from `json.load`, and an out-of-range id receives HTTP 400 and aborts. Those cases do not falsely pass. A structurally incomplete but valid JSON response does.

All 44 animation sources contain an Xtensa path. Thirty-three have a named `GM_BGANIM_<NAME>_ASM` switch. Aurora, Caustics, Ember, Fireflies, Mandala, Nebula, Orbits, Plasma, Ripples, Starfield, and Steam use only the bare Xtensa plus `GM_BGANIM_NO_ASM` guard. A build-time A/B for one of those eleven cannot disable that animation alone: `GM_BGANIM_NO_ASM` changes the whole fleet. The runtime `useref=1` path remains the only isolated A/B unless a named switch is added.

The tool header is also inaccurate about venue. `/api/debug/animtest` is inside the real-panel guard, not `GM_ANIM_BENCH`, and therefore ships in production firmware.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The default inventory is checked against an authoritative firmware or registry count, and appending one registry entry without changing the tool makes the run fail.
- [ ] Every requested result must contain the expected animation id, string id, frame count, positive band count, `has_ref`, `init_failed`, and `mismatch_px`; an omitted field makes the run fail.
- [ ] `has_ref=false` and `init_failed=true` produce a non-zero process exit.
- [ ] A path identical to its reference by construction is reported as noncoverage, not parity. The shipped Silk configuration is covered explicitly.
- [ ] Automated tests exercise the four mutations above, plus a missing endpoint, malformed JSON, and an out-of-range id.
- [ ] `tools/anim_parity.py` documents the actual route guard and the per-animation A/B limitation for the eleven animations without named switches.
notes:
Done in db0a62df (tools/anim_parity.py only; no firmware change, no new file).

WHERE THE INVENTORY COUNT COMES FROM

The registry source, not the board. tools/anim_parity.py now parses REGISTRY[]
out of src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimRegistry.cpp, takes each animation's
id string from the source that defines its bg_anim_<name> symbol, and requires
symbol and id string to agree. That list is compared against the NAMES snapshot
kept in the tool, and a disagreement aborts before a single request goes out.
The board was not needed and would have been the weaker answer: bg_animation_count()
over HTTP would tell you what the flashed firmware has, which is exactly the
thing that can be stale. tools/animbench compiles the same registry and would
have worked too, but it costs a build and answers the same question.

MUTATION TABLE

Driven against a scripted /api/debug/animtest (FakeDevice in the tool), the way
tools/gradient_fb_check.py --host-test drives its gate. The before column is
the pre-fix tool at HEAD~ executed against the same fake.

  mutation                                  before            after
  1 registry grown to 45, tool knows 44     exit 0, PASS      abort: "the registry has moved under this tool"
  2 an animation with a null bandRef        exit 0, PASS      exit 1: "no reference path"
  3 result without bands or mismatch_px     exit 0, PASS      exit 1: "the result omits bands, mismatch_px"
  3a result without has_ref                 exit 0, PASS      exit 1: "the result omits has_ref"
  3b band count of zero                     exit 0, PASS      exit 1: "no band was compared"
  3c token band count of 1                  exit 0, PASS      exit 1: "not a multiple of 8 frames x 3 parameter sets"
  4 the shipped Silk, band() is bandRef()   exit 0, counted   NOT COMPARED, "0 of 1 asked for compared clean",
                                            as one of 44      exit 1 when it is the only target
  4b a second kernel compiled out           exit 0, PASS      abort: "is not declared" noncoverage
  a stale DORMANT declaration               n/a               abort: "the sources no longer agree"
  5 missing endpoint                        raises, aborts    abort, exit 2, "HTTP 404"
  6 body that is not JSON                   raises, aborts    abort, exit 2, "not JSON"
  7 out-of-range animation id               raises, aborts    abort, "HTTP 400"
  8 result for the wrong animation          exit 1 after a    exit 1 at once: "the result is for animation 0, not 1"
                                            120 s timeout
  9 a differing pixel                       exit 1            exit 1 (unchanged)
  10 init_failed                            exit 1            exit 1 (unchanged)
  board caught mid-publish (new)            takes the         skipped: the accept condition is seq >= seq0 + 2,
                                            in-flight run's   not "different and even"
                                            result as ours

MUTATION 4, HONESTLY

Breaking Silk's dormant kernel cannot be caught by anything reachable from the
board, and this change does not claim to catch it. What it stops is the tool
reporting it as parity. GM_BGANIM_SILK_ASM is 0, band() is one line that calls
bandRef(), so the device compares a function with itself and must report 0
differing pixels. Silk is now listed under NOT COMPARED with the reason, is
excluded from the compared count, and a run whose whole target list is
noncoverage (for example `anim_parity.py 2`) exits non-zero rather than
reporting success. A second kernel going dormant without being declared in
DORMANT aborts the run, and a DORMANT entry the sources no longer support
aborts it too, so the declaration cannot rot into a blanket excuse. Testing the
kernel itself needs the flag turned on and then the ladder in CLAUDE.md.

THE ELEVEN WITHOUT A NAMED SWITCH

Computed, not asserted: the tool prints them at the end of every run. The scan
finds exactly the eleven the bead names (plasma, starfield, aurora, ripples,
caustics, mandala, orbits, fireflies, steam, ember, nebula). The match is by
naming convention, GM_BGANIM_<ID upper>_ASM, which the compiler does not
enforce; a differently named switch would be listed as absent, which understates
what can be A/B'd and never overstates what was compared. The header documents
the limitation and the runtime useref=1 alternative.

VENUE

#if !defined(GAGGIMATE_HEADLESS) && !defined(GAGGIMATE_SIM). The GM_TOUCH_PROBE
block above it opens at 707 and closes at 722. It ships in production firmware.

CHECKS

else reads the problem list and a caller reads $?.

NOT CHECKED

Nothing was run on the board. Another lane held it and this change touches no
