since the rewrite, and the first real run should be watched: the parts that only
the board exercises are the retry path in make_getter and the poll timing.

title: Keep touched animation gradients live during reconciliation
description:
Commit affbc12f reasserts the touched global gradient during `animReconcile`, but touched per-animation and standby gradient slots are also live writes to `bgAnimThemeMap`.

Today a user can choose gradient A for the current animation, then a web POST can replace that slot with B. Reconciliation keeps A in the row draft but does not restore the map. `DefaultUI::updateState()` therefore continues resolving and publishing B until the category exits, when `animCommit()` finally restores A. This is worse than the documented global window of one update pass.

Every touched animation slot must be restored during reconciliation, while untouched slots from the same web map remain as posted. Restoring every touched map slot is necessary because a touched noncurrent or standby animation can become the current animation later in the same visit.

The global timing analysis stands: a POST before service is restored before update, one landing after service but before update can be visible for that update, and a POST after update is restored by the next service before another update. Do not broaden this bead into eliminating that bounded window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `animReconcile` merges every touched animation's draft ref back into the live `bgAnimThemeMap` under the settings transaction guard.
- [ ] A web POST replacing the current animation's touched slot cannot leave the row on A while the live resolver uses B, checked before the category is popped.
- [ ] The same case is checked with the picker at its group level and gradient-list level.
- [ ] A touched standby or noncurrent slot is restored, including a case that makes that animation current later in the visit.
- [ ] An untouched slot in the same posted map keeps the web value.
- [ ] Removing the reconcile-time map restoration makes the new checks fail.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md no longer claims that the global gradient is the only touched live field requiring reconciliation.
notes:
Landed in 1e585f2e on anims/astra. Files: src/display/ui/default/settings/CatAnimation.cpp, tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py.

The fault was real. A per-animation pick writes the stored map at once (animGradientAssign, CatAnimation.cpp:902), the panel resolves from the stored map (DefaultUI.cpp:4642 read, 4657 bg_resolve_anim_theme), and nothing between reconcile and commit put it back: animReconcile only re-derived the draft's index, and the old commit loop at 1566 was the only writer.

Fix: animReconcile merges every touched slot back into bgAnimThemeMap, through mergeTouchedGradientSlots, which animCommit now calls too so the two cannot drift. Untouched slots keep the web's value. Runs inside the shell's Settings::Guard (SettingsUI.cpp:194).

Checks, all in test_gradientdraft.py: touched_anim_gradient_agrees_with_panel (the current animation, with the category page on top and at both picker levels), touched_noncurrent_slot_agrees_with_panel (a slot touched then stepped away from and returned to, plus an untouched slot keeping the web's value), touched_standby_slot_agrees_with_panel (the Standby grad row's own slot, with a second save after that animation becomes the current one).

Measured: test_gradientdraft.py PASS 188/188 with the fix. Against a scratch copy of the worktree carrying HEAD's CatAnimation.cpp, FAIL 8/188, and the eight are exactly the new map assertions (anim_agree_row/group/list_panel_back_to_draft, noncurrent_offscreen/onscreen_slot_back_to_draft, noncurrent_slot_is_draft_when_current, standby_slot_back_to_draft, standby_slot_back_to_draft_as_current). pio test -e native_settingsui 68/68. pio run -e display SUCCESS, 5,910,223 bytes, 90.2% of the app partition, RAM 105,248 bytes.

Two criteria not done by me, on purpose.

CLAUDE.md: the brief said not to edit it and to hand the replacement wording to the lead. Delivered in the report.

test_animation.py is held by another lane, and this change breaks one line in it. check_gradient_precedence_across_animations confirms its interference POST landed by reading bgAnimThemeMap back (line 1942), which the display now overwrites within a UI pass by design, so rig.wait_until raises and the scenario reports gradient_precedence_across_animations_exception: TimeoutError and skips its restore. That is the same weakness the bead's reviewer named: the check also judges only after rig.settingsui(pop=1) at line 1938, so it passed either way. The fix is to carry a witness field in the same POST and wait on that, the way store_over_draft does. Raised with the lead.

Also failing in that scenario before and after this change: gradient_row_has_no_arrows, which asserts the gradient row has no arrows, contradicting gm-nov3.32. Verified against a pre-fix build (1 failure of 230).

title: Require a clean simulator exit for restart checks
description:
Commit e86f39da correctly stopped treating request failures as restart evidence, but both restart checks now accept any simulator exit status.

The simulator maps the intended `ESP.restart()` to exit status 0. Replace that call with `exit(17)`, `abort()`, or another abnormal process termination and both checks still pass because they test only `code is not None`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both restart checks require exit status 0.
- [ ] A simulated restart that exits with status 17 makes each affected check fail.
- [ ] A simulated signal termination makes each affected check fail.
- [ ] HTTP 500, malformed JSON, and socket-failure injections with the simulator still running continue to fail rather than count as restart evidence.
- [ ] The `Sim.wait_exited` documentation distinguishes the expected clean restart status from arbitrary process death.
notes:
Done in 94c49038 (tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py, tools/settings_ui_tests/test_status.py).

Both restart checks now compare the simulator's exit status against the new
Sim.CLEAN_RESTART_STATUS (0, what sim/platform/Esp.h's exit(0) leaves) instead of
"is not None". Sim.describe_exit() writes the detail line, because Popen reports a
signal death as the negated signal number and -6 alone does not read as SIGABRT.
Sim.wait_exited's docstring now names the clean restart status and says why any
other status is a firmware fault rather than the restart the caller is testing for.

Mutation table. Firmware mutations were compiled in a copy of the worktree under
the job tmp directory, never in the shared tree; harness faults were injected at
urllib.request.urlopen inside the rig module, so the harness archived from HEAD
and the fixed harness saw the same fault. Columns are long_hold_restarts_process
and second_hold_restarts_after_forced_failure.

  ESP.restart() is exit(17)   at HEAD: pass, pass   fixed: fail, fail
  ESP.restart() is abort()    at HEAD: pass, pass   fixed: fail, fail
  HTTP 500 on the hold        at HEAD: fail, fail   fixed: fail, fail
  malformed JSON on the hold  at HEAD: fail, fail   fixed: fail, fail
  socket reset on the hold    at HEAD: fail, fail   fixed: fail, fail

The last three are regression rows: e86f39da already made them fail and they still
do. Detail lines from the fixed runs read "exited with status 17, want status 0",
"killed by signal 6 (SIGABRT), want status 0" and "still running, want status 0".

The two mutant builds also fail the status scenario's display_firmware_matches_build
and info_screen_display_version_found checks, because the scratch copy is not a git
repository and its build writes an empty BUILD_GIT_VERSION. That is the artefact the
harness README records, not the mutation.

Runs, all on the simulator (this lane did not hold the bench board, so nothing was
checked on the device):

- pio run -e display-sim: SUCCESS.
- python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only status,rig: PASS at HEAD before the
  change (status 40 checks, rig 19) and PASS after (status 40, rig 19).
- python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py: 684 checks, one failure, in the animation
  scenario (gradient_precedence_across_animations_exception, a 5 s timeout). That
  scenario belongs to another lane whose test_animation.py edits were uncommitted
  in the shared tree during this run; nothing it uses was changed here (no caller
  of wait_exited, describe_exit or CLEAN_RESTART_STATUS outside test_status.py).
  Reported to the lead rather than investigated.

One earlier full run also reported the status scenario erroring with
"127.0.0.1:8181 is already answering connections". That was another lane's
simulator holding the port, not a defect; the rerun on clear ports passed.

title: Swatch checks in the device script and the legacy fallback must name the gradient
description:
Two more swatch checks count colours where their names claim they establish which gradient a row drew. Same fault as gm-nov3.33, different files. The gm-nov3.32 lane found them while reading nearby and neither is in a file it owned.

## The two, with the lines read on 2026-09-13

- `tools/picker_device_checks.py:164`, `global_row_draws_a_ramp`: `strip is not None and len(set(strip)) > 4`, on the "Global" row of the picker's first page.
- `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py:1021`, the `legacy_<name>_draws_a_ramp` family inside `check_legacy_unparsable_custom_falls_back`, three cases (empty, malformed, one_stop). Its threshold is **one** distinct colour, so anything that is not a flat block passes. The finder reported this at line 739, which is stale; 1021 is where it is now.

## Why the thresholds are meaningless

Measured on the simulator against the fixture library: all twelve entries draw between 46 and 80 distinct colours in their swatch. A threshold of 4 is cleared tenfold by every entry and a threshold of 1 by nearly anything. So a row drawing the wrong gradient, a built-in where a library entry belongs, or a fallback, passes either check.

## The oracle already exists and already handles tone

`swatch_matches_stops(strip, stops, tol=20)` in `test_animation.py`, with `toned_stops(settings, stops)`, `builtin_stops(index)` and the `check_swatch` wrapper around them. gm-nov3.33 built them and its docstring records why the two ends are the whole oracle. Reuse them rather than writing a second one; if reuse means moving them to a module both files can import, say so in the report and keep the move mechanical.

The legacy case has an exactly known target. Its sibling check `legacy_<name>_names_builtin_zero` already asserts the row names `THEME_NAMES[0]`, so the ramp to compare against is built-in 0's stops, toned.

`picker_device_checks.py` runs against the board, so say where its expected stops come from, and confirm the tone question there too: the board's stored tone is not guaranteed to be the identity.

## Do this after gm-nov3.33

That bead is landing the oracle and pointing four checks in `test_animation.py` at it, and may still move or rename it. Take your baseline at its HEAD.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both checks compare the strip against the stops of the entry the row is meant to show, with the tone setting applied, rather than against a colour count.
- [ ] The threshold of one distinct colour is gone, not raised.
- [ ] A mutation that makes each row draw a different gradient fails its check, shown passing before and failing after. Build the broken version in a scratch copy, never in the shared tree; the recipe is in `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md`.
- [ ] A repository search finds no remaining swatch check whose assertion is a count of distinct colours.
- [ ] The full settings UI suite passes, with before and after counts from the same tree. Say whether `picker_device_checks.py` was run against the board or only read, and if only read, say so plainly.

## Sizing, measured by the gm-nov3.33 lane after its work landed

**The legacy family in `test_gradientdraft.py` is small.** That file already
imports from `test_animation`. All three fixtures resolve to built-in 0, which
the neighbouring check asserts by name, so it is three names on the existing
import and one call site:

    check_swatch(rig, name, strip, toned_stops(rig.settings(), builtin_stops(0)))

**`tools/picker_device_checks.py` is the larger half, and it needs a decision.**
That script imports only `Rig` and carries its own copy of every helper on
purpose, because it is a standalone device script. The oracle needs eight
functions: `hex_rgb`, `swatch_matches_stops`, `builtin_stops`, `library_entries`,
`legacy_builtin`, `custom_theme_valid`, `global_stops` and `toned_stops`, about
90 lines.

Do not copy them. A second transcription of the palette reading is the same
fault this epic keeps closing, and nothing would hold the copy to the original.
Two acceptable shapes, and say which you took and why:

- Move the eight into a module both import, for example
  `tools/settings_ui_tests/swatch.py`, and have `test_animation.py`,
  `test_gradientdraft.py` and `picker_device_checks.py` all read them from
  there. This keeps the device script free of any dependency on a scenario
  module, which is the reason its stance exists.
- Import them from `test_animation` directly. Cheaper, and it makes the device
  script depend on a scenario file. Only take this if the move turns out to
  drag other definitions with it.

Either way the parity that matters is unchanged: `GradientSwatch.cpp` is held
to the real palette code by `tools/animbench/swatch_parity.cpp`, and the Python
side must have exactly one reading of it.
notes:
Implemented from the anims/astra worktree (/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/.claude/worktrees/gm-2cl-6-dials), commit f0db1611.

Changed: tools/picker_device_checks.py (global_row_draws_a_ramp now computes
global_stops/toned_stops and asserts swatch_matches_stops instead of
len(set(strip))>4), tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py (the three
legacy_<name>_draws_a_ramp cases now compare against toned_stops(settings,
builtin_stops(0)) instead of len(set(strip))>1), and a new shared module
tools/settings_ui_tests/swatch.py holding the oracle (hex_rgb,
swatch_matches_stops, library_entries, custom_theme_valid, legacy_builtin,
BG_THEME_LEGACY_CUSTOM, builtin_stops, stops_for_ref, global_stops,
toned_stops) that test_animation.py, test_gradientdraft.py and
picker_device_checks.py all import from. Went with the "move to a shared
module" shape rather than "import from test_animation" for
picker_device_checks.py, to keep it free of any scenario-file dependency, per
its own header comment. test_animation.py's move was mechanical (no bodies
changed); check_swatch stayed there since it reports through that file's own
check()/FAILURES globals, which differ per caller file, so it is not
reusable across files as-is.

Verified: python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only gradientdraft on the
simulator (already built in this worktree) passed 219/219, including the
three legacy_*_draws_a_ramp checks, now showing real stop comparisons.
Proved the checks actually discriminate: in a throwaway scratch copy of the
worktree (rsync'd, excluding .pio/.git, run against the same built simulator
binary on a separate port, per tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md's recipe)
I pointed the legacy check's want_ramp at builtin_stops(1) instead of
builtin_stops(0); all three legacy_*_draws_a_ramp checks failed as expected
(reporting the mismatch between the actually-drawn built-in 0 colours and
the wrong built-in 1 stops), then passed again against the real code.

Not run: picker_device_checks.py needs the bench board (192.168.1.121),
unreachable from here. Checked with python3 -m py_compile and a standalone
exercise of global_stops/toned_stops/swatch_matches_stops against
simulator-shaped settings (string-valued fields, matching what Rig.settings()
returns) to confirm no runtime errors in the new code path. Left for the
bench.

Scope note: a repo grep also finds two other distinct-colour swatch checks
in test_gradientdraft.py (untouched_row_has_swatch,
legacy_ground_%s_has_swatch, lines ~432 and ~947). Left alone on purpose:
both are "is there a non-degenerate swatch" preconditions before capturing
ground-truth pixels that a later check compares pixel-for-pixel
(strip == ground[...]), not "which gradient" identity assertions, and
neither was named in this bead's scope or its sizing section.
close_reason: picker_device_checks.py global row and test_gradientdraft.py legacy family now compare swatch pixels against the gradient's real stops via swatch_matches_stops, not a colour count

title: Keep touched live animation settings on the panel during reconciliation
description:
Commit 1e585f2e correctly re-asserted every touched `bgAnimThemeMap` slot, but the same live-field rule applies more broadly than commit ac4115f5 records.

Animation rows write `Settings` immediately for the current animation, frame rate, all-screens mode, theme, plates, plate colour, plate opacity, element tint, scrim, fade settings and interlace. `DefaultUI` reads those stored values while the category is still open. A conflicting web save currently replaces the stored value while `animReconcile` retains only the row draft, so the row and panel can disagree until commit restores it.

The Parameters page has the same problem per slot. `paramOnStep` writes `bgAnimParams` immediately, but `animParamsReconcile` only retains touched values in its local draft. `DefaultUI::updateState` therefore consumes the web value for a touched slot until the pushed page is popped.

`check_frame_rate_live_and_precedence` has the same blind shape previously fixed for gradients. It reads `bgAnimFps` itself to confirm the web save, then checks the touched result only after pop. Leaving reconciliation broken while commit restores the value still passes. `check_parameters_web_precedence` checks the touched row draft before pop, but does not check that the stored touched slot used by the panel was restored before pop.

Standby animation selection is not included merely because its row writes storage. Its callback documents that it does not change the screen covered by the settings page. Inventory fields by whether the display reads their stored value during the open visit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reading `CatAnimation.cpp`, `CatAnimParams.cpp` and `DefaultUI.cpp` identifies every immediately stored field that the display can consume while the Animation category or Parameters page is open.
- [ ] Reconciliation re-asserts every touched live scalar and touched parameter slot before the following `DefaultUI::updateState`, while untouched fields and slots retain the web value.
- [ ] Reconcile and commit preserve the same touched set for aggregate fields, with shared merge logic or tests that prevent the two paths from drifting.
- [ ] `check_frame_rate_live_and_precedence` confirms the POST through a changed witness field that the open Animation category does not write, and asserts the stored `bgAnimFps` value before pop.
- [ ] `check_parameters_web_precedence` asserts before pop that the stored touched slot has the draft value and the stored untouched slot has the web value.
- [ ] In a scratch worktree, removing the frame-rate reconciliation write while leaving commit intact makes the frame-rate check fail.
- [ ] In a scratch worktree, removing one touched parameter slot from reconciliation while leaving commit intact makes the parameter check fail.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` and `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md` describe the complete live-field rule and witness requirement rather than listing only gradient fields.
- [ ] The settings UI host suite passes.

title: Gradient contact sheet and the set-quality checker
description:
Provide a contact sheet for reviewing the gradient collection and a reproducible checker that keeps new entries distinct.

Both tools read data/gradients.json. This bead depends on gm-nov3.1 and blocks gm-nov3.5.

Built-ins remain dark-to-bright ramps as a design policy. Saved gradients can have other shapes, and Plasma uses a cyclic palette.

## Establish the sampling contract

The current JS helpers are not an exact firmware palette oracle. sampleGradient uses positional interpolation, while the firmware keeps separate uniform arithmetic. toneColor rounds percentage conversions that DefaultUI truncates. gradientCss delegates interpolation to CSS.

Provide a reusable JS sampler that matches the production ramp arithmetic and verify it against the real C++ implementation. Preserve the firmware's existing output. Do not alter firmware palette arithmetic to make a preview test pass.

The sampler must distinguish uniform gradients from explicitly positioned gradients according to their wire semantics. Evenly spaced explicit positions are not proof that the firmware uses its uniform path.

Apply the highlight knee to stops, then brightness, then interpolate and quantize to RGB565. Match DefaultUI's integer percentage conversions. Use the normal ramp with extra palette gain 256 as the review contract. It represents the gradient, not every animation's later gain, reversal, cyclic mapping or spatial pattern.

The Python tools must obtain samples through the tested JS module or a host helper using the real C++ implementation. Do not add another tone-curve implementation in Python.

## Contact sheet

tools/gradient_sheet.py writes one PNG covering every source gradient, grouped by the declared category order and labelled with name, index and category.

Draw sampled toned RGB565 ramps, not six CSS-interpolated stops. Accept explicit brightness and highlight-rolloff settings and put them in the output metadata or labels. Defaults are 100 and 100. At those defaults the tone transform is the identity, so a second strip solely to compare raw and toned colours is unnecessary.

A device comparison must use known ramp sample positions with matched tone, extra gain and overlay conditions. An arbitrary animated framebuffer is not a horizontal palette strip. Add a test-only controlled fixture if necessary and record its command and sampled region.

## Checker

tools/gradient_check.py runs from tools/animbench make check and enforces:

- Exactly six valid lower-case #rrggbb stops.
- Strictly increasing relative luminance at the source stops.
- A documented dark-first-stop ceiling. The current brightest first stop is Teal Reef at relative luminance about 0.00284.
- A documented highlight floor in L*. The lowest current endpoint is Ember Coal at about 74.9. Choose the floor based on the intended highlights, including saturated candidates, rather than automatically using that current minimum.
- A reproducible near-duplicate rule applied to the toned, quantized samples.
- A category from the declared list.

Separate source design rules from rendered appearance checks. Quantization can create equal adjacent samples, and zero brightness makes every gradient black. Neither is a reason to reject a valid source ramp.

Choose and record fixed, non-degenerate tone settings, sampling positions, RGB565 expansion, colour metric and aggregation for the duplicate gate. The CI result must not depend on a device's stored settings or the last contact-sheet command.

Print the ten closest pairs and the threshold margins. Establish named exemptions using only the original 18 under this exact method. Earlier raw-stop CIEDE2000 figures are not automatically valid thresholds or exemptions for a different metric or tone setting. Once established, the exemption list cannot grow to admit new entries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both tools run from a clean checkout with the repo's Python and Node and no new apt packages. Ask before adding a required package.
- [ ] Neither Python tool implements its own tone curve. Both use the tested sampling path.
- [ ] An automated parity test compares all 256 RGB565 ramp entries from JS with the real C++ implementation for all original built-ins, uniform 2-stop and 16-stop fixtures, explicit positions, repeated positions, and flat runs before and after the endpoints.
- [ ] Parity tests include tone settings 100/100 and 60/65, plus values that exercise percentage truncation. The test includes Espresso at position 255.
- [ ] The checker records its fixed evaluation settings, thresholds, measured baseline margins and named exemptions in its source or an adjacent checked-in configuration.
- [ ] The current 18 pass unchanged. A copy of an existing gradient with a small stop change fails the near-duplicate rule without adding an exemption.
- [ ] Unit tests assert the specific failure for an invalid hex stop, a five-stop entry, a luminance dip, an overly bright first stop, an overly dim endpoint, a near duplicate and an unknown category.
- [ ] The sheet contains every source gradient in declared category order, with name, index, category and tone settings, and its strips use the verified RGB565 samples.
- [ ] A controlled device framebuffer comparison checks known ramp samples at matched settings and records the fixture, command and result. It does not compare an arbitrary moving animation with a linear strip.
- [ ] tools/animbench make check runs the generation check, palette parity tests and gradient checker and exits non-zero on a failing input.
notes:
Done in 71bd9f20 on anims/astra.

SAMPLING CONTRACT (recorded in the docstring of tools/gradient_check.py)
Source: data/gradients.json stops as written, sent to the firmware parser
without positions, so the uniform path a built-in actually takes.
Samples: the 256-entry RGB565 ramp from buildThemeRamp, read at 32 positions
t_k = k * 255 // 31, k in 0..31.
Tone: brightness 100%, rolloff 100% (the shipped defaults, identity, not
degenerate). Extra palette gain 256, plain forward ramp, not the wheel.
RGB565 expanded back to 8 bits by replication. Metric CIEDE2000 in CIELAB,
sRGB D65. Aggregation: the mean over the 32 positions; the minimum is printed
as well but does not gate.
Who computes it: web/src/config/gradientRamp.js (new), reached from Python
through tools/gradient_samples.js (new). Neither Python tool has a tone curve.

PARITY, NOT ASSUMPTION
tools/animbench/ramp_dump.cpp links the real BgAnimThemes.cpp and
BgAnimCommon.cpp on the host. tools/animbench/web/ramp_parity.js compares all
256 entries of 2160 ramps (552,960 entries): 18 built-ins, 2/3/16 stops,
explicit positions including evenly spaced ones, uneven positions, one
positioned stop among five, repeated positions, zero-width segments, flat runs
before and after the ends, unordered positions that the parser repairs, 8 tone
pairs (100/100, 60/65, 7/7, 33/71, 99/1, 0/100, 100/0, 50/50), gains 256/128/
400, and the ramp, reversed and wheel modes. Result: agree everywhere.
Why the JS in bgAnimations.js could not be the oracle, measured: Espresso ramp
entry 255 is 63288 through the firmware's uniform arithmetic and 65337 through
the positional path that module always takes; 49 of the 256 entries differ.
7% exercises the truncation the firmware does and the editor rounds
(7*256/100 = 17.92 and 7*255/100 = 17.85, both truncate to 17).

THRESHOLDS AND MEASURED MARGINS (original 18, 2026-09-12, under this contract)
First stop relative luminance ceiling 0.0040. Brightest first stop Teal Reef
0.00284, margin 0.00116. About 40% of headroom, roughly #0e0e0e in grey.
Endpoint floor L* 58.0 at the last stop. Dimmest endpoint Ember Coal 74.89,
margin 16.89. The floor is deliberately not the current minimum: saturated
highlights sit low in L*, and magenta #ff00ff (60.3) and orange #ff6a1e (63.1)
have to be admissible, while a mid grey #808080 (53.6) must not be.
Near duplicate: mean CIEDE2000 8.0. 153 pairs, median 29.01, max 67.48.
Four exemptions, all pairs of the original 18: Forest/Lime 4.71,
Rose/Sakura 5.45, Ocean/Ice 6.99, Espresso/Fire 7.88. Closest non-exempt pair
Sunset/Fire 8.96, so 0.96 of margin. The raw-stop figures quoted in the bead
did not survive re-measurement under this contract (for instance Forest/Lime
4.26 raw against 4.71 here), which is why the numbers above are the ones that
count.
Exemptions cannot grow: both names of an exemption must be in ORIGINAL_18, and
a violation is its own finding (exemption_invalid), tested.
Also enforced: ids 0..17 are still the original 18 in order (the list is
append only).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
[x] Both tools run with the repo's Python 3.10 and Node 22, no new apt
    packages. The sheet uses Pillow, already used by tools/campanel/campanel.py
    and present in the user site-packages; it is not needed by anything make

[x] Neither Python tool implements a tone curve.
[x] Parity over all 256 entries against the real C++, all the listed fixtures.
[x] Tone 100/100 and 60/65 plus truncation cases; Espresso at 255 asserted in
    both the parity test and the unit tests.
[x] Contract, thresholds, margins and exemptions recorded in the checker's
    source.
[x] The current 18 pass. A copy of Espresso with one stop moved from #b8703a
    to #b8703e measures 0.13 and fails, with no exemption available.
[x] Unit tests assert the specific code for an invalid hex stop (three

[x] The sheet has every gradient in declared category order with name, id,

[ ] Controlled device framebuffer comparison. NOT DONE. This loop may not

    read-back through /api/debug/fb, and why an arbitrary animated frame

[x] tools/animbench make check runs the generation check, the parity test, the

WHAT RAN

to date, ramp parity OK (2160 cases), gradient check OK, unit tests all pass,
bench golden compare OK, interlace check OK, page_vs_golden 40 of 44 exact.

Not run: pio run -e display (does not build in this worktree on WSL1), any

NOT DONE ALSO: file reservations. The agent-mail server at 127.0.0.1:8765 was

title: Derive parity noncoverage from the actual kernel compile guard
description:
Commit db0a62df prevents the currently known Silk reference-versus-reference run from counting as parity, but its source inventory does not inspect the condition that actually selects each kernel.

`asm_switches` recognizes only literal `GM_BGANIM_<IDENT>_ASM` definitions. `build_inventory` connects them to registry entries by uppercase naming convention. The compiler does not enforce that convention, and the scanner does not see an effective `-D` build override. A kernel guarded by a differently named false macro, or directly changed to a reference-only conditional while its conventional macro remains enabled, is classified as compared even though the board compares `bandRef` with itself.

The existing 26 host cases use fake getter functions and scratch conventional definitions. They do not instantiate `make_getter`, so they do not reach transport retry and exhaustion or HTTP response JSON decoding. Their run responses do not exercise `run_one`'s `pending` branch, and they do not reach the main program's unavailable-pclk fallback. These limitations should be explicit so a host pass is not read as coverage of real-board transport.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory classification is derived from the actual conditional or metadata used by each registered animation's `band()` dispatch, not solely from the registry identifier naming convention.
- [ ] A scratch mutation that guards a kernel with an alternate false macro is reported as noncoverage or aborts the run.
- [ ] A scratch mutation that makes `band()` call only `bandRef()` while leaving `GM_BGANIM_<IDENT>_ASM` enabled is reported as noncoverage or aborts the run.
- [ ] Effective build overrides that change kernel selection are included in classification or cause an explicit refusal to run.
- [ ] The existing second-dormant-kernel and stale-declaration mutations continue to abort.
- [ ] The tool documents which transport, decoding, pending-response and pclk paths its host cases do not exercise.
- [ ] `python tools/anim_parity.py --host-test` passes, and the unmodified source inventory reports only the genuinely dormant shipped kernels.
notes:
Done in 992d22c5, tools/anim_parity.py only.

What decides dormancy now, at the guard rather than by name:
 - band and reference come from the `const BgAnimation bg_anim_<id> = {...}`
   initialiser fields, not from function names (Steam's reference is
   bandPortable).
 - the file is evaluated as the preprocessor would for the target build, so
   only the branch that compiles is read. Object-like macros are expanded,
   which Crescent needs: it dispatches through `#define CR_OUTER
   crescentOuterAsm` inside band()'s own body.
 - dormant by any of four routes: one function in both fields, band() is one
   call to the reference, the two bodies are the same tokens (Hills:
   render<true> vs render<false>), or no inline assembly is reachable from
   band() through the file's call graph (Steam: renderRow<Asm>).
 - which macros select a kernel is measured: each macro the file's conditions
   mention is forced on, forced to 0 and removed, and the ones that change the
   classification are the switches. The same eleven animations as before come
   back with only __XTENSA__ and GM_BGANIM_NO_ASM.

Build line: [env:display] of platformio.ini, ${a.b} expanded and `extends`
followed, so a -D there is part of the classification. --pio-env picks
another. The run stops rather than reporting a pass it cannot support when
PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS is set, when an extra_script touches CPPDEFINES or
BUILD_FLAGS, or when a build_flags line is only a reference PlatformIO
expands. A build driven by hand with extra -D arguments cannot be detected
and is printed on every run, with the environment and the overrides that
reach a switch.

Mutation table. Each is built in a scratch copy of Tide and read once before
its own edit, so the abort is the mutation's doing and not a broken tree's.
The HEAD column is the tool as it stood at db0a62df, run against the same
mutated tree (script kept at
/mnt/c/Users/Oystein/.claude/jobs/54de0aae/tmp/nov3_40/old_vs_new.py):

  mutation                                        at db0a62df   now
  guard changed to #if 0, define left at 1        compared      aborts
  guard moved to a macro nothing defines          compared      aborts
  band() body replaced by a call to the reference compared      aborts
  -DGM_BGANIM_TIDE_ASM=0 in platformio.ini        compared      aborts
  switch renamed off the convention, set to 0     compared      aborts
  switch renamed off the convention, left on      compared      passes, and
                                                                the run names
                                                                the switch

Two more refusals have cases of their own: a build_flags line that is only
${sysenv.EXTRA_FLAGS}, and an extra_script with env.Append(CPPDEFINES=...)
added to the scratch copy.

Checks run:
 - python3 tools/anim_parity.py --host-test: PASS, 45 printed cases in 12 s.
   At HEAD it was PASS, 27 cases, 100 s.
 - the four gm-nov3.35 closures keep their cases and stay green: the registry
   parsed from BgAnimRegistry.cpp with symbol and id agreeing, the abort when
   that list differs from NAMES, every result field required with the right
   type, and a run whose whole target list is noncoverage exiting non-zero.
   Six cases still drive main() for its exit code (0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2).
 - on unmodified sources the inventory reports one dormant kernel, Silk, and
   43 of 44 compared, and the eleven with no switch of their own are the
   eleven the docstring names.
 - flake8 clean at the file's existing line length.

Also in this commit, because the host cases were unusable otherwise:
run_one() and check_fleet() resolve sleep and the clock inside the call
instead of binding time.sleep in the signature. The end-to-end cases were
waiting 0.7 s per animation on a scripted board that answers at once, which
was 97 s of the 100 s host run.

Not checked: the tool has never been driven against a real board. That is
task 33 and was not mine, and the module docstring now records what the host
cases do not reach: make_getter's retry and exhaustion loop, a real HTTP
response, run_one's pending branch, and main's unavailable-pclk fallback.

One thing the next reader should know: AnimCrescent.cpp changed under this
work (another lane holds it). The first version of the scan called crescent
dormant, correctly, because its new macro dispatch hid the kernel from the
call graph. That is what added macro expansion. A scan that stops following
calls at a macro will get this wrong again.

Follow-up in 6d7d1fda (lead's request after review), same file.

The question that prompted it: can a reader of a run tell "this animation's
switch is named unconventionally" from "this animation has no switch of its
own"? Yes, and that part was already right. The eleven line is computed from
the measured macros, so an unconventionally named switch keeps its animation
out of it. Checked on a scratch tree with Tide's switch renamed to
TIDE_WANTS_THE_KERNEL and left on: tide absent from the line, steam, which
genuinely has none, present.

The gap that was real: a run said whether an animation had a switch, never
which macro. So the tool knew the flag and made the reader guess it, and the
name they would guess is the convention the same work had just stopped
trusting. The fleet summary now carries the counterpart line, every animation
one -D of its own can turn off with the macro measured at the guard, the
fleet-wide pair set aside so the name printed is the flag to pass, and a
separate line for any whose macro is not what its id suggests. Summary only,
no new column on the per-animation rows.

On the shipped sources: 33 switched, 11 with none of their own, 44 covered
between them, and no mismatch line, because all 33 do follow the convention.

Two host cases hold it, and both bite. Silencing print_switches in memory
takes the host run to 35 problems; making it print the conventional name
instead of the measured one takes it to 2; as shipped, 0. Script kept at
/mnt/c/Users/Oystein/.claude/jobs/54de0aae/tmp/nov3_40/nov3_40_bite.py.

python3 tools/anim_parity.py --host-test after this: PASS, 46 printed cases,
12 s. flake8 clean at the file's existing line length. Still not driven
against a real board, which is task 33.

title: A per-animation gradient row on Global follows a stepped global
description:
The Animation category's page 0 carries "Gradient all" (row 2) and the main
animation's "Gradient" (row 4). A per-animation row with no override of its own
shows "Global (<name>)" and draws the global's swatch, so it is a second view of
the same value.

Stepping the "Gradient all" row with its arrows redraws only that row
(globalGradientOnCycle, CatAnimation.cpp). The "Gradient" row two rows below it,
and "Standby grad" on page 1 when the standby animation is separate, go on
naming and sampling the gradient the global used to be. Nothing rebuilds the
page after a step, which is the difference from the picker: a pick pops back and
the pop rebuilds the page from the draft, so that route was already correct.

Reported by the owner on 2026-09-13: "the specific gradient does not update if
it is set to global AND changing the global gradient on the animation subview".

## Fix

One helper that redraws every row that reads the global, called from
globalGradientPicked so both routes are covered (on the picker route the rows
are already deleted and the null checks skip them). The refresh writes exactly
what animBuildRow writes for cases 2, 4 and 6, so a stepped row and a rebuilt
one show the same thing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stepping "Gradient all" updates the "Gradient" row's label and swatch in
      the same pass, whenever that row is on "Global".
- [ ] A "Gradient" row with an override of its own is left alone by the step.
- [ ] "Standby grad" follows the same rule when the standby animation is
      separate, and stays "Same as main" when it is not.
- [ ] A check in tools/settings_ui_tests/test_gradientdraft.py that fails
      without the fix.
- [ ] pio run -e display-sim, python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only
      animation,gradientdraft, pio test -e native_settingsui.

comments.author: oystein
comments.text:
Fixed in 95b378da.

refreshRowsReadingGlobalGradient (CatAnimation.cpp) redraws every row that
reads the global, and globalGradientPicked calls it, so the arrow step and the
picker both go through it. On the picker route the page's rows are already
deleted and the null checks skip them.

The check is check_stepping_the_global_redraws_a_row_on_global in
test_gradientdraft.py. Proven both ways on the simulator:

  without the fix  global_redraw_row_follows   row 'Global (Espresso)' want 'Global (Cappuccino)'
                   global_redraw_swatch_follows  failed
                   217 of 219 checks passed
  with the fix     PASS (219/219)

The first version of the check passed on the unfixed build and proved nothing.
It read the row through page_with_row, which sweeps pages to find a row by
name, and SettingsUI::gotoPage calls rebuildPage() whether or not the page
number changes, so every reading saw a freshly built row. Every reading after
the step is a plain touchmap of the active screen now.

"Standby grad" is on page 1 while "Gradient all" is on page 0, so reaching it
rebuilds that page and its text is right either way. The check asserts its
stored slot instead, which is what says the step wrote the global and nothing
else.

title: About 42 new gradients, taking the set to 60
description:
Add about 42 built-in gradients, taking the collection from 18 to about 60, roughly seven or eight per category.

Depends on the generator through gm-nov3.4, the quality checker in gm-nov3.4, the compatibility work in gm-nov3.7, and the generated runner data in gm-nov3.8. The latter two must land before any production entry is appended.

The current split is Coffee 1, Fire and Heat 3, Water and Ice 4, Nature 2, Night Sky 3, Neon 1, Pastel 2, Metal and Stone 2. Coffee and Neon need the most entries.

## Authoring

Work in batches of about eight, one category at a time, appending in declared category order. Never insert entries among the original gradients.

For each batch: author candidates, run the checker, render and inspect the contact sheet, regenerate every checked-in output with scripts/gen_gradients.py, and run its --check before committing. Editing data/gradients.json alone does not change the firmware or web bundle.

Rework or drop a rejected candidate. Do not relax a threshold or extend the baseline exemption list to admit it.

Keep this as one bead because every batch appends to the same indexed file. Competing append operations can silently change stored ids.

Sixty is the target, not a quota. Keep candidates that pass the checker and review. A category may stop at five if further candidates are too similar; record the dropped candidates and reasons when it stops below seven.

Inspect at least one batch, ideally the first, on the device as well as on the sheet. Match the sheet's recorded tone and sampling contract. Framebuffer comparisons establish rendered pixels, not the physical panel's gamma.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The first 18 entries are unchanged in name, order and stops, checked against the source at this bead's start. Later batches also preserve all entries already appended by earlier committed batches.
- [ ] Every category holds at least five gradients and the total is at least 50, with about 60 the target. A category below seven records which candidates were dropped and why.
- [ ] tools/gradient_check.py passes with the thresholds and baseline exemptions established by gm-nov3.4. None is relaxed or expanded for a new entry.
- [ ] Each batch regenerates the firmware header, web table and Python runner module. scripts/gen_gradients.py --check passes on the final committed outputs.
- [ ] The generated outputs have the same gradient count, names, categories and indexed order as data/gradients.json.
- [ ] The final contact sheet is rendered, reviewed and linked here, with its brightness and rolloff settings recorded.
- [ ] At least one batch has a recorded device comparison using the controlled sample method established by gm-nov3.4.
- [ ] The compatibility fixtures from gm-nov3.7 pass against the final table, including legacy Custom, explicit refs 18 and above, empty legacy Custom, existing library and map contents, and deferred migration.
- [ ] A device with active legacy Custom boots on the final build and preserves its rendered gradient. Record the fixture and matched-state before and after comparison.
- [ ] The final firmware and web checks select at least the first appended entry and the final entry and verify their exact refs and names after reopening settings and after reboot.
- [ ] Flash rodata growth is measured from the linker map and recorded. Web bundle growth is measured from a real scripts/build_webui.sh build and recorded. Do not substitute an estimated per-entry size for either measurement.
notes:
Done in e3555bc6 on anims/astra. data/gradients.json goes from 18 to 60.

Final count per category: Coffee 7, Fire and Heat 8, Water and Ice 7,
Nature 7, Night Sky 8, Neon 7, Pastel 8, Metal and Stone 8. No category is
below seven, so nothing is recorded as a short category.

The 42 appended entries and their ids, in file order:
Coffee: Cappuccino 18, Cold Brew 19, Crema 20, Dark Roast 21, Flat White 22,
Mocha 23. Fire and Heat: Blowtorch 24, Brimstone 25, Forge 26, Magma 27,
Solar Flare 28. Water and Ice: Abyss 29, Glacier 30, Lagoon 31. Nature:
Fern 32, Jungle 33, Moss 34, Olive Grove 35, Wheat 36. Night Sky: Eclipse 37,
Midnight 38, Moonrise 39, Nebula Drift 40, Starlight 41. Neon: Cyan Pulse 42,
Electric Blue 43, Hot Magenta 44, Laser Pink 45, Neon Amber 46, Neon Lime 47.
Pastel: Lavender 48, Lilac Haze 49, Mint Cream 50, Peach 51, Powder Blue 52,
Seafoam 53. Metal and Stone: Basalt 54, Copper 55, Graphite 56, Sandstone 57,
Slate 58, Steel 59.

## How they were authored

Hand authoring did not work. A first pool of 57 hand-tuned candidates put only
14 through the 8.0 dE gate, because a 10 degree hue step is worth 3 to 5 dE
while hue drift along the ramp is worth 14 to 17. So each concept was given a
parameter band in LCh (a hue window every stop must stay inside, a chroma
profile, a rising lightness profile and a per-stop hue drift) and the set was
picked by a search that chose the most constrained concept first and swept
randomised orders.

Two things that went wrong and are worth knowing. The first search constrained
only the first stop's hue, and the drift carried later stops out of the window:
it produced a pink Coffee, an olive Water and Ice and a green Night Sky. Every
stop's hue is constrained now. And my own hue to name mapping was wrong, so the
bands were rewritten after measuring the CIELAB hue angle of 25 reference
colours and of all 18 shipped gradients (red 40, orange 60, amber 77, yellow
103, green 136, teal 196, azure 285, blue 306, violet 312, magenta 328, pink 3,
brown 57, copper 64, gold 91). That mapping is in the search notes.

## Dropped and reworked

Nothing was dropped by the checker except one candidate. Brimstone was first
authored as crimson (hue 352 to 16) and was infeasible at every margin: it was
reworked as sulphur yellow, which fits the name and restored feasibility.

Five entries passed the checker and still looked wrong on the sheet, so their
bands were tightened and they were re-searched: Brimstone was magenta, Midnight
was lavender, Neon Lime was olive, Graphite was lavender, Mocha was bright red.
Neon Orange was renamed Neon Amber because hue 72 is amber, rather than forcing
the colour to the name.

Ten concepts were cut by me to land near 60, not by the gate: Macchiato,
Bronze, Chicory, Tidepool, Meltwater, Meadow, Ultraviolet, Acid Yellow,
Buttercream, Kiln.

## Checks that passed

tools/gradient_check.py: OK, every rule passes. 60 gradients, 8 categories,
1770 pairs. No threshold loosened, no pair added to the exemption list, and
the four exemptions are still the same four pairs inside the original 18. The
closest pair that is not exempt is still Sunset and Fire at 8.96 mean dE2000,
and the closest pair involving a new gradient is 8.99 (Crema and Blowtorch,
and Aurora and Fern). Brightest first stop Copper at 0.00301 relative luminance
against the 0.0040 ceiling. Dimmest endpoint Eclipse at L* 72.93 against the
58.0 floor.

First 18 unchanged: sha256 of the first 18 entries is
866c1602a3567594daaeef3398f750c10823990ce6fd107d9b1a7aba4a007f57 before and
after. The diff of data/gradients.json is 504 insertions and 0 deletions.

scripts/gen_gradients.py --check: all three outputs up to date. Their names,
categories, order and every stop triple were compared against the source
programmatically, not by eye. The three generated diffs are pure insertions
too: header 42, web table 210, runner module 84, all with 0 deletions.

pio test -e native_settingsui: 67 of 67 pass. Two gm-nov3.7 fixtures had to be
repointed, described in the commit message.

tools/animbench make check: every stage OK, ending 40 of 44 exact, 4 within a
recorded allowance, 0 over. ramp parity OK on 5184 cases and 1327104 ramp
entries. swatch_parity PASS on 511 ramps. gradient_check_test all cases pass.
ramp_parity.js needed a fix to get there: at 60 gradients its pipe to ramp_dump
deadlocked on WSL1 and make check hung, so the exchange goes through temp files.

pio run -e display-sim: SUCCESS.
python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only animation: PASS, 215 checks, 0 failed,
4 pages audited clean, smallest target 56x56.
npx prettier --check on the web table: clean. npm run lint:check: 0 errors.

## Cost

Flash rodata, from the linker map of two display-loadtest builds that differ
only in the generated header, with src/display/webassets held constant:
.flash.rodata 2,620,916 bytes at 18 and 2,622,500 at 60, so 1,584 bytes for 42
gradients. That splits into the THEME_DEFS table (0x1f8 = 504 bytes at 18,
0x690 = 1,680 at 60, so 1,176 bytes at 28 bytes an entry), 375 bytes of name
strings and 33 bytes of padding. Total flash image growth is the same 1,584
bytes (5,941,339 to 5,942,923). Internal RAM is 110,040 bytes in both builds,
unchanged, which is expected since the table is rodata.

Web bundle, from a real scripts/build_webui.sh run: src/display/webassets/
web_ui.bin goes from 506,851 to 508,506 bytes, up 1,655 bytes or 0.33%.

## Contact sheet

tools/gradient_sheet.png in the worktree
/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/.claude/worktrees/gm-2cl-6-dials. 770 x 3248, all 60
gradients, brightness 100%, rolloff 100%, gain 256, ramp mode. It is gitignored
(.gitignore line 50), so it is a local artifact, not part of the commit. Every
batch was looked at on a sheet before the next one was authored, which is how
the five off-name entries above were caught.

## Acceptance criteria not met, and why

I did not hold the bench board, so four criteria are untouched and this bead
should not be considered finished on them:

- the recorded device framebuffer comparison for at least one batch
- a device with an active legacy Custom booting on the final build and keeping
  its rendered gradient
- the firmware and web check that selects the first and last appended entries
  and verifies their refs and names after reopening settings and after reboot
- the gm-nov3.7 compatibility fixtures against the final table on hardware
  (they pass on the host)

gm-nov3.13 in the board queue covers the sentinel migration on hardware and now
has a build with more than 18 built-ins to run against.

pio run -e display: SUCCESS, 2 min 27 s, flash 5,899,267 bytes at 90.0%,

title: Web browse grid of gradient swatches
description:

sixty names.

The grouped `<select>` from that bead stays the control that owns the value
and keeps keyboard and screen reader use working. This adds a "Browse" button
beside it that opens a dialog showing every gradient as a swatch, grouped by
category, with the current one marked. Choosing one closes the dialog and
writes the same ref the select would have written.

## Acceptance criteria

      category order, and the user's saved gradients first when the library is

      `npm run build` alone.

title: Freeze the legacy custom gradient sentinel and finish the migration
description:
Freeze the legacy custom-gradient meaning and migrate without changing existing selections or losing stored data.

This blocks gm-nov3.5. Do not append production gradients until this bead lands. Larger tables used only by tests are allowed.

## Separate legacy settings from explicit refs

The legacy integer namespace is historical: 0 to 17 are the original built-ins, and 18 means the old single custom gradient. Other legacy integers fall back to built-in 0. Use a named constant equal to 18, independent of the generated table length.

An explicit decimal ref in bgAnimGradientRef or bgAnimThemeMap names the built-in at that index. Resolve a valid built-in ref directly, without passing it through the legacy custom branch. Thus ref "18" can select the first appended built-in even while an old custom string remains stored.

Legacy integer 18 with an empty or malformed custom string still falls back to built-in 0. Do not make clearing the string change that integer into an appended built-in.

Keep the resolution order: resolving per-animation ref, resolving global ref, legacy fallback. Preserve decimal and c<id> storage formats.

## Migration rules

The current migration leaves the old custom string behind. Its presence alone is not evidence that the user still selects it.

Preserve existing library entries, ids, names, global refs, and map slots. In particular, do not replace a newer global selection, fill empty map slots, or infer that a map full of c1 entries should be cleared.

A valid legacy custom gradient may be copied into the library without activating it. Reuse an existing entry with the same gradient semantics before allocating an unused id in the accepted range 1 to 99999. Do not rely on the name "Custom" or assume id 1 is free.

Only replace an empty global ref with c<id> when legacy integer 18 and a valid custom string supply the global fallback. Preserve non-empty global refs, including currently unresolved refs that could resolve after an upgrade. Where preserving such a ref requires the legacy fallback to remain, retain the legacy fields.

Respect BG_GRADIENT_LIB_MAX and BG_GRADIENT_LIB_MAX_LEN. If no valid destination fits, keep the source and legacy resolution intact, leave the existing library and refs unchanged, and report that migration was deferred. Never evict a saved gradient or write an invalid library to force completion.

Preserve the legacy rendering semantics. The legacy resolver discards explicit positions and uses uniform interpolation. Copying a positioned legacy string into a positional library entry must not change the active image. Existing library entries retain their own position semantics.

Clear the old custom string only after its replacement is durable and no retained legacy fallback needs it. Reset the legacy theme to 0 only when doing so preserves the intended resolution. An inactive leftover must never become the new global selection.

## Persistence

Settings::Guard prevents task interleaving but does not make NVS writes atomic. Settings::doSave writes properties separately and continues after failures. A failed empty-string write can also report success.

Use staged, checked persistence or an equivalent recoverable design. Persist the library destination before publishing its ref, and persist the ref before retiring the active legacy fallback. Do not mark all these fields dirty together and assume setter order is persistence order.

Recovery after any failed write or reboot must keep the custom data available and preserve the effective gradient. Re-running after partial completion must reuse the destination rather than add duplicates. Treat an unverified clear as potentially incomplete.

## Rollback mirrors and surfaces

A selected built-in 0 to 17 mirrors unchanged into bgAnimTheme. A selected built-in above 17 mirrors as 0, not 17. Library selections keep the existing legacy fallback.

Apply that policy to the web form assignment, the firmware POST handler, and both the display's live assignment and commit paths. Otherwise a later library selection or category commit can restore an unsafe mirror.

Delete BG_THEME_CUSTOM or freeze it at 18 with a historical comment. Update the corresponding API comments.

Both settings surfaces must represent a retained legacy Custom fallback accurately. They must not label or preview it as appended built-in 18, and opening or cancelling an editor must not rewrite it. A read-only current-value representation is sufficient when migration is deferred; no new stored ref grammar is needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Source inspection finds one named historical sentinel equal to 18, no custom sentinel derived from table length, and direct resolution of valid explicit built-in refs.
- [ ] Host tests invoke the migration logic used by the boot path, not a separate test-only implementation. Extract host-testable logic from DefaultUI if needed.
- [ ] Tests with the original table and a larger test table cover legacy integers 0 to 17, 18 with valid, empty and malformed custom strings, and invalid legacy integers. Their legacy meanings remain unchanged.
- [ ] With a larger test table, explicit global and per-animation refs "18" and "30" resolve to those built-ins even with a valid retained legacy custom string.
- [ ] A pre-library active Custom fixture gains a library entry and global c<id> ref, keeps its map unchanged, and resolves to the same stops and interpolation semantics before and after migration.
- [ ] Fixtures with a newer built-in global ref, a library global ref, a non-empty unresolved global ref, mixed map overrides, and an inactive old custom string preserve the existing refs and effective gradients.
- [ ] Fixtures cover an existing matching entry, occupied id 1, non-contiguous ids including 99999, a full 12-entry library, the serialized length limit, and a malformed existing library. No existing entry is overwritten and no invalid library is produced.
- [ ] A positioned legacy custom fixture preserves its old uniform rendering. Existing positional library gradients remain positional.
- [ ] Fault tests fail each migration persistence step and reboot after each durable step. The source remains available, the effective gradient is preserved, and recovery creates no duplicate destination.
- [ ] Fault tests include a clear that fails while reporting success. A second boot remains safe and does not reactivate an inactive custom string.
- [ ] A completed migration followed by another boot changes no settings and adds no entries.
- [ ] Tests cover web assignment, POST handling, display live assignment and display commit for built-ins 17, 18 and 30. The last two mirror as 0. Selecting an appended built-in and then a library entry before saving does not leave an appended integer in the mirror.
- [ ] Upgrade, rollback and upgrade tests assert exact results: global built-in 30 resolves as 30 on the larger build, as built-in 0 on the 18-theme build, and as 30 again after upgrade. Repeat for index 18 and for a per-animation override falling back through the global.
- [ ] Web and display checks cover a deferred legacy Custom fallback: correct current name and preview, with no setting change on open and cancel.
- [ ] pio test -e native_settingsui passes with the new cases. Device and simulator builds link after the resolver and migration changes.
- [ ] A device test build with a larger temporary table preserves an active legacy custom gradient across boot. Record the fixture, tone, animation parameters and comparison method. Use a controlled sample or repeatable frame state for the framebuffer comparison, not equality between unrelated moving frames. Do not commit temporary production table entries.
notes:
Landed as 2fd637eb on anims/astra.

What was built

- BG_THEME_LEGACY_CUSTOM = 18 in BgAnim.h, the one named historical sentinel,
  independent of the table length. Mirrored as BG_THEME_CUSTOM = 18 in
  web/src/config/bgAnimations.js, which was BG_THEMES.length before.
- bg_resolve_theme applies the frozen rules: 0 to 17 built-ins, 18 the custom
  string (built-in 0 when it is empty or malformed), anything else built-in 0.
- bg_resolve_anim_theme fills a valid explicit built-in ref straight from the
  table and returns, so it never passes through the legacy branch. Resolution
  order (map ref, global ref, legacy) and the decimal and c<id> formats are
  unchanged.
- Migration split into bg_plan_gradient_migration (pure) and
  bg_run_gradient_migration (over a BgGradientStore), both in BgAnimThemes.cpp.
  DefaultUI::migrateBgAnimGradients supplies the store over Settings and is
  the boot path, so the host tests drive the shipped code, not a copy.
- The plan never reads a parsable custom string as "in use", never touches
  bgAnimThemeMap, never replaces a non-empty global ref, reuses an existing
  entry with the same gradient semantics, skips ids any stored ref names,
  writes the uniform form (the legacy resolver discards positions), and defers
  with no writes when the library is full, over the length cap, or malformed.
  It retires the legacy pair only when it published the ref itself, when
  bgAnimTheme does not name the custom gradient, or when the stored global ref
  already resolves to the same entry (the re-run case).
- Staged persistence: library, then ref, then the legacy pair, each its own
  flushNow(), because doSave writes bg_th and bg_ct before bg_gl and bg_gref
  and continues past a failed key. The clear is treated as unverifiable.
- One mirror policy, bg_legacy_mirror_for_ref (and legacyThemeMirror in JS),
  applied by all four writers: the web form's globalAssignFields, the firmware
  POST handler, the display's live row and the display's commit. 0 to 17
  unchanged, 18 and above as 0, library and unresolvable refs leave it alone.
  The POST handler also clamps a raw bgAnimTheme argument to 0..18.
- Both surfaces name a retained legacy fallback "Custom (legacy)" and show its
  real stops, read only. Web: BG_LEGACY_CUSTOM_REF, a disabled option, and
  globalAssignFields writes nothing for it. Display: globalGradientLabel.

Checked

- pio test -e native_settingsui: PASS, 57 cases. New groups I (frozen
  namespace, direct ref resolution, upgrade/rollback/upgrade, mirror policy),
  J (migration fixtures) and K (fault injection). Groups I and J run against
  the shipped table and a 60-entry test table swapped in by
  bg_test_set_theme_table, which is compiled only under GM_BGANIM_TEST_TABLE
  and defined only by the test file. No temporary table is committed.
- node tools/gradient_mirror_check.mjs: PASS, 53 checks (new file).
- pio run -e display-sim: SUCCESS. pio run -e display-loadtest: SUCCESS.
- python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py: animation scenario PASS, 93 checks, 0
  failed; also temps, display, machine, status, rig all pass. One pre-existing
  failure in schedules (malformed_fixture_wire) that this bead did not touch:
  commit afb1c58f made the web handler drop a schedule entry whose time is not
  HH:MM, and test_schedules.py still expects it stored.
- web: npm run lint:check clean for the changed files (6 pre-existing warnings
  elsewhere), prettier clean, npm run build succeeds.

Not checked, and why

- The device criterion (a test build with a larger temporary table, preserving
  an active legacy custom gradient across a boot and comparing framebuffers).
  This loop forbids flashing the bench board. Nothing about the migration has
  run on hardware.
- pio run -e display was not built: the display libdeps do not install in this
  worktree on WSL1. display-loadtest covers the same sources.
- The display surface's "Custom (legacy)" label cannot be exercised on the
  simulator: the sim excludes BgAnimThemes.cpp, so bg_custom_valid is a stub
  returning false and the state is unreachable there. The label's inputs
  (bg_legacy_builtin, bg_custom_valid) are covered by host tests; the LVGL
  glue in CatAnimation.cpp is verified by reading. The stub keeps the sim's
  existing behaviour, so the settings runner is unaffected.
- "No setting change on open and cancel" is checked on the web side by
  globalAssignFields returning an empty map for the legacy ref, and on the
  display side by reading: the row's only writer is globalGradientOnCycle.

One behaviour change worth knowing: the migration no longer writes c1 into
every bgAnimThemeMap slot the way the first version did. It sets
bgAnimGradientRef instead, which draws the same gradient everywhere and leaves
the user's map alone.

title: Rebuild the palette parity oracle when its headers change
description:
Commit 71bd9f20 introduced build/ramp_dump without dependencies on its project headers. tools/animbench/Makefile lists the C++ sources and selected shim headers, but omits BgAnimCommon.h, whose inline rgb565 function contributes directly to the sampled output.

A read-only reproduction from tools/animbench:

```sh
make -n -W ../../src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimCommon.h build/ramp_dump
```

This reports that the binary is up to date. A header-only change can therefore leave make check comparing JS against an older implementation.

Track the oracle's included project headers, using complete explicit dependencies or compiler-generated dependencies. Preserve firmware arithmetic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an initial host build, the dry-run command above schedules recompilation of build/ramp_dump.
- [ ] Changes to BgAnim.h and BgAnimThemeTable.h also invalidate the oracle.
- [ ] In an isolated test checkout, changing only the header's RGB565 arithmetic rebuilds the oracle and makes parity fail against unchanged JS.
- [ ] With the mutation removed, palette parity and the gradient checker pass.
notes:
Done in 8ca18627. tools/animbench/Makefile now has the compiler write the header
list for build/ramp_dump, build/bench and build/interlace_check: one extra -MM -MP
pass per link, target set to the binary, written to <binary>.d and included on the
next run. One file per binary because agents build here at the same time with
different BIN values. A single -MF pass cannot do it: with several sources on one
command line, -MF keeps only the last source's headers (checked directly). The
Makefile is a prerequisite too, so a CXXFLAGS change rebuilds, and so does the
first build after this commit, which is the build that writes the first .d.

tools/animbench/dep_check.sh is the new guard and make check runs it first. For
each binary and each of BgAnimCommon.h, BgAnim.h and BgAnimThemeTable.h it builds
the binary, then asks make -n -W what it would do.

All four acceptance criteria checked.

1. After a build, `make -n -W .../BgAnimCommon.h build/ramp_dump` schedules the
   link plus the dep pass, in the live worktree and in a clean checkout made from
   HEAD. Before the change the same command in the same clean checkout said
   "up to date".
2. BgAnim.h and BgAnimThemeTable.h behave the same, and the generated .d lists
   all eight headers the oracle includes: BgAnim.h, BgAnimCommon.h,
   BgAnimThemeTable.h, mathcount.h and the four shims, one of which (esp_wifi.h)
   the hand-written list did not have.
3. Isolated checkout unpacked from HEAD into a temp dir, the bench board not
   touched. Changed `(b >> 3)` to `(b >> 4)` in rgb565 in BgAnimCommon.h. With
   the old Makefile: make said "up to date" and `node web/ramp_parity.js` passed
   over all 552,960 entries, which is the defect in full. With the new Makefile
   the same header state rebuilt the oracle and parity failed, 1,620 of 2,160
   cases differing, exit 1.
4. Mutation reverted: the .d alone triggered the rebuild (no touch of anything

title: Decide whether secondary web text needs a contrast floor
description:
Secondary text across the web UI sits below the usual 4.5 to 1 contrast floor
for small text, on the light theme and on coffee.

Found while fixing one instance of it (gm-nov3.20). The gradient browser's
category headings were `text-base-content/60`, which measures 3.05 to 1 on
light and 3.25 on coffee. Raising them to `/80` cleared 4.5 in all four
themes: light 4.97, dark 7.35, coffee 4.76, nord 6.03.

The same treatment is in roughly forty other places, including the shared
`CardTitle` component at `/55` and the gradient browser's own notice
paragraph at `GradientBrowser.jsx:111`. Those were deliberately left alone,
because changing a shared component and forty call sites is a wider decision
than one bead about one dialog.

This is a tracking item, not a decision. Someone has to choose whether the
project wants a contrast floor for secondary text, and if so whether it is
enforced by raising the shared tokens or by a check.

## How it was measured

Real Chrome, painting the heading's computed colour over the panel's
`base-100` on a canvas and reading the pixel back, so the opacity modifier's
`color-mix()` is resolved by the browser rather than parsed. An offline
calculation from the oklch values in `web/src/style.css` agreed within
rounding. `tools/gradient_browse_browser.py` carries the working method.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether secondary text has a contrast floor
      and what it is.
- [ ] If there is a floor, every place below it is listed with its measured
      ratio per theme, not estimated.
- [ ] If the fix is shared tokens, the four themes are each measured after the
      change, and the visual hierarchy still reads (secondary text must stay
      visibly secondary, not become body text).
- [ ] If the project decides not to raise them, that decision is written down
      so this is not rediscovered.
notes: Decision 2026-10-01 (owner, conservative default): no contrast floor for secondary web text in this pass. Secondary text is text-base-content/N, not a named token. Measured with tools/web_contrast.mjs (oklch from web/src/style.css, alpha-composited in sRGB, within 0.07 of the gm-nov3.20 Chrome readback), over base-100: /50 light 2.44 dark 3.65 coffee 2.70 nord 2.71; /55 (CardTitle) 2.72 4.15 2.99 3.08; /60 (66 uses) 3.05 4.71 3.28 3.49; /70 3.86 5.95 3.97 4.57; /80 4.97 7.42 4.81 6.09 (lowest level clearing 4.5 in all four). Lowest for a common level: /60 light over base-200, 2.95. Lowest overall: /20 light over base-200, 1.37 (3 uses). Recorded in the comment above the themes in web/src/style.css (bb4d806b).
