title: Schedules scenario fails on a fixture the web handler no longer accepts
description:
check_malformed_time_editor in tools/settings_ui_tests/test_schedules.py
writes "07:00|1111111;|1111111" through the web settings POST and asserts the
device stores it back unchanged. The device stores "07:00|1111111": since
2026-09-09 WebUIPlugin's isScheduleTime drops any entry whose time is not HH:MM
in range, and the second entry's time is empty. So the check fails on every
run, and with it the whole schedules scenario, which hides any real regression
the rest of that scenario would catch.

The crash the check guards against is still worth guarding. The editor used to
slice the stored string and substr(3, 2) on an empty time threw out_of_range,
which aborts a firmware built without exceptions; both rows now read it through
the model's scheduleTimeParts. What changed is that the web path can no longer
create the entry, so the test has to plant it another way or assert against
what the firmware actually stores.

Done when: python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only schedules passes on the
simulator; the malformed-time path is still exercised, either through a route
that can still store such an entry or by asserting the editor opens on 00:00
for the entry the firmware does keep; the docstring says which, and says that
the web handler drops a malformed time so the next reader does not put the old
assertion back.
notes:
Done in 788a2e0c (tools/settings_ui_tests/test_schedules.py only).

Which option: both. The check now asserts what the firmware actually stores
(a POST of "07:00|1111111;|1111111" comes back as "07:00|1111111"), and then
plants the malformed entry through the one route that can still store it, so
the editor is still made to read an empty time.

Why a planting route exists at all: the web POST is the only live writer that
can be reached from the test, and isScheduleTime filters it; the display's own
commit always formats HH:MM. But the NVS codec
(PreferencesCodec<vector<AutoWakeupSchedule>>::read, Settings.cpp) keeps any
entry that has a "|" in it, which is why a device that stored one before
2026-09-09 still carries it. The simulator keeps its preferences as one JSON
file per namespace (sim/platform/preferences_shim.cpp), so the new helper
plant_stored_schedules writes ab_schedules in sim_data/nvs/controller.json and
restarts the process through Sim.restart(), whose docstring says it exists for
exactly this. Verified by probe before writing the check: the restarted
simulator reports '07:00|1111111;|1111111' and the editor opens on 00 and 00.

Two details the helper has to get right. Settings writes a key only when its
value changes, so a marker save is what puts ab_schedules in the file at all,
and waiting for the file to carry the marker also proves the save task flushed
everything else the run had changed, which the terminate would otherwise drop.
The relaunch truncates the simulator's log, so the log so far is copied aside.

The docstring says, in those words, that the web handler drops a malformed
time and that the old assertion must not come back.

Ran on the simulator (no board, another agent held it):
- python3 tools/settings_ui_tests/test_schedules.py: PASS, 91 of 91.
- python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --only schedules: PASS, 91 checks, 0 failed.
- python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py (whole suite): PASS, 550 checks across 8
  scenarios, 0 failures (temps 48, display 35, animation 222, gradientdraft 56,
  machine 39, schedules 91, status 40, rig 19). The run before this one was
  542 checks with 1 failure, this check.

Left undone: nothing in the criteria. One nearby staleness not fixed, because
it is in another agent's file: the comment above
test_schedule_time_parts_reads_malformed_as_midnight in
test/test_settings_model/test_settings_model.cpp still says "the web handler
stores any time string the browser sends", which stopped being true on
2026-09-09. The test itself is correct and still the home of the midnight rule.

title: Deploy a locally built display image over the air
description:
The machine is plumbed in and its USB port is not reachable, so the only way
to change the firmware is over the air. The device's OTA today is
GitHubOTA: it resolves a GitHub release, compares semver, and refuses to
install anything that is not newer. That is a release flow. There is no way to
point it at an image a developer has just built, and every URL it uses is
built from the compile-time RELEASE_URL, so the OTA channel setting cannot
reach one either.

## What to add

`POST /api/ota/dev?url=<http url>` records the URL; `WebUIPlugin::loop()` runs
the download on the display task, where every other OTA already runs.
`GitHubOTA::updateFromUrl` skips the version check and the release lookup,
takes a plain client for http, and reboots on success.

`GET /api/ota/info` reports what is running, so a deploy can be verified:
`esp_app_get_elf_sha256` is the only field that moves between two builds of
the same dirty tree.

`tools/ota_dev.py` builds, serves the image from the host, asks the board to
pull it, and checks the sha changed.

Pull rather than push, because a POST carrying the 6 MB image would have to
write flash from the async_tcp callback: the erases block for tens of seconds
and would stall the web server and sit under the task watchdog. The pull path
is the one the release update already uses, down to the ota:update:start event
that stops the panel for the download.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A build with the endpoint can be deployed to a board with no USB
      connection, and the board comes back running the new image.
- [ ] /api/ota/info reports a different sha before and after.
- [ ] A URL that is not http:// or https:// is refused with 400, and so is a
      missing or over-long one.
- [ ] A POST while a process is running is refused with 409.
- [ ] A second POST while one is pending is refused with 409.
- [ ] A failed update leaves the board answering and able to accept another.
- [ ] A single-slot build refuses the update rather than erasing the running
      app.
- [ ] -DGM_DEV_OTA=0 compiles both routes out.
- [ ] pio run -e display and -e display-sim link.

## Tests

- The route plumbing on the simulator: every refusal, the queue, and recovery
  after the stub reports a failed update.
- One real deploy to the bench board, USB unplugged.

## Bootstrap

The board has to be running a build that carries the endpoint before any of
this works. The image that first carries it has to arrive over USB or through
a GitHub release; that is a one-time cost and it is the owner's call which.
notes: Closed 2026-10-01 from the bench. Used three times that day to flash the bench board (no COM port on the PC): POST /api/ota/dev?url= against python3 -m http.server in the session scratchpad, /api/ota/info sha moved each time and the board came back on the new image. The route is in the merged production build (v1.9.22-idf5, GM_DEV_OTA on). The 400/409/single-slot/GM_DEV_OTA=0 items are covered by e7d0315c's own checks; the display and display-sim builds link on 307297d1.

comments.author: oystein
comments.text:
Bootstrap staged 2026-09-17. The board has no reachable USB port and its
running build has no /api/ota/dev, so the first image carrying the endpoint
goes through the nightly GitHub release, which is the only arbitrary-ish URL
the running firmware will accept (RELEASE_URL is compile-time and the channel
setting is narrowed to "latest" or "nightly" at each use).

Published to oysteinkrog/gaggimate releases/nightly:
  display-firmware.bin  5,942,096 B, sha256 9c983fea00cc281cdaa5d0a70b6a81455deec0db01f08304f79bdc25e7c0b930
  version.txt           v1.9.9-otaboot

The image is -e display built from the tree at b268df60 plus the uncommitted
OTA work (BUILD_GIT_VERSION v1.9.8-sleep9-724-gb268df60-dirty), with the real
509,026 B web blob, and it carries /api/ota/dev, /api/ota/info and the dev OTA
log line. The published bytes were re-downloaded and hash-matched against the
local build.

Why 1.9.9: semver_compare compares major/minor/patch before any prerelease
identifier (semver.c:308), so 1.9.9-otaboot beats the board's 1.9.8 whatever
the suffixes say. version.txt is trimmed and its leading "v" stripped by
checkForUpdates, so the file holds "v1.9.9-otaboot".

GitHub broke while this was being published. `gh release upload --clobber`
deleted display-firmware.bin and version.txt and then failed with HTTP 500
"Error creating asset temp dir", leaving the public release without the two
assets a display OTA needs (the filesystem image is not used since GM-106).
Every retry to that release id failed the same way while a fresh draft release
in the same repo accepted an upload, so the release object itself was in a bad
state. Repaired by downloading all ten surviving assets, deleting the release
(the nightly git tag is a separate object and was left alone), recreating it on
the same tag, and re-uploading all twelve. Three of those twelve still hit a
500 on the first try and landed on a retry, so the failure is intermittent per
asset, not per release: retry rather than re-engineer. CI publishes to this
same release with removeArtifacts on every push to master or idf5, so the next
nightly run overwrites all of it, including version.txt.

Nothing auto-applies an update: checkForUpdates only compares, and ota->update
runs from a user request (WebUIPlugin.cpp:240).

Still to do: the owner sets the OTA channel to nightly and presses the display
update button, then the real dev path gets its first hardware run through
tools/ota_dev.py, and the CI display-firmware.bin and version.txt go back on
the release.

title: A brew the display started keeps the pump running with no upper bound
description:
2026-10-01, bench board linked over BLE to the real controller. A scripted settings test (/api/debug/tap) landed taps on the brew screen's start control after the settings cover had closed under them (the board reset at about 15:39), and the resulting brew ran the pump for about 65 minutes until the owner cut the power. Nothing stopped it: not a brew time limit on the controller, not a volumetric target, not the display's tap-driven runner moving on, and a display reset does not end a running brew on the controller.

What should bound it, to decide:
- A controller-side maximum brew duration (manual brew included), so the pump never runs longer than any real shot plus margin, whatever the display does.
- The controller ending a running brew when the display's BLE link drops or the display reboots (the display is the only thing that can stop it today).
- The bench: the debug tap route and the synthetic rig must refuse to run while a real controller link is up, or the tap runner must check the active screen before every tap. The runner's assumption that the cover is still open is what put taps on the brew screen.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A manual brew started on the display stops on the controller after a configured maximum (default to decide; well under 10 minutes) even if the display never sends stop.
- [ ] A running brew ends when the BLE link to the display drops.
- [ ] /api/debug/tap (and the settings runner) refuse or guard when a real controller is connected, with a test.
notes: bc71891e implements all three acceptance items; not closed. (1) Controller: BrewGuard.h bounds a brew (brew valve open) at BREW_MAX_DURATION_MS = 300 s, the conservative first choice. THE DEFAULT IS THE OWNER'S TO CONFIRM; the display's own brew cap is also 300 s, so a longer real shot needs both raised. Past it the pump goes off and the valve closes, and the controller sends ERROR_CODE_BREW_STOPPED (7). The stop latches until the display closes the valve, because the display resends full state on reconnect. The display ends its process on code 7; an older display shows 'Unknown error'. (2) Controller: GaggiMateServer::onConnectionChange; a link drop or ping timeout during a brew stops it and latches the same way. (3) Display: /api/debug/tap and /api/debug/settingsui commands answer 409 controller_linked while g_bleClientConnected; the shell state reports controller_linked; the settings runner refuses on a linked or unknown device; on a device every tap reads the shell state and the run halts (latched) if the cover closed. Tests: make -C tools/brew_guard_check check (52 guard checks under ASan/UBSan, 22 rig checks against a fake device); settings_ui_test --only rig,status PASS on the simulator; controller, display and display-sim build. Not done: THE CONTROLLER ON THE BENCH BOARD STILL RUNS THE OLD FIRMWARE, so items 1 and 2 are unverified on hardware and do not protect the bench yet; display-loadtest (the build where the tap gate is live on a board) was not built; nothing ran on the board.

title: Fix three defects in the shared settings runner harness
description:
Three defects in the shared settings-runner harness, found by gm-nov3.11 while
running the picker checks on the bench board. Each was left in place because
another agent held the file at the time, and the drift they caused was
repaired by hand for that run.

1. `Rig.rows_on_page` keys rows by their visible name, so two rows with the
   same name collapse into one. With two saved gradients both called "Custom"
   a page of 12 rows reads as 11. Any check that counts rows, or that locates
   a row by name when names repeat, is wrong on that page. Saved gradient
   names are user supplied and repeat easily.

2. `swatch_strip` reads `/api/debug/fb?step=1`. The bench board answers that
   with 4800 bytes of the 460800 it asked for. That is gm-6ivh, not a harness
   defect in itself, but the harness accepts the short read without saying so,
   which turns a degraded endpoint into a quiet sampling change.

3. `web_save()` refuses a real host by design, so four device checks in
   `test_animation.py` skip the restore they were written to perform. The
   fixture they set up is then left on the board for the next check.

A fourth item, recorded here because it was found in the same run and has the
same shape: `gradient_precedence_across_animations` assumes the category it
picks contains at least two built-ins. Coffee contains one on the 18 entry
table, so the check fails on a board whose stored ref lands in Coffee. That is
a latent flake in the check, not a firmware defect, and the expanded table
changes which categories are at risk rather than removing the assumption.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Rig.rows_on_page` returns every row on a page when two or more rows
      share a name, and a check that counts rows on a page with two gradients
      named "Custom" reads 12, not 11. Add that fixture.
- [ ] `swatch_strip` either gets the bytes it asked for or fails loudly with
      the byte counts. A short read never silently becomes a narrower sample.
- [ ] The four `test_animation.py` device checks restore what they changed, or
      they refuse to run against a real host and say why. Silent skipping of a
      restore is not acceptable either way.
- [ ] `gradient_precedence_across_animations` chooses a category by what the
      live table actually contains, and passes on a board whose stored ref is
      in a single entry category.
- [ ] The whole runner passes on the simulator after the changes, and the
      counts in the report are stated before and after.
notes:
Done in 66526a20 on anims/astra. Five files, all harness: rig.py,
test_animation.py, picker_device_checks.py, gradient_sheet.py,
dial_elem_check.py. No firmware change.

1. Rig.rows_on_page returns one entry per row, repeats kept (it collected
   rows into a dict keyed by the visible name). test_animation.py's
   rows_across_pages no longer drops a name it has already seen either, and
   picker_device_checks.py's local rows_with_repeats now uses the shared
   helper instead of walking the tagged objects itself.

   The fixture is check_gradient_picker_repeated_names: a twelve entry
   library with two entries called "Custom", not adjacent, listed through
   the picker's My gradients page. It asserts twelve rows across the pages,
   the stored order, two rows named Custom, and five rows on the first page
   read through Rig.rows_on_page directly.

   Shown failing first against the unfixed helper, built from git archive
   HEAD into a scratch tree with the new test file and HEAD's rig.py (the
   shared tree only ever held the fix): 11 rows listed for 12 entries, 4
   rows on a full first page, 5 of 7 checks failed. With the fix, 7 of 7
   pass and the library is restored byte for byte.

2. swatch_strip reads through a new Rig.fb(step), which raises when the body
   is shorter than the X-FB-Size header promised and names both byte counts.
   The reads are back at step 1. The short reads were gm-6ivh (28cec8ec),
   the response filler and not the heap, so the step 1 workarounds and the
   comments asserting them are gone from test_animation.py,
   picker_device_checks.py, gradient_sheet.py and dial_elem_check.py.
   picker_device_checks.py's third check now asserts that the whole dump
   arrives at step 1 rather than that it does not.

3. The four checks that used to catch web_save's refusal and return
   (gradient_picker_high_library_ids, the empty library half of
   gradient_picker_reachability, gradient_picker_web_interference,
   parameters_web_precedence) ask web_save_available() before they change
   anything and record a counted skip with the reason, the way
   test_temps.py does. parameters_web_precedence was the one that left a
   fixture behind: it stepped a parameter row before the save and returned
   without the reset. The reachability check asks only for the half that
   needs the save, so a device still runs the listing half.
   check_frame_rate_live_and_precedence and the precedence check's
   interference step took the same treatment.

4. category_for_ref(ref, preferred) picks a gradient category that holds a
   built-in other than ref: the preferred one when it can, else the first in
   table order that can. gradient_precedence_across_animations used it for
   all four of its categories, and the five other sites with the same
   assumption use it too.

Checks run: python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py on the simulator, before and
after.

  before  535 checks, 1 failed  (animation 215)
  after   542 checks, 1 failed  (animation 222)

The one failure is the same in both runs and is not this bead:
schedules/malformed_fixture_wire. test_schedules.py posts
"07:00|1111111;|1111111" and expects it back verbatim, and the firmware
drops an entry whose time is not HH:MM in range (isScheduleTime in
WebUIPlugin.cpp, 2026-09-09, recorded in CLAUDE.md). test_schedules.py is
not one of this bead's files and was left alone.

Not checked: nothing here ran on the board. Another agent held it. The three
device scripts (picker_device_checks.py, dial_elem_check.py, the
gradient_sheet.py notes) compile and import, and their behaviour on hardware
is unverified. picker_device_checks.py's fb_step1_is_whole is the check that
will confirm gm-6ivh from that script's side on the next board session.

title: Per-frame time from a wrapped delta: Lava, Silk, Silk2 (gm-bzu.50 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to gm-bzu.50 (bganim F2, Astra notes 2026-09-30). These frame() functions still build motion from absolute millis() in float (angle and wobble terms; Silk and Silk2's g_wtTurn/g_sheenWt already use an int64 product), so motion steps in 32 ms jumps after 3.1 days of uptime (256 ms after 24.9 days) and jumps at the 49.7-day wrap and on a speed change.

Where (line numbers from the review, at the commit before gm-bzu.50): AnimLava.cpp:611 and :617, AnimSilk.cpp:633-634, AnimSilk2.cpp:449-450 and :545.

How: move each onto bganim::AnimClock (src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnimClock.h, added by gm-bzu.50, commit e0288060). Keep each oscillator's own phase (a Q48 rate per oscillator, oscRad/oscTurnQ32), not one shared modulus. Keep the clock in a file-scope static that release() does not reset. A rate that depends on a parameter accumulates its own phase (see AnimFireflies.cpp g_ringQ32). Fireflies, Aurora, Starfield and Ember are worked examples. Lava and Silk2 have asm kernels behind GM_BGANIM_LAVA_ASM / GM_BGANIM_SILK2_ASM; keep the kernels bit-exact.

Acceptance: add each animation to kOnClock in tools/animbench/clock_check.cpp; make -C tools/animbench check passes (goldens, interlace_check and clock_check at 480, 240, 466 and 233); fuzz under ASan and make -f Makefile.lifecycle check pass; QEMU check_copies and the animation's test pass if a kernel changes; one bench animtest per animation.
notes:
2026-10-01, commit 1e538777.

Changed (AnimLava.cpp, AnimSilk.cpp, AnimSilk2.cpp, frame() and timing state only):
- All three take motion from bganim::AnimClock. Each oscillator has its own Q48 rate. Speed-scaled terms run on g_clock. Terms that never followed the speed setting run on g_wall, a second AnimClock at speed 1: Lava's radius pulse, and the k wobble in Silk and Silk2.
- Lava: BlobDef carries rx1, rx2, ry1, ry2 and rR, set in init(). The old 1.7, 1.13 and 0.9 factors are folded into the rates.
- Silk: SilkWave keeps A0, phk, kx and ky. The rates are constexpr tables kRateRot, kRateWt and kRateK. g_wtTurn comes from oscTurnQ32.
- Silk2: the angle wobbles, sheen rotation and sheen wt run on g_clock, and the sheen k wobble on g_wall. The fold phase has its own linear speed map (foldSpeed), so g_foldQ4 accumulates wall step x foldSpeed in 64 bits. Only bits 8 to 17 of foldBase*n are used, so the uint32 wrap of foldBase is continuous.
- The clocks and g_foldQ4 are file-scope statics that release() does not reset.
- No asm kernel changed. band() reads the same globals as before. check_copies passes with no re-transcription.

Verified:
- make check: GOLDENS OK. Lava matches exactly. Silk has 6, 8 and 16 px differing at frames 030, 120 and 210, max 9. Silk2 has 0, 6 and 4 px, max 9. All are float rounding out of 230,400 px and inside tolerance, so no golden was regenerated. interlace_check ALL OK at 480, 240, 466 and 233.
- clock_check with lava, silk and silk2 named explicitly: OK at 480, 240, 466 and 233, 39 of 39 steps moved. Against HEAD's three sources it fails all three (frame 0 from 10 days differs).
- Flags flipped on the host (LAVA_ASM=0, SILK_ASM=1, SILK2_ASM=0): goldens OK and clock_check OK at all four sizes.
- render_one --shapes ALL OK for all three, at 480 and 240.
- Fuzz under ASan and UBSan: exit 0, all three ok in the sweep and the align pass.
- make -f Makefile.lifecycle check: ALL OK.
- QEMU: check_copies PASS (15 tests). anim_lava, anim_silk and anim_silk2 all PASS on the firmware toolchain.
- pio run SUCCESS for display-sim, display and display-loadtest.

Not done:
- kOnClock in tools/animbench/clock_check.cpp still lacks lava, silk and silk2. The file was outside my reservation, and another teammate has an uncommitted edit there adding orbits and steam. The lead has been told.
- agent-mail did not respond on 127.0.0.1:8765, so no file reservations were made.

For the kdev rig: these three now carry state in frame(). Compare blobref against blob, not blob against the firmware's band().

Left for the bench (no board access). Registry ids are from BgAnimRegistry.cpp order:
  http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=1   (lava)
  http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=2   (silk)
  http://192.168.1.121/api/debug/animtest?anim=13  (silk2)
close_reason: Lava, Silk and Silk2 on AnimClock (1e538777); kOnClock entry pending in clock_check.cpp

title: Centre the settings tile on the menu and reach the info screen from Status
description:
The menu's centre held the info button and the mode word (BREW/STEAM/WATER, an EEZ expression on system.mode). Decided 2026-09-06: the settings tile moves to the centre, the mode word is dropped, and the info button is hidden. The info screen stays reachable from Settings > Status through a new "Device info" action row, because it is the only place that shows the WiFi setup QR code while the config access point is active.

## Acceptance
- On the menu the settings tile sits at (0, 0), the info button and the mode label are hidden, the ring holds the mode tiles only (four with grind or scale, three without), and rig.audit() on the menu reports no violations.
- Status page 1 has rows Scale, Time, Device info, Restart; tapping Device info leaves settings (committing) and shows the info screen; the runner's Status scenario checks it on the simulator.
- Production display builds; the simulator runner passes; the bench board run of temps, display, machine, schedules, status and rig passes.
close_reason: Settings tile centred, info button and mode word hidden, Device info row on Status opens the info screen. Menu audit clean on simulator and board; simulator status and rig scenarios pass; device run 8 PASS on six scenarios; webcam photo of the board confirms the layout. Commits b88e110a, 45a2fa42 and the docs commit.
